## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $D=B(x_0,a)\subset(0,1)^2$ be a disk with $a>0$, let $0<r\le a/2$, and let $\beta>0$. Define $\gamma_1\equiv1$ on $D$ and $\gamma_r:=1+\beta\chi_{B(x_0,r)}$, and put $\eta:=\beta/(2+\beta)$. Both conductivities belong to $\Gamma_{1,1+\beta}(D)$. For each $k\in\mathbb Z\setminus\{0\}$, with $n:=|k|$ and boundary Fourier mode $e_k(\theta):=e^{ik\theta}$, the induced weak DN maps on the trace quotient by constants satisfy
$$\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}e_k,\qquad \dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}[e_k]=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta(r/a)^{2n}}{1-\eta(r/a)^{2n}}e_k,$$
under the $L^2(\partial D)$ dual pairing; both maps annihilate the constant boundary class. If $Q_n:=\|[e_k]\|_{\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1}^2$ is the squared trace-quotient-by-constants norm of the mode, then
$$2\pi n\le Q_n\le 2\pi n+\frac{\pi a^2}{n+1},$$
and
$$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|_{\mathcal L(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1,(\mathcal D(D)/\mathbb C\mathbf1)^*)}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}(r/a)^2.$$

## Statement references

[[def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-class|The uniformly elliptic coefficient class $\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$.]]

[[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation|The $H^1$ and $H_0^1$ Sobolev spaces.]]

[[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities|The weak energy-form DN map on the trace quotient.]]

[[lem-ip-calderon-boundary-trace-quotient-identification|The trace quotient norm used for $\mathcal D(D)$.]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the disk $D=B(x_0,a)$; $0<r\le a/2$; $\beta>0$; and the measurable conductivities $\gamma_1,\gamma_r$.

[F1] For $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(D)$ the coefficient is real and uniformly bounded below and above; $H_0^1(D)$ is the closure of $C_c^\infty(D)$; and the DN map is the weak energy form on $\mathcal D(D)=H^1(D)/H_0^1(D)$ with representative-independent boundary functional. ([[def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-class]], [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]], [[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities]], [[lem-ip-calderon-rough-dn-map-wellposedness]])

[F2] The Fourier characters $e^{ik\theta}$ form a complete orthogonal basis of $L^2$ on the circle; Parseval and angular mode projections hold. ([[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]])

[F3] For $H^1$ functions on a smooth disk, integration by parts identifies the weak energy form with the outward normal flux when the solution is smooth near the boundary. ([[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]])

[F4] The trace quotient norm is the infimum of the $H^1$ norm over all interior representatives with the prescribed boundary class, and the trace identifies this quotient with the $W^{1/2,2}$ boundary space. ([[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities]], [[lem-ip-calderon-boundary-trace-quotient-identification]])

[F5] Restrictions of smooth ambient functions are dense in $H^1(D)$ because the disk is a bounded smooth domain. ([[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]])

[F6] Monotone convergence allows the nonnegative angular Parseval sums to pass through the radial integral. ([[thm-monotone-convergence-for-the-integral]])

[F7] An $H^1$ function is an $L^2$ class whose first distributional derivatives are also $L^2$ classes. ([[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]])

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed at the weak DN and smooth-density interfaces. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Countable Choice is assumed at the Fourier basis, weak solution and monotone-convergence interfaces. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

**Given:** The data in the statement.

1.1 Let $n=|k|$, $s=r/a$, and $\sigma=1+\beta$. In polar coordinates $\rho=|x-x_0|$, seek a solution with angular mode $e^{ik\theta}$, using $u_i=A\rho^ne^{ik\theta}$ for $\rho<r$ and $u_o=(B\rho^n+C\rho^{-n})e^{ik\theta}$ for $r<\rho<a$. Continuity of $u$ and continuity of $\gamma\partial_\rho u$ at $\rho=r$ give $C r^{-2n}=-\eta B$ because $(\sigma-1)/(\sigma+1)=\eta$. The boundary condition $u_o(a,\theta)=e_k(\theta)$ then gives $Ba^n=(1-\eta s^{2n})^{-1}$. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 Each piece is harmonic on its subdomain, and its value and conductivity-weighted normal derivative agree at $\rho=r$ by step 1.1. Both pieces and their classical gradients are bounded up to the interface because $r>0$. Testing a distributional first derivative against $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ and integrating by parts on the inner disk and annulus produces interface terms equal to the jump in $u$ times $\varphi$; the matching values cancel these terms, leaving the bounded piecewise classical derivatives. By [F7] the glued function belongs to $H^1(D)$. For any $z\in C_c^\infty(D)$, integration by parts on the inner disk and outer annulus cancels the interface flux terms and proves the weak equation. Since $C_c^\infty(D)$ is dense in $H_0^1(D)$ by [F1] and the energy form is continuous, the equation holds for every $z\in H_0^1(D)$. By [F1] the function is the unique solution for trace $e_k$. At $\rho=a$, the conductivity is $1$, so the outward flux is $$\partial_\rho u_o(a,\theta)=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}e_k(\theta).$$ The Gauss–Green identity [F3] identifies this flux with the weak DN functional. For $\gamma_1\equiv1$, the harmonic extension $(\rho/a)^n e_k(\theta)$ gives flux $(n/a)e_k$, and the constant solution has zero flux. [A1, A2, F1, F3, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 For each angle $\theta$, define $(R_\theta U)(x)=U(x_0+Q_\theta(x-x_0))$ on $D$, where $Q_\theta$ is the planar rotation matrix, and define $P_kU=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-ik\theta}R_\theta U\,d\theta$. By density [F5] and the rotation isometries, $\theta\mapsto R_\theta U$ is strongly continuous in $H^1(D)$ for every $U$, so this integral is the $H^1$ limit of its Riemann sums. Rotations preserve the $H^1(D)$ inner product; Minkowski's inequality makes $P_k$ a contraction, and character orthogonality [F2] makes it a self-adjoint projection with pairwise orthogonal ranges. For $w\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the map $\theta\mapsto R_\theta w$ is continuous in $H^1$ and every Riemann sum of the displayed integral is in $C_c^\infty(D)$, so $P_kw\in H_0^1(D)$; contraction and density in the definition of $H_0^1$ extend this invariance to all of $H_0^1(D)$. For a smooth restriction $U$, the polar-coordinate chain rule gives the $H^1$ norm as the integral of $|U|^2+|\partial_\rho U|^2+\rho^{-2}|\partial_\theta U|^2$ against $\rho\,d\rho d\theta$. Parseval [F2] for these three terms and monotone convergence [F6] in the radial integral show that the finite orthogonal sums $S_N:=\sum_{|k|\le N}P_k$ converge to $U$ in $H^1(D)$. For a general $U\in H^1(D)$, approximate by smooth restrictions using [F5]; on each annulus $\epsilon<\rho<a$ the polar map is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism, so the polar norm and Fourier identities pass to the limit there, and monotone convergence [F6] as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ gives the full-disk identities. Each $S_N$ is an orthogonal projection and hence a contraction; density [F5] therefore extends $S_NU\to U$ to every $U\in H^1(D)$. The induced quotient modes are thus a complete orthogonal family in $\mathcal D(D)$, and the constant mode is orthogonal to every nonzero mode. Since the trace is bounded and rotation-equivariant on smooth functions, [F4] and [F5] extend commutation to all of $H^1(D)$; the trace-kernel identity in [F4] then shows that each projected boundary class is a scalar multiple of one mode. For any $H^1$ representative $U$ of the boundary mode $e_k$, let $v(\rho)$ be its $k$th angular Fourier coefficient. Parseval gives $$\|U\|_{H^1(D)}^2\ge 2\pi\int_0^a\left(|v'(\rho)|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v(\rho)|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho.$$ The trace condition gives $v(a)=1$. On every interval $[\epsilon,a]$, the one-dimensional Sobolev representative of $v$ is absolutely continuous, and expansion of the square yields $$\int_\epsilon^a\left(|v'|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho=\int_\epsilon^a\left|v'-\frac n\rho v\right|^2\rho\,d\rho+n|v(a)|^2-n|v(\epsilon)|^2.$$ The full energy being finite implies $\int_0^a|v(\rho)|^2\rho^{-1}d\rho<\infty$, so there is a sequence $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ with $v(\epsilon_j)\to0$; otherwise $|v|$ would be bounded below near zero and this integral would diverge. Letting $\epsilon=\epsilon_j$ and using nonnegativity of the square proves that the radial energy is at least $n$. Thus every representative has squared $H^1$ norm at least $2\pi n$, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}:=\|e_k\|_{\mathcal D(D)}^2\ge2\pi n$. The harmonic lift $(\rho/a)^ne_k$ has squared $H^1$ norm $2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$ by direct radial integration, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}\le2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$. Orthogonality of the constant mode to $e_k$ gives $\|e_k+c\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2=Q_n^{\mathcal D}+|c|^2\|\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2$; the constant class has positive norm by the trace isomorphism [F4]. Taking the infimum over $c$ shows that the statement's further quotient norm satisfies $Q_n=Q_n^{\mathcal D}$. [A1, A2, F2, F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The weak DN map is diagonal on the complete orthogonal quotient modes from step 3.1; the constant mode is orthogonal to all nonzero modes, so quotienting by constants leaves $Q_n$ unchanged: angular integration makes the pairing of mode $e_k$ with any distinct mode zero, and step 2.1 gives its diagonal coefficient. For finite sums, the dual norm of the difference applied to $\sum a_ke_k$ is $\bigl(\sum_{k\ne0}|a_k|^2(2\pi a|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|)^2/Q_n\bigr)^{1/2}$; boundedness [F1] and density extend this formula to all inputs. Therefore $$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|=\sup_{k\ne0}\frac{2\pi a\,|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|}{Q_n},\qquad \lambda_n(r)-\frac na=\frac{2n}{a}\frac{\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}.$$ Using $Q_n\ge2\pi n$, $0<s\le1/2$, and $0<\eta<1$, this is at most $$\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{2\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}s^2.$$ This proves all asserted eigenvalue and operator-norm formulas. [A1, A2, F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

1.1 Let $n=|k|$, $s=r/a$, and $\sigma=1+\beta$. In polar coordinates $\rho=|x-x_0|$, seek a solution with angular mode $e^{ik\theta}$, using $u_i=A\rho^ne^{ik\theta}$ for $\rho<r$ and $u_o=(B\rho^n+C\rho^{-n})e^{ik\theta}$ for $r<\rho<a$. Continuity of $u$ and continuity of $\gamma\partial_\rho u$ at $\rho=r$ give $C r^{-2n}=-\eta B$ because $(\sigma-1)/(\sigma+1)=\eta$. The boundary condition $u_o(a,\theta)=e_k(\theta)$ then gives $Ba^n=(1-\eta s^{2n})^{-1}$. [given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Each piece is harmonic on its subdomain, and its value and conductivity-weighted normal derivative agree at $\rho=r$ by step 1.1. Both pieces and their classical gradients are bounded up to the interface because $r>0$. Testing a distributional first derivative against $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(D)$ and integrating by parts on the inner disk and annulus produces interface terms equal to the jump in $u$ times $\varphi$; the matching values cancel these terms, leaving the bounded piecewise classical derivatives. By [F7] the glued function belongs to $H^1(D)$. For any $z\in C_c^\infty(D)$, integration by parts on the inner disk and outer annulus cancels the interface flux terms and proves the weak equation. Since $C_c^\infty(D)$ is dense in $H_0^1(D)$ by [F1] and the energy form is continuous, the equation holds for every $z\in H_0^1(D)$. By [F1] the function is the unique solution for trace $e_k$. At $\rho=a$, the conductivity is $1$, so the outward flux is
$$\partial_\rho u_o(a,\theta)=\frac{n}{a}\frac{1+\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}e_k(\theta).$$
The Gauss–Green identity [F3] identifies this flux with the weak DN functional. For $\gamma_1\equiv1$, the harmonic extension $(\rho/a)^n e_k(\theta)$ gives flux $(n/a)e_k$, and the constant solution has zero flux. [A1, A2, F1, F3, F7, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 For each angle $\theta$, define $(R_\theta U)(x)=U(x_0+Q_\theta(x-x_0))$ on $D$, where $Q_\theta$ is the planar rotation matrix, and define $P_kU=(2\pi)^{-1}\int_0^{2\pi}e^{-ik\theta}R_\theta U\,d\theta$. By density [F5] and the rotation isometries, $\theta\mapsto R_\theta U$ is strongly continuous in $H^1(D)$ for every $U$, so this integral is the $H^1$ limit of its Riemann sums. Rotations preserve the $H^1(D)$ inner product; Minkowski's inequality makes $P_k$ a contraction, and character orthogonality [F2] makes it a self-adjoint projection with pairwise orthogonal ranges. For $w\in C_c^\infty(D)$, the map $\theta\mapsto R_\theta w$ is continuous in $H^1$ and every Riemann sum of the displayed integral is in $C_c^\infty(D)$, so $P_kw\in H_0^1(D)$; contraction and density in the definition of $H_0^1$ extend this invariance to all of $H_0^1(D)$. For a smooth restriction $U$, the polar-coordinate chain rule gives the $H^1$ norm as the integral of $|U|^2+|\partial_\rho U|^2+\rho^{-2}|\partial_\theta U|^2$ against $\rho\,d\rho d\theta$. Parseval [F2] for these three terms and monotone convergence [F6] in the radial integral show that the finite orthogonal sums $S_N:=\sum_{|k|\le N}P_k$ converge to $U$ in $H^1(D)$. For a general $U\in H^1(D)$, approximate by smooth restrictions using [F5]; on each annulus $\epsilon<\rho<a$ the polar map is a $C^1$ diffeomorphism, so the polar norm and Fourier identities pass to the limit there, and monotone convergence [F6] as $\epsilon\downarrow0$ gives the full-disk identities. Each $S_N$ is an orthogonal projection and hence a contraction; density [F5] therefore extends $S_NU\to U$ to every $U\in H^1(D)$. The induced quotient modes are thus a complete orthogonal family in $\mathcal D(D)$, and the constant mode is orthogonal to every nonzero mode. Since the trace is bounded and rotation-equivariant on smooth functions, [F4] and [F5] extend commutation to all of $H^1(D)$; the trace-kernel identity in [F4] then shows that each projected boundary class is a scalar multiple of one mode. For any $H^1$ representative $U$ of the boundary mode $e_k$, let $v(\rho)$ be its $k$th angular Fourier coefficient. Parseval gives
$$\|U\|_{H^1(D)}^2\ge 2\pi\int_0^a\left(|v'(\rho)|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v(\rho)|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho.$$
The trace condition gives $v(a)=1$. On every interval $[\epsilon,a]$, the one-dimensional Sobolev representative of $v$ is absolutely continuous, and expansion of the square yields
$$\int_\epsilon^a\left(|v'|^2\rho+\frac{n^2|v|^2}{\rho}\right)d\rho=\int_\epsilon^a\left|v'-\frac n\rho v\right|^2\rho\,d\rho+n|v(a)|^2-n|v(\epsilon)|^2.$$
The full energy being finite implies $\int_0^a|v(\rho)|^2\rho^{-1}d\rho<\infty$, so there is a sequence $\epsilon_j\downarrow0$ with $v(\epsilon_j)\to0$; otherwise $|v|$ would be bounded below near zero and this integral would diverge. Letting $\epsilon=\epsilon_j$ and using nonnegativity of the square proves that the radial energy is at least $n$. Thus every representative has squared $H^1$ norm at least $2\pi n$, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}:=\|e_k\|_{\mathcal D(D)}^2\ge2\pi n$. The harmonic lift $(\rho/a)^ne_k$ has squared $H^1$ norm $2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$ by direct radial integration, so [F4] gives $Q_n^{\mathcal D}\le2\pi n+\pi a^2/(n+1)$. Orthogonality of the constant mode to $e_k$ gives $\|e_k+c\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2=Q_n^{\mathcal D}+|c|^2\|\mathbf1\|_{\mathcal D}^2$; the constant class has positive norm by the trace isomorphism [F4]. Taking the infimum over $c$ shows that the statement's further quotient norm satisfies $Q_n=Q_n^{\mathcal D}$. [A1, A2, F2, F4, F5, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The weak DN map is diagonal on the complete orthogonal quotient modes from step 2.1; the constant mode is orthogonal to all nonzero modes, so quotienting by constants leaves $Q_n$ unchanged: angular integration makes the pairing of mode $e_k$ with any distinct mode zero, and step 1.2 gives its diagonal coefficient. For finite sums, the dual norm of the difference applied to $\sum a_ke_k$ is $\bigl(\sum_{k\ne0}|a_k|^2(2\pi a|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|)^2/Q_n\bigr)^{1/2}$; boundedness [F1] and density extend this formula to all inputs. Therefore
$$\|\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_r}-\dot{\Lambda}_{\gamma_1}\|=\sup_{k\ne0}\frac{2\pi a\,|\lambda_n(r)-n/a|}{Q_n},\qquad \lambda_n(r)-\frac na=\frac{2n}{a}\frac{\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}.$$
Using $Q_n\ge2\pi n$, $0<s\le1/2$, and $0<\eta<1$, this is at most
$$\sup_{n\ge1}\frac{2\eta s^{2n}}{1-\eta s^{2n}}\le\frac{2\eta}{1-\eta}s^2.$$
This proves all asserted eigenvalue and operator-norm formulas. [A1, A2, F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $d\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$ be a nonempty bounded connected $C^1$ domain, let $0<m\le M<\infty$, and let $\gamma\in L^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ satisfy $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. Define $\mathcal D(\Omega):=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$ with its quotient norm. For every boundary trace class $f\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ there is a unique $u_{\gamma,f}\in f$ such that
$$\int_\Omega\gamma\,\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx=0\qquad\text{for every }z\in H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C).$$
For every $g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$, the value $\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla u_{\gamma,f}\cdot\overline{\nabla V_g}\,dx$ is independent of the representative $V_g\in g$ and defines a bounded linear map $\Lambda_\gamma:\mathcal D(\Omega)\to\mathcal D(\Omega)^*$. Constants are in its kernel and its range functionals annihilate constants.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-class|The uniformly positive bounded conductivity class.]]

[[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities|The weak energy-form DN map convention.]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the domain and conductivity class of [[def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-class]]; the trace quotient $\mathcal D(\Omega)=H^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)/H_0^1(\Omega;\mathbb C)$; and the weak DN map convention of [[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities]].

[F1] Every $\gamma\in\Gamma_{m,M}(\Omega)$ is real measurable and satisfies $m\le\gamma\le M$ almost everywhere. ([[def-ip-calderon-admissible-conductivity-class]])

[F2] $\mathcal D(\Omega)$ is the quotient $H^1/H_0^1$ with the quotient norm; its elements are cosets with $H^1$ representatives, and $H_0^1$ is the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. ([[def-ip-calderon-weak-dn-map-for-bounded-conductivities]], [[lem-ip-calderon-boundary-trace-quotient-identification]], [[def-hk-and-hk-zero-notation]], [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]])

[F3] Since $\Omega\subset(0,1)^d$, it is contained in the slab $0<x_1<1$; for $w\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ the Poincaré inequality gives $\|w\|_{L^2}\le\|\nabla w\|_{L^2}$. ([[thm-poincare-inequality-for-w-one-p-zero]])

[F4] On a Hilbert space, a bounded coercive sesquilinear form and a bounded conjugate-linear functional determine a unique weak solution, with solution norm bounded by the functional norm divided by the coercivity constant. ([[thm-lax-milgram]])

[A1] The Axiom of Choice is assumed at the zero-boundary Poincaré and trace-space interfaces. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Countable Choice is assumed at the Poincaré and Lax–Milgram interfaces. ([[def-countable-choice]])

## Proof

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; $\Omega$ and $\gamma$ as in the statement; and the quotient trace classes $f,g\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$.

1.1 For $w\in H_0^1(\Omega)$, [F3] gives $\|w\|_{H^1}^2=\|w\|_2^2+\|\nabla w\|_2^2\le2\|\nabla w\|_2^2$. By [F1], the form $a_\gamma(w,z):=\int_\Omega\gamma\nabla w\cdot\overline{\nabla z}\,dx$ is bounded by $M\|w\|_{H^1}\|z\|_{H^1}$ and satisfies $a_\gamma(w,w)\ge(m/2)\|w\|_{H^1}^2$. Thus it is bounded and coercive on $H_0^1(\Omega)$. [F1, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Choose any representative $U\in f$. The functional $z\mapsto-a_\gamma(U,z)$ is bounded and conjugate-linear on $H_0^1$, with norm at most $M\|U\|_{H^1}$. Lax–Milgram [F4] applied to step 1.1 gives a unique $w\in H_0^1$ satisfying $a_\gamma(w,z)=-a_\gamma(U,z)$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Then $u:=U+w\in f$ satisfies the required weak equation. [A1, A2, F2, F4, step 1.1, choose]

3.1 If $u_1,u_2\in f$ both solve the weak equation, then $v:=u_1-u_2\in H_0^1$ by the quotient definition in [F2], and $a_\gamma(v,z)=0$ for every $z\in H_0^1$. Taking $z=v$ gives $m\|\nabla v\|_2^2\le a_\gamma(v,v)=0$; [F3] then gives $\|v\|_2=0$, so $v=0$. This proves uniqueness. [F1, F2, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 If $V_g,V'_g\in g$, then $V_g-V'_g\in H_0^1$ by [F2], so the weak equation for $u_{\gamma,f}$ makes $a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V_g)=a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V'_g)$. Thus the defining functional is independent of the representative. [F2, step 2.1]

3.3 For a representative $U\in f$, the solution estimate in [F4] and step 1.1 give $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|U\|_{H^1}$. Taking the infimum over representatives gives $\|u_{\gamma,f}\|_{H^1}\le(1+2M/m)\|f\|_{\mathcal D}$. Applying the same representative bound to $g$ yields $$|a_\gamma(u_{\gamma,f},V_g)|\le M(1+2M/m)^2\|f\|_{\mathcal D}\|g\|_{\mathcal D},$$ so $\Lambda_\gamma$ is bounded into $\mathcal D^*$. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 For $f_1,f_2\in\mathcal D(\Omega)$ and $c_1,c_2\in\mathbb C$, the function $c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$ belongs to the trace class $c_1f_1+c_2f_2$. The weak equation is linear in its solution because the energy form is linear in its first argument, so this combination solves the weak problem for that class. Uniqueness from step 3.1 gives $u_{\gamma,c_1f_1+c_2f_2}=c_1u_{\gamma,f_1}+c_2u_{\gamma,f_2}$. The energy definition is also linear in this first argument, hence $\Lambda_\gamma$ is linear. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 For a constant input $c$, the constant function $u=c$ solves the weak equation and uniqueness gives $u_{\gamma,c}=c$, whose gradient is zero. For a constant test class $c$, its constant representative has zero gradient. The energy formula therefore vanishes on constant inputs and constant tests, so it induces the stated map on the quotient by constants. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, step 3.2, step 3.3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive, put $\rho=\sqrt{\gamma}$, and define $q=(\Delta_g\rho)/\rho$. If $v$ solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv)=0$ and $u=\rho v$, then $u$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q)u=0$. The potential $q$ has trivial Dirichlet kernel. For boundary data $f=v|_{\partial M}$, with $\rho_b=\rho|_{\partial M}$ and the physical flux convention $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v|_{\partial M}$, the exact boundary relation is
$$\Lambda_\gamma f=\rho_b\Lambda_q(\rho_b f)-\rho_b(\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}\rho)|_{\partial M}f.$$

## Statement references

[[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map|Physical conductivity and Schrödinger DN maps]]

[[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity|Nonresonant elliptic solvability]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the weak conductivity and nonresonant Dirichlet solvability suppliers [F2]--[F3].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the weak conductivity and nonresonant Dirichlet solvability suppliers [F2]--[F3].

**Given:** the data in the statement, and the weak formulations of the conductivity and Schrödinger equations.

[F1] [[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: the conductivity DN map is the physical flux $\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v$; the Schrödinger DN map is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u$; both are defined by their weak boundary forms, and the $H^1$ trace is continuous into $L^2(\partial M)$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness]]: for every boundary datum in $H^{1/2}$ and every smooth positive conductivity, the conductivity equation has a unique weak $H^1$ solution.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $(M,g)$ be a compact connected smooth Riemannian domain with nonempty smooth boundary and no orientability assumption, and let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ satisfy $\gamma>0$. There is a constant $C_P>0$ such that $\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C_P\|\nabla_gw\|_{L^2(M)}$ for every $w\in H_0^1(M)$. For every $h\in L^2(M)$ and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$ there is a unique $v\in H^1(M)$ with trace $f$ satisfying $\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla_gv,\nabla_g\overline z)\,dV_g=-\int_Mh\overline z\,dV_g$ for every $z\in H_0^1(M)$. If $h$ and $f$ are smooth, this weak solution is smooth up to the boundary.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain|Fixed-atlas Sobolev and trace spaces]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function; this is assumed by the Rellich, trace-right-inverse, higher-order regularity, and Sobolev embedding suppliers.

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]]: every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function; this is assumed by the Lax--Milgram, partition, and collar suppliers.

**Given:** AC and Countable Choice; the compact connected smooth Riemannian domain and positive smooth conductivity in the statement; and $f\in H^{1/2}(\partial M)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]]: $H^1(M)$ is defined by finitely many chartwise $W^{1,2}$ norms, and $H_0^1(M)$ is the $H^1$ closure of $C_c^\infty(M^\circ)$.

[F2] [[thm-rellich-compactness-from-w-one-p-zero-to-lp]]: on a bounded Euclidean open set, $W_0^{1,2}$ is compactly embedded in $L^2$.

[F3] [[thm-lax-milgram]]: a bounded coercive sesquilinear form on a Hilbert space has a unique weak solution.

[F4] [[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]]: on a bounded $C^1$ Euclidean domain, the trace is a bounded operator from $H^1$ to $L^2$ and agrees with restriction for smooth functions; therefore every class in the closure $H_0^1$ has zero trace.

[F5] [[thm-bounded-right-inverse-for-the-sobolev-trace]]: on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain, every $H^{1/2}$ boundary datum has an $H^1$ extension; after localization this supplies boundary-chart extensions on $M$.

[F6] [[thm-higher-order-boundary-regularity-for-dirichlet-problems]]: a zero-trace weak solution of a smooth uniformly elliptic divergence-form equation on a bounded smooth Euclidean domain gains two Sobolev derivatives when its right-hand side has the corresponding Sobolev regularity.

[F7] [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]: membership in every chartwise integer Sobolev space gives a smooth representative up to the boundary.

[F8] [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]: smooth boundary data extend smoothly into a collar by constant normal extension and a cutoff.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement, including $h\in L^2(M)$.

1.1 There is a constant $C_P$ such that $\|w\|_{L^2(M)}\leq C_P\|\nabla w\|_{L^2(M)}$ for $w\in H_0^1(M)$. Otherwise choose $w_j\in H_0^1(M)$ with $\|w_j\|_{L^2}=1$ and $\|\nabla w_j\|_{L^2}\to0$. The sequence is bounded in $H^1$. A finite chart partition and [F2] give an $L^2$-convergent subsequence; a further subsequence converges weakly in the Hilbert space $H^1$, so its limit $w$ belongs to the weakly closed subspace $H_0^1(M)$, has weak gradient zero, and has $L^2$ norm one. In each connected coordinate ball, convolution of a function with zero weak gradient is constant on smaller balls; overlapping balls force the constants to agree, so connectedness makes $w$ constant on $M^\circ$. Its trace is zero by [F4], whereas the trace of a nonzero constant is that same nonzero constant on the nonempty boundary. This contradiction proves the inequality. [A1, F1, F2, F4, given, contradiction]

2.1 Compactness of $M$ and positivity of $\gamma$ give $\gamma_*:=\min_M\gamma>0$. Thus $a_\gamma(w,z)=\int_M\gamma\,g(\nabla w,\nabla\bar z)\,dV_g$ is bounded on $H_0^1(M)$ and $a_\gamma(w,w)\geq c\|w\|_{H^1(M)}^2$ by step 1.1 and $\gamma_*$. By [F3], for any bounded conjugate-linear functional $G$ on $H_0^1(M)$ there is a unique $w\in H_0^1(M)$ with $a_\gamma(w,z)=G(z)$ for all $z$. [A2, F1, F3, step 1.1, given]

3.1 Flatten each boundary chart, apply the local half-space trace lift, and patch the finitely many chart lifts with a smooth partition. The resulting $Ef\in H^1(M)$ has trace $f$ and norm bounded by $C\|f\|_{H^{1/2}(\partial M)}$ by [F5]. For $h\in L^2(M)$ take $G(z)=-\int_Mh\overline z\,dV_g-a_\gamma(Ef,z)$ in step 2.1 and set $v=Ef+w$. Then $v$ has trace $f$ and satisfies the weak equation. If $v_1,v_2$ are two such solutions, their difference $w$ lies in $H_0^1$ and $a_\gamma(w,w)=0$; since $\gamma\geq\gamma_*>0$, $\nabla w=0$, and step 1.1 gives $w=0$. [A1, A2, F1, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Suppose $h$ and $f$ are smooth. By [F8], extend $f$ smoothly from the boundary into a collar and multiply by a cutoff to obtain a smooth extension $Ef$ on $M$. Then $w=v-Ef$ has zero trace and solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gw)=h-\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gEf)$, whose right-hand side is smooth. In each boundary chart, flatten the boundary and write the principal matrix as $|g|^{1/2}\gamma g^{ij}$; it is smooth and uniformly elliptic because $g$ is positive definite and $\gamma$ has a positive minimum. For the base case, localize $w$ by a cutoff; its equation has an $L^2$ right-hand side since $w\in H^1$, so [F6] gives local $H^2$ regularity. If $w\in H^{m+1}$, each cutoff commutator contains derivatives of $w$ of order at most $m+1$ with smooth bounded coefficients, hence lies in $H^m$; the localized right-hand side is therefore in $H^m$, and [F6] gives $H^{m+2}$ regularity. Induction over $m$ and a finite chart cover give $w\in H^m(M)$ for every integer $m$. By [F7], $w$ and hence $v=Ef+w$ are smooth up to the boundary. [A1, A2, F1, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1, induction, algebra] ∎

3.1 Suppose $h$ and $f$ are smooth. By [F8], extend $f$ smoothly from the boundary into a collar and multiply by a cutoff to obtain a smooth extension $Ef$ on $M$.       url: "https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.08123v1"

## Statement

Let $(M_0,g_0)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian manifold with smooth boundary and let $\gamma:[0,L]\to M_0$ be a unit-speed nontangential geodesic segment. For every real $\lambda$ and every $K>0$, there is a family $v_{\tau+i\lambda}\in C^\infty(M_0)$, $\tau\geq1$, such that
$$\|(-\Delta_{g_0}-(\tau+i\lambda)^2)v_{\tau+i\lambda}\|_{L^2(M_0)}=O(\tau^{-K}),\qquad \|v_{\tau+i\lambda}\|_{L^2(M_0)}=O(1),$$
and for every $\psi\in C(M_0)$,
$$\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\int_{M_0}|v_{\tau+i\lambda}|^2\psi\,dV_{g_0} =\int_0^L e^{-2\lambda t}\psi(\gamma(t))\,dt.$$
The statement permits transversal manifolds without an orientability assumption and makes no boundary condition assertion for the quasimodes.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain|Transversal manifold]]

[[def-ip-injective-geodesic-ray-transform|Nontangential geodesic segment]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** the compact Riemannian transversal, a nontangential segment, a real attenuation $\lambda$, and $K>0$.

[F1] [[def-riemannian-metric-and-riemannian-manifold]]: geodesic normal coordinates, the metric volume density, and the Laplace-Beltrami operator are defined locally without choosing an orientation.

[F2] [[thm-local-existence-uniqueness-and-smooth-dependence-for-manifold-integral-curves]]: the geodesic ODE has local solutions and smooth dependence on initial data, so parallel frames and exponential-coordinate maps vary smoothly along an embedded geodesic subsegment.

[F3] **External input:** Dos Santos Ferreira--Kurylev--Lassas--Salo, Proposition 3.1, PDF p. 14, supplies exactly the residual, norm, and attenuated ray limit in the statement on an oriented compact transversal of dimension at least two. Its finite Taylor-jet construction and distinct-branch cross-term estimate (equation (3.6), PDF pp. 21--22) are imported, including overlap matching at self-intersections. For this repair the proposition and the cross-term argument on pp. 21--22 were inspected; the entire proof on pp. 14--22 is not claimed as newly reconstructed. Historical source coverage is distinct from this reading extent.

[F4] The construction for each fixed $K$ uses finitely many charts, finite Taylor orders, and linear transport and matrix ODEs with fixed initial data. Increasing the finite order suffices for that $K$; no simultaneous choice of quasimodes for unrelated $K$ or $\lambda$ is required. The parameter $\tau$ then enters the resulting explicit formula. Thus the use here adds no choice axiom to the statement.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 Embed the segment in a collar extension across $\partial M_0$ and cover it by finitely many coordinate neighborhoods. On an embedded subsegment, parallel transport an orthonormal normal frame and set $F(t,y)=\exp_{\gamma(t)}(\sum_\alpha y_\alpha E_\alpha(t))$. The inverse function theorem gives local Fermi coordinates with $g_{jk}(t,0)=\delta_{jk}$ and $\partial_i g_{jk}(t,0)=0$. This construction is along an interval and uses no orientation of $M_0$. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 In one such chart, seek $v_s=e^{is\Theta}a$, $s=\tau+i\lambda$, with $\Theta(t,0)=t$ and $\operatorname{Im}\Theta(t,y)\geq c|y|^2$. Expand $\Theta$ into homogeneous transverse Taylor polynomials. The quadratic polynomial is $\frac12H(t)y\cdot y$; substituting into $g(d\Theta,d\Theta)=1$ gives the matrix Riccati equation $H'+H^2=F(t)$, where $F$ is determined by the second transverse Taylor coefficient of the inverse metric. An initial complex symmetric $H(t_0)$ with positive-definite imaginary part yields a smooth solution with positive imaginary part on a short subsegment. Each higher homogeneous phase term then solves a linear first-order ODE along $t$, because its newest coefficient occurs linearly in the eikonal equation. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Substituting $a=\tau^{(m-1)/4}\sum_{j=0}^N s^{-j}a_{-j}$ into $(-\Delta_{g_0}-s^2)e^{is\Theta}a$ cancels successive powers of $s$ by linear transport ODEs for the transverse Taylor coefficients of each $a_{-j}$. The leading coefficient solves $a_0(t,0)=c_0\exp(-\frac12\int_{t_0}^t\operatorname{tr}H(r)\,dr)$. A finite Taylor realization to the order required for the fixed $K$ and a transverse cutoff produce a smooth local beam; Gaussian integration gives bounded $L^2$ norm and a residual that tends to zero faster than any prescribed power after increasing the Taylor order. [F1, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 On an oriented transversal of dimension at least two, apply [F3] to complete the finite overlap matching and eliminate all distinct-branch cross terms. This gives the stated global family and limit; steps 1.1--2.1 describe its local ingredients, without claiming a new proof of the imported global estimates. [F3, F4, step 1.1, step 2.1]

4.1 For a nonorientable transversal let $\pi:\widetilde M_0\to M_0$ be its orientation double cover, with deck involution $\sigma$, and lift $\gamma$ to $\widetilde\gamma$. Let $w_s$ be the oriented beam from [F3] along that lift. Define the descended function by $\pi^*v_s=w_s+\sigma^*w_s$. The residual and norm bounds follow by a finite sum and the covering integral formula. The two lifted segments have no common tangent branch: equality of position and velocity at different times would make the geodesic periodic, contrary to its nontangential boundary exit; opposite velocities at a repeated point would force a zero midpoint velocity by geodesic uniqueness. There are only finitely many crossing branches, by compactness and local uniqueness. The distinct-branch estimate in [F3], applied to these two lifts, therefore gives a zero mixed-term limit. For every continuous $\psi$ the covering formula is $$\int_{M_0}|v_s|^2\psi\,dV=\int_{\widetilde M_0}|w_s|^2(\psi\circ\pi)\,dV+\operatorname{Re}\int_{\widetilde M_0}w_s\overline{\sigma^*w_s}(\psi\circ\pi)\,dV.$$ The first term has precisely the required ray limit and the second tends to zero. In particular there is no extra factor two in the normalization. The same argument works if the cover is disconnected. [F1, F3, F4, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 If the transversal has dimension one, the component containing the segment is an interval with arclength coordinate $t$ beginning at its incoming endpoint. Set $v_s=e^{ist}$ on this component and zero on all other components. The residual is zero and the asserted integral formula is exact. In dimension zero the given unit-speed segment cannot exist. This covers the dimensions not needed in the CTA application as well. [F1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact transversally anisotropic product domain of dimension $n\geq3$ and let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$. Fix an integer $s>n/2+2$ and a finite family $h_1,\ldots,h_m\in C^\infty(\partial M,\mathbb C)$. For $\epsilon=(\epsilon_1,\ldots,\epsilon_m)\in\mathbb R^m$ sufficiently near zero, the equation
$$-\Delta_g u+q u^3=0\quad\text{in }M^\circ,\qquad u|_{\partial M}=\sum_{j=1}^m\epsilon_jh_j$$
has a unique solution in a fixed small $H^s(M)$ ball. The parameter map $\epsilon\mapsto u_\epsilon$ is $C^3$ into $H^s(M)$, and the corresponding nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann data $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}u_\epsilon|_{\partial M}$ is $C^3$ into $C^0(\partial M)$.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain|Product geometry and Laplacian convention]]

[[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain|Chartwise Sobolev spaces]]

[[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity|Dirichlet inverse and higher regularity]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed by the Sobolev algebra, embedding, and Banach implicit-function suppliers [F4]--[F6].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed by the Sobolev and elliptic regularity interfaces [F1], [F3].

**Given:** the product domain, real smooth $q$, integer $s>n/2+2$, and the fixed finite smooth boundary directions.

[F1] [[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]]: the chartwise integer Sobolev spaces are Banach spaces, and $H_0^1(M)$ is the closed zero-trace subspace.

[F2] [[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness]]: on a compact connected domain, $\|w\|_{L^2}\leq C_P\|\nabla w\|_{L^2}$ for zero-trace $w$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity]]: the zero Dirichlet operator $-\Delta_g$ is invertible; for integer $k\geq0$, zero-trace $F\in H^k$ gives $u\in H^{k+2}$ with $\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\leq C_k\|F\|_{H^k}$.

[F4] [[cor-sobolev-algebra-above-the-critical-index]]: for integer $s$ with $2s>n$ on a bounded smooth domain, multiplication is continuous in $W^{s,2}$, so the Sobolev space is a Banach algebra.

[F5] [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]: for $s>n/2+2$ on a bounded smooth domain, $H^s$ embeds continuously in $C^2(\overline M)$.

[F6] [[thm-implicit-function-theorem-for-banach-spaces]]: if a $C^3$ map between Banach spaces vanishes at a point and its derivative in the unknown variable is a bounded isomorphism, its nearby zero set is the graph of a unique $C^3$ map.

[F7] [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]: boundary data on a compact smooth boundary extend smoothly into a collar by constant normal extension followed by a smooth cutoff and finite patching.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 For $q=0$, the Dirichlet kernel of $-\Delta_g$ is trivial: if $w\in H_0^1(M)$ is weakly harmonic, testing with $w$ gives $\int_M|\nabla w|^2dV_g=0$, and the zero-trace Poincare inequality in [F2] gives $w=0$. Thus [F3] supplies the zero-boundary inverse $G=(-\Delta_g)^{-1}:H^{s-2}(M)\to X_s$, where $X_s=\{w\in H^s(M):w\in H_0^1(M)\}$. The high-order estimate in [F3], together with its bounded $H^1$ inverse, makes $G$ bounded. [A2, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 Since $s>n/2+2$, [F4] makes $H^s(M)$ an algebra by localizing to finitely many smooth charts, extending each localized representative to a bounded Euclidean chart domain, applying the Euclidean algebra estimate, and summing the finite norms. Thus the map $(\epsilon,w)\mapsto q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3$ is a continuous polynomial from $\mathbb R^m\times X_s$ into $H^{s-2}(M)$, where $f_\epsilon=\sum_j\epsilon_jh_j$ and $Ef_\epsilon$ is the smooth collar extension from [F7]. Define $$\mathcal F(\epsilon,w)=w-G\big[\Delta_g(Ef_\epsilon)-q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3\big]\in X_s.$$ It is $C^3$ (indeed polynomial plus bounded linear maps) and $\mathcal F(0,0)=0$. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F7, given, construct]

2.1 At $(0,0)$, the derivative $D_w\mathcal F(0,0)$ is the identity on $X_s$, because the derivative of $u\mapsto q u^3$ at $u=0$ vanishes. By [F6], there is a neighborhood of $\epsilon=0$ and a unique $C^3$ map $w(\epsilon)\in X_s$ near zero such that $\mathcal F(\epsilon,w(\epsilon))=0$. The fixed-point equation is exactly $-\Delta_g(Ef_\epsilon+w)+q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3=0$ with boundary trace $f_\epsilon$, so $u_\epsilon=Ef_\epsilon+w(\epsilon)$ gives the unique small solution. [A1, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By [F5], $u_\epsilon\in C^2(\overline M)$ and the outward normal derivative has a continuous boundary trace. The trace map from $C^1(\overline M)$ to $C^0(\partial M)$ is bounded in the chartwise norms, so composing the $C^3$ map $\epsilon\mapsto u_\epsilon$ with this bounded linear trace of $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}$ proves $C^3$ dependence of the nonlinear DN data. [A1, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

[[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity|Dirichlet inverse and higher regularity]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is assumed by the Sobolev algebra, embedding, and Banach implicit-function suppliers [F4]--[F6].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed by the Sobolev and elliptic regularity interfaces [F1], [F3].

**Given:** the product domain, real smooth $q$, integer $s>n/2+2$, and the fixed finite smooth boundary directions.

[F1] [[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]]: the chartwise integer Sobolev spaces are Banach spaces, and $H_0^1(M)$ is the closed zero-trace subspace.

[F2] [[lem-ip-conductivity-map-wellposedness]]: on a compact connected domain, $\|w\|_{L^2}\leq C_P\|\nabla w\|_{L^2}$ for zero-trace $w$.

[F3] [[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity]]: the zero Dirichlet operator $-\Delta_g$ is invertible; for integer $k\geq0$, zero-trace $F\in H^k$ gives $u\in H^{k+2}$ with $\|u\|_{H^{k+2}}\leq C_k\|F\|_{H^k}$.

[F4] [[cor-sobolev-algebra-above-the-critical-index]]: for integer $s$ with $2s>n$ on a bounded smooth domain, multiplication is continuous in $W^{s,2}$, so the Sobolev space is a Banach algebra.

[F5] [[thm-higher-order-sobolev-embedding]]: for $s>n/2+2$ on a bounded smooth domain, $H^s$ embeds continuously in $C^2(\overline M)$.

[F6] [[thm-implicit-function-theorem-for-banach-spaces]]: if a $C^3$ map between Banach spaces vanishes at a point and its derivative in the unknown variable is a bounded isomorphism, its nearby zero set is the graph of a unique $C^3$ map.

[F7] [[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]: boundary data on a compact smooth boundary extend smoothly into a collar by constant normal extension followed by a smooth cutoff and finite patching.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 For $q=0$, the Dirichlet kernel of $-\Delta_g$ is trivial: if $w\in H_0^1(M)$ is weakly harmonic, testing with $w$ gives $\int_M|\nabla w|^2dV_g=0$, and the zero-trace Poincare inequality in [F2] gives $w=0$. Thus [F3] supplies the zero-boundary inverse $G=(-\Delta_g)^{-1}:H^{s-2}(M)\to X_s$, where $X_s=\{w\in H^s(M):w\in H_0^1(M)\}$. The high-order estimate in [F3], together with its bounded $H^1$ inverse, makes $G$ bounded. [A2, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

1.2 Since $s>n/2+2$, [F4] makes $H^s(M)$ an algebra by localizing to finitely many smooth charts, extending each localized representative to a bounded Euclidean chart domain, applying the Euclidean algebra estimate, and summing the finite norms. Thus the map $(\epsilon,w)\mapsto q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3$ is a continuous polynomial from $\mathbb R^m\times X_s$ into $H^{s-2}(M)$, where $f_\epsilon=\sum_j\epsilon_jh_j$ and $Ef_\epsilon$ is the smooth collar extension from [F7]. Define
$$\mathcal F(\epsilon,w)=w-G\big[\Delta_g(Ef_\epsilon)-q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3\big]\in X_s.$$
It is $C^3$ (indeed polynomial plus bounded linear maps) and $\mathcal F(0,0)=0$. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F3, F4, F6, F7, given, construct]

2.1 At $(0,0)$, the derivative $D_w\mathcal F(0,0)$ is the identity on $X_s$, because the derivative of $u\mapsto q u^3$ at $u=0$ vanishes. By [F6], there is a neighborhood of $\epsilon=0$ and a unique $C^3$ map $w(\epsilon)\in X_s$ near zero such that $\mathcal F(\epsilon,w(\epsilon))=0$. The fixed-point equation is exactly $-\Delta_g(Ef_\epsilon+w)+q(Ef_\epsilon+w)^3=0$ with boundary trace $f_\epsilon$, so $u_\epsilon=Ef_\epsilon+w(\epsilon)$ gives the unique small solution. [A1, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 By [F5], $u_\epsilon\in C^2(\overline M)$ and the outward normal derivative has a continuous boundary trace. The trace map from $C^1(\overline M)$ to $C^0(\partial M)$ is bounded in the chartwise norms, so composing the $C^3$ map $\epsilon\mapsto u_\epsilon$ with this bounded linear trace of $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}$ proves $C^3$ dependence of the nonlinear DN data. [A1, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, let $q\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$, and let $\Lambda_q^{\rm NL}$ be the small-data nonlinear Dirichlet-to-Neumann map for $-\Delta_g u+qu^3=0$. For smooth boundary directions $h_1,h_2,h_3,h_4$, let $v_j$ be the harmonic solution with boundary value $h_j$. If
$$w_{123}=\left.\partial_{\epsilon_1}\partial_{\epsilon_2}\partial_{\epsilon_3}u_\epsilon\right|_{\epsilon=0},$$
where $u_\epsilon$ has boundary value $\epsilon_1h_1+\epsilon_2h_2+\epsilon_3h_3$, then
$$-\Delta_gw_{123}+6qv_1v_2v_3=0,\qquad w_{123}|_{\partial M}=0,$$
and
$$\left\langle (D^3\Lambda_q^{\rm NL})_0[h_1,h_2,h_3],h_4\right\rangle =6\int_Mq\,v_1v_2v_3\overline{v_4}\,dV_g.$$

## Statement references

[[lem-ip-cubic-dn-small-data-differentiability|Small-data cubic solution and DN map differentiability]]

[[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map|Boundary normal derivative and pairing]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the small-data differentiability supplier [F1] and nonresonant regularity supplier [F2].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the small-data differentiability supplier [F1] and nonresonant regularity supplier [F2].

**Given:** the data in the statement and the finite-parameter solution family from the small-data lemma.

[F1] [[lem-ip-cubic-dn-small-data-differentiability]]: for every finite list of smooth boundary directions, the small solution and nonlinear DN data depend $C^3$ on the real parameters $\epsilon_j$.

[F2] [[lem-ip-smooth-manifold-elliptic-nonresonant-regularity]]: the zero-Dirichlet Laplacian has a unique weak inverse and smooth data yield smooth solutions.

[F3] [[def-ip-conductivity-dirichlet-to-neumann-map]]: the smooth Schrödinger DN convention is the outward normal derivative, and the boundary pairing is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the second.

[F4] [[def-riemannian-volume-density]] and [[def-laplace-beltrami-operator-as-trace-of-the-hessian]]: integration by parts for $\Delta_g$ is performed with the positive density $dV_g$ and outward boundary density $dS_g$.

[F5] [[thm-sobolev-gauss-green-formula-on-c-one-domains]]: on a bounded $C^1$ Euclidean domain, integration by parts for smooth functions has the outward-normal boundary term; the Riemannian identity follows chartwise from the coordinate divergence formula and positive volume density.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the statement.

1.1 Differentiate $-\Delta_g u_\epsilon+q u_\epsilon^3=0$ once in $\epsilon_j$ at $\epsilon=0$. Since $u_0=0$, the derivative $v_j=\partial_{\epsilon_j}u_\epsilon|_0$ solves $-\Delta_gv_j=0$ with trace $h_j$. Differentiating twice in distinct parameters gives $-\Delta_g(\partial_{\epsilon_i}\partial_{\epsilon_j}u_\epsilon|_0)=0$ with zero trace, so this second derivative vanishes by [F2]. [A1, A2, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 The third mixed derivative of $u_\epsilon^3$ at zero has exactly the six permutations of $v_1v_2v_3$, hence equals $6v_1v_2v_3$; all other chain-rule terms contain $u_0$ or one of the vanishing second derivatives from step 1.1. Differentiating the equation gives $-\Delta_gw_{123}+6qv_1v_2v_3=0$, with zero boundary trace. By [F1], the third derivative of the nonlinear DN data is $\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}w_{123}|_{\partial M}$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Since $v_4$ is harmonic and $w_{123}$ has zero trace, chartwise Green's formula and a finite partition of unity give $$\int_{\partial M}(\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}w_{123})\overline{h_4}\,dS_g =\int_M(\Delta_gw_{123})\overline{v_4}\,dV_g.$$ Indeed, the second Green identity has boundary term $w_{123}\partial_{\nu}\overline{v_4}$ equal to zero, and interior term $w_{123}\Delta_g\overline{v_4}=0$. In each boundary chart, write $\Delta_g w=|g|^{-1/2}\partial_i(|g|^{1/2}g^{ij}\partial_jw)$ and apply [F5] to the coordinate components; summing with the finite partition leaves the displayed Riemannian boundary integral by [F4]. [F2, F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The equation in step 2.1 gives $\Delta_gw_{123}=6qv_1v_2v_3$. Substituting this into step 3.1 and using the definition of the third DN derivative proves the displayed identity. [F3, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

kind: lemma
title: The full collared EIT class satisfies the centered range and source interfaces
status: draft
origin: pipeline
pipeline_run: inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19
deps:

  - lem-ip-sharp-centered-eit-hone-logarithmic-stability
  - lem-ip-collared-sobolev-besov-source-functional-cutoff
  - lem-ip-logarithmic-index-conjugate-and-parameter-rates
  - def-ip-relaxed-range-invariance-objective

sources:

    - title: Barbara Kaltenbacher, Convergence rates under a range invariance condition with application to electrical impedance tomography
      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.18704
      locator: Example 4, Theorem 10, and Section 2.4; all interfaces and the source exponent are proved locally here
    - title: Frederic Weidling, Variational Source Conditions and Conditional Stability Estimates for Inverse Problems in PDEs
      url: https://univerlag.uni-goettingen.de/bitstream/handle/3/isbn-978-3-86395-411-6/weidling.pdf?sequence=1
      locator: Theorems 6.11–6.15
dependency_level: 6
---

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, Countable Choice and Dependent Choice. Let $\Omega=B_1\subset\mathbb R^3$, $0<\rho<1$, $0<m<1<M$, and $5/2<s_1<7/2$. Use the exact intrinsic $H^{s_1}(\Omega)$ Hilbert norm from the collared source-functional lemma, and put
$$V=\{a\in H^{s_1}(\Omega;\mathbb R):a=0\text{ a.e. on }\Omega\setminus B_\rho\},\qquad \mathcal C=\{\sigma\in1+V:m\le\sigma\le M\}.$$
Let $\sigma_0,\sigma^\dagger\in\mathcal C$, and assume $\sigma^\dagger\in B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}(\Omega)$ for $s_1<s_2<2s_1-1$. Set $a^\dagger=\sigma^\dagger-\sigma_0$, and choose $R>\|a^\dagger\|_V$. Write $Y=\ell^2(L^2(S^2;\mathbb C))$ for the centered mean-zero Neumann voltage sequence space, regarded as a real Hilbert space, and give $X=Z=V\times Y$ the sum norm. Let $X_0=V\times\{0\}$, $D=X$, $x_0=(0,0)$ and $P(a,z)=(0,z)$.

There is a globally Lipschitz, continuously Fréchet differentiable map $\Gamma:V\to Y$ with globally Lipschitz derivative, agreeing for $\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C$ with the centered physical observation $((\mathscr N_{\sigma_0+a}-\mathscr N_1)Y_{\ell k})_{\ell,k}$. Define
$$T(a)=\Gamma(a)-\Gamma(0)-\Gamma'(0)a,\quad r(a,z)=(a,z+T(a)),\quad K(a,b)=\Gamma'(0)a+b,\quad F(a,z)=\Gamma(a)+z.$$
Then $F(x)-F(x_0)=Kr(x)$ on $D$, $r$ and its inverse $r^{-1}(a,b)=(a,b-T(a))$ are globally Lipschitz, and these facts hold on the admitted set
$$U=\{(a,z):\sigma_0+a\in\mathcal C,\ \|a\|_V<R,\ \|z\|_Y<R\}.$$
The projected points $(I-P)r^{-1}(\widehat r)$ belong to $U\cap X_0$ for $\widehat r\in r(U)$.

On the ambient linear space $V$ define the proper convex regularizer
$$\check R(a)=\tfrac12\|\sigma_0+a\|_{s_1,\Omega}^2+I_{\mathcal C}(\sigma_0+a),$$
where the indicator is zero on $\mathcal C$ and $+\infty$ elsewhere. On every admitted physical coefficient this is exactly the original quadratic Sobolev penalty. The functional $\xi^\dagger(v)=(\sigma^\dagger,v)_{s_1,\Omega}$ is a subgradient at $a^\dagger$, and its Bregman distance on $\mathcal C-\sigma_0$ is exactly $\frac12\|a-a^\dagger\|_V^2$. On every fixed sublevel containing the truth, the VSC holds with $b=3/4$ and a continuous nondecreasing concave truncated logarithmic index
$$\psi(u)=C[\log(1/u)]^{-\nu}\quad(0<u\le u_0),\qquad \psi(0)=0,\qquad \nu=\frac{(s_2-s_1)(2s_1-3)}{s_2-1},$$
continued constantly above a sufficiently small $u_0>0$. Its subadditivity constant may be taken as $C_\psi=1$.

Put $L_T=\operatorname{Lip}(T)$ and let $L=\operatorname{Lip}(\Gamma')$. For $Q(\widehat r,\widehat r')=\|\widehat r-\widehat r'\|_Z$, the projection-coupling constant may be taken as $1+L_T$, and
$$\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)-r'(x_2)(x_1-x_2)\|_Z\le LR\|r(x_1)-r(x_2)\|_Z\qquad(x_1,x_2\in U).$$
For the frozen method choose $C_P\ge2\|K\|^2\operatorname{Lip}(r)^2$, $\gamma>1$ and $R_P(z)=\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_Y^2)$. Then the required compatibility bound holds with
$$\widetilde C_Q=\max\left\{4(1+L_T)^2,\frac{2R^2}{\psi(C_PR^2)}\right\}.$$
In particular, the structural hypotheses of the joint and frozen one-step estimates hold with $p=2$, the displayed exact regularizer, $R_P=0$ for the joint method, and the displayed $R_P$ for the frozen method. For frozen rates additionally require $LR<c_{\rm tcr}<1/\sqrt{20}$, choose $c_{\beta\alpha}\le\min\{1/4,\gamma-1\}/(4\widetilde C_Q)$, and use the remaining parameter, tolerance and stopping conditions of the frozen rate theorem. This small-neighborhood hypothesis is local around the chosen initial conductivity; it restricts neither the stated Besov truth class nor its logarithmic exponent.

## Statement references

[[lem-ip-centered-neumann-sequence-map-and-differentiability]]

[[lem-ip-sharp-centered-eit-hone-logarithmic-stability]]

[[lem-ip-collared-sobolev-besov-source-functional-cutoff]]

[[def-ip-relaxed-range-invariance-objective]]

[[lem-ip-joint-range-invariance-vsc-estimate]]

[[lem-ip-frozen-newton-one-step-error-recursion]]

[Kaltenbacher, Example 4 and Theorem 10](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2403.18704)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The choice assumptions and full conductivity, Sobolev, Besov, collar and local-admission data in the Statement.

[F1] The centered physical map on uniformly elliptic collared $L^\infty$ coefficients is globally Lipschitz on each fixed ellipticity class, is continuously Fréchet differentiable there, and has a uniform Lipschitz derivative. [[lem-ip-centered-neumann-sequence-map-and-differentiability]]

[F2] Uniform collared $H^{s_1}$ classes satisfy $H^1$ stability with modulus $O([\log(1/\delta)]^{-(s_1-3/2)})$ in their centered sequence distance. [[lem-ip-sharp-centered-eit-hone-logarithmic-stability]]

[F3] For the exact intrinsic quadratic penalty, the sharp $H^1$ modulus and $B^{s_2}_{2,\infty}$ truth imply a VSC with coefficient $3/4$ and logarithmic exponent $\nu$ in the Statement. The proof treats the exact domain inner product. [[lem-ip-collared-sobolev-besov-source-functional-cutoff]]

[F4] Truncated logarithmic indices are concave when the truncation point is small enough, and their conjugates satisfy $H(q)\sim C(\log q)^{-\nu}$. [[lem-ip-logarithmic-index-conjugate-and-parameter-rates]]

[A1] All three choice assumptions are retained from [F1]–[F4]. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]

## Proof

**Domains for the generic estimates.** The canonical maps $i_V:V\to X_0$, $i_V(a)=(a,0)$, and $i_Y:Y\to P(X)$, $i_Y(z)=(0,z)$, are linear isometries onto $X_0=V\times\{0\}$ and $P(X)=\{0\}\times Y$. In the generic one-step estimates, transport the regularizer and subgradient by
$$\check R_0(i_V(a)):=\check R(a),\qquad \xi_0^\dagger(i_V(v)):=\xi^\dagger(v),$$
and the frozen penalty by $R_{P,0}(i_Y(z)):=\gamma\psi(C_P\|z\|_Y^2)$. The map $i_V$ preserves the dual pairing, so the subgradient inequality verified in step 3.2 transports to $\xi_0^\dagger\in\partial_{X_0}\check R_0(i_V(a^\dagger))$. It also preserves the Bregman distance:
$$D_{\check R_0}^{\xi_0^\dagger}(i_V(a),i_V(a^\dagger))=D_{\check R}^{\xi^\dagger}(a,a^\dagger).$$
The penalty is a functional on $P(X)$ under $i_Y$ and has the required norm there. These are the domains used by the generic joint and frozen estimates.

1.1 The space $V$ is closed in the intrinsic Sobolev Hilbert space, since convergence there implies $L^2$ convergence and preserves vanishing on the collar. For its elements, zero extension is bounded into $H^{s_1}(\mathbb R^3)$ by [F3]. Fourier Cauchy–Schwarz gives $\|a\|_\infty\le C\|a\|_V$ because $s_1>3/2$. Thus $V$ embeds continuously into the bounded collared coefficient space. The set $\mathcal C-\sigma_0$ is convex and closed in $V$: convexity preserves the pointwise bounds, and uniform convergence from this embedding preserves them under a norm limit. [A1, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Choose a smooth scalar function $\vartheta$ with $0\le\vartheta\le1$, equal to one on $[m,M]$ and zero outside $(m/2,2M)$, and set $g(t)=1+\int_1^t\vartheta(u)du$. Then $g(t)=t$ on $[m,M]$, $g(1)=1$, and $m/2\le g(t)\le2M$ globally. All its first and second derivatives are bounded. Put $b(a):=g(\sigma_0+a)-1$. Since $\sigma_0+a=1$ outside $B_\rho$ and $g(1)=1$, $b(a)\in E$ for every $a\in V$. ## Statement

Assume Countable Choice. Let $n\geq3$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded smooth domain contained in a ball $B(0,R)$, and let $q\in L^\infty(\Omega,\mathbb C)$. There are constants $C>0$ and $\tau_0\geq1$, depending only on $n$, $R$, and $\|q\|_{L^\infty}$, such that for every $\zeta\in\mathbb C^n$ satisfying $\zeta\cdot\zeta=0$ and $|\zeta|\geq\tau_0$, there is $r_\zeta\in H^1(\Omega,\mathbb C)$ for which
$$u_\zeta(x)=e^{i\zeta\cdot x}(1+r_\zeta(x))$$
solves $(-\Delta+q)u_\zeta=0$ distributionally in $\Omega$, and
$$\|r_\zeta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq C|\zeta|^{-1}\|q\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|\nabla r_\zeta\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\leq C\|q\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
The dot product in the null-phase condition is complex bilinear, and $|\zeta|=(\sum_{j=1}^n|\zeta_j|^2)^{1/2}$.

## Statement references

[[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm|Euclidean Sobolev spaces and weak derivatives]]

[[def-riemannian-gradient|Gradient convention]]

[[def-laplace-beltrami-operator-as-trace-of-the-hessian|Euclidean Laplacian convention]]

[[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus|Fourier basis and Parseval on the torus]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable Choice; a bounded smooth domain $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$; $q\in L^\infty(\Omega,\mathbb C)$; and a null vector $\zeta$ above the stated size threshold.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is assumed by the Fourier-basis supplier [F1].

[F1] [[thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus]]: on a normalized $n$-torus, the coordinate characters form a complete orthonormal basis of $L^2$ and satisfy Parseval's identity. Rescaling the fundamental cube and multiplying by a unit-modulus exponential preserve completeness and orthonormality.

[F2] [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]], [[def-riemannian-gradient]], and [[def-laplace-beltrami-operator-as-trace-of-the-hessian]]: $H^1$ consists of $L^2$ functions with $L^2$ weak first derivatives, $D=-i\nabla$ has the same norm as $\nabla$, and $D^2=-\Delta$.

## Proof

**Given:** the data in the Statement.

1.1 Write $\zeta=a+ib$. The null condition gives $|a|=|b|=:s=|\zeta|/\sqrt2$ and $a\cdot b=0$. Choose an orthogonal map $U$ with $Ua=se_1$ and $Ub=se_2$. Work temporarily with $U\Omega$, $q\circ U^{-1}$, and the phase $U\zeta$, relabeling them $\Omega$, $q$, and $\zeta$ for the construction; the Euclidean Laplacian, Lebesgue norms, and null phase are invariant under this change, and the constructed remainder is pulled back by $U$ at the end. As $\Omega\subset B(0,R)$, choose $L>\max\{1,(R+1)/\pi\}$; then $\Omega\subset Q_L=(-\pi L,\pi L)^n$. Put $\eta_k=(k+\tfrac12e_2)/L$ and $w_k(x)=(2\pi L)^{-n/2}e^{i\eta_k\cdot x}$ for $k\in\mathbb Z^n$. By [F1], these form an orthonormal basis on $Q_L$: they are the rescaled standard Fourier characters multiplied by the unitary factor $e^{ix_2/(2L)}$. For $A_\zeta=D^2+2\zeta\cdot D$, one has $A_\zeta w_k=p_kw_k$, where $p_k=|\eta_k|^2+2\zeta\cdot\eta_k$ and $|\operatorname{Im}p_k|=2s|k_2+\tfrac12|/L\geq s/L$. If $|\eta_k|\leq4s$, then $|p_k|\geq s/L$ and $|\eta_k/p_k|\leq4L$. If $|\eta_k|>4s$, then $|\operatorname{Re}p_k|\geq|\eta_k|^2-2s|\eta_k|\geq|\eta_k|^2/2$, so $|p_k|^{-1}<1/(8s^2)\leq L/s$ and $|\eta_k/p_k|<1/(2s)$. Thus $\sup_k|p_k|^{-1}\leq L/s$ and $\sup_k|\eta_k/p_k|\leq C_L$. Define $G_\zeta f=\sum_k p_k^{-1}(f,w_k)w_k$. Parseval [F1] gives $\|G_\zeta f\|_2\leq (L/s)\|f\|_2$ and $\|\nabla G_\zeta f\|_2\leq C_L\|f\|_2$. For finite Fourier sums $f_N$, the corresponding partial sums $G_\zeta f_N$ satisfy $A_\zeta G_\zeta f_N=f_N$ termwise. Parseval and the multiplier bounds give $f_N\to f$ in $L^2(Q_L)$ and $G_\zeta f_N\to G_\zeta f$ in $H^1(Q_L)$. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\ge2$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded connected domain with smooth nonempty boundary, and regard $\overline\Omega$ as a compact smooth manifold with the Euclidean metric. Write $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)=W^{1,2}(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ and let $H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$ be the closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega;\mathbb R)$ in that norm; put $\mathcal B_{\rm E}:=H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$. Let $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ and $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas spaces on $\overline\Omega$ and let $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ be the fixed-atlas boundary space using localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ norms. The identity on smooth functions extends to bounded linear isomorphisms between $H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)$ and $H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$, and between their zero-boundary subspaces. Classical boundary restriction extends to a bounded linear trace $T:H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)$ with kernel $H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)$. The induced quotient map is a bounded linear isomorphism

$$H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)\;\cong\;H^1_{\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)/H^1_{0,\rm fix}(\overline\Omega)\;\cong\;H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega).$$

Thus the Euclidean trace quotient and the fixed-atlas $H^{1/2}$ boundary space are canonically equivalent.

[[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary|Fractional Sobolev space on a compact boundary]]

[[lem-half-space-trace-has-the-fractional-slobodeckij-bound|Half-space trace estimate into the fractional boundary space]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice; the bounded connected smooth Euclidean domain and fixed-atlas conventions in the statement.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]])

[A2] Countable Choice. ([[def-countable-choice]])

[F1] $H^1_{\rm fix}$ is the completion of smooth functions in the fixed finite chartwise $W^{1,2}$ norm; $H^1_{0,\rm fix}$ is the closure of interior compactly supported smooth functions; $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$ is the fixed finite sum of localized Euclidean $W^{1/2,2}$ boundary norms. ([[def-ip-sobolev-spaces-on-compact-riemannian-domain]])

[F2] The compact-boundary fractional space consists of $L^2$ classes with finite chartwise Slobodeckij norm, and different finite atlases and subordinate partitions give equivalent norms. ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]], [[lem-fractional-boundary-norm-is-independent-of-atlas]])

[F3] Smooth flattening-chart compositions and multiplication by the fixed smooth cutoffs are bounded in $W^{1,2}$; restrictions of ambient smooth functions are dense in Euclidean $W^{1,2}(\Omega)$, which is complete. ([[lem-c-k-boundary-flattening-preserves-wkp-locally]], [[lem-weak-leibniz-rule-with-a-smooth-factor]], [[thm-smooth-up-to-the-boundary-density-on-smooth-domains]], [[thm-sobolev-spaces-are-banach-spaces]])

[F5] The usual trace from Euclidean $H^1(\Omega)$ to $L^2(\partial\Omega)$ is bounded and agrees with classical restriction on continuous Sobolev functions. ([[thm-lp-trace-operator-on-a-bounded-c-one-domain]])

[F6] The kernel of that $L^2$ trace is exactly the Euclidean $H^1$-closure of $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, namely $H^1_{0,\rm E}(\Omega)$. ([[thm-kernel-of-the-trace-is-w-one-p-zero]], [[def-wkp-zero-as-a-sobolev-closure]])

## Proof

1.1 On the common smooth core, the identity between the fixed-atlas and Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norms is bounded in both directions. Indeed, each fixed chart representative is obtained by multiplying by a fixed smooth cutoff and composing with a smooth flattening chart, so [F3] bounds the finite fixed-atlas sum by the Euclidean norm. Conversely, the finite partition of unity writes $u$ as the sum of its localized chart pieces; pull each piece back and use [F3] to bound the Euclidean $W^{1,2}$ norm by the fixed-atlas sum. The constants are finite because the atlas and partition are finite. By the density and completeness in [F3], the identity extends to bounded inverse maps on the completions. Since the two norms are equivalent on $C_c^\infty(\Omega)$, their closures give the same zero-boundary subspace. [A1, A2, F1, F3, construct]

2.1 For $u\in H^1_{\rm fix}$, take its localized boundary-chart representatives in the fixed-atlas definition. Apply [F4] to each representative (reflecting $t<0$ to $t>0$ when required), and sum the finitely many resulting local traces. The fixed-atlas norm [F1] gives a bounded map $T:H^1_{\rm fix}\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$. For smooth $u$ this sum is the classical boundary restriction because the partition equals one near the boundary and the half-space traces agree with classical restriction. As an $L^2$-valued map, this trace agrees with the Euclidean trace [F5]: the maps are bounded into $L^2$ by [F2] and [F5], and the Euclidean and fixed $H^1$ norms are equivalent by step 1.1, so equality on the dense smooth core extends to all of $H^1$. Conversely, if $u\in H^1_{0,\rm fix}$, approximate it in the fixed $H^1$ norm by interior compactly supported smooth functions. Each has zero classical trace, so continuity of $T$ gives $Tu=0$. Therefore $\ker T=H^1_{0,\rm fix}$. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, given]

4.1 By [F7] and the boundary-norm equivalence [F2], the Euclidean $L^2$ trace has a bounded right inverse $R:H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}(\partial\Omega)\to H^1_{\rm E}(\Omega)$. The norm equivalence of step 1.1 makes $R$ bounded into $H^1_{\rm fix}$ as well. For every boundary class $f$, the Euclidean trace of $Rf$ is $f$; by step 2.1 the fixed trace agrees with it in $L^2$, hence as an $H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$ class. So $T$ is onto. The kernel identity of step 3.1 induces a bounded bijection $\bar T:H^1_{\rm fix}/H^1_{0,\rm fix}\to H^{1/2}_{\rm fix}$. Composing with the quotient identity isomorphism of step 1.1 proves the asserted Euclidean quotient identification. [A1, A2, F1, F2, F7, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice, the Hahn–Banach theorem, and countable choice. Let $B$ be a real separable Banach space, and let $W$ be a centered Borel Gaussian random element with law $\mu$. Define its covariance by $C\ell=\mathbb E[\ell(W)W]$ for $\ell\in B^*$, let $N=\{\ell:\mathbb E[\ell(W)^2]=0\}$, and let $E$ be the completion of $B^*/N$ with inner product $\langle[\ell],[m]\rangle_E=\mathbb E[\ell(W)m(W)]$. Let $i:E\to B$ be the canonical injection extending $[\ell]\mapsto C\ell$. For $z\in B$ and $r>0$, write $\overline B_B(z,r)=\{x\in B:\|x-z\|_B\le r\}$. Then for any $h_1,h_2\in E$,
$$ \frac{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_1,r))}{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_2,r))} \longrightarrow \exp\!\left(\frac{\|h_2\|_E^2-\|h_1\|_E^2}{2}\right) \qquad(r\downarrow0). $$
The denominator is positive for every $r>0$.

## Statement references

[[def-borel-gaussian-random-element-on-a-separable-banach-space|a centered Borel Gaussian random element has centered normal continuous-linear projections]]

[[def-banach-gaussian-covariance-operator-and-rkhs|the covariance-induced Cameron–Martin Hilbert space]]

[[thm-cameron-martin-translation-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law|the Cameron–Martin change-of-measure formula]]

[[thm-support-of-banach-gaussian-is-closure-of-rkhs|the support is the Banach closure of the Cameron–Martin space]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, HB, countable choice, a real separable Banach space $B$, a centered Borel Gaussian random element $W$ with law $\mu$, and its covariance-induced Cameron–Martin Hilbert space $E$ with canonical injection $i$.

[A1] AC is assumed by the Cameron–Martin and support interfaces below. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[A2] HB and countable choice are assumed for the norming-family interface used to justify symmetry on the centered ball. [[def-hahn-banach-extension-principle-relative]], [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] $W$ is Borel measurable, and every $\ell\in B^*$ applied to $W$ is a centered real normal variable. [[def-borel-gaussian-random-element-on-a-separable-banach-space]]

[F2] The Cameron–Martin space is the completion of the covariance quotient, its canonical injection is continuous and injective, and the range of the covariance quotient is dense in $E$. [[def-banach-gaussian-covariance-operator-and-rkhs]], [[thm-banach-gaussian-covariance-rkhs-is-well-defined]]

[F3] For each $h\in E$, the law of $W+ih$ has density $\exp(z_h-\|h\|_E^2/2)$ with respect to $\mu$, where $h\mapsto z_h\in L^2(\mu)$ is linear and isometric, $z_h$ is centered normal with variance $\|h\|_E^2$, and $z_{C\ell}=\ell(W)$ almost surely. Since the covariance range is dense in $E$, this also makes $z_h$ an $L^2$ limit of continuous-linear Gaussian coordinates. [[thm-cameron-martin-translation-for-separable-banach-gaussian-law]], [[def-multivariate-normal-law]], [[def-standard-normal-and-normal-laws]]

[F4] A separable Banach space is Polish, every Borel probability on a Polish space is tight, and the support of a centered tight Borel Gaussian is $\overline{iE}$ in $B$. Thus $0$ belongs to the support and every open ball about $0$ has positive $\mu$-mass. [[def-polish-space]], [[thm-every-borel-probability-on-a-polish-space-is-tight]], [[thm-support-of-banach-gaussian-is-closure-of-rkhs]]

[F5] For every $h\in E$ and $r>0$, $\mu(\overline B_B(ih,r))\le\mu(\overline B_B(0,r))$. [[lem-ip-banach-gaussian-cm-shift-ball-bound]]

[F6] A real separable Banach space has a countable family $(\ell_j)$ with $\|x\|_B=\sup_j|\ell_j(x)|$. [[lem-separable-banach-has-countable-norming-family]]

## Proof

**Proof technique:** use the Cameron–Martin formula on a centered ball, approximate each Cameron–Martin coordinate by a continuous linear functional, and control the residual exponential by the shift-ball bound.

1.1 Put $A_r=\overline B_B(0,r)$. By [F4], $\mu(A_r)>0$ because it contains the open ball of radius $r$ about the support point $0$. Let $(\ell_j)$ be the norming family from [F6], and define $A_{r,n}=\bigcap_{j\le n}\{|\ell_j(W)|\le r\}$. The sets decrease to $A_r$. For fixed $n$, the vector $(z_s,\ell_1(W),\ldots,\ell_n(W))$ is centered Gaussian: [F3] makes $z_s$ an $L^2$ limit of continuous-linear Gaussian coordinates, so adjoining the finitely many displayed coordinates gives a centered Gaussian limit. Its law is invariant under simultaneous sign reversal, and $A_{r,n}$ is invariant under that reversal. Hence $$ \mathbb E[e^{z_s}\mathbf1_{A_{r,n}}]=\mathbb E[e^{-z_s}\mathbf1_{A_{r,n}}], \qquad \mathbb E[z_s\mathbf1_{A_{r,n}}]=0. $$ The variables $e^{\pm z_s}$ are integrable by the Gaussian moment formula in [F3]. Dominated convergence as $n\to\infty$ therefore gives conditional symmetry and conditional mean zero on $A_r$. Thus $$ 1\le \mathbb E_\mu[e^{-z_s}\mid A_r]\le e^{\|s\|_E^2/2}. $$ For the lower bound, conditional Jensen applies. For the upper bound, [F3] applied to $-s$ gives $$ \mathbb E_\mu[e^{-z_s}\mathbf 1_{A_r}] =e^{\|s\|_E^2/2}\,\mu(\overline B_B(is,r)), $$ and [F5] bounds the last probability by $\mu(A_r)$. [A1, A2, F1, F3, F4, F5, F6, given, algebra]

2.1 For any $h\in E$, choose $\ell_n\in B^*$ with $h_n:=C\ell_n\to h$ in $E$, possible by the completion in [F2], and put $s_n=h-h_n$. The Cameron–Martin formula [F3], applied to the translate by $-h$, gives $$ \frac{\mu(\overline B_B(ih,r))}{\mu(A_r)} =e^{-\|h\|_E^2/2}\,\mathbb E_\mu[e^{-z_h}\mid A_r]. $$ Since $z_{h_n}=\ell_n(W)$ almost surely and $z_h=z_{h_n}+z_{s_n}$, the bound $|\ell_n(W)|\le r\|\ell_n\|_{B^*}$ on $A_r$ and step 1.1 imply $$ e^{-r\|\ell_n\|_{B^*}} \le \mathbb E_\mu[e^{-z_h}\mid A_r] \le e^{r\|\ell_n\|_{B^*}}e^{\|s_n\|_E^2/2}. $$ For fixed $n$, let $r\downarrow0$; then let $n\to\infty$, so $\|s_n\|_E\to0$. The two bounds show $\mathbb E_\mu[e^{-z_h}\mid A_r]\to1$. [F2, F3, step 1.1, given, choose, algebra]

3.1 Applying step 2.1 separately to $h_1$ and $h_2$ yields $$ \frac{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_1,r))}{\mu(\overline B_B(ih_2,r))} =e^{(\|h_2\|_E^2-\|h_1\|_E^2)/2} \frac{\mathbb E[e^{-z_{h_1}}\mid A_r]}{\mathbb E[e^{-z_{h_2}}\mid A_r]}. $$ Both conditional expectations tend to $1$, so the ratio has the stated limit. Positivity of the denominator follows from [F4], since each closed ball contains the corresponding open neighborhood of a support point. [F4, step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $M\Subset\mathbb R\times M_0^\circ$ be a three-dimensional transversally anisotropic product domain with compact connected simple surface transversal $(M_0,g_0)$. For every $p\in M_0^\circ$ choose two nontangential unit-speed geodesic segments $\gamma_1,\gamma_2$ meeting transversely at $p$ and nowhere else. For every $\xi\in\mathbb R$ and every $Q\in C^\infty(\overline M)$, there are four exact harmonic solutions $u_{\tau,1}^+,u_{\tau,1}^-,u_{\tau,2}^+,u_{\tau,2}^-\in H^1(M)$, with no prescribed boundary values, such that
$$\lim_{\tau\to\infty}\int_MQ(x_1,x')u_{\tau,1}^+u_{\tau,1}^-u_{\tau,2}^+u_{\tau,2}^-\,dV_g =c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)\int_{I_p}e^{-i\xi x_1}Q(x_1,p)\,dx_1,$$
where $I_p=\{x_1\in\mathbb R:(x_1,p)\in M^\circ\}$ and $c(p,\gamma_1,\gamma_2)>0$ is the nonzero Gaussian normalization divided by $|\sin\angle(\dot\gamma_1(p),\dot\gamma_2(p))|$.

## Statement references

[[def-ip-transversally-anisotropic-product-domain|Product domain]]

[[def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform|Simple transversal and nontangential geodesics]]

[[thm-ip-cgo-solvability-and-remainder-bound|Exact CGO solutions and remainder]]

## Facts & Assumptions
[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]] is inherited from the CGO solver supplier [F2].

[A2] [[def-countable-choice]] is inherited from the CGO solver supplier [F2].

**Given:** the simple surface product, an interior transversal point, two crossing nontangential geodesics, a longitudinal frequency $\xi$, and $Q\in C^\infty(\overline M)$.

[F1] [[def-ip-simple-surface-and-geodesic-xray-transform]]: strict convexity and unique geodesic segments define the simple surface convention.

[F2] [[thm-ip-cgo-solvability-and-remainder-bound]]: the intended supplier constructs exact harmonic solutions from transport amplitudes and controls the correction in $L^2$.

[F3] **External input:** Lassas--Liimatainen--Lin--Salo, Proposition 5.1, arXiv:1903.12562v1, PDF p. 14: on a compact oriented transversally anisotropic manifold of dimension at least three, if $f\in C^1(M)$ satisfies $\int_M f v_1\cdots v_m\,dV=0$ for all smooth harmonic $v_j$, with $m\ge4$, then $f=0$. We import this density statement. The complete proof in Section 5, PDF pp. 14--23, including the supporting Lemma 5.2, was inspected for this repair; it is not claimed to be reconstructed locally.

[F4] The literal quantifiers in the statement permit the four witnesses to depend on $Q$. They impose no uniformity in $Q$, no nonzero-solution requirement, and no quantitative remainder or beam-profile estimate.
