## Statement

For each nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its
determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$
The value assigned to $L$ is independent of reversing the orientation of any
whole component. The Dubrovnik value has the stated difference-skein, curl and
circle rules; the Kauffman value has the sum-skein, curl and circle rules; and
$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z)$ is unchanged by planar isotopy and every oriented
Reidemeister move of types I, II, and III. The claim concerns these finite
diagram moves and uses the universal coefficient relations without dividing
by a skein variable.

## Statement references

[[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions|The local polynomial conventions]]

[[lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation|The scalar Dubrovnik evaluation]]

[[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing|Determinant crossing sign and writhe]]

[[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance|Earlier AC$_\omega$ parity proof, not used here]]

[Kauffman, *An Invariant of Regular Isotopy* (1990), §VII](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~kauffman/IRH.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A nonempty regular oriented link diagram, its determinant crossing
signs, and the Dubrovnik scalar evaluation.

[F1] The Dubrovnik scalar $P$ is regular-isotopy invariant, has $P(\varnothing)=1$,
positive/negative curl factors $a,a^{-1}$, loop factor $d$, and skein
$P_+-P_-=z(P_0-P_\infty)$ over $z(d-1)=a-a^{-1}$
([[lem-framed-kauffman-link-evaluation]]).

[F2] The determinant writhe is the signed sum of crossing signs; reversing one
strand negates that crossing sign, while reversing both strands preserves it
([[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]]).

[F3] A regular oriented diagram is a finite generic planar projection with only
transverse double crossings and no triple points; distinct component shadows
therefore have finitely many transverse intersections
([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]).

[F4] A type-I move changes one self-crossing, type II adds or removes two
opposite-sign crossings, and type III preserves its three crossing signs
([[def-oriented-reidemeister-moves]]).

[F5] In the stated polynomial convention, $D=P/d$ on nonempty diagrams,
$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ)$, and $F=A^{-w}L$
([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]]).

## Proof


1.1 Fix distinct components $K_r,K_s$ and let their projected shadows be $\gamma_r,\gamma_s$. Smooth each of the finitely many self-crossings of $\gamma_r$ inside a small disk disjoint from $\gamma_s$; the disk exists because there are no triple points, and the smoothing leaves every mixed intersection with $\gamma_s$ unchanged. After finitely many such smoothings, $\gamma_r$ is a finite disjoint union of embedded circles. As $\gamma_s$ traverses any embedded circle, every transverse intersection changes whether it is inside or outside that circle, and the closed traversal returns to its initial region. Hence the original number of mixed intersections of $K_r,K_s$ is even. Each determinant crossing sign is $+1$ or $-1$, both congruent to $1$ modulo $2$, so the signed mixed-crossing sum $S_{rs}$ is even. Summing over $s\ne r$ shows that the total mixed-crossing sum $S_r$ involving $K_r$ is even. Reversing $K_r$ leaves its self-crossing signs fixed by [F2] and negates its mixed crossing signs, so $w$ changes by $-2S_r\in4\mathbb Z$. Thus $i^w$ is unchanged; $c$ and the unoriented value $D$ are unchanged as well. Therefore the formula defining $L$ is independent of reversing $K_r$, and repeating for every component proves orientation independence. [F2, F3, F5, construct, algebra]

1.2 For a positive curl, $D$ gains a factor $a$ and $w$ increases by $1$; substituting $a_D=-iA$ and $z_D=iZ$ in [F5] shows that $L$ gains the factor $i a_D=A$. For a negative curl, $D$ gains $a^{-1}$ and $w$ decreases by $1$, so $L$ gains $i^{-1}a_D^{-1}=A^{-1}$. Adding a disjoint trivial circle increases $c$ by $1$ and multiplies $D$ by $d$, so the factor $(-1)^c$ makes $L$ acquire the factor $-d$. Set $\delta_L=-d$. Under $a_D=-iA$ and $z_D=iZ$, the coefficient relation $z_D(d-1)=a_D-a_D^{-1}$ becomes $Z(1-d)=A+A^{-1}$, hence $Z(\delta_L+1)=A+A^{-1}$. This gives the Kauffman circle rule using the universal relation without inverting $Z$. [F1, F4, F5, algebra]

2.1 Consider a positive crossing and write $w=w(K_+)$ and $c=c(K_+)$. Switching it gives $w(K_-)=w-2$ and leaves $c$ fixed. Each smoothing deletes that crossing, so before any orientation adjustment its writhe is $w-1$. The orientation-preserving smoothing $K_0$ has $c+1$ components at a self-crossing and $c-1$ at a mixed crossing. The other smoothing $K_\infty$ has $c$ components at a self-crossing and $c-1$ at a mixed crossing. To orient $K_\infty$ at a self-crossing, first use the orientation-preserving smoothing to split the original component into two closed components, then join their arcs by the other smoothing and reverse one of the two orientations. This changes signs at exactly the crossings between that component and the other split component or any remaining component; the pairwise sums are even by step 1.1, so $w(K_\infty)\equiv w-1\pmod4$. At a mixed crossing, reverse one whole incident component in the original diagram. Its writhe changes by minus twice a mixed-crossing sum, which is divisible by $4$ by step 1.1; this reversal changes the displayed crossing from positive to negative and makes $K_\infty$ the orientation-preserving smoothing. Removing that negative crossing raises writhe by $1$, so $w(K_\infty)\equiv w+1\pmod4$. By [F5], the phase $-i^w(-1)^c$ multiplying the Dubrovnik value changes by the factor $i$ on $K_0$ and by $-i$ on $K_\infty$. It also changes sign when the crossing is switched, since $w(K_-)=w-2$. Therefore the Dubrovnik difference skein in [F1] becomes the Kauffman sum skein $L_++L_-=Z(L_0+L_\infty)$ after substituting $a=-iA$ and $z=iZ$, equivalently $A=ia$ and $Z=-iz$. The calculation uses the positive member $K_+$ of the crossing pair; since the resulting sum-skein is symmetric in $K_+$ and $K_-$, it applies whether the input diagram displays the positive or negative member. [F1, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 By [F1], $D$ is unchanged under planar isotopy and Reidemeister II and III. The determinant writhe is unchanged under II and III by [F2, F4], so the formula in [F5] gives the corresponding regular-isotopy rules for $L$. The positive and negative curl factors are those computed in step 1.2. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 1.2]

3.1 For a positive type-I move, $$A^{-(w+1)}A L=A^{-w}L;$$ for a negative type-I move, $$A^{-(w-1)}A^{-1}L=A^{-w}L.$$ Moves II and III leave $w$ unchanged, hence also preserve $F$. Therefore $F$ is unchanged by every listed move, while the conversion identity is the defining relation in [F5]. [F2, F4, F5, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth $3$-manifold with nonempty boundary, and fix a finite triangulation of $M$ with $t$ triangular faces. If $\mathcal T$ is any finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible tori in $M$ such that no component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is homeomorphic to $T^2\times[0,1]$, then
$$
|\mathcal T|\le 4t+\dim_{\mathbb Z_2}H_2(M;\mathbb Z_2)-1.
$$
Consequently, any iterative process that cuts along tori and for which every finite stage satisfies this no-product condition terminates after finitely many cuts.

## Statement references

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, Proposition 1.7 and Corollary 1.8](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

[Ryan Budney, *JSJ-decompositions of knot and link complements in the 3-sphere*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0506523)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth three-manifold $M$ with nonempty boundary, the fixed finite compatible triangulation with $t$ triangular faces, and the finite torus family in the Statement. Here compatible triangulation is used in the original smooth-manifold sense required by the smooth-strata transversality argument: its simplex maps and whole-star manifold charts are compatible with the given smooth structure. No new assertion for an arbitrary TOP marking unrelated to that structure is inferred.

[A1] Countable choice is [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] Incompressibility, irreducibility and a product cut component have the given conventions. [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]]

[F2] For this supplied compatible smooth triangulation, a finite incompressible smooth torus family has simultaneous smooth normal position. The actual cut tetrahedra and normal face disks retain their marked ball and rectangle parameters. [[lem-smooth-incompressible-tori-admit-normal-position-in-a-compatible-triangulation]]

[F3] A rectangular-only cut component with those actual parameters is an interval bundle. If it is not $T^2\times I$, it has a compact one-sided locally flat core whose removal leaves the component connected. [[lem-rectangular-normal-cut-components-are-interval-bundles]]

[F4] In a connected boundaryless three-manifold, disjoint compact locally flat closed surfaces with connected complement have independent mod-two homology classes, including one-sided surfaces. [[lem-connected-complement-surfaces-have-independent-mod-two-homology-classes]]

[F5] The accepted Haken bound proof constructs the finite normal face-cell and rectangle parameters and the finite inward collar push, and identifies finite simplicial and singular homology. These finite constructions and their declared countable-choice hypothesis apply to the exact same supplied triangulation here. [[lem-haken-torus-bound-for-a-supplied-compatible-smooth-triangulation]], Proof1.1 and4.1; [[thm-simplicial-and-singular-homology-agree-for-simplicial-complexes]]

## Proof

1.1 Apply [F2] to the given finite torus family for the very triangulation in the Statement. Its smooth ambient isotopy retains incompressibility, all cut-component homeomorphism types and the no-product condition. It puts the family into actual normal disks in each parametrized tetrahedron and disjoint arcs in each triangular face, joining distinct edges. This invokes the accepted marked normal-position construction rather than treating a surgery that changes a torus as an isotopy. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct]

2.1 In each triangular face group the arcs by the pair of distinct edges they join. Within each of the three types they occur in a parallel stack. Between consecutive arcs of a stack is a rectangle, and collapsing those strips leaves at most one arc of each type, hence at most four complementary regions. Every nonrectangular region survives distinctly in this collapsed picture, so there are at most $4t$ such regions over all faces. The successive finite face-disk cuts and the marked rectangle product maps are supplied by [F2] and [F5]; no unparametrized polygon or missing side matching is being assumed. [F2, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Let $m$ be the number of cut components meeting all faces only in rectangles. By [F3] each is an interval bundle. The torus-product possibility is excluded by hypothesis. Thus they have disjoint one-sided compact locally flat cores $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$, and removing each core leaves its component connected. No ambient triangulation or smoothness of these cores is required. [F1, F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Form the connected finite dual graph of all torus cuts, allowing loops, and choose a spanning tree. Let $k$ be the number of edges outside that tree. The corresponding $k$ tori, together with all the $Q_j$, have connected complement: remove the cores in the fully cut pieces, which remain connected by step2.1, and glue back the tree faces. A tree joins all the pieces and cannot create a new disconnection. Pass to $\operatorname{Int}M$ by the finite inward collar push in [F5], chosen disjoint from these compact surfaces; its homotopy fixes them and proves that the interior inclusion induces a homology isomorphism, while their complement remains connected. Now [F4] gives $k+m$ independent mod-two classes, so $k+m\le\beta$, where $\beta=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M;\mathbb F_2)$. This number is finite because the supplied triangulation is finite and its simplicial homology computes singular homology. [F3, F4, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Write $n=|\mathcal T|$ and let $v$ be the number of cut components. The dual graph has $n$ edges, $v$ vertices and $k=n-v+1$ non-tree edges; thus $v=n-k+1$. Each component other than the $m$ rectangular-only ones contains a nonrectangular face region. A physical region belongs to just one cut component: its two tetrahedral sides are glued through its interior, or it is a boundary face with only one incident side. ## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $M$ be a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth $3$-manifold with nonempty boundary, and fix a finite triangulation of $M$ with $t$ triangular faces. If $\mathcal T$ is any finite family of pairwise disjoint, two-sided, incompressible tori in $M$ such that no component obtained by cutting $M$ along $\mathcal T$ is homeomorphic to $T^2\times[0,1]$, then
$$
|\mathcal T|\le 4t+\dim_{\mathbb Z_2}H_2(M;\mathbb Z_2)-1.
$$
Consequently, any iterative process that cuts along tori and for which every finite stage satisfies this no-product condition terminates after finitely many cuts.

## Statement references

[Allen Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, Proposition 1.7 and Corollary 1.8](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

[Ryan Budney, *JSJ-decompositions of knot and link complements in the 3-sphere*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0506523)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, a compact connected irreducible orientable smooth three-manifold $M$ with nonempty boundary, the fixed finite compatible triangulation with $t$ triangular faces, and the finite torus family in the Statement. Here compatible triangulation is used in the original smooth-manifold sense required by the smooth-strata transversality argument: its simplex maps and whole-star manifold charts are compatible with the given smooth structure. No new assertion for an arbitrary TOP marking unrelated to that structure is inferred.

[A1] Countable choice is [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] Incompressibility, irreducibility and a product cut component have the given conventions. [[def-incompressibility-seifert-fibration-and-jsj-system]]

[F2] For this supplied compatible smooth triangulation, a finite incompressible smooth torus family has simultaneous smooth normal position. The actual cut tetrahedra and normal face disks retain their marked ball and rectangle parameters. [[lem-smooth-incompressible-tori-admit-normal-position-in-a-compatible-triangulation]]

[F3] A rectangular-only cut component with those actual parameters is an interval bundle. If it is not $T^2\times I$, it has a compact one-sided locally flat core whose removal leaves the component connected. [[lem-rectangular-normal-cut-components-are-interval-bundles]]

[F4] In a connected boundaryless three-manifold, disjoint compact locally flat closed surfaces with connected complement have independent mod-two homology classes, including one-sided surfaces. [[lem-connected-complement-surfaces-have-independent-mod-two-homology-classes]]

[F5] The accepted Haken bound proof constructs the finite normal face-cell and rectangle parameters and the finite inward collar push, and identifies finite simplicial and singular homology. These finite constructions and their declared countable-choice hypothesis apply to the exact same supplied triangulation here. [[lem-haken-torus-bound-for-a-supplied-compatible-smooth-triangulation]], Proof1.1 and4.1; [[thm-simplicial-and-singular-homology-agree-for-simplicial-complexes]]

## Proof

1.1 Apply [F2] to the given finite torus family for the very triangulation in the Statement. Its smooth ambient isotopy retains incompressibility, all cut-component homeomorphism types and the no-product condition. It puts the family into actual normal disks in each parametrized tetrahedron and disjoint arcs in each triangular face, joining distinct edges. This invokes the accepted marked normal-position construction rather than treating a surgery that changes a torus as an isotopy. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct]

1.2 In each triangular face group the arcs by the pair of distinct edges they join. Within each of the three types they occur in a parallel stack. Between consecutive arcs of a stack is a rectangle, and collapsing those strips leaves at most one arc of each type, hence at most four complementary regions. Every nonrectangular region survives distinctly in this collapsed picture, so there are at most $4t$ such regions over all faces. The successive finite face-disk cuts and the marked rectangle product maps are supplied by [F2] and [F5]; no unparametrized polygon or missing side matching is being assumed. [F2, F5, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Let $m$ be the number of cut components meeting all faces only in rectangles. By [F3] each is an interval bundle. The torus-product possibility is excluded by hypothesis. Thus they have disjoint one-sided compact locally flat cores $Q_1,\ldots,Q_m$, and removing each core leaves its component connected. No ambient triangulation or smoothness of these cores is required. [F1, F3, step 1.2, construct]

2.2 Form the connected finite dual graph of all torus cuts, allowing loops, and choose a spanning tree. Let $k$ be the number of edges outside that tree. The corresponding $k$ tori, together with all the $Q_j$, have connected complement: remove the cores in the fully cut pieces, which remain connected by step2.1, and glue back the tree faces. A tree joins all the pieces and cannot create a new disconnection. Pass to $\operatorname{Int}M$ by the finite inward collar push in [F5], chosen disjoint from these compact surfaces; its homotopy fixes them and proves that the interior inclusion induces a homology isomorphism, while their complement remains connected. Now [F4] gives $k+m$ independent mod-two classes, so $k+m\le\beta$, where $\beta=\dim_{\mathbb F_2}H_2(M;\mathbb F_2)$. This number is finite because the supplied triangulation is finite and its simplicial homology computes singular homology. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

2.3 Write $n=|\mathcal T|$ and let $v$ be the number of cut components. The dual graph has $n$ edges, $v$ vertices and $k=n-v+1$ non-tree edges; thus $v=n-k+1$. Each component other than the $m$ rectangular-only ones contains a nonrectangular face region. A physical region belongs to just one cut component: its two tetrahedral sides are glued through its interior, or it is a boundary face with only one incident side. Distinct components therefore use distinct such regions, and step1.2 gives $v\le m+4t$. [step 1.2, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

3.1 Combining these inequalities yields $n+1\le k+m+4t\le\beta+4t$, which is exactly the stated bound. It also holds for the empty family. If an accumulating cutting process continued past $4t+\beta-1$ cuts while each finite accumulated family retained the stated hypotheses, that stage would contradict the same bound for the fixed original triangulation. Thus no such process continues indefinitely. The proof retains the original countable-choice and smooth-compatible triangulation scope; it does not postulate an arbitrary unrelated TOP marking. [step 2.2, step 2.3, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. If $K_0$ and $K_1$ are concordant in the smooth category and $J_0$ and $J_1$ are concordant in the same category, then $K_0\#J_0$ and $K_1\#J_1$ are smoothly concordant. The same implication holds when both given concordances and the resulting concordance are required to be locally flat and topological.

## Statement references

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth concordance annuli]]

[[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance|Locally flat topological concordance annuli]]

[[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot|The oriented connected sum]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, concordance annuli $A$ from $K_0$ to $K_1$ and $B$ from $J_0$ to $J_1$ in one of the two categories.

[F1] Each annulus is proper, has product collars at its endpoint knots, and has boundary orientation $-K_0\sqcup K_1$ or $-J_0\sqcup J_1$. ([[def-smooth-knot-concordance]], [[def-locally-flat-topological-knot-concordance]])

[F2] The oriented connected sum is obtained by deleting short trivial arcs and gluing with the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map; its class is independent of the local choices under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-knot-connected-sum-and-prime-knot]], [[lem-knot-connected-sum-well-defined]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $S^3$ is simply connected, continuous homotopies into a smooth manifold can be smoothly approximated relative to a closed region where they are already smooth, finite-dimensional smooth perturbations can be chosen transverse, and isotopies of compact smooth sources extend ambiently in a boundaryless target with support in any prescribed neighborhood of their tracks. In the isotopy-extension construction, the velocity extension may be prescribed to be zero on a closed subtrack where the input isotopy is stationary, so that subtrack is fixed pointwise. Smooth submanifolds have tubular neighborhoods. ([[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]], [[thm-relative-whitney-approximation-for-manifold-valued-maps]], [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F4] Ambient-isotopic oriented knot representatives may be changed by smooth families of orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$. A chosen point on a knot can be moved to any prescribed point by an isotopy of embeddings of that point, which extends ambiently under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]], [[def-countable-choice]])

[F5] Bare locally flat proper arcs with specified product end collars can be straightened by [[thm-locally-flat-codimension-three-arc-unknotting]]. This retained local result is not being strengthened into a relative transverse pair-tube or complement theorem.

[F6] **External TOP input, initially in ordinary ZFC:** connected sum descends to locally flat topological concordance classes of smooth oriented knots represented by proper annuli in $S^3\times I$. Donald and Owens, §2, Lemma 2.3 and proof, establish well-definedness by taking connected sum along the concordance annulus; §4, Theorem 4.1 and proof, state the locally flat TOP version and identify the topological knot concordance group as a direct summand. The paper gives the annulus construction as a proof sketch, not a detailed pair-tube proof. Ray, §3, Definition 3.5 and discussion through Proposition 3.6, also states the TOP concordance group, while explicitly saying the group claim is asserted but not proved there. We use the well-defined TOP operation as an external input, not as a locally reconstructed annulus-adapted tube/complement argument. For the collared annuli of [F1], it implies that the two given concordances yield an oriented locally flat annulus between the endpoint connected sums. The compact real-code/$L[r]$ specialization below addresses the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis; it does not enlarge the external input's geometric scope.

[F7] **External set-theoretic input:** for a real $r\subseteq\omega$, the relativized constructible class $L[r]$ is a transitive inner model of ZFC containing $r$ and all natural numbers. Karagila, §8.3, closing remarks, printed p.42, gives the $L[A]$ construction and its inner-ZFC conclusion; for a real parameter, $r\subseteq\omega\subseteq L[r]$, so the parameter belongs to that model. No ambient full AC is assumed by this input. The compact coding argument below, rather than an implication from ambient full AC, supplies the Countable Choice specialization of [F6].

## Proof

**Given:** The two annuli $A,B$ and the fixed connected-sum convention.

1.1 First consider smooth concordances. Pick one point on each endpoint knot. By [F4], apply separate endpoint ambient isotopies carrying both marked points to a common point $p\in S^3$; extend them over disjoint product collars of the concordance and interpolate by the identity between the collars. This changes the representatives only within their ambient-isotopy classes. Choose a smooth spanning arc in each annulus joining the marked points and fixed in product collars. For one annulus, write this arc as $\alpha$ and the standard product arc as $\beta(s)=(p,s)$. Since $S^3\times(0,1)$ is simply connected by [F3], the middle portions of $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are homotopic rel endpoints after their common endpoint collars are deleted. Relative smooth approximation in [F3] gives a smooth homotopy $H(s,t)$ fixed on those collars. We now perturb this homotopy through a finite-dimensional family. First, local coordinate bumps whose $s$-derivatives span the four target coordinates at each zero of $\partial_sH$ make the total derivative family transverse to the zero section of the rank-four tangent bundle; its source has dimension two, so a generic parameter has $\partial_sH\ne0$ everywhere. Compactness then supplies a uniform $\delta>0$ for local injectivity of every slice when $|s-s'|<\delta$. On the compact configuration set $|s-s'|\ge\delta$, use two disjoint source-supported coordinate bumps near each pair to vary $H(s,t)$ and $H(s',t)$ independently. A finite cover of the possible diagonal preimage makes the total pair map transverse to the diagonal in $(S^3\times I)^2$. Its source-pair-time dimension is three and the diagonal has codimension four, so the generic slice has no double points. Both perturbations are supported away from the endpoint collars and can be chosen small enough to preserve immersion and local injectivity. Thus every time-slice is a smooth embedding, giving an isotopy of proper arcs rel collars. The isotopy is stationary on common source end collars, so restrict to the compact middle arcs containing its moving part; these lie in $S^3\times(0,1)$, a boundaryless smooth manifold. Apply [F3] there with support in the interior, choosing the extension to fix the adjacent stationary arc collars, and extend it by the identity across the fixed end collars. This gives an ambient isotopy of $S^3\times I$ fixed near both end levels and carrying the whole spanning arc to the vertical product arc without changing the concordance or its oriented endpoint knot types. [F1, F2, F3, F4, given, construct, choose]

1.2 For the TOP implication, first code the actual input as compact metric data. Parametrize the two annuli by the standard compact annulus, and choose finitely many local pair charts covering each, together with their inverses and the given end-collar maps. Such a finite selection is possible by compactness and finite choice; using countably many relatively compact chart restrictions instead would require only $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Include the endpoint knots and the chosen connected-sum representatives from [F2]. For these smooth knots and the finite smooth coordinate maps used in their sums, also code the derivatives of every finite order, their continuity moduli and rational difference-quotient remainder bounds; thus the inner model sees smooth knots, not merely continuous embeddings. Continuous maps on these standard metric domains are coded by their values on fixed countable rational dense sets and uniform continuity moduli on compact exhaustions; include inverse moduli for embeddings and chart inverses. All this countable numerical data is one real $r$. [F1, F2, F6, F7, given, construct, choose]

2.1 For each vertical arc, double the ambient product across its two boundary levels by gluing to a second copy of $S^3\times I$, and glue a second copy of the concordance annulus using its product collars. The doubled ambient manifold is $S^3\times S^1$ and the doubled annulus is a smooth embedded torus. Doubling the spanning arc across its endpoints gives a smooth embedded circle $C$ in that torus. Apply the tubular-neighborhood theorem to the closed torus in $S^3\times S^1$ and to $C$ inside the torus. Over $C$, the normal line of $C$ in the torus and the rank-two normal bundle of the torus in the ambient manifold are trivial, so their product gives a neighborhood $D^1\times D^2\times S^1$ of $C$ whose intersection with the torus is exactly $D^1\times S^1$. Restrict to the half corresponding to the original arc; this gives the required product neighborhood $D^3\times I$ meeting the original annulus exactly in $D^1\times I$, with product end faces from the collars. Removing the interior of this strip from each annulus leaves a rectangle. Remove the two product neighborhoods from two copies of $S^3\times I$ and glue their boundary cylinders $S^2\times I$ by the fixed product identification. At each level this glues two three-balls along their boundary spheres, giving $S^3\#S^3\cong S^3$; since the gluing is independent of the interval parameter, the resulting ambient cobordism is $S^3\times I$. Glue the two surface rectangles across the two side intervals in the connecting cylinder, choosing the side identifications to extend the orientations on the cut annuli. At the lower end the fixed orientation-reversing boundary map joins the incoming arcs with boundary orientation $-(K_0\#J_0)$; at the upper end the same product convention gives $K_1\#J_1$. The result is connected, orientable, has two boundary circles, and has Euler characteristic $0$ (two rectangles, each of Euler characteristic $1$, glued along two intervals); hence it is an annulus. The product collars give the required smooth concordance. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.2 We use certificates, not an unqualified assertion that homeomorphism existence is absolute. For every open chart domain record its rational-ball code (relative rational half-balls at a boundary chart), compact exhaustion, and positive-distance margins putting the images of exhaustion pieces in the corresponding open image. Record both map/inverse identities on dense sets. For the pair condition record the parametrization of the linear plane section and its identities with the annulus parametrization; on smaller charts also record positive separation from the compact remainder of the annulus outside that patch. A finite parameter-patch cover and a Lebesgue-number certificate cover the entire annulus. Properness is certified on the compact subannuli $S^1\times[1/j,1-1/j]$ by positive separation from the ambient end levels. Equalities with the oriented endpoint parametrizations and the product collars are dense-set equalities with their continuity moduli. The smooth derivative identities are certified by rational difference quotients and their coded remainder bounds at each finite order. These certificates express input validity using only rational inequalities, integer indices and quantification over natural numbers. They therefore have the same truth in $L[r]$ and in the ambient universe; in particular the coded input is valid in $L[r]$. [F1, F2, F7, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 The preceding construction proves the smooth implication. [step 1.1, step 2.1]

3.2 Apply [F6] inside $L[r]$, which satisfies full Choice by [F7]. It gives a locally flat annulus for the two connected sums. In that model choose its finite pair-chart cover, inverse maps, compact-exhaustion moduli, open-image margins and end-collar certificates of the same form as in step 2.2; collect them into a real $s\in L[r]$. Decode $s$ in the ambient universe by completion from the rational dense domains. The coded forward and inverse moduli give continuous inverse maps on their coded domains; the dense-set identities extend to all points, and the open-image and separation certificates make these actual local pair charts with no additional surface branch. The finite cover certificate, properness margins, and endpoint/collar identities likewise persist. Thus the decoded object is an actual oriented proper locally flat annulus in the ambient $S^3\times I$, with the required endpoint connected sums and product collars. This transfer uses arithmetic certificates for the particular compact objects, not preservation of arbitrary sets or homeomorphisms between inner models. [F1, F2, F6, F7, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct]

4.1 Steps 1.2, 2.2, 3.2 earn the required compact specialization of the external TOP input under the stated $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, without assuming ambient full AC. Together with the retained smooth construction in steps 1.1–3.1, this proves both implications in the unchanged Statement. No annulus-adapted transverse tube or ambient complement is inferred from the bare-arc theorem [F5]; that former local proof gap is bypassed by the explicitly external input [F6]. [F1, F2, F5, F6, F7, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

The paper gives the annulus construction as a proof sketch, not a detailed pair-tube proof. Ray, §3, Definition 3.5 and discussion through Proposition 3.6, also states the TOP concordance group, while explicitly saying the group claim is asserted but not proved there. First, local coordinate bumps whose $s$-derivatives span the four target coordinates at each zero of $\partial_sH$ make the total derivative family transverse to the zero section of the rank-four tangent bundle; its source has dimension two, so a generic parameter has $\partial_sH\ne0$ everywhere. Compactness then supplies a uniform $\delta>0$ for local injectivity of every slice when $|s-s'|<\delta$. On the compact configuration set $|s-s'|\ge\delta$, use two disjoint source-supported coordinate bumps near each pair to vary $H(s,t)$ and $H(s',t)$ independently. A finite cover of the possible diagonal preimage makes the total pair map transverse to the diagonal in $(S^3\times I)^2$. Its source-pair-time dimension is three and the diagonal has codimension four, so the generic slice has no double points. Both perturbations are supported away from the endpoint collars and can be chosen small enough to preserve immersion and local injectivity. Thus every time-slice is a smooth embedding, giving an isotopy of proper arcs rel collars. 2.1 For each vertical arc, double the ambient product across its two boundary levels by gluing to a second copy of $S^3\times I$, and glue a second copy of the concordance annulus using its product collars. All this countable numerical data is one real $r$. [F1, F2, F6, F7, given, construct, choose]

For every open chart domain record its rational-ball code (relative rational half-balls at a boundary chart), compact exhaustion, and positive-distance margins putting the images of exhaustion pieces in the corresponding open image. For the pair condition record the parametrization of the linear plane section and its identities with the annulus parametrization; on smaller charts also record positive separation from the compact remainder of the annulus outside that patch. Properness is certified on the compact subannuli $S^1\times[1/j,1-1/j]$ by positive separation from the ambient end levels. Equalities with the oriented endpoint parametrizations and the product collars are dense-set equalities with their continuity moduli. Thus the decoded object is an actual oriented proper locally flat annulus in the ambient $S^3\times I$, with the required endpoint connected sums and product collars. ## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot with a chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and let $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$. Every smoothly embedded two-sphere in the interior of $E_K$ bounds a smoothly embedded closed three-ball contained in $E_K$.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-exterior|Chosen compact knot exterior]]

[[def-countable-choice|Countable choice]]

[[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three|Smooth Schoenflies in the three-sphere]]

[Hatcher, *Notes on Basic 3-Manifold Topology*, Chapter 1, Theorem 1.1](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~hatcher/3M/3M.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, a smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, its chosen closed tubular neighborhood $N(K)$, and a smooth embedded sphere $S\subset\operatorname{int}E_K$.

[F1] Countable choice is the axiom that every countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function ([[def-countable-choice]]).

[F2] Under countable choice, $S$ separates $S^3$ into two components whose closures are smooth three-balls with common boundary $S$ ([[thm-smooth-schoenflies-for-embedded-two-sphere-in-s-three]], Statement).

[F3] $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, where $N(K)$ is connected and contains $K$ ([[def-knot-exterior]], Definition).

## Proof

1.1 By [F2], $S^3\setminus S$ has two components. The connected set $K$ is disjoint from $S$, so it lies in one component. The connected neighborhood $N(K)$ is also disjoint from $S$ and contains $K$, hence it lies in that same component. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 The closure of the other component is a smooth three-ball disjoint from $N(K)$, so it is contained in $E_K$ and has boundary $S$. This proves irreducibility of the chosen exterior. [F2, F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $(W,\Sigma,\mathcal A)$ be a decorated knot cobordism between doubly pointed knots in $S^3$, and let $\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$. The representative maps from any two parametrized Kirby decompositions and admissible regular Heegaard choices are filtered $\mathbb F_2[U,V]$-equivariantly chain homotopic. If the decorated cobordism is a composite of $(W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1)$ followed by $(W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2)$, then for fixed Spin-c structures $\mathfrak s_i$ on $W_i$,
$$
\widetilde F_{W_2,\Sigma_2,\mathcal A_2,\mathfrak s_2}\circ \widetilde F_{W_1,\Sigma_1,\mathcal A_1,\mathfrak s_1} \simeq \sum_{\substack{\mathfrak s\in\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)\\ \mathfrak s|_{W_i}=\mathfrak s_i,\ i=1,2}} \widetilde F_{W,\Sigma,\mathcal A,\mathfrak s}.
$$
The sum is over Spin-c structures on the glued cobordism restricting to the specified structures on the two pieces. For $W=S^3\times[0,1]$, $\operatorname{Spin}^c(W)$ has one element, so the sum has one term and the composition law is ordinary composition up to filtered equivariant chain homotopy.

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $S$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$, with product collars and oriented boundary $-K_0\times\{0\}\sqcup K_1\times\{1\}$ for smooth oriented knots $K_0,K_1$. Let $g$ be the genus of $S$, and use the standard absolute Alexander normalization for the endpoint knot Floer complexes. Then
$$|\tau(K_1)-\tau(K_0)|\le g.$$
In particular, a smooth concordance annulus gives equal tau values, and a genus-$g$ surface from a knot to the unknot gives the four-ball genus estimate.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The normalized tau value from the filtered complex]]

[[def-smooth-knot-concordance|Smooth cobordisms with oriented boundary and product collars]]

[[def-knot-floer-cobordism-map|The representative map for a decorated knot cobordism]]

[[lem-knot-floer-holomorphic-triangle-transversality-compactness-gluing|The required triangle moduli spaces]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Knot Floer homology and the four-ball genus*, Theorem 1.1 and §§3.3–3.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0301149v4)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §§3.1–3.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

[Zemke, *Link cobordisms and absolute gradings on link Floer homology*, Theorem 10.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1701.03454v2)

[F1] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] supplies the normalized full filtered comparison between the local knot model and the standard knot Floer invariant used in the cited genus theorem.

[F2] **External input, authorized by the run-specific source boundary.** Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §3.1, Theorem 3.1(2), printed p.8, states $|\tau(K)|\le g_4(K)$ for every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$. In §3.1 the threshold is the least Alexander level at which the filtered inclusion surjects onto $\widehat{HF}(S^3)\cong\mathbb F_2$; this agrees with the nonzero-image convention here because the target is one-dimensional. For any actual smooth genus-$h$ spanning surface, $g_4(K)\le h$, so the imported theorem gives $|\tau(K)|\le h$. [F3] [[lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product]] supplies connected-sum additivity, and [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] identifies the normalized reverse-mirror complex with the bifiltered dual. 1.1 Let $C$ be the normalized finite filtered hat complex for a knot and put $t=\tau(C)$. Choose a cycle $x\in F_tC_n$ representing the generator of $H(C)\cong\mathbb F_2$ in degree $n$. By minimality of $t$, every cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ is a boundary. Hence $x\notin B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$, where $B_n=\operatorname{im}(\partial_{n+1})$; otherwise $x-b$ would be a cycle in $F_{t-1}C_n$ representing the same nonzero class. Extend a linear functional $\lambda:C_n\to\mathbb F_2$ that vanishes on $B_n+F_{t-1}C_n$ and satisfies $\lambda(x)=1$. It is a cocycle and represents the nonzero class in the dual homology, since it evaluates nontrivially on the cycle $x$. By [F3], the reflected knot's normalized Laurent complex is the R-dual with both coordinates negated. In the normalized $i=0$ hat slice, the $U^0$ terms are exactly the hat differential, while positive $U$ powers leave that slice in both original and dual complexes; transposing therefore gives the finite hat dual. The evaluation pairing identifies $H(C^\vee)$ with $H(C)^\vee$ and is nondegenerate; therefore no such lower filtration level maps nontrivially to total dual homology. This gives $\tau(C^\vee)\ge -t$, and hence $\tau(-K)=-\tau(K)$ in the normalized knot setting. [F1, F3, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 Choose a smooth embedded arc on $S$ joining its two boundary components. ## Statement

Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact smooth knot and let $b\in\mathbb R^3\setminus K$. The inclusion $\mathbb R^3\setminus K\hookrightarrow S^3\setminus K$ induces an isomorphism
$$\pi_1(\mathbb R^3\setminus K,b)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\pi_1(S^3\setminus K,b).$$

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy|Compact smooth knots in the standard three-sphere]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A compact knot $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ and a basepoint $b$ in its complement.

[F1] When a valid finite diagram code is supplied, the crossing-ball construction gives a path-connected knot complement. [[lem-wirtinger-crossing-ball-cover]]

[F2] The two-sphere is simply connected at every basepoint. [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]

[F3] A path-connected space is simply connected when its fundamental group is trivial. [[def-simply-connected]]

[F4] Van Kampen computes a path-connected open cover by a group pushout. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

[F5] If one open set and the overlap are simply connected, inclusion from the other set induces an isomorphism. [[cor-seifert-van-kampen-simply-connected-overlap]]

[F6] A pointed inclusion induces a homomorphism on fundamental groups. [[def-induced-homomorphism-on-fundamental-groups]]

[F7] Induced fundamental-group maps are functorial under composition. [[thm-induced-fundamental-group-map-functoriality]]

[F8] A path between basepoints induces the usual basepoint-change isomorphism. [[thm-fundamental-group-laws]]

## Proof

1.1 Since $K$ is compact, choose $R>0$ with $K$ and $b$ in the open ball $D=B_R(0)$. Put $U=S^3\setminus(K\cup\{\infty\})=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$ and $V=S^3\setminus\overline D$. Then $V$ is an open ball about infinity, disjoint from $K$, and $U\cap V=V\setminus\{\infty\}$. First verify that $U$ is path-connected without assuming a diagram code. Parameterize the smooth embedded circle by $k:S^1\to K$. For $p\in U$, the cone $$C_p=\{p+t(k(s)-p):s\in S^1,\ t\ge1\}$$ has three-dimensional outer volume zero: on each of finitely many smooth coordinate intervals of $S^1$ and each bounded interval $1\le t\le n$, the defining map is Lipschitz on a compact rectangle; subdividing into $O(N^2)$ squares of side $1/N$ covers its image by balls of radius $O(1/N)$, whose total three-dimensional volume is $O(1/N)$. Thus each truncated image has outer volume zero, and the countable union over $n$ does also. Given $p,q\in U$, choose $r$ in an open ball outside $C_p\cup C_q$, which is possible because that union has outer volume zero. If the segment $[p,r]$ met $K$ at $k(s)$, then $r=p+t(k(s)-p)$ for some $t\ge1$, contrary to $r\notin C_p$; similarly $[q,r]$ misses $K$. The broken line from $p$ to $r$ to $q$ lies in $U$. Under inversion $J(x)=x/\|x\|^2$, extended by $J(\infty)=0$, the set $V$ is the open ball of radius $1/R$ about $0$. The radial homotopy $y\mapsto(1-t)y$ contracts it to $0$, so it is nonempty and path-connected. Since this ball is convex, every based loop contracts to its own basepoint by the straight-line homotopy inside the ball; [F3] therefore makes $V$ simply connected. The same inversion identifies $U\cap V$ with $0<\|y\|<1/R$. ## Statement

Let $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a compact smooth knot and let $b\in\mathbb R^3\setminus K$. The inclusion $\mathbb R^3\setminus K\hookrightarrow S^3\setminus K$ induces an isomorphism
$$\pi_1(\mathbb R^3\setminus K,b)\xrightarrow{\ \cong\ }\pi_1(S^3\setminus K,b).$$

## Statement references

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy|Compact smooth knots in the standard three-sphere]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A compact knot $K\subset\mathbb R^3$ and a basepoint $b$ in its complement.

[F1] When a valid finite diagram code is supplied, the crossing-ball construction gives a path-connected knot complement. [[lem-wirtinger-crossing-ball-cover]]

[F2] The two-sphere is simply connected at every basepoint. [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]

[F3] A path-connected space is simply connected when its fundamental group is trivial. [[def-simply-connected]]

[F4] Van Kampen computes a path-connected open cover by a group pushout. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

[F5] If one open set and the overlap are simply connected, inclusion from the other set induces an isomorphism. [[cor-seifert-van-kampen-simply-connected-overlap]]

[F6] A pointed inclusion induces a homomorphism on fundamental groups. [[def-induced-homomorphism-on-fundamental-groups]]

[F7] Induced fundamental-group maps are functorial under composition. [[thm-induced-fundamental-group-map-functoriality]]

[F8] A path between basepoints induces the usual basepoint-change isomorphism. [[thm-fundamental-group-laws]]

## Proof

1.1 Since $K$ is compact, choose $R>0$ with $K$ and $b$ in the open ball $D=B_R(0)$. Put $U=S^3\setminus(K\cup\{\infty\})=\mathbb R^3\setminus K$ and $V=S^3\setminus\overline D$. Then $V$ is an open ball about infinity, disjoint from $K$, and $U\cap V=V\setminus\{\infty\}$. First verify that $U$ is path-connected without assuming a diagram code. Parameterize the smooth embedded circle by $k:S^1\to K$. For $p\in U$, the cone
$$C_p=\{p+t(k(s)-p):s\in S^1,\ t\ge1\}$$
has three-dimensional outer volume zero: on each of finitely many smooth coordinate intervals of $S^1$ and each bounded interval $1\le t\le n$, the defining map is Lipschitz on a compact rectangle; subdividing into $O(N^2)$ squares of side $1/N$ covers its image by balls of radius $O(1/N)$, whose total three-dimensional volume is $O(1/N)$. Thus each truncated image has outer volume zero, and the countable union over $n$ does also. Given $p,q\in U$, choose $r$ in an open ball outside $C_p\cup C_q$, which is possible because that union has outer volume zero. If the segment $[p,r]$ met $K$ at $k(s)$, then $r=p+t(k(s)-p)$ for some $t\ge1$, contrary to $r\notin C_p$; similarly $[q,r]$ misses $K$. The broken line from $p$ to $r$ to $q$ lies in $U$.
Under inversion $J(x)=x/\|x\|^2$, extended by $J(\infty)=0$, the set $V$ is the open ball of radius $1/R$ about $0$. The radial homotopy $y\mapsto(1-t)y$ contracts it to $0$, so it is nonempty and path-connected. Since this ball is convex, every based loop contracts to its own basepoint by the straight-line homotopy inside the ball; [F3] therefore makes $V$ simply connected. The same inversion identifies $U\cap V$ with $0<\|y\|<1/R$. Fix $\rho=1/(2R)$; the puncture-preserving radial homotopy
$$y\longmapsto\left((1-t)+t\frac{\rho}{\|y\|}\right)y$$
is a strong deformation retraction of this punctured ball onto the sphere $S^2_\rho$. The punctured ball is path-connected. For any basepoint $y$ in it, let $i:S^2_\rho\hookrightarrow U\cap V$ be inclusion and let $r$ be the radial retraction. Then $r_*i_*$ is the identity, while $i_*r_*$ is an isomorphism: the radial deformation from $\operatorname{id}$ to $i r$ has a basepoint track, and [F7, F8] identify its induced map with the corresponding basepoint-change isomorphism. Hence $r_*$ is an isomorphism. Scaling identifies $S^2_\rho$ with $S^2$, which is simply connected at every basepoint by [F2]; thus [F3] makes $U\cap V$ simply connected. [given, F2, F3, F7, F8, choose, construct]

2.1 Choose $b_0\in U\cap V$. The open sets $U,V$ cover $S^3\setminus K$; [F4] applies by the path-connectedness in step 1.1. Since $V$ and $U\cap V$ are simply connected by step 1.1, the special case [F5] shows that inclusion induces an isomorphism $\pi_1(U,b_0)\to\pi_1(S^3\setminus K,b_0)$. [F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 The inclusion induces the based map by [F6]. A path in $U$ from $b$ to $b_0$ exists by step 1.1 and gives basepoint-change isomorphisms by [F8]; functoriality [F7] makes the inclusion square commute. Thus the map at $b$ is also an isomorphism. [F6, F7, F8, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $D_+(T_{2,3},2)$ be the positive-clasped Whitehead double of the right-handed trefoil with two full twists in the clasp, using the twist convention of Hedden and Ording. The normalized knot Floer threshold and Rasmussen invariant satisfy
$$\tau(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=0,\qquad s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2.$$

## Statement references

[[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau|The normalized tau threshold]]

[[def-rasmussen-s-invariant|Rasmussen's s invariant and filtration convention]]

[Hedden and Ording, *The Ozsvath-Szabo and Rasmussen concordance invariants are not equal*, Theorem 1.1 and §§2.1–2.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0512348v1)

[Rasmussen, *Khovanov homology and the slice genus*, §§3–4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0402131v1)

[Hom, *A survey on Heegaard Floer homology and concordance*, §§3.1 and 5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1512.00383v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Countable Choice, the specified positive-clasped two-twisted Whitehead double, and the source's twist convention.

[A1] [[def-countable-choice]] is the axiom branch used by the knot invariant, the finite diagrams, and the smooth four-ball genus.

[F1] [[def-knot-floer-filtration-and-tau]] defines tau by the first Alexander filtration level mapping nontrivially to total hat homology.

[F2] [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]] defines $s$ from the filtration levels of the two Lee homology generators.

[L1] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] identifies the actual full grid rectangle complex with the analytic knot Floer complex, preserving the normalized Seifert Alexander and Maslov gradings and all positive marked degrees. Its all-variable-zero specialization is the full hat complex tensored with the stated bigraded basepoint factors.

[L2] [[thm-rasmussen-s-bounds-smooth-four-ball-genus]] states the smooth genus bound used in the source to choose the value $s=2$ from the Khovanov calculation's alternatives, for actual embedded smooth surfaces; the bound alone does not compute the finite Khovanov groups, whose calculation is now supplied by [F3].

[L3] [[lem-lee-cobordism-filtration-genus-bound]] is the exact Lee-cobordism input required by [L2]; its smooth surface is required to be properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$ with product collars.

[F3] [[lem-two-twisted-positive-whitehead-trefoil-double-has-s-two]] proves $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$ from the admitted code, its exact finite Khovanov matrices, the Lee spectral sequence and the actual embedded genus-one bound.

[F4] [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] supplies the normalized Maslov-zero same-oriented-knot conjugation with both filtrations exchanged, its inverse and homotopies, and the normalized full reverse-mirror duality. Its finite hat dual has filtration given by the annihilator of the complementary filtration; the total three-sphere hat class has Maslov degree zero.

## Proof

**Given:** Countable Choice and the positive-clasped double with the two-full-twist convention in the Statement. All grid differentials below retain positive $X$ multiplicity.

1.1 Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. These conditions verify the individual isotopies and the displayed endpoint. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and two-full-twist framing retained. The complete integer arrows and finite move list are recorded with the computation data below; neither a knot-table name nor a Floer rank identifies this knot. [given, construct, algebra]

2.1 The orientation junction preserves the normalized filtered invariant without an ambient invertibility assumption. For a doubly-pointed diagram of an oriented knot $J$, swapping only $w,z$ presents $J^r$. The actual disks are unchanged and their two marked degrees exchange, so $I:[x,i,j]\mapsto[x,j,i]$ is a Laurent-linear swap-filtered chain isomorphism to that diagram. The carried zero-Seifert cap gives $A'(x)=-A(x)$. The relative disk index then gives $M'(x)=M(x)-2A(x)+c$ for one integer $c$, so $I$ has constant full Maslov degree $c$. Compose it with the normalized same-oriented-knot conjugation of [F4], whose Maslov degree is zero and which swaps the two filtrations, including its inverse and homotopies. The composite is an ordinary bifiltered equivalence to $J^r$ of degree $c$. Its vertical hat quotient is an isomorphism between the two total three-sphere hat groups, each concentrated in normalized Maslov degree zero; hence $c=0$. This proves equality of the normalized inclusion thresholds for $J,J^r$. It also identifies their normalized bigraded knot Floer homologies. Apply this to the grid in step 1.1. Reflecting its columns, $O_r\mapsto11-O_r$ and $X_r\mapsto11-X_r$, gives a grid for its mirror: $(x,y,h)\mapsto(-x,y,h)$ reverses ambient orientation and keeps vertical strands over horizontal strands. No further knot-recognition premise is needed for this second grid. [F1, F4, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 Compute the full tilde differential of each of these two explicit grids. For a permutation state $p$, use $M_O(p)=I(p,p)-I(p,O)-I(O,p)+I(O,O)+1$ and $2A(p)=M_O(p)-M_X(p)-11$, with marks at half-integer cell centers and $I$ counting pairs strictly increasing in both coordinates. In the quotient $Q=C/F_0C$ retain exactly the states with $A>0$. Only Maslov degrees $-1,0,1$ enter $H_0(Q)$; discarding the outgoing differential from degree $-1$ does not change that group. The inventory is exhaustive by the following finite assignment recurrence. For used columns $S$ in the first $r=|S|$ rows, choosing $c\notin S$ increments the state-state term by $|\{b\in S:b<c\}|$. Add $-\#\{k\ge r:O_k\ge c\}-\#\{k<r:O_k<c\}$ to obtain the Maslov increment; the Alexander increment is the corresponding $X$ expression minus its $O$ expression. Accumulating the resulting two-variable polynomial over the $4096$ column subsets counts every permutation exactly once. For every retained state and ordered pair of distinct rows, take its southwest/northeast rectangle, reject a rectangle containing an interior state point or $O$, and retain every other rectangle, including those containing $X$. Its output transposes the two chosen columns; discard that output only when its Alexander value is at most zero. Summing modulo two gives the actual quotient matrix. The first grid has $45\,824$ retained states, $159\,685$ rectangle orbits, including $24\,181$ with positive $X$ multiplicity, and $158\,523$ nonzero matrix entries. The reflected grid has $6080$ retained states and $11\,474$ rectangle orbits and nonzero entries. Every term has Maslov drop one and Alexander drop exactly its $X$ multiplicity; actual matrix multiplication gives $d^2=0$ in both quotients. These are the literal rectangle counts of [L1], rather than a formal-domain enumeration. [L1, step 1.1, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 Exact column elimination over $\mathbb F_2$ gives $$\begin{array}{c|rrrrr}&\dim Q_1&\dim Q_0&\dim Q_{-1}&\operatorname{rank}d_1&\operatorname{rank}d_0\\\hline G&12347&17919&15558&8384&9535\\G^{\mathrm{mirror}}&4385&1463&232&1243&220.\end{array}$$ To specify the finite rank operation, encode a column by its row bits; repeatedly cancel its highest nonzero row with the previously retained pivot column at that row, or retain it as a new pivot if no such column exists. The counts of retained pivots are the displayed ranks. The saved complete columns and pivot-reduction traces give these computations directly. A separate exact verification used the complete joint assignment polynomial, checked every state and both normalized grid gradings, reconstructed every retained rectangle, checked $d^2$, and recomputed both ranks. Thus $$\dim H_0(Q_G)=17919-8384-9535=0,\qquad\dim H_0(Q_{G^{\mathrm{mirror}}})=1463-1243-220=0.$$ This uses the full filtered quotients, including the positive-$X$ terms in the first matrix. [L1, step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 Apply [L1]'s absolutely normalized filtered comparison and specialize all marking variables to zero. The full tilde complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the doubly-pointed full hat complex tensored with $V^{\otimes11}$, where the two degrees of $V$ are $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$. Its total Maslov-zero homology is consequently one-dimensional, represented by the normalized three-sphere generator tensored with the sole degree-zero vector of $V^{\otimes11}$. Its filtration threshold is exactly $\tau(J)$: inclusion into that tensor factor and projection onto it are filtered degree-zero chain maps, so they give both threshold inequalities. The exact sequence $0\to F_0C\to C\to Q\to0$ and step 4.1 show that this total Maslov-zero class comes from $H_0(F_0C)$ for each grid. Hence $\tau(J)\le0$ and $\tau(mJ)\le0$, for the actual knot $J$ of step 1.1 and its mirror. [F1, L1, step 2.1, step 4.1, algebra]

6.1 For completeness derive the required threshold sign from [F4]'s normalized reverse-mirror duality. Let $D$ be the finite normalized doubly-pointed full hat complex and write $t$ for its inclusion threshold. Its dual filtration is $F_sD^\vee=\{\lambda:\lambda(F_{-s-1}D)=0\}$. Choose a total generator cycle $z\in F_tD_0$. Then $z\notin\operatorname{im}(d:D_1\to D_0)+F_{t-1}D_0$: any such expression would give a homologous cycle at level $t-1$. Finite-dimensional linear algebra therefore gives a functional $\lambda$ vanishing on that sum and taking value one on $z$. It is a nonzero dual homology class at filtration $-t$. Conversely every functional at level $s<-t$ vanishes on $F_tD$, hence on $z$, and cannot represent the nonzero dual class. Thus the dual threshold is exactly $-t$. The absolute normalization and full duality in [F4], together with the orientation junction of step 2.1, give $\tau(mJ)=-\tau(J)$. Combining the two actual quotient inequalities of step 5.1 forces $\tau(J)=0$. By step 2.1 this is the normalized tau value of the actual two-twisted positive Whitehead trefoil in the Statement. [F1, F4, step 2.1, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

7.1 The admitted diagram and framing in step 1.1 are also those of [F3]. That accepted finite Lee computation gives $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$. Together with the independently established normalized value in step 6.1 this proves both numerical assertions of the Statement. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, step 6.1, algebra] ∎

## Computation data

The complete new geometric certificate is [the sixteen-crossing-to-twelve-grid admission](../research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-supervision-20261020/floer-weighted/d2-grid/admission-proof.md), with the integer arrows and all $986$ moves in that directory. The exact quotient inputs, state inventories, full positive-$X$ matrix columns and pivot traces are in [the direct D2 computation](../research/inverse-problems-knot-theory-all-109-2026-10-19-supervision-20261020/floer-whitehead/d2-grid-count/). The count is implemented by `count-high-quotient.cpp`; the separate complete verification is `verify-quotients.py`, with its successful output in `quotient-verification.json`. The formulas, finite enumeration and linear-algebra operations are specified in the proof; these files retain their full finite execution data.

[F2] [[def-rasmussen-s-invariant]] defines $s$ from the filtration levels of the two Lee homology generators.

[L1] [[thm-grid-homology-independent-of-grid-and-equals-knot-floer]] identifies the actual full grid rectangle complex with the analytic knot Floer complex, preserving the normalized Seifert Alexander and Maslov gradings and all positive marked degrees. Its all-variable-zero specialization is the full hat complex tensored with the stated bigraded basepoint factors.

[L2] [[thm-rasmussen-s-bounds-smooth-four-ball-genus]] states the smooth genus bound used in the source to choose the value $s=2$ from the Khovanov calculation's alternatives, for actual embedded smooth surfaces; the bound alone does not compute the finite Khovanov groups, whose calculation is now supplied by [F3].

[L3] [[lem-lee-cobordism-filtration-genus-bound]] is the exact Lee-cobordism input required by [L2]; its smooth surface is required to be properly embedded in $S^3\times[0,1]$ with product collars.

[F3] [[lem-two-twisted-positive-whitehead-trefoil-double-has-s-two]] proves $s(D_+(T_{2,3},2))=2$ from the admitted code, its exact finite Khovanov matrices, the Lee spectral sequence and the actual embedded genus-one bound.

[F4] [[lem-knot-floer-duality-and-filtration-swap]] supplies the normalized Maslov-zero same-oriented-knot conjugation with both filtrations exchanged, its inverse and homotopies, and the normalized full reverse-mirror duality. 1.1 Use the admitted cable/clasp diagram of [[lem-explicit-two-twisted-whitehead-double-has-sixteen-crossing-code]]. Its four-strand cable word is $\sigma_1^{-2}(\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_3\sigma_2)^3$, with the separate two-crossing clasp and the admitted wiring. The correction to blackboard framing is $-1$ full twist; the trefoil's blackboard framing is $+3$, giving exactly two full twists relative to the zero longitude. Here is a finite grid admission for this same diagram. Draw its sixteen crossing disks and joining orthogonal arrows, scale by $100$, and rotate the drawing by a quarter turn. At a horizontal overcrossing replace its overarc by the ordered vertices $(-10,0),(2,0),(2,4),(10,4),(10,0)$ and its underarc by $(0,-10),(4,-10),(4,2),(0,2),(0,10)$, reversing either order to retain its directed strand. The sole crossing is now $(2,2)$ with the same signed boundary ports. The six required replacements have disjoint supports. Delete straight subdivisions, separate coincident levels by perturbations smaller than $1/100$, and rank the levels. This gives a $33$-grid with exactly the sixteen original signed crossings. Its saved $986$ exchanges, cyclic cuts and three-corner destabilizations give the following $12$-grid, with zero-based rows: $$O=(4,9,6,1,2,11,0,8,5,3,7,10),\qquad X=(8,2,0,7,10,4,5,3,1,9,11,6).$$ Each exchange has nonalternating endpoint intervals or the permitted shared endpoint; each destabilization has three alternating marks in adjacent rows and columns. The directed word is the negative reverse of the input traversal: the negative is the orientation-preserving change of viewing direction $(x,y,h)\mapsto(x,-y,-h)$, while the reverse records the independently chosen component orientation. Thus the actual grid is for the reverse of the oriented knot in the Statement, with its positive clasp and two-full-twist framing retained. The complete integer arrows and finite move list are recorded with the computation data below; neither a knot-table name nor a Floer rank identifies this knot. [given, construct, algebra]

1.2 The orientation junction preserves the normalized filtered invariant without an ambient invertibility assumption. For a doubly-pointed diagram of an oriented knot $J$, swapping only $w,z$ presents $J^r$. The actual disks are unchanged and their two marked degrees exchange, so $I:[x,i,j]\mapsto[x,j,i]$ is a Laurent-linear swap-filtered chain isomorphism to that diagram. The carried zero-Seifert cap gives $A'(x)=-A(x)$. The relative disk index then gives $M'(x)=M(x)-2A(x)+c$ for one integer $c$, so $I$ has constant full Maslov degree $c$. The composite is an ordinary bifiltered equivalence to $J^r$ of degree $c$. Its vertical hat quotient is an isomorphism between the two total three-sphere hat groups, each concentrated in normalized Maslov degree zero; hence $c=0$. This proves equality of the normalized inclusion thresholds for $J,J^r$. It also identifies their normalized bigraded knot Floer homologies. Apply this to the grid in step 1.1. The reflected grid has $6080$ retained states and $11\,474$ rectangle orbits and nonzero entries. Thus $$\dim H_0(Q_G)=17919-8384-9535=0,\qquad\dim H_0(Q_{G^{\mathrm{mirror}}})=1463-1243-220=0.$$ This uses the full filtered quotients, including the positive-$X$ terms in the first matrix. 2.3 Apply [L1]'s absolutely normalized filtered comparison and specialize all marking variables to zero. The full tilde complex is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to the doubly-pointed full hat complex tensored with $V^{\otimes11}$, where the two degrees of $V$ are $(M,A)=(0,0),(-1,-1)$. Its total Maslov-zero homology is consequently one-dimensional, represented by the normalized three-sphere generator tensored with the sole degree-zero vector of $V^{\otimes11}$. Its filtration threshold is exactly $\tau(J)$: inclusion into that tensor factor and projection onto it are filtered degree-zero chain maps, so they give both threshold inequalities. ## Statement

Assume countable choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K$ in $S^3$, there are an oriented normal-bundle trivialization, a tubular map $\Phi$ defined on an open neighbourhood containing $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}$ for some $\epsilon>0$, and a closed tubular neighbourhood $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. This $N(K)$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times D^2$, its boundary $T_K$ is diffeomorphic to $S^1\times S^1$, and its exterior $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is a compact smooth oriented three-manifold with boundary $T_K$. The open complement $S^3\setminus K$ strongly deformation retracts onto $E_K$.

## Statement references

[Cattabriga and Francaviglia, §4.1](https://poisson.phc.dm.unipi.it/~camponovo/libri/knot.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice and a smooth oriented embedding $K:S^1\to S^3$.

[A1] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]] defines a smooth oriented knot as a smooth embedding of an oriented circle in the standard oriented $S^3$; its image is a smoothly embedded circle.

[F2] [[def-knot-exterior]] defines $E_K$ using a closed disk subbundle determined by a chosen smooth fibre norm, and orients it from $S^3$.

[F3] [[lem-knot-normal-circle-bundle-trivialization]] gives a smooth oriented trivialization of the rank-two normal bundle of $K$.

[F4] [[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]] states that under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ a closed smooth embedded submanifold has an open normal-bundle neighbourhood diffeomorphic to an open neighbourhood in the ambient manifold, by a map fixing the zero section. A tubular neighbourhood has this meaning by [[def-tubular-neighbourhood-of-an-embedded-submanifold]].

## Proof

**Proof technique:** direct.

1.1 By [F1], $K$ is continuous and $K(S^1)$ is compact because $S^1$ is compact. Since $S^3$ is Hausdorff, $K(S^1)$ is closed; [F1] also identifies it as a smooth embedded submanifold. Thus the closed smooth embedded hypothesis of [F4] holds, and [A1] permits its application. Take a tubular map $\Phi:\Omega\to U\subset S^3$ defined on an open neighbourhood of the zero section of $\nu(K)$. [A1, F1, F4, given, construct]

2.1 Use the trivialization [F3] and its product Euclidean norm as the chosen smooth fibre norm in [F2], so $\Omega$ is open in $S^1\times\mathbb R^2$. For each $s\in S^1$, openness gives an arc $I_s$ about $s$ and a radius $r_s>0$ with $I_s\times D^2_{r_s}\subset\Omega$. Compactness of $S^1$ gives a finite subcover by such arcs; taking $\epsilon$ smaller than half the least of their radii yields $S^1\times D^2_{2\epsilon}\subset\Omega$. The closed disk subbundle $S^1\times D^2_\epsilon$ therefore lies in $\Omega$. [A1, F2, F3, step 1.1, choose, construct]

3.1 Put $N(K)=\Phi(S^1\times D^2_\epsilon)$. The restricted map is a smooth embedding, so $N(K)$ is a compact embedded solid torus with boundary $T_K=\Phi(S^1\times\partial D^2_\epsilon)\cong S^1\times S^1$. Since $S^3$ is compact and $E_K=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ is closed, $E_K$ is compact. The annulus $S^1\times\{z:\epsilon/2<|z|<2\epsilon\}$ maps to a collar of $T_K$; in these coordinates $E_K$ is the side $|z|\ge\epsilon$. Thus $E_K$ is a smooth three-manifold with boundary exactly $T_K$, oriented by restriction of the orientation of $S^3$ as in [F2]. [F2, F3, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

4.1 On $S^3\setminus K$, define $H_t$ to be the identity outside $N(K)$ and, in the punctured disk fibres with $0<|z|\le\epsilon$, set $H_t(\Phi(s,z))=\Phi(s,((1-t)|z|+t\epsilon)z/|z|)$ for $0\le t\le1$. The formula is continuous for $z\ne0$ and is the identity at $|z|=\epsilon$, so it glues continuously to the identity outside $N(K)$. It fixes every point of $E_K$, stays in $S^3\setminus K$, and at $t=1$ sends every point of the punctured tube to $T_K\subset E_K$. Hence $H_t$ is a strong deformation retraction of $S^3\setminus K$ onto $E_K$. [F2, step 1.1, step 3.1, construct, algebra] ∎

kind: lemma
title: Tangential KZ regularization and the hump normalization
status: draft
origin: pipeline

deps:

sources:

      url: https://www.math.cinvestav.mx/~mostovoy/cdbook/cdbook-as-submitted.pdf
    - title: The Universal Vassiliev–Kontsevich Invariant for Framed Oriented Links, §4
      url: https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/UN_PAPER.pdf
    - title: The Fundamental Theorem of Vassiliev Invariants, §2.5.4
      url: https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9702009v1
---

## Statement

For each finite degree cutoff $N$, every parenthesized endpoint cluster of the KZ connection has a unique coefficientwise tangentially regularized transport, obtained by removing its local residue factor. For three strands, fix the normalized positions $(0,z,1)$ and put $a=t_{12}/(2\pi i)$ and $b=t_{23}/(2\pi i)$. The equation $G'(z)=\left(\frac{a}{z}+\frac{b}{z-1}\right)G(z)$ has unique solutions $G_0,G_1$ with $G_0(z)=f(z)z^a$, $G_1(z)=g(1-z)(1-z)^b$, where $f$ and $g$ are analytic near $0$ and $f(0)=g(0)=1$. Their ratio $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}:=G_1(z)^{-1}G_0(z)$ is independent of $z$ and equals the regularized limit $\Phi_{\mathrm{KZ}}=\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\varepsilon^{-b}G_\varepsilon(1-\varepsilon)\varepsilon^a,\qquad G_\varepsilon(\varepsilon)=1$.
If $K^+$ is obtained from a strict Morse knot presentation $K$ by inserting one copy of the fixed standard hump $H$, model the local birth by cutting the knot to a one-in one-out tangle $T_K$, composing with the standard one-in one-out hump tangle whose closure is $H$, and closing the composite. Then $Z(K^+)=Z(H)Z(K)$, $r(K^+)=r(K)+1$, and hence $I(K^+)=I(K)$. The inverse in $I(K)$ exists degreewise because the degree-zero coefficient of $Z(H)$ is $1$. The associator identities and independence under arbitrary changes of parenthesization are separate claims.

## Statement references

[[def-kontsevich-integral-on-parenthesized-braids|KZ connection, tangential endpoint convention, and fixed hump normalization]]

[Chmutov, Duzhin, and Mostovoy, §§8.4, 8.6–8.7, and 10.1.5–10.1.7, printed pp. 228–240 and 273–277](https://www.math.cinvestav.mx/~mostovoy/cdbook/cdbook-as-submitted.pdf)

[Le and Murakami, §4, PDF pp. 6–7](https://letu.math.gatech.edu/Papers/UN_PAPER.pdf)

[Bar-Natan and Stoimenow, §2.5.4, PDF pp. 15–16](https://arxiv.org/pdf/q-alg/9702009v1)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The completed strand algebra, the KZ form, the compactified level cells, the fixed standard hump $H$, and a finite degree cutoff $N$.

[F1] [[def-kontsevich-integral-on-parenthesized-braids]]: the KZ form is $\Omega_q=(2\pi i)^{-1}\sum_{i<j}t_{ij}\,d\log(z_i-z_j)$; parenthesizations specify nested tangential collision directions; $Z(K)$ is the degreewise improper configuration integral in the unframed 4T+1T quotient; $I(K)=Z(K)Z(H)^{-r(K)}$.

[F2] [[lem-kontsevich-configuration-space-compactification-faces]]: each nested collision has a nonnegative radial coordinate and a smooth limiting direction; branch evaluations extend smoothly to its resolved face.

[F3] [[lem-kontsevich-long-knot-closure-and-connected-sum]]: closing the standard one-in one-out hump tangle gives $H$, and closure of a vertical composite multiplies the closed series by connected sum.

## Proof

**Given:** As above. Work first in the finite-dimensional quotient through degree $N$; all limits and products below are coefficientwise. No choice axiom is used.

1.1 For a three-strand configuration, translation and positive scaling put the three points at $0,z,1$. The $t_{13}$ term of $\Omega_3$ is constant in these coordinates, while $d\log(z_1-z_2)=d\log z$ and $d\log(z_2-z_3)=d\log(z-1)$. Thus the reduced equation is exactly the displayed equation with residues $a$ at $0$ and $b$ at $1$. [given, F1, algebra]
