## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $I^*$ be the binary icosahedral group, the group of $120$ unit quaternions acting on the unit sphere $S^3$ by left multiplication, and put $P=S^3/I^*$. The quotient is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with universal cover $S^3$ and deck group $I^*$. Then $H_*(P;\mathbb Z)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Z)$ and $\pi_1(P)\cong I^*$ is nontrivial.

## Statement references

[Algebraic Topology, Winter Semester 2021/22, §4.5.12](https://loeh.app.ur.de/teaching/topologie1_ws2122/lecture_notes.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, the binary icosahedral group presentation $I^*=\langle s,t\mid (st)^2=s^3=t^5\rangle$ of order $120$, its free orientation-preserving action on $S^3$, and the quotient $P=S^3/I^*$.

[A1] [[def-axiom-of-choice]]: every family of nonempty sets has a choice function. The local Poincaré-duality supplier below assumes this axiom.

[F1] [[thm-higher-dimensional-spheres-are-simply-connected]]: $S^3$ is simply connected.

[F2] [[def-universal-covering-space]]: a universal cover is a covering map with simply connected total space.

[F3] [[thm-deck-group-of-a-universal-cover-is-the-fundamental-group]]: for a universal cover, its deck group is isomorphic to the fundamental group of its path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected base.

[F4] [[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]: for a path-connected space, $H_1(-;\mathbb Z)$ is the abelianization of $\pi_1$.

[F5] [[thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds]]: under AC, compact oriented boundaryless $P$ has cap-duality isomorphisms $H_i(P;\mathbb Z)\cong H^{3-i}(P;\mathbb Z)$ in every degree.

[F6] [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]: under AC, the free integral singular chain complex of $P$ gives $0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1(H_0(P),\mathbb Z)\to H^1(P;\mathbb Z)\to\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(P),\mathbb Z)\to0$.

## Proof

1.1 The free action makes $S^3\to P$ a covering; since $S^3$ is simply connected by [F1], it is universal by [F2]. Its deck group is $I^*$, so [F3] gives $\pi_1(P)\cong I^*$. Since $|I^*|=120$, this fundamental group is nontrivial. [given, F1, F2, F3]

1.2 In the abelianization, write the images of $s,t$ additively. The relation $(st)^2=s^3=t^5$ gives $2s+2t=3s=5t$. The first equality yields $s=2t$; substituting into $3s=5t$ gives $6t=5t$, hence $t=0$ and $s=0$. Thus $(I^*)^{\mathrm{ab}}=0$, and [F4] gives $H_1(P;\mathbb Z)=0$. [given, F4, algebra]

2.1 The quotient is connected, compact, and oriented, so $H_0(P;\mathbb Z)=H^0(P;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$. By [F6], $H^1(P;\mathbb Z)$ is an extension of $\operatorname{Hom}(0,\mathbb Z)=0$ by $\operatorname{Ext}^1(\mathbb Z,\mathbb Z)=0$, so $H^1(P;\mathbb Z)=0$. The AC assumption is the one in [A1], needed for [F6]. [given, A1, F6, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 By [F5] and step 2.1, $H_2(P;\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_3(P;\mathbb Z)\cong H^0(P;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$. For $i>3$, [F5] identifies $H_i(P;\mathbb Z)$ with negative-degree cohomology, which is zero. Together with steps 1.2 and 2.1, this is exactly the integral homology of $S^3$. Step 1.1 shows that $P$ is not simply connected, so it is not $S^3$. The use of [F5] requires [A1]. [A1, F5, given, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $B$ be a smooth compact four-manifold with $H_*(B;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(\mathrm{point};\mathbb Q)$ and oriented boundary the rational homology sphere $Y$, where $H_*(Y;\mathbb Q)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Q)$. Let $\mathfrak t$ be a boundary Spin$^c$ structure extending over $B$. Removing an open four-ball from the interior gives a Spin$^c$ cobordism $W$ with boundary $-S^3\sqcup Y$, and each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism on rational homology. In both orientations, the induced Heegaard Floer infinity map is an isomorphism of degree zero and the corresponding plus-map inequality gives $d(Y,\mathfrak t)\ge0$ and $d(Y,\mathfrak t)\le0$.

## Statement references

[[def-heegaard-floer-plus-infinity-absolute-grading|The cobordism degree convention]]

[[lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance|The generic Heegaard Floer package needed for correction terms]]

[Ozsvath and Szabo, *Absolutely Graded Floer Homologies and Intersection Forms for Four-Manifolds with Boundary*, Theorem 9.6 and Proposition 9.9](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0110170v1)

[Baranowski, Borodzik, and Serrano de Rodrigo, *Heegaard Floer Homologies and Rational Cuspidal Curves*, Section 4](https://www.numdam.org/item/10.5802/wbln.12.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[lem-punctured-rational-homology-balls-are-rational-cobordisms]] gives the two rational homology inclusion isomorphisms, the boundary orientations, $\chi(W)=0$ and the zero rational intersection module.

[F2] [[lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps]] and [[lem-rational-heegaard-floer-infinity-standardness-and-rational-cobordism-isomorphism]] construct, for each fixed extending Spin$^c$ structure, the compatible infinity and plus maps and prove the degree-zero infinity isomorphism.

[F3] [[lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance]] supplies the grading-preserving tower and its bottom degree, with $d(S^3)=0$; [[lem-commuting-laurent-and-plus-maps-give-bottom-degree-inequalities]] supplies the bottom-degree comparison for the commuting square.

## Proof

**Given:** The stated rational homology ball, its oriented boundary, and an extending Spin$^c$ structure; let $W$ be obtained by removing an interior open ball.

1.1 The two boundary inclusions are rational homology isomorphisms and $H^2(W;\mathbb Q)=0$. In particular the square of the Chern class is zero, and $\chi(W)=\sigma(W)=0$. The same assertions hold for the reverse cobordism from $Y$ to $S^3$. For each of the fixed induced Spin$^c$ structures, the constructed infinity map is an isomorphism with degree $(0-2\cdot0-3\cdot0)/4=0$, and the corresponding plus map commutes with the infinity-to-plus projection. This uses the individual fixed-structure conclusion, including torsion extensions. [F1, F2]

2.1 Apply the supplied commuting-square comparison first to $W:S^3\to Y$ and then to its reverse $Y\to S^3$. The degree-zero isomorphisms give respectively $d(Y,\mathfrak t)\ge d(S^3)=0$ and $d(S^3)=0\ge d(Y,\mathfrak t)$. These are exactly the two stated inequalities in both orientations. [F3, step 1.1] ∎

## Statement

Let $H$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$ and let $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form. Write $H_{\mathbb Q}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and extend $V$ $\mathbb Q$-bilinearly to $H_{\mathbb Q}$. If $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace of dimension $g$ and $V(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in L$, then $M=H\cap L$ is a rank-$g$ direct summand of $H$ and $V|_{M\times M}=0$.

## Statement references

[[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance|A metabolizer is a primitive rank-half direct summand on which the integral Seifert pairing vanishes]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite-rank free abelian group $H$, an integral bilinear form $V$, and a $g$-dimensional rational isotropic subspace $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$, where $\operatorname{rank}H=2g$.

[A1] The displayed hypotheses are the complete input; no choice axiom is used.

## Proof

1.1 Choose a $\mathbb Q$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_g$ of $L$. Clearing the finitely many denominators in the coordinates of each $v_i$ gives nonzero integer multiples $x_i\in H\cap L$. The $x_i$ remain $\mathbb Q$-linearly independent, so $M=H\cap L$ has rank at least $g$; it has rank at most $\dim_{\mathbb Q}L=g$. Hence $\operatorname{rank}M=g$. [given, A1, choose, algebra]

2.1 If $n\ne0$, $x\in H$, and $nx\in M$, then $nx\in L$ and therefore $x=n^{-1}(nx)\in L$ because $L$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace. Thus $x\in M$, so $M$ is saturated in $H$. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 We prove by induction on $r$ that every saturated subgroup $P\subset\mathbb Z^r$ is a direct summand. The cases $P=0$ and $P=\mathbb Z^r$ are immediate. Otherwise choose a nonzero $p\in P$, divide its coordinates by their greatest common divisor, and use saturation to see that the resulting primitive vector $e_1$ still lies in $P$. The Euclidean algorithm gives a unimodular change of basis carrying $e_1$ to the first standard basis vector, so write $\mathbb Z^r=\mathbb Ze_1\oplus H'$. Every $p'\in P$ has a unique form $ae_1+h'$ with $h'\in H'$, and $h'=p'-ae_1\in P\cap H'$. Therefore $P=\mathbb Ze_1\oplus(P\cap H')$. The subgroup $P\cap H'$ is saturated in $H'$; its rank is $\operatorname{rank}P-1$, since the projection of $P$ to $\mathbb Ze_1$ is onto. ## Statement

Let $H$ be a free abelian group of rank $2g$ and let $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ be a bilinear form. Write $H_{\mathbb Q}=H\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathbb Q$ and extend $V$ $\mathbb Q$-bilinearly to $H_{\mathbb Q}$. If $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace of dimension $g$ and $V(x,y)=0$ for all $x,y\in L$, then $M=H\cap L$ is a rank-$g$ direct summand of $H$ and $V|_{M\times M}=0$.

## Statement references

[[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance|A metabolizer is a primitive rank-half direct summand on which the integral Seifert pairing vanishes]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A finite-rank free abelian group $H$, an integral bilinear form $V$, and a $g$-dimensional rational isotropic subspace $L\subset H_{\mathbb Q}$, where $\operatorname{rank}H=2g$.

[A1] The displayed hypotheses are the complete input; no choice axiom is used.

## Proof

1.1 Choose a $\mathbb Q$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_g$ of $L$. Clearing the finitely many denominators in the coordinates of each $v_i$ gives nonzero integer multiples $x_i\in H\cap L$. The $x_i$ remain $\mathbb Q$-linearly independent, so $M=H\cap L$ has rank at least $g$; it has rank at most $\dim_{\mathbb Q}L=g$. Hence $\operatorname{rank}M=g$. [given, A1, choose, algebra]

1.2 If $n\ne0$, $x\in H$, and $nx\in M$, then $nx\in L$ and therefore $x=n^{-1}(nx)\in L$ because $L$ is a $\mathbb Q$-subspace. Thus $x\in M$, so $M$ is saturated in $H$. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $D$ be a finite regular oriented diagram of a
nonempty labeled smooth link $L\subset\mathbb R^3$, and assume every component
has at least one underpassing point. Then $L$ is ambient isotopic through links
with the same projection and crossing data to a smooth height realization
$$\widehat L=\{(\gamma_i(s),\widehat\eta_i(s)):s\in S^1,\ 1\le i\le r\} \subset\mathbb R^2\times[-1,0]$$
such that $\widehat\eta_i(s)=-1$ exactly at the underpassing parameters on
component $i$ and $\widehat\eta_i(s)>-1$ at every other parameter.

## Statement references

[[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram|Regular oriented link diagrams and crossing data]]

[[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy|Ambient isotopy extension for compact embedded submanifolds]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice, a finite regular oriented diagram, its smooth embedded realization, and at least one underpassing parameter on each component.

[A1] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is [[def-countable-choice]].

[F1] A regular oriented diagram has a fixed planar projection which is an immersion with finitely many transverse double points and records which branch is over at each point. [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]]

[F2] A smooth isotopy of a compact embedded link in a boundaryless smooth $3$-manifold extends to an ambient isotopy under countable choice. [[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-countable-choice]]

## Proof

**Given:** The diagram, its initial height functions, and [A1].

1.1 Parameterize component $i$ by $S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, and let $U_i=\{u_{i,1},\ldots,u_{i,m_i}\}$ be its nonempty finite set of underpassing parameters. Define $$p_i(s)=\prod_{a=1}^{m_i}\bigl(1-\cos(2\pi(s-u_{i,a}))\bigr).$$ Every factor is smooth and nonnegative, and it vanishes exactly when $s=u_{i,a}$ in $S^1$. Thus $p_i$ is smooth, vanishes exactly on $U_i$, and is positive somewhere because a finite subset does not exhaust $S^1$. Its maximum $P_i$ is positive by compactness. Set $\widehat\eta_i(s)=-1+p_i(s)/P_i$. Then $-1\le\widehat\eta_i\le0$, equality at $-1$ holds exactly on $U_i$, and all other heights are greater than $-1$. [A1, F1, given, construct, construct]

2.1 At every projected double point, the overpassing parameter is not an underpassing parameter: regularity excludes triple points, so the two source parameters at that double point have distinct over/under roles. Hence the new height difference between the over and under branches is strictly positive. Let $\eta_i$ be the original height function and choose a smooth $\varphi:[0,1]\to[0,1]$ equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. The family $$F_t(i,s)=\bigl(\gamma_i(s),(1-\varphi(t))\eta_i(s)+\varphi(t)\widehat\eta_i(s)\bigr)$$ is smooth and stationary near both endpoints. At each crossing its over-minus- under height is a convex combination of two positive numbers, so it remains positive. Since [F1] lists all projected multiple points, each $F_t$ is injective; its projection remains an immersion, so each compact-source map is a smooth embedding. [A1, F1, given, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The track of the isotopy in step 2.1 is compact, so choose an open ball containing it and apply [F2] with that ball as the support neighborhood. The resulting ambient isotopy of $\mathbb R^3$ has compact support and therefore extends by the identity at $\infty$ to an ambient isotopy of $S^3$. It carries the original link to $\widehat L$ and fixes the planar projection and over/under data throughout, because every slice of $F$ has those same data. This proves the stated normalized realization. [A1, F2, step 2.1, choose, construct] ∎

## Statement

For the fixed root parameter, the normalized double-handlebody pairing on the admissible spine states of a marked handlebody is nondegenerate after quotienting by its radical. The inverse pairing defines the sewing map for gluing along a closed marked surface, and these maps satisfy the stated weighted Lagrangian anomaly correction.

## Statement references

[[def-skein-tqft-state-space-and-handlebody-pairing|State-space pairing]]

[[lem-root-handlebody-spine-state-space-finite-generation|Finite spine spanning set]]

[[def-extended-skein-cobordism-anomaly-data|Weighted Lagrangian anomaly convention]]

[Blanchet, Habegger, Masbaum, and Vogel, *Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket*, §§1 and 4–5](https://webhomes.maths.ed.ac.uk/~v1ranick/papers/bhmv.pdf)

[Kauffman and Lins, *Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds*, Chapters 6–7](https://api.pageplace.de/preview/DT0400.9781400882533_A27764847/preview-9781400882533_A27764847.pdf)

[Pohorence, *3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs*, §3](https://categorified.net/RTinvariants/Jan29-Feb3.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The finite spanning set of admissible spine states and the normalized gluing pairing.

[F1] [[def-skein-tqft-state-space-and-handlebody-pairing]] defines the radical quotient and pairing.

[F2] [[lem-root-handlebody-spine-state-space-finite-generation]] supplies the finite admissible spine spanning set via its explicitly labelled external BHMV input.

[F3] [[def-extended-skein-cobordism-anomaly-data]] fixes the weight and Maslov convention.

[F4] **External input — perfect pairing and sewing.** BHMV, Theorem1.4 p.887, property(F) on p.886, Proposition1.9 p.891, and Theorem4.11 p.909: in this even-root theory the radical quotient is finite free with unimodular dual pairing, the admissible spine states form a basis with unit diagonal norms in the double pairing, and the universal gluing maps satisfy the TQFT axioms. Proposition1.9 permits the complementary handlebody giving $S^3$, rather than assuming the self-double and $S^3$ pairings have the same matrix. Their normalization is the $Z_p$ normalization explicitly fixed in [F1]. Only perfectness/basis/sewing at this actual convention is imported.

[F5] **External input — actual weighted variant.** Gilmer–Masbaum, arXiv:0912.4706v3, §2 equation(1) pp.4–6 and §11 pp.23–25, states the colored TQFT with Lagrangians and integer weights and one-weight multiplier $\nu=\kappa^3$ in BHMV notation. The finite sign comparison $\mu_{GM}=-\mu_{Wall}$ is as recorded in the Kirby lemma, so its composition is exactly that of [F3]. The source states rational Lagrangians. For the real Lagrangians of [F3], take the rational handlebody-kernel reference on each marked surface and transport by the weight-zero identity cylinder to its specified real Lagrangian; the reverse cylinder is its inverse because $\mu(L,L',L)=0$. Conjugating morphisms by these cylinders is a functor to the rational-reference category, with the integer weights computed by [F3], so the imported functor extends to these real objects. This is a finite categorical transport, not an assumption that every real Lagrangian is rational.

## Proof

**Given:** A marked handlebody spine, its admissible colorings, and the gluing pairing.

1.1 On a fixed finite spine, each admissible coloring gives a finite colored graph state. Gluing a pair of handlebodies evaluates the resulting closed colored graph using the specified root bracket and anomaly normalization. [F1, F2, F3, given]

2.1 By [F4], the radical quotients for the two orientations are finite-dimensional dual spaces and their normalized pairing is perfect. This is stronger than left nondegeneracy by the definition of a radical alone. Choose bases $v_i,w_j$ and let $B_{ij}$ be their pairing matrix. Its inverse gives the coevaluation tensor $\sum_{i,j}(B^{-1})_{ji}v_i\otimes w_j$; contraction with $B$ on either side is the identity. This finite linear-algebra identity is exactly the sewing contraction in the imported gluing theorem and is independent of the chosen dual bases. [F1, F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The imported weighted gluing in [F5] gives the prescribed anomaly factor, with weight law [F3]. Its parameter is the cube of the selected sixth root, not an independently chosen square root with an unchecked sign. The real-Lagrangian transport in [F5] respects composition because the intervening reference cylinders cancel. Thus the inverse-pairing sewing maps satisfy precisely the registered weighted law. No unweighted anomaly cancellation or positivity of every complex-root Hermitian form is asserted. [F3, F4, F5, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Fix even $p\ge4$, a primitive $2p$-th root $A$, the BHMV semisimplified category, and its quantum dimensions $d_j$ and twists $\theta_j$ for $0\le j\le r-2$. Put $\Omega_p=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_jp_j$, $\Delta_+=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j$, and $\Delta_-=\sum_jd_j^2\theta_j^{-1}$. The Statement asserts that both $\Delta_+$ and $\Delta_-$ are nonzero. For a finite integral framed link $L$ in the oriented three-sphere, color each surgery component by $\Omega_p$ and normalize the bracket evaluation by $\Delta_+^{b_+(L)}\Delta_-^{b_-(L)}$, where $b_\pm(L)$ are the positive and negative indices of the framing matrix. With the stated BHMV root and weighted anomaly convention, the resulting value is unchanged under framed isotopy, handle slides, and addition or deletion of a split $\pm1$-framed unknot.

## Statement references

[[def-sl-two-root-of-unity-skein-parameter|Root, coefficient, and loop conventions]]

[[def-semisimplified-temperley-lieb-fusion-category|Simple projectors and category convention]]

[[lem-root-fusion-rules-and-simple-object-completeness|Fusion dimensions and twists]]

[[def-extended-skein-cobordism-anomaly-data|Weighted anomaly normalization]]

[Blanchet, Habegger, Masbaum, and Vogel, *Three-Manifold Invariants Derived from the Kauffman Bracket*, §§2–4](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/004093839290002Y)

[Kauffman and Lins, *Temperley-Lieb Recoupling Theory and Invariants of 3-Manifolds*, Chapters 8 and 12](https://www.jstor.org/stable/j.ctt1bgzb7v)

[Pohorence, *3-manifold Invariants and TQFTs*, §3.1](https://categorified.net/RTinvariants/Jan29-Feb3.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The root parameter, the semisimplified category, its simple projectors, quantum dimensions, twist, and a finite integral framed surgery link.

[F1] [[def-sl-two-root-of-unity-skein-parameter]] fixes $p$, $A$, $r$, $\delta$, and $\mathbb C$.

[F2] [[def-semisimplified-temperley-lieb-fusion-category]] defines the quotient and the root-specific projectors.

[F3] [[lem-root-fusion-rules-and-simple-object-completeness]] supplies the resolved finite simple list, dimensions, twists and invertible Hopf-link matrix in the registered root/pivotal convention. Its accepted interface is reused, not its body.

[F4] [[def-extended-skein-cobordism-anomaly-data]] fixes the weighted Lagrangian composition and the selected sixth root $\kappa$.

[F5] **External input — actual BHMV Kirby color and Gauss units.** BHMV, *Topological Quantum Field Theories Derived from the Kauffman Bracket*, Topology34(1995), §2 p.897, the displayed definition of $\theta_p$ and equations(*)–(**), together with §5.8 p.913: for the primitive $2p$-th root and even $p=2r$, the Kirby element is $\Omega_p=\sum_{j=0}^{r-2}d_jp_j$ and
$$\Delta_\varepsilon=\eta^{-1}\kappa^{3\varepsilon}\quad(\varepsilon=\pm1),\qquad \eta\in\mathbb C^\times.$$
Here $\kappa$ is the selected BHMV SIXTH root from [F4], not the square-root weight parameter used by some later sources. The source's usual signed quantum dimensions are exactly $d_j=[j+1]$ for the registered negative-loop recurrence. Its recalled invariant $\theta_p(S^3(L))=\langle L(\Omega_p)\rangle/(\Delta_+^{b_+}\Delta_-^{b_-})$ includes the actual Kirby handle-slide identity. This established identity is imported, not claimed as a new local recoupling proof.

A split signed-unit unknot multiplies the numerator by $\Delta_\varepsilon$ and increases exactly the corresponding index by one. The denominator therefore cancels that factor. Deletion is the inverse operation. This proves the displayed surgery invariance with the exact normalization of the Statement. [F1, F2, F3, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 The weighted interpretation is [F6]: the signature unit is $\nu=\kappa^3$, with the source's Maslov sign converted to the registered Wall order. The distinct additional $\eta^{b_0+b_1}$ normalization is retained when these closed values enter the TQFT pairing; no anomaly-free ordinary-oriented functor follows. The finite color and cancellation calculations add no choice assumption. [F4, F5, F6, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let P⊂S¹×D² be a smooth oriented pattern. If oriented knots K₀ and K₁ are concordant in one of the four categories C_sm, C_top, C_ex or C^{1/n}, then P(K₀) and P(K₁) are concordant in the same category. Thus P induces a well-defined set map on each of these concordance sets.

## Statement references

[CDR, §2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.5058v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A pattern P and a concordance annulus A from K₀ to K₁ in one of the stated ambient categories.

[F1] Satellite insertion uses a zero-framed tubular copy of S¹×D² around each endpoint knot ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

[F2] Each category specifies the ambient 4-manifold and regularity of its concordance annulus ([[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]).

[F3] **External TOP input (not reconstructed here).** A locally flat proper surface in a topological four-manifold has an actual rank-two normal VECTOR-bundle neighborhood; where such a neighborhood is prescribed near a closed subset, including the boundary collars, it can be chosen to agree with that germ on a smaller neighborhood. This is Freedman–Quinn Theorem9.3A, printed137–141, used under the run-specific external-source boundary. It supplies the actual tube, not automatic agreement of arbitrary global framings. The cited statement and proof pages137–141 were read; no full-book reading or local reconstruction is claimed.

[F4] Every ambient concordance manifold here is oriented and is an $R$-homology $S^3\times I$, with $R=\mathbb Z$ in the standard, TOP and exotic cases and $R=R_n$ in the localized case. This follows from the defining ambient conditions. [[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]

[F5] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. This uses the peer-checked compact annulus coding pattern of the standard connected-sum compatibility supplier only at its geometric scope; it does not assert that arbitrary homology or fundamental-group hypotheses are absolute.

## Proof

1.1 For the TOP annulus the ambient manifold is the standard compact product, and the given annulus and end collars have exactly the finite pair-code description in [F5]. Apply the external normal theorem [F3] inside $L[r]$ with those collars. Restrict the resulting tube to a compact disk bundle, still with a slightly wider domain, and export its forward/inverse, pair and collar certificates as in [F5]. This gives an actual relative tube in $V$ without ambient AC. For the smooth annuli in the other three categories, a finite chart partition of unity gives a metric and connection along the compact annulus; parallel transport and the compact inverse-function construction give the smooth tube. Only finitely many chart choices and least integer radii are needed. Thus the external TOP input used below is earned at this particular finite input; no global choice-free version of FQ is being asserted. [F2, F3, F5, given, construct]

1.2 In the smooth product category, choose a tubular neighborhood of the smooth annulus A. Its oriented normal 2-plane bundle over A has relative Euler obstruction in H²(A,∂A;Z)≅Z. The boundary trivializations are the zero framings of K₀ and K₁; the relative obstruction is the difference of their self-linking numbers, hence zero. A relative framing therefore identifies a neighborhood of A with A×D² and agrees with the two prescribed endpoint zero-framed neighborhoods. [F1, F2, given]

2.1 In that framed neighborhood insert $P$ in every disk fiber. Orient the inserted annulus by the interval direction followed by the pattern orientation. Its oriented boundary is then $-P(K_0)$ at the lower end and $P(K_1)$ at the upper end. The product collars of $A$ and the endpoint framings give product collars matching the ambient end collars, and the two endpoint patterns use the preferred zero framings. This proves concordance preservation for smooth annuli in a standard product. [F1, F2, step 1.2, algebra]

2.2 In the exotic and localized cases the annulus is smooth, so the same smooth tubular construction is available in its given smooth ambient manifold. In the TOP case use the external input [F3] relative to the two actual smooth endpoint collars. In every case this gives an oriented rank-two vector normal bundle over $A$. Its obstruction to a framing extending the two preferred zero framings is its relative Euler number in $H^2(A,\partial A;\mathbb Z)$. Cap $A$ by boundary Seifert chains with opposite boundary orientations and push the caps into the product collars. Their union is a closed two-cycle. Its intersection with a relative small parallel copy of $A$ is the relative Euler number, because the two cap terms are precisely the endpoint zero-linking numbers. The cycle is zero over $R$ by [F4], so that Euler number is zero in $R$. The inclusion $\mathbb Z\hookrightarrow R$ is injective, hence it is zero integrally. Classification of oriented plane bundles with boundary framing now gives a framing of the actual normal bundle agreeing with both preferred endpoint framings. This proves the required relative framing, rather than inferring it from absolute triviality. [F1, F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, given, algebra]

3.1 Insert the product annulus $P\times I$ into this framed neighborhood, as in step1.2. Its endpoint knots are the untwisted satellites because both endpoint framings are the preferred zero framings. In the TOP case the product model makes the new annulus locally flat; in the three smooth categories it is smooth. The ambient manifold is the original $W$, so its homeomorphism or $R$-homology conditions do not change. Thus the satellite assignment preserves concordance in all four categories and descends to the stated set maps. [F1, F2, step 2.1, step 2.2, construct] ∎

Let P⊂S¹×D² be a smooth oriented pattern. If oriented knots K₀ and K₁ are concordant in one of the four categories C_sm, C_top, C_ex or C^{1/n}, then P(K₀) and P(K₁) are concordant in the same category. Thus P induces a well-defined set map on each of these concordance sets.

## Statement references

[CDR, §2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1205.5058v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** A pattern P and a concordance annulus A from K₀ to K₁ in one of the stated ambient categories.

[F1] Satellite insertion uses a zero-framed tubular copy of S¹×D² around each endpoint knot ([[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator]]).

[F2] Each category specifies the ambient 4-manifold and regularity of its concordance annulus ([[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]).

[F3] **External TOP input (not reconstructed here).** A locally flat proper surface in a topological four-manifold has an actual rank-two normal VECTOR-bundle neighborhood; where such a neighborhood is prescribed near a closed subset, including the boundary collars, it can be chosen to agree with that germ on a smaller neighborhood. This is Freedman–Quinn Theorem9.3A, printed137–141, used under the run-specific external-source boundary. It supplies the actual tube, not automatic agreement of arbitrary global framings. The cited statement and proof pages137–141 were read; no full-book reading or local reconstruction is claimed.

[F4] Every ambient concordance manifold here is oriented and is an $R$-homology $S^3\times I$, with $R=\mathbb Z$ in the standard, TOP and exotic cases and $R=R_n$ in the localized case. This follows from the defining ambient conditions. [[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories]]

[F5] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. The external relative-constructibility input is that $L[r]$ is an inner model of ZFC containing $r$ (Karagila, §8.3, p.42); no ambient choice hypothesis is required. All compact maps are decoded using these same moduli, so the inverse identities, covers, pair sections and collar equalities are checked on dense rational sets with their displayed buffers and remain valid in the ambient universe $V$. An internally produced compact witness is exported with the same certificates, and hence is an actual ambient compact witness. This uses the peer-checked compact annulus coding pattern of the standard connected-sum compatibility supplier only at its geometric scope; it does not assert that arbitrary homology or fundamental-group hypotheses are absolute.

## Proof

0.1 For the TOP annulus the ambient manifold is the standard compact product, and the given annulus and end collars have exactly the finite pair-code description in [F5]. Apply the external normal theorem [F3] inside $L[r]$ with those collars. Restrict the resulting tube to a compact disk bundle, still with a slightly wider domain, and export its forward/inverse, pair and collar certificates as in [F5]. This gives an actual relative tube in $V$ without ambient AC. For the smooth annuli in the other three categories, a finite chart partition of unity gives a metric and connection along the compact annulus; parallel transport and the compact inverse-function construction give the smooth tube. Only finitely many chart choices and least integer radii are needed. Thus the external TOP input used below is earned at this particular finite input; no global choice-free version of FQ is being asserted. [F2, F3, F5, given, construct]


1.1 In the smooth product category, choose a tubular neighborhood of the smooth annulus A. Its oriented normal 2-plane bundle over A has relative Euler obstruction in H²(A,∂A;Z)≅Z. The boundary trivializations are the zero framings of K₀ and K₁; the relative obstruction is the difference of their self-linking numbers, hence zero. A relative framing therefore identifies a neighborhood of A with A×D² and agrees with the two prescribed endpoint zero-framed neighborhoods. [F1, F2, given]

1.2 In that framed neighborhood insert $P$ in every disk fiber. Orient the inserted annulus by the interval direction followed by the pattern orientation. Its oriented boundary is then $-P(K_0)$ at the lower end and $P(K_1)$ at the upper end. The product collars of $A$ and the endpoint framings give product collars matching the ambient end collars, and the two endpoint patterns use the preferred zero framings. This proves concordance preservation for smooth annuli in a standard product. [F1, F2, step 1.1, algebra]

2.1 In the exotic and localized cases the annulus is smooth, so the same smooth tubular construction is available in its given smooth ambient manifold. In the TOP case use the external input [F3] relative to the two actual smooth endpoint collars. In every case this gives an oriented rank-two vector normal bundle over $A$. Its obstruction to a framing extending the two preferred zero framings is its relative Euler number in $H^2(A,\partial A;\mathbb Z)$. The ambient manifold is the original $W$, so its homeomorphism or $R$-homology conditions do not change. Thus the satellite assignment preserves concordance in all four categories and descends to the stated set maps. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, construct] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard three-sphere and let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its induced boundary orientation agrees with the given orientation of $K$. Choose a sufficiently small oriented product tubular neighborhood $N(K)$ compatible with the inward conormal of $F$, set $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ and $T=\partial E$, and put $S=F\cap E$. Thus $S$ is a connected properly embedded surface in $E$ and its boundary on $T$ projects to $K$ with degree $+1$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. Choose a product bicollar of $S$ in $E$, with $S_+$ on the $+n$ side and $S_-$ on the $-n$ side, and let $Y$ be the compact cut-open complement with these boundary copies. The inclusion $j:S\hookrightarrow F$ obtained by removing the boundary collar induces an isomorphism $j_*:H_1(S;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. Let $\iota_\pm:S\to Y$ be the two collar-face inclusions and define
$$i_\pm:=(\iota_\pm)_*\circ j_*^{-1}:H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(Y;\mathbb Z).$$
Form a space $\widetilde E_F$ from copies $Y_n$ ($n\in\mathbb Z$) by gluing $S_-(Y_n)$ to $S_+(Y_{n+1})$ for every $n$, with the remaining boundary faces glued by the inherited product collar. Let $t$ be the deck shift $Y_n\to Y_{n+1}$, which is the shift of the positive meridian, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$. Then $Y$ is connected, $\partial S$ is the preferred longitude, and the linking-evaluation map
$$H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z),\qquad [\gamma]\longmapsto\bigl([a]\mapsto\operatorname{lk}(\gamma,a)\bigr)$$
is an isomorphism. There is an exact sequence of $\Lambda$-modules
$$H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\xrightarrow{i_- -t i_+}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\longrightarrow H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow0,$$
Thus $H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)$ is the cokernel of the displayed map.

## Statement references

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot $K$, a connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$, an adapted tubular neighborhood, a proper cut surface $S$, and a product bicollar used to form $Y$.

[A1] Full AC supplies Alexander duality, the universal-coefficient theorem, and the countable-choice hypotheses inherited by the surface and tubular-neighborhood suppliers. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The exterior is $E=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$ with boundary torus $T$; the positive meridian is the oriented boundary of a normal disk. [[def-knot-exterior]], [[def-knot-meridian-and-preferred-longitude]]

[F2] The exterior has $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, and its kernel on the boundary torus has a unique degree-one class, the preferred longitude. [[thm-knot-exterior-homology-and-longitude]]

[F3] The normal-form result gives $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2g}$, $H_0(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$, and $H_2(F;\mathbb Z)=0$; deleting a boundary collar does not change homology. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F4] Alexander duality identifies $\widetilde H_1(S^3\setminus F;\mathbb Z)$ with $\widetilde H^1(F;\mathbb Z)$, and the universal-coefficient exact sequence identifies $H^1(F;\mathbb Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$ because $H_0(F;\mathbb Z)$ is free. [[thm-alexander-duality-for-compact-locally-contractible-subsets-of-a-sphere]], [[thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-cohomology-over-a-pid]]

[F5] Under this duality, a positive meridian evaluates as $+1$; for a cycle disjoint from $F$, its associated cohomology class evaluates on a curve of $F$ by their linking number. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]], [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F6] The Laurent ring $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ is an integral domain, and its element $1-t$ is nonzero. [[def-the-laurent-polynomial-ring]]

[F7] Mayer–Vietoris is exact for an open cover; connected-cover classification identifies covers by their subgroups, and a normal kernel gives the regular deck group. [[thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology]], [[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]], [[thm-regular-covering-characterizations]], [[cor-deck-group-of-a-regular-covering]], [[def-deck-transformation-and-deck-group]]

## Proof

1.1 **The boundary class.** The boundary circle $\partial S$ follows the inward conormal collar of $F$ once around $K$, so its projection to the core has degree $+1$. It bounds the oriented surface $S$ in $E$, hence maps to zero in $H_1(E;\mathbb Z)$. By [F2] it is the unique degree-one class in the boundary kernel, namely the preferred longitude. The collar removed from $F$ is an annulus, so [F3] also identifies $H_1(S;\mathbb Z)$ with $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct]

1.2 **Homology of the cut complement.** In an interior product chart $F\times(-\delta,\delta)$, the complement has the two half-collars $r<0$ and $r>0$; on either half replace $r$ during the homotopy by $(1-s)r+s\,\operatorname{sign}(r)\delta$ for $0\le s\le1$. At the boundary collar, the adapted tube gives the corresponding punctured half-disk fibers, and radial projection to their outer boundary arcs is the same deformation. These maps agree with the identity off the collar and exhibit the cut-open complement $Y$ as homotopy equivalent to $S^3\setminus F$. Since $H_2(F)=0$ by [F3], Alexander duality in [F4] gives $\widetilde H_0(S^3\setminus F)=0$, hence $Y$ is connected. In degree one, [F4] and the universal-coefficient sequence identify $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),\mathbb Z)$. The natural duality map sends $[\gamma]$ to $([a]\mapsto\operatorname{lk}(\gamma,a))$; the meridian normalization in [F5] fixes its sign. [A1, F3, F4, F5, given, construct]

2.1 **The stacked space is the positive-linking cover.** Product neighborhoods of the cut faces show that the quotient map $\widetilde E_F\to E$ is a covering: away from $S$ it is the identity on a sheet, and at $S$ the two product half-collars of adjacent copies give the two half-neighborhoods of a point in $E$. The stack is connected because each $Y_n$ is connected by step 1.2 and consecutive copies meet along the connected surface $S$. The shift $t$ is a deck transformation with quotient group $\mathbb Z$. To fix the sign, let $k$ be the positive tangent to $K$ and $u$ the inward conormal of $F$ at its boundary. The outward-normal-first boundary convention makes $(k,u)$ positive in $TF$, so $(n,k,u)$ is positive in $TS^3$ for the declared positive normal $n$. The positive meridian disk then has oriented basis $(u,n)$; at its intersection with $F$ its positive boundary tangent is $n$, so it crosses from the negative to the positive side. Under the specified gluing this moves from $Y_n$ to $Y_{n+1}$ and has monodromy $+1$. Every loop's sheet change is its signed intersection with $S$, which equals its total linking with $K$ because $\partial S$ is parallel to $K$ and the omitted boundary collar misses loops in $E$. Therefore the cover subgroup is the kernel of the one-variable total-linking homomorphism, and [F7] identifies this as the cyclic cover with the stated positive deck generator. [A1, F2, F5, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, given]

3.1 **Mayer–Vietoris presentation.** Cover the stack by open thickenings of the copies $Y_n$; consecutive thickenings overlap in one copy of $S$ and nonconsecutive ones are disjoint. A singular chain has compact image and therefore meets only finitely many sheets, so the finite-chain Mayer–Vietoris sequences pass to the direct limit over finite consecutive stacks. Identifying translates with powers of $t$ gives the exact sequence $$H_1(S;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\xrightarrow{i_- -t i_+}H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\longrightarrow H_1(\widetilde E_F;\mathbb Z)\longrightarrow H_0(S;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda\xrightarrow{1-t}H_0(Y;\mathbb Z)\otimes\Lambda.$$ Both $S$ and $Y$ are connected, so the last map is multiplication by $1-t$. If $q\in\Lambda$ and $(1-t)q=0$, a nonzero $q$ has a largest exponent $m$ with nonzero coefficient $q_m$, while the coefficient of $t^{m+1}$ in $(1-t)q$ is $-q_m\ne0$; hence $q=0$. The last map is therefore injective. Exactness makes the preceding map onto $H_1(\widetilde E_F)$ with kernel exactly the image of $i_- -t i_+$; using $H_1(S)\cong H_1(F)$ from step 1.1 gives the asserted cokernel presentation. [F3, F6, F7, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1, given, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The left-to-right stack direction is chosen so a positive meridian moves from index $n$ to index $n+1$. The seam convention is shown below. The proof verifies the cover and its monodromy in step 2.1 and derives the map from exactness in step 3.1; the drawing supplies no additional premise.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[>=stealth, node distance=1.5cm]
  \node[draw,minimum width=1.55cm,minimum height=0.8cm] (yn) {$Y_n$};
  \node[draw,minimum width=1.55cm,minimum height=0.8cm,right=2.6cm of yn] (ynp) {$Y_{n+1}$};
  \draw[thick] (yn.east) -- node[above,align=center] {$S_-(Y_n)$\\{}$=S_+(Y_{n+1})$} (ynp.west);
  \draw[->,red,thick] ([yshift=-0.35cm]yn.east) -- node[below] {positive meridian: $t$} ([yshift=-0.35cm]ynp.west);
  \node[left=0.3cm of yn] {$\cdots$};
  \node[right=0.3cm of ynp] {$\cdots$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

Each rectangle is one cut complement. The seam identifies the negative face of copy $n$ with the positive face of copy $n+1$; the induced Mayer–Vietoris relation is $i_- - t i_+$.

## Statement

Assume full AC for any knot-derived Seifert matrix. Let $V$ be an integral Seifert matrix and let $E_0(V;x,y,z)$ or $E_1(V;x,y,z)$ be either elementary enlargement in the definition of S-equivalence, where $x,y\in\mathbb Z^{2g}$ and $z\in\mathbb Z$. Then $E_0(V;x,y,z)$ and $E_1(V;x,y,z)$ are integral Seifert lattices, and each represents the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$ as $V$.

## Statement references

[[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence|The two elementary enlargement matrices]]

[[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance|The integral algebraic concordance group and metabolic lattices]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** An integral Seifert matrix $V$ of size $2g$, integers $x,y,z$ of the stated sizes, and full AC only when $V$ is instantiated as a knot pairing.

[A1] Full AC is required by the knot Seifert-pairing interface; the matrix argument below is choice-free. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The elementary enlargement matrices are
$$E_0=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&0\\0^T&1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad E_1=\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\y^T&z&1\\0^T&0&0\end{pmatrix}.$$
[[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

[F2] An integral Seifert lattice has even rank and unimodular skew part; it represents zero in $G_{\mathbb Z}$ when it has a rank-half direct summand on which its bilinear form vanishes, and direct sum is the group operation. [[def-metabolic-seifert-form-and-algebraic-knot-concordance]]

[F3] The negative lattice $-V$ represents the additive inverse of $V$ in $G_{\mathbb Z}$. [[lem-negative-seifert-form-represents-algebraic-inverse]]

## Proof

1.1 For each displayed enlargement, its skew part has block form $$E_i-E_i^T=\begin{pmatrix}J&u&0\\-u^T&0&s_i\\0^T&-s_i&0\end{pmatrix},$$ where $J=V-V^T$, $u=x-y$, $s_0=-1$, and $s_1=1$. If $V$ is knot-derived, [A1] is the choice hypothesis for its Seifert-pairing convention; the following lattice calculation itself is choice-free. Since $J$ is unimodular, choose the integral vector $c=-J^{-1}u$ and replace the penultimate basis vector by itself plus the old-basis combination $c$. This integral basis change removes the $u$ block and leaves $J\oplus\begin{pmatrix}0&s_i\\-s_i&0\end{pmatrix}$. Both blocks are unimodular, so each enlargement is an integral Seifert lattice. [A1, F1, F2, given, algebra, construct]

1.2 In $E_i\oplus(-V)$, take the subgroup generated by $(e_j; e_j)$ for the old basis vectors $e_1,\ldots,e_{2g}$ and by $(b;0)$, where $b$ is the last basis vector of the enlarged lattice. Its rank is $2g+1$, half the total rank. The two displayed enlargement matrices have zero old-to-$b$, $b$-to-old, and $b$-to-$b$ entries. The $V$ and $-V$ blocks cancel on the diagonal generators, while all pairings involving $(b;0)$ vanish. Therefore the form vanishes on this subgroup. [F1, given, algebra]

2.1 The subgroup in step 1.2 is a direct summand: its generators, together with $(a;0)$ and $(0;e_j)$ for every old basis vector, form an integral basis because subtracting $(0;e_j)$ from $(e_j;e_j)$ gives $(e_j;0)$. It is therefore a metabolizer. By [F2], $[E_i]+[-V]=0$, and [F3] gives $[E_i]=[V]$ in $G_{\mathbb Z}$. [F2, F3, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(K,F)$ and $(K',F')$ be oriented knot and spanning-surface pairs in the oriented standard three-sphere, and let $h_t:S^3\to S^3$ be a smooth ambient isotopy with $h_0$ the identity, $h_1(K)=K'$, and $h_1(F)=F'$, preserving the given orientations. If $V$ and $V'$ are their Seifert matrices in any integral bases, then the basis transported by $h_1$ has matrix $V$, and any other target basis with transition matrix $P$ has matrix $V'=P^TVP$. Hence $V$ and $V'$ are S-equivalent, meaning they are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two elementary rank-two enlargement moves or their reverses.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert pairing and matrix]]

[[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence|The congruence and elementary enlargement moves defining S-equivalence]]

[[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined|Well-definedness and ambient linking convention]]

[[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy|Oriented knots and ambient isotopy]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, two oriented knot-surface pairs and an orientation-preserving smooth ambient isotopy carrying the first pair to the second.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Alexander-duality linking convention used by the Seifert pairing. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The Seifert pairing is bilinear on homology classes and is computed by linking positive normal push-offs. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-pairing-well-defined]]

[F2] An orientation-preserving ambient isotopy induces homology isomorphisms on complements and carries positive meridians to positive meridians; naturality of Alexander duality preserves the total-linking coefficient. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[prop-singular-chains-and-homology-are-covariantly-functorial]], [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F3] The positive normal is fixed by the ambient and surface orientations, so an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism carrying the oriented surface carries positive normal levels to positive normal levels. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]]

[F4] S-equivalence is generated by integral unimodular congruences, the two elementary rank-two enlargements, and their reverses. [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

## Proof

1.1 Put $h=h_1$. Because $h$ preserves the ambient orientation and the orientations of $K,F$, [F3] sends each positive normal push-off of a curve $a_i$ to a positive normal push-off of $h(a_i)$, up to a homotopy within the positive collar. By [F2] the induced map on the complement preserves the positive-meridian coefficient, so $$ \operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(h(a_i)^+,h(a_j)). $$ Thus the transported basis $b_i=h_*[a_i]$ of $H_1(F';\mathbb Z)$ has exactly the same matrix $V$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given, construct]

2.1 Let $c_1,\ldots,c_n$ be any chosen integral basis on $F'$. There is a unique integer matrix $P$ with $[c_j]=\sum_iP_{ij}b_i$; since both lists are integral bases, $P\in\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb Z)$. Bilinearity [F1] gives the matrix in the $c$ basis as $V'=P^TVP$. By [F4], this unimodular congruence is one of the defining S-equivalence moves, so the two matrices are S-equivalent. [F1, F4, step 1.1, given, algebra] ∎

The conclusion uses only the congruence move in the stated S-equivalence relation; the elementary enlargements are included to fix the relation's full convention for later consumers.

## Statement

In the model the surface retracts to the graph of these $2g$ core generators, so their homology classes form an integral basis; the same is true on $F$. Write $V^0$ for the Seifert matrix in this basis. By [F5] choose a compact oriented spanning surface $\Sigma_j$ for $b_j$, and choose regular diagrams for the resulting link pairs. For $i=j$ the desired skew-entry identity is $0=0$, and the diagonal surface-intersection entry is zero by the handle model in step 1.1; hence take $i\ne j$ in the intersection construction. Choose an open collar $G$ of $b_j$ disjoint from this target and protect a smaller collar. Its complement $K=X\setminus G$ is compact. By [F7] choose a smooth $\chi:X\to[0,1]$, equal to one near $K$, compactly supported in a relatively compact open neighbourhood of $K$ avoiding the smaller collar. Then $\chi=0$ only where $f$ is already transverse. For $\|v\|<1/2$ define $\mathcal F(p,v)=(f(p)+\chi(p)v)/\|f(p)+\chi(p)v\|$. Where $\chi>0$ its parameter derivative is $\chi/\|f+\chi v\|$ times the tangent projection onto $TS^3$, hence surjective; where $\chi=0$, $d\chi=0$ and old transversality applies. Thus the family is transverse. By [F7] every small parameter ball has a transverse slice. Compact support and direct differentiation give uniform $C^1$ convergence to the inclusion. A sufficiently small slice therefore extends by the unchanged boundary to an embedded spanning surface: finite compact coordinate subcharts keep a differential lower bound near the diagonal, and the remaining compact pairs keep positive image separation. Denote this surface again by $\Sigma_j$; it is transverse to $\partial C_i$. Let $P=C_i\cap b_j$. These points are finite, and the tangent of $b_j$ is not in $TC_i$ there because the handle curves cross transversely in $F$. Consequently $C_i$ is already transverse to $\Sigma_j$ near $P$. It is also transverse near $\partial C_i\cap\Sigma_j$, since $\Sigma_j$ was made transverse to $\partial C_i$. Put $U=S^3\setminus b_j$ and $X=\operatorname{Int}C_i\setminus P$. The target $Z=\Sigma_j\setminus b_j$ is a closed embedded boundaryless submanifold of $U$: $\Sigma_j$ is compact and all its boundary was removed. The inclusion $X\to U$ is a map between boundaryless manifolds. Protect a closed inner collar of $\partial C_i$ and, at every point of $P$, a sufficiently small punctured closed disk neighbourhood. These are closed subsets of $X$, and the inclusion is already transverse to $Z$ on their neighbourhoods. Choose these neighbourhoods small enough to retain all the original endpoint data. For the inclusion $f:X\to U\subset S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$, choose an open protected region $G$ containing all boundary ends and punctured disks at $P$, on which $f$ is transverse to $Z$; protect smaller such regions. Then $K=X\setminus G$ is compact. Choose a relatively compact open $W\subset X$ containing $K$ and missing the smaller protected regions, and use [F7] to choose $\chi\in[0,1]$ equal to one near $K$, with compact support in $W$. As above, where $\chi>0$ the parameter derivative surjects onto $TS^3$ and where $\chi=0$ the old derivative is unchanged, so the total family is transverse to $Z$. 4.1 **Identify the intersection matrix in every basis.** Step 3.1 proves $V^0-(V^0)^T=J_0$. If $g=0$, the matrices are empty and the determinant is the empty product $1$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

The orientation sign can be checked in a local oriented chart: when the positive normal is the first vector, the strip orientation $(n,u)$ and the surface intersection orientation $(u,v)$ give the same sign. The family is identically the original inclusion on smaller punctured endpoint disks and boundary collars, so extends by the identity at $P$ and across $\partial C_i$, fixes all endpoint intersection germs, and creates no new intersection with $b_j$. 2.2 The pair $(b_i^-,b_j)$ can be translated through the normal collar by $+\epsilon$ while keeping the two curves disjoint; it becomes $(b_i,b_j^+)$. Hence $\operatorname{lk}(b_i^-,b_j)=\operatorname{lk}(b_i,b_j^+)$ by [F2]. Symmetry of linking in [F2] changes the latter to $\operatorname{lk}(b_j^+,b_i)=V^0_{ji}$. Therefore step 2.1 gives $V^0_{ij}-V^0_{ji}=b_i\cdot_F b_j$. [F2, step 2.1, given]

3.1 **Identify the intersection matrix in every basis.** Step 2.2 proves $V^0-(V^0)^T=J_0$. For any other integral basis $a_j=\sum_i b_iP_{ij}$, the change matrix $P$ lies in $\mathrm{GL}_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$. Bilinearity of the Seifert pairing [F2] and of surface intersection gives $V=P^TV^0P$ and $J_F=P^TJ_0P$. Hence $V-V^T=J_F$, $J_F^T=-J_F$, and $\det J_F=(\det P)^2\det J_0=1$. ## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ be the ordered integral basis and positive normal push-off convention used to define the Seifert matrix $V$ above. Every class of $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$ has a representative that is a finite integral sum of pairwise disjoint smooth oriented embedded circles in $F$. For such representatives $x$ and $y$, the sum of the pairwise linking numbers between the positive push-off of $x$ and $y$ depends only on $[x]$ and $[y]$, is independent of the sufficiently small positive push-off, and equals the bilinear extension of $V_{ij}=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The linking number of two disjoint oriented circle components is symmetric. In particular, the Seifert pairing is a well-defined bilinear map $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\times H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\to\mathbb Z$.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix|The positive-push Seifert pairing and its matrix convention]]

[[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups|A compact genus-$g$ surface with one boundary component has free first homology of rank $2g$ with simple handle generators]]

[[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link|Alexander duality normalizes the positive meridian as the linking-number generator]]

[[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection|Linking number is the signed intersection with a supplied spanning surface]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the oriented knot $K$, the connected compact oriented spanning surface $F$, its positive normal collar, and the chosen basis from the Seifert-pairing definition.

[A1] Full AC is the choice-function axiom. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[L1] Full AC implies the countable-choice hypothesis used by the supplied surface normal-form theorem: for a sequence of nonempty sets, apply the AC choice function to its range and use the chosen element on each index. [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]

[F1] The supplied surface is connected, compact, smooth, oriented, and has boundary the oriented knot; its genus satisfies $\chi(F)=1-2g$. [[def-oriented-seifert-surface]]

[F2] Under the countable-choice interface, a compact genus-$g$ surface with one boundary component has $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z^{2g}$ and standard handle generators represented by simple smooth curves. Resolving finitely many transverse crossings in a cycle inside small oriented disks preserves its homology class and gives a disjoint-union representative. [[lem-finite-chart-surface-normal-forms-supply-jordan-disks-and-torsion-free-groups]]

[F3] For a disjoint oriented circle $J$ and an oriented circle $L$, the linking number is the coefficient of the positive meridian in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$; the positive meridian maps to $1$ under the Alexander-duality normalization. The coefficient map is a homomorphism. [[def-one-variable-alexander-module-of-an-oriented-link]]

[F4] The local oriented intersection sign is the sign of the determinant of the ordered tangent and normal bases. [[def-oriented-intersection-number]], [[def-local-oriented-intersection-sign]]

[F5] If an oriented circle is supplied with a compact oriented spanning surface and a regular diagram of the two-component link, the positive-meridian linking coefficient equals the signed intersection count with that surface. [[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]]

[F6] Homotopic maps induce the same map on singular homology, and continuous maps induce chain maps functorially. [[cor-homotopic-maps-induce-the-same-map-on-singular-homology]], [[prop-singular-chains-and-homology-are-covariantly-functorial]]

[F7] The regular-projection supplier provides a regular diagram for each oriented link, so the stated linking/intersection theorem applies to each pair of embedded circle components used below. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]], [[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]]

[F8] Every smooth oriented knot bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded spanning surface under countable choice. [[thm-every-oriented-knot-bounds-a-seifert-surface]]

[F9] Under countable choice, a smooth map can be made transverse to a closed embedded submanifold, and the relative theorem fixes a smaller neighbourhood of a closed region where transversality already holds. For a map from a manifold with boundary, the transverse-preimage theorem identifies the boundary of the preimage with the preimage of the boundary face when the boundary restriction is transverse. [[thm-transversality-homotopy-theorem]], [[prop-relative-transversality-preserves-a-map-on-a-closed-good-region]], [[thm-transverse-preimage-for-manifolds-with-boundary]]

[F10] The signed boundary sum of a compact oriented one-manifold is zero. [[lem-oriented-boundary-of-a-compact-oriented-one-manifold-has-zero-signed-count]]

[F11] Under countable choice, the half-sum of mixed crossing signs of a regular two-component diagram is symmetric under interchanging the named components. Together with [F5], this identifies the topological linking coefficients in both orders with the same integer. This uses the exact diagram and supplied-surface conclusions, not any Seifert-pairing result. [[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]

[F12] The exact parametric transversality statement says that a smooth family transverse to an embedded target has a null set of nontransverse slice parameters under countable choice. A null subset of an open ball in $\mathbb R^4$ has dense complement. The compact-set bump statement supplies a smooth $\chi\in[0,1]$, equal to one near a specified compact set and supported in a specified open neighbourhood. Choosing that neighbourhood relatively compact makes its support compact. Step 1.1 explicitly constructs the family and earns its compact support and $C^1$ smallness; these are not extra conclusions attributed to the relative-transversality Statement. [[thm-parametric-transversality]], [[prop-a-null-set-has-dense-complement-in-a-positive-dimensional-manifold]], [[lem-manifold-bump-for-a-compact-set-inside-an-open-set]]

## Proof

1.1 **Symmetry of linking.** Let $c,d\subset S^3$ be disjoint oriented embedded circles. Choose compact oriented embedded surfaces $A,B$ with boundaries $c,d$ by [F8], and a regular diagram $D$ of their boundary link by [F7]. For $X=\operatorname{Int}A$, let $f:X\to S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the inclusion. A sufficiently small boundary collar misses $d$; choose an open collar region $G$ on which $f$ is transverse to $d$, and protect a smaller collar. Then $K=X\setminus G$ is compact. Choose a relatively compact open $W\subset X$ containing $K$ and avoiding the protected smaller collar, using finitely many coordinate neighbourhoods of $K$. By [F12] choose $\chi:X\to[0,1]$, equal to one near $K$ and with compact support in $W$. Where $\chi=0$, $f$ is already transverse to $d$. For $v$ in a small open ball in $\mathbb R^4$ put $\mathcal F(p,v)=(f(p)+\chi(p)v)/\|f(p)+\chi(p)v\|$. The denominator is nonzero for $\|v\|<1/2$. Where $\chi>0$, the derivative in $v$ is $\chi/\|f+\chi v\|$ times the orthogonal projection onto $T_{\mathcal F(p,v)}S^3$, hence is surjective. Where $\chi=0$, nonnegativity gives $d\chi=0$, and the old source transversality applies. Thus the total family is transverse to $d$. Parametric transversality and the dense-complement statement [F12] give a transverse slice in every sufficiently small parameter ball. The family equals $f$ off the compact support and converges uniformly in value and first derivative to $f$ there as $v\to0$, directly by differentiation of the displayed smooth formula on the compact set. It therefore extends by the identity across $\partial A$ and remains an embedding for sufficiently small $v$: finite compact coordinate subcharts retain a uniform differential lower bound for nearby source points, and compact pairs outside those chart neighbourhoods retain positive image separation. The surface still has oriented boundary $c$ and is transverse to $d$. Apply the identical explicit family to $\operatorname{Int}B$, protecting a collar of $d$ and taking target $c$. No closed double or disjointness of an added half is asserted. Now [F5] applies to these actual transverse spanning surfaces in both orders, with the same boundary diagram $D$. It equates $\operatorname{lk}(c,d)$ and $\operatorname{lk}(d,c)$ with the two diagram half-sums, which agree by [F11]. Linking is therefore symmetric. It is additive in its first cycle by the homological coefficient homomorphism [F3], and symmetry gives additivity in the other cycle. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, F11, F12, given, construct]

1.2 **Independence of the small positive push.** In the oriented normal bicollar, any two sufficiently small positive normal sections are joined by linear interpolation through positive sections after shrinking the collar. This homotopy stays disjoint from $F$ and therefore from every representative $y\subset F$. By [F6], the two pushed cycles have the same homology class in the complement of each component of $y$, so their linking sums coincide. [F1, F3, F6, given, construct]

2.1 **Independence of cycle representatives.** Write a class $x$ as $\sum_i m_i[a_i]$ and a class $y$ as $\sum_j n_j[a_j]$ using the basis from [F1]–[F2]. If $x'$ is another disjoint-union representative of $x$, then $x'-\sum_i m_i a_i=\partial C$ for a 2-chain $C$ on $F$. Pushing $C$ to a sufficiently small positive normal level gives a chain disjoint from $y$ whose boundary is the difference between the positive push-offs of the two representatives. Hence they determine the same class in the homology of the complement of each component of $y$, so their linking sums agree by [F3]. If $y'$ represents $y$, symmetry from step 1.1 changes the comparison to linking with $x^+$; the chain on $F$ bounding $y-y'$ is disjoint from $x^+$ and gives the same conclusion. Therefore the value is independent of both representatives. [F1, F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, given, construct]

3.1 **Bilinearity and the matrix formula.** Additivity of linking in step 1.1 and representative independence in step 2.1 show that the value is additive in each homology variable. For $x=\sum_i m_i[a_i]$ and $y=\sum_j n_j[a_j]$, additivity gives $\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)=\sum_{i,j}m_i n_j\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)=\sum_{i,j}m_i n_jV_{ij}$. This is exactly the pairing defined by the matrix, proving the claim. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 1.2, algebra] ∎

## Remarks

The argument uses full AC through Alexander duality and through the supplied countable-choice interfaces. It does not assert that $V$ is independent of the spanning surface or the basis.

1.1 **Symmetry of linking.** Let $c,d\subset S^3$ be disjoint oriented embedded circles. Choose compact oriented embedded surfaces $A,B$ with boundaries $c,d$ by [F8], and a regular diagram $D$ of their boundary link by [F7]. For $X=\operatorname{Int}A$, let $f:X\to S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the inclusion. A sufficiently small boundary collar misses $d$; choose an open collar region $G$ on which $f$ is transverse to $d$, and protect a smaller collar. Then $K=X\setminus G$ is compact. Choose a relatively compact open $W\subset X$ containing $K$ and avoiding the protected smaller collar, using finitely many coordinate neighbourhoods of $K$. By [F12] choose $\chi:X\to[0,1]$, equal to one near $K$ and with compact support in $W$. Where $\chi=0$, $f$ is already transverse to $d$. For $v$ in a small open ball in $\mathbb R^4$ put $\mathcal F(p,v)=(f(p)+\chi(p)v)/\|f(p)+\chi(p)v\|$. The denominator is nonzero for $\|v\|<1/2$. Where $\chi>0$, the derivative in $v$ is $\chi/\|f+\chi v\|$ times the orthogonal projection onto $T_{\mathcal F(p,v)}S^3$, hence is surjective. Where $\chi=0$, nonnegativity gives $d\chi=0$, and the old source transversality applies. Thus the total family is transverse to $d$. Parametric transversality and the dense-complement statement [F12] give a transverse slice in every sufficiently small parameter ball. The family equals $f$ off the compact support and converges uniformly in value and first derivative to $f$ there as $v\to0$, directly by differentiation of the displayed smooth formula on the compact set. It therefore extends by the identity across $\partial A$ and remains an embedding for sufficiently small $v$: finite compact coordinate subcharts retain a uniform differential lower bound for nearby source points, and compact pairs outside those chart neighbourhoods retain positive image separation. The surface still has oriented boundary $c$ and is transverse to $d$. Apply the identical explicit family to $\operatorname{Int}B$, protecting a collar of $d$ and taking target $c$. No closed double or disjointness of an added half is asserted. Now [F5] applies to these actual transverse spanning surfaces in both orders, with the same boundary diagram $D$. It equates $\operatorname{lk}(c,d)$ and $\operatorname{lk}(d,c)$ with the two diagram half-sums, which agree by [F11]. Linking is therefore symmetric. It is additive in its first cycle by the homological coefficient homomorphism [F3], and symmetry gives additivity in the other cycle. [A1, F3, F5, F7, F8, F11, F12, given, construct]

2.1 **Independence of cycle representatives.** Write a class $x$ as $\sum_i m_i[a_i]$ and a class $y$ as $\sum_j n_j[a_j]$ using the basis from [F1]–[F2]. If $x'$ is another disjoint-union representative of $x$, then $x'-\sum_i m_i a_i=\partial C$ for a 2-chain $C$ on $F$. Pushing $C$ to a sufficiently small positive normal level gives a chain disjoint from $y$ whose boundary is the difference between the positive push-offs of the two representatives. Hence they determine the same class in the homology of the complement of each component of $y$, so their linking sums agree by [F3]. If $y'$ represents $y$, symmetry from step 1.1 changes the comparison to linking with $x^+$; the chain on $F$ bounding $y-y'$ is disjoint from $x^+$ and gives the same conclusion. Therefore the value is independent of both representatives. [F1, F2, F3, L1, step 1.1, given, construct]

3.1 **Independence of the small positive push.** In the oriented normal bicollar, any two sufficiently small positive normal sections are joined by linear interpolation through positive sections after shrinking the collar. This homotopy stays disjoint from $F$ and therefore from every representative $y\subset F$. By [F6], the two pushed cycles have the same homology class in the complement of each component of $y$, so their linking sums coincide. [F1, F3, F6, given, construct]

4.1 **Bilinearity and the matrix formula.** Additivity of linking in step 1.1 and representative independence in step 2.1 show that the value is additive in each homology variable. For $x=\sum_i m_i[a_i]$ and $y=\sum_j n_j[a_j]$, additivity gives $\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)=\sum_{i,j}m_i n_j\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)=\sum_{i,j}m_i n_jV_{ij}$. This is exactly the pairing defined by the matrix, proving the claim. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

The argument uses full AC through Alexander duality and through the supplied countable-choice interfaces. It does not assert that $V$ is independent of the spanning surface or the basis.

## Statement

Assume full AC. For every $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$, changing an ordered basis by an integral unimodular congruence or changing a knot Seifert matrix by either elementary enlargement or reduction preserves the signature of $H_\omega$. Consequently, the nonroot Levine–Tristram signature and its one-sided-average value at every Alexander root are independent of the spanning surface and basis.

## Statement references

[[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature|The Hermitian matrix and signature convention]]

[[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence|The two elementary enlargement matrices]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, an oriented knot Seifert matrix $V$, its two enlargement matrices, and $\omega\in S^1\setminus\{1\}$.

[A1] Full AC supplies the Seifert pairing and surface hypotheses. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] A basis change is $V\mapsto P^TVP$ for $P\in GL_{2g}(\mathbb Z)$; knot surfaces are related by isotopies and the two enlargements. [[def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix]], [[lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent]], [[def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence]]

[F2] Signature is the positive eigenvalue count minus negative eigenvalue count of a finite Hermitian matrix. [[def-levine-tristram-hermitian-form-and-signature]]

[F3] The one-sided signature limits at every Alexander root exist, so their arithmetic averages are defined. [[lem-levine-tristram-one-sided-averages-exist]]

## Proof

1.1 Since $P$ is real, $H_\omega(P^TVP)=P^TH_\omega(V)P$. An invertible congruence is a change of coordinates in the associated Hermitian form, so its positive and negative indices are unchanged: a maximal positive subspace maps bijectively by $P$, and likewise for negative subspaces. Hence the signature is invariant under basis change. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Put $c=1-\omega\ne0$. For either enlargement, the enlarged Hermitian matrix has block form $$\widetilde H=\begin{pmatrix}H&b&0\\b^*&z(c+\bar c)&\lambda\\0&\bar\lambda&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad |\lambda|=|c|>0,$$ where $H=H_\omega(V)$, $b$ is the column determined by the enlargement vectors, and $z\in\mathbb Z$. The lower $2\times2$ block $D$ has determinant $-|c|^2<0$, hence one positive and one negative eigenvalue. Its inverse has $(D^{-1})_{11}=0$. The block congruence eliminating $b$ therefore has Schur complement $H-b(D^{-1})_{11}b^*=H$, so $\widetilde H$ is congruent to $H\oplus D$. The block $D$ contributes signature $0$, proving enlargement invariance for every $\omega\ne1$, including singular parameters. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F1], any two knot matrices are connected by the operations of steps 1.1 and 2.1, so their signatures agree at every nonroot parameter. The one-sided signatures are equal as functions on each punctured neighboring arc; by [F3] their arithmetic averages are defined and agree at a root as well. Reductions reverse the same equalities. [A1, F1, F3, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Let $M$ be a connected smooth $3$-manifold without boundary, and let $S\subset M$
be a nonempty closed connected smooth embedded surface with
$\pi_1(S)=1$. Suppose there is an open neighborhood $N$ of $S$ such that
$N$ is path-connected and simply connected, and $N\setminus S$ has exactly two
path-connected simply connected components $N_-$ and $N_+$. Suppose also that
$M\setminus S$ is path-connected and contains an embedded compact arc
$\nu$ joining $N_-$ to $N_+$, with an open tubular neighborhood $T$ such that
$T\cap N$ consists of exactly two disjoint open $3$-balls, one in each side
component. Then
$$
\pi_1(M)\cong \pi_1(M\setminus S)*\mathbb Z.
$$
The cyclic factor is represented by a loop that joins the two sides of $N$ and
returns between them through $M\setminus S$.

## Statement references

[Friedl, Theorem 5.1](https://friedl.app.uni-regensburg.de/papers/2024_knot-theory-final.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The manifold, embedded surface, neighborhood, and path-connectivity and simple-connectivity hypotheses in the statement.

[F1] For an open cover by two path-connected sets with path-connected intersection, the fundamental group of the union is the pushout of the two inclusion homomorphisms. [[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]

## Proof

**Given:** The data above.

1.1 Put $U=M\setminus S$ and $V=N\cup T$. These are path-connected open sets covering $M$. Their intersection consists of $N_-$, $N_+$, and the tube joining their end balls. Cover the intersection by the two side components with the respective half of the tube. Each set is path-connected and simply connected, and their overlap is a contractible middle tube. Hence [F1] gives $\pi_1(U\cap V)=1$. [given, F1, construct]

2.1 Join the centers of the two end balls by an embedded arc $\alpha$ in the connected smooth $3$-manifold $N$, and let $Q$ be a thin open tubular neighborhood of $\alpha$ in $N$, enlarged at its ends to meet those balls. The open sets $N$ and $W=T\cup Q$ cover $V$. The set $W$ is a thickened loop formed by the two tubes $T$ and $Q$, so $\pi_1(W)\cong\mathbb Z$; $N\cap W$ is $Q$ together with the two end balls and is contractible. Since $N$ is simply connected, [F1] gives $\pi_1(V)\cong\mathbb Z$. [given, F1, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Apply [F1] to the open cover $M=U\cup V$. Step 1.1 gives $\pi_1(U\cap V)=1$, while $\pi_1(U)=\pi_1(M\setminus S)$ and step 2.1 gives $\pi_1(V)=\mathbb Z$. The pushout is therefore the free product $\pi_1(M\setminus S)*\mathbb Z$. A generator of the second factor is represented by $\alpha$ followed by $\nu^{-1}$, proving the stated description. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra] ∎
