## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot with exterior $E_K$, meridian $\mu$, and preferred longitude $\lambda$. Restriction to the peripheral torus induces an algebraic map from the character variety of $E_K$ to that of the torus. Every one-dimensional peripheral eigenvalue image component is contained in the zero set of the ordinary A-polynomial, while isolated image points are not treated as curve factors. For a primitive pair $(p,q)\in\mathbb Z^2$ (with $q=0$ denoting the meridional slope), a representation $\rho:\pi_1(E_K)\to SL_2(\mathbb C)$ descends to the filling that kills $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ exactly when $\rho(\mu)^p\rho(\lambda)^q=I_2$. If the peripheral matrices are simultaneously diagonalizable with eigenvalues $(M,L)$ on a common eigenline, this matrix condition is equivalent to $M^pL^q=1$; without that diagonalizability, the eigenvalue equation is only necessary and the matrix relation must be checked.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-a-polynomial|Ordinary A-polynomial and reduced boundary curve]]

[[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling|Slope and Dehn-filling convention]]

[Cooper, Culler, Gillet, Long, and Shalen, §§2–3](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~culler/papers/PlaneCurves/curves.pdf)

[Bénard, Florens, and Rodau, §§2.1–2.3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.14151)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the marked knot exterior and peripheral basis, a finite presentation of its group, a representation, and coprime integers $p,q$.

[F1] The boundary inclusion induces restriction on representations; evaluation of each fixed peripheral word is regular in matrix entries because inverse letters in $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ are adjugate polynomials ([[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]]). This restriction is equivariant under simultaneous conjugation, and the character variety is the affine categorical quotient ([[def-sl-two-character-variety-and-peripheral-eigenvalues]]; [[thm-invariant-ring-finite-generation-and-affine-categorical-quotient]]).

[F2] The ordinary A-polynomial defines the reduced union of one-dimensional components of the peripheral eigenvalue image; zero-dimensional image components are omitted ([[def-knot-a-polynomial]]; [[lem-knot-a-polynomial-boundary-elimination]]).

[F3] Dehn filling kills the primitive slope $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ and glues a solid torus ([[def-oriented-slope-and-knot-dehn-filling]]).

[F4] Seifert–van Kampen identifies the filled fundamental group with the pushout of the exterior and attached solid-torus groups ([[thm-seifert-van-kampen]]; [[thm-group-pushout-as-an-amalgamated-quotient]]).

[F5] A deformation retraction induces mutually inverse isomorphisms on fundamental groups at each basepoint of the retract ([[prop-retracts-inject-fundamental-groups]]).

[F6] The fundamental group of the quotient circle is isomorphic to $(\mathbb Z,+)$ by the degree map ([[thm-fundamental-group-of-the-circle]]); the based homeomorphism $[t]\mapsto e^{2\pi i t}$ identifies it with the unit circle.

[A1] Full AC implies countable choice, the hypothesis of the collar theorem ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]; [[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]]).

[F7] Under countable choice, a smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar; a collar is a product embedding of the boundary with a half-open interval whose image is a neighbourhood ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]; [[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]]).

## Proof

1.1 Inclusion of the boundary torus into the exterior gives a homomorphism of fundamental groups. Precomposing a representation with this homomorphism is polynomial in matrix entries, so it is a regular map of representation varieties and is equivariant for simultaneous conjugation. [F1, algebra]

1.2 Write the attached solid torus as $V=D^2\times S^1$, let $A=\{0\}\times S^1$, and base at $(0,1)$. The retraction $r(z,w)=(0,w)$ and inclusion $i:A\hookrightarrow V$ satisfy $r\circ i=\operatorname{id}_A$, and the homotopy $((z,w),t)\mapsto((1-t)z,w)$ from $\operatorname{id}_V$ to $i\circ r$ fixes the basepoint. By [F5] and [F6], $\pi_1(V,(0,1))\cong\pi_1(S^1,1)\cong\mathbb Z$. [F5, F6, construct]

1.3 By [A1] and [F7], the exterior boundary has a collar; $V$ has its product collar. Thickening the two pieces across opposite halves of the gluing collar gives an open cover of the filled manifold whose sets retract to $E_K$ and $V$ and whose intersection retracts to the torus. These spaces are path connected, so [F4] identifies the filled fundamental group as their pushout. [A1, F4, F7, construct]

2.1 Pullback along this equivariant map sends conjugation-invariant regular functions to conjugation-invariant regular functions, hence induces the algebraic restriction morphism on affine categorical quotients. [F1, step 1.1]

2.2 Since $\mu,\lambda$ commute, the primitive class $p[\mu]+q[\lambda]$ is represented by $\mu^p\lambda^q$. It maps to the identity in $\pi_1(V)$ because it is the meridian. Complete $(p,q)$ to a unimodular basis of $\mathbb Z^2$ by Bézout; the complementary class has longitude coefficient $\pm1$ on $\partial V$, hence maps to a generator of $\pi_1(V)$ by step 1.2. The pushout from step 1.3 identifies this generator with the image of the complementary class in $\pi_1(E_K)$ and imposes only the relation $\mu^p\lambda^q=1$. Eliminating the generator gives $\pi_1(E_K(p/q))\cong\pi_1(E_K)/\langle\!\langle\mu^p\lambda^q\rangle\!\rangle$. [F3, step 1.2, step 1.3, construct, algebra]

3.1 By [F2], the defining equation of the reduced curve union vanishes on each of its one-dimensional image components. The definition takes only those components, so an isolated image point outside their union is not added as a curve factor. [F2, step 2.1]

3.2 A homomorphism from this quotient is exactly a homomorphism from $\pi_1(E_K)$ that kills $\mu^p\lambda^q$. Since $\rho(\mu)$ and $\rho(\lambda)$ commute, this condition is the matrix equation $\rho(\mu)^p\rho(\lambda)^q=I_2$. [step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 If the two peripheral matrices are simultaneously diagonalized, their product of powers is $\operatorname{diag}(M^pL^q,(M^pL^q)^{-1})$, which is the identity exactly when $M^pL^q=1$. For a merely triangular pair, the diagonal entries still give this necessary equation, but they do not determine the off-diagonal entries of the product; the matrix relation remains the exact test. [given, step 3.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $L$ be a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link with $r\ge1$, compact exterior $E_L=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(L)$ obtained from pairwise-disjoint closed normal disk tubes, a finite oriented simplicial triangulation $K$ of $E_L$ with ordered vertices and simplices, with least vertex $v_0$ as the basepoint used in the cover definition, and one certified positive-meridian edge loop $\mu_i$ per component. Orient each normal disk so the positive tangent to its component followed by the positive disk basis agrees with the orientation of $S^3$, and assume the resulting classes form the standard basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$. If an integer-vector edge labeling is antisymmetric under edge reversal, sums to zero on every oriented 2-simplex, and evaluates to the $i$th standard basis vector on $\mu_i$, then the chain procedure returns a finite free chain complex over $\Lambda_r=\mathbb Z[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_r^{\pm1}]$. The first homology of this complex is the absolute maximal-abelian-cover Alexander module $A_L$. Its Fitting ideals are independent of the triangulation and cell lifts, and its order is defined up to multiplication by a unit $\pm t_1^{k_1}\cdots t_r^{k_r}$.

## Statement references

[[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]

[[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]

[[lem-multivariable-alexander-order-and-specialization]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC; a nonempty oriented smooth $r$-component link; its chosen compact exterior and finite ordered oriented simplicial triangulation; certified positive-meridian edge loops forming the basis of $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$; and an edge labeling accepted by the chain procedure.

[A1] AC is assumed in the maximal-abelian-cover definition and its link-complement supplier ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] The module $A_L$ is $H_1(X_L^{\mathrm{ab}};\mathbb Z)$ with Laurent variables acting by positive-meridian deck transformations ([[def-maximal-abelian-cover-alexander-module]]).

[F2] Inclusion of the compact exterior into the open complement lifts to a deck-equivariant homotopy equivalence of maximal abelian covers and preserves the positive-meridian basis ([[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-link-exterior-retraction]]).

[F3] The procedure checks edge reversal, all oriented 2-simplex sums and the marked meridian images, returning invalid-labeling upon any failed check ([[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]).

[F4] On each encoded admissible input the procedure terminates and rejects exactly inputs that fail one of its three label checks ([[thm-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior-procedure-properties]]).

[F5] A finite CW structure on $E_L$ lifts to a finite-rank free $\Lambda_r$ cellular chain complex whose first homology is $A_L$ ([[lem-maximal-abelian-cover-cellular-chain-model]]).

[F6] For every CW complex, cellular homology agrees naturally with singular homology and the comparison is natural for cellular maps ([[thm-cellular-homology-computes-singular-homology]]).

[F7] The first Hurewicz homomorphism identifies $\pi_1(E_L,b)^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with $H_1(E_L;\mathbb Z)$ ([[prop-the-first-hurewicz-map-in-degree-one-is-abelianization]]).

[F8] The Fitting ideals of $A_L$ and its order are independent of finite triangulation and cell lifts; the order has the signed Laurent-monomial unit ambiguity ([[lem-multivariable-alexander-order-and-specialization]]).

[F9] Connected covers of a path-connected, locally path-connected, semilocally simply connected space are classified by their induced subgroups ([[thm-classification-of-connected-covering-spaces]]).

[F10] For each lifted face incidence, the procedure inserts the signed incidence number times the deck monomial of its lift displacement ([[alg-abelian-cover-chain-model-from-triangulated-exterior]]).

## Proof

1.1 By [F4], an admissible input passes all three label checks and the finite procedure terminates. Thus its output is the finite free complex whose cells and boundary matrices are prescribed in [F3]. [A1, F3, F4, given]

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot, and let $X$ be a one-dimensional irreducible component of its $SL_2(\mathbb C)$ character variety whose peripheral image is a curve in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$. With Bénard–Florens–Rodau's variable order $A_K(L,M)$ and their slope convention, on the admissible smooth locus where the displayed derivatives are nonzero,
$$s_K(\rho)=-\frac{M}{L}\frac{\partial_M A_K}{\partial_L A_K}.$$
At an ideal point of the curve, if the associated Culler-Shalen surface has boundary slope $r$ measured by $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ with $r=b/a$, the limiting Bénard–Florens–Rodau slope is $-r$.

## Statement references

[Bénard, Florens, and Rodau, Theorems 1.3, 1.5, 4.1 and 5.2](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2103.14151)

[Hatcher, *Boundary Slopes of Incompressible Surfaces*](https://www.math.unl.edu/~mbrittenham2/classwk/990s08/public/hatcher.bdyslopes.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and the ENTIRE original locus in the Statement. The rational extension and the actual specialized homology slope are distinguished; no smaller locus is silently substituted into that Statement.

[F1] The accepted local theorem proves the rational projective logarithmic Gauss identity, its finite affine values, and the conditional peripheral ideal-point limit for the actual stipulated Culler–Shalen construction. Its proof explicitly does not identify every exceptional specialized homology kernel with the rational extension. [[thm-adjoint-logarithmic-gauss-slope-and-ideal-point]]

[F2] The ordered boundary basis is $(v_\rho\otimes\lambda,v_\rho\otimes\mu)$, and a kernel generator $(a,b)$ has slope $-b/a$. Admissibility means the given basis exists and the inclusion kernel is a line; it does not impose dimension one on the exterior cohomology or reducedness of a relator scheme. The rational extension is projective-valued and is not defined to replace every actual admissible homology value. [[def-character-variety-logarithmic-slope-invariant]]

[F3] The actual generic adjoint calculation supplies a generic matrix representation, the rank-one boundary inclusion, all word-cocycle evaluations and common-eigenbasis correction, and specialization compatibility on a nonempty dense rank-chart open. Its field-linear rank and derivation operations are reproduced over the needed finitely generated field in step1.1 rather than assuming a tangent-space identification. [[lem-generic-adjoint-peripheral-kernel-is-the-logarithmic-conormal-line]]

[F4] Actual representation and common-eigenline incidence varieties are finite type and have finitely many components; affine-domain dimension is function-field transcendence degree. [[lem-sl2-representation-variety-is-affine]] [[lem-classical-affine-algebraic-set-finite-irreducible-components]] [[thm-affine-domain-dimension-transcendence-degree]]

[F5] The ordinary A-polynomial is the square-free Laurent equation for the union of one-dimensional eigenvalue-image components, and is defined up to a Laurent unit. Boundary class $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ has unoriented slope $b/a$, with $a=0$ interpreted projectively. [[def-knot-a-polynomial]] [[def-boundary-slope-of-an-incompressible-surface]]

[L1] **External input for the exceptional actual-point clause:** Bénard–Florens–Rodau, *A slope invariant and the A-polynomial of knots*, arXiv:2103.14151, Theorem 4.1 (p.15), states the displayed identity for ALL characters on an irreducible component with one-dimensional peripheral image; Remark 4.2 explicitly includes characters not scheme-reduced. Definitions 3.1–3.2 use exactly the actual homology inclusion kernel and slope $-b/a$. This theorem is imported at the admissible locus of the Statement, rather than inferred from generic rational equality. Theorem 5.2 (pp.16–17; introduction Theorem 1.5) supplies the ideal-point interpretation. These statements, definitions, Remark 3.7, Proposition 3.8 and the complete displayed §4–§5 arguments were consulted; their exceptional specialization assertion is used externally and is not represented as a new local proof.

## Proof

1.1 **The image curve is an actual A-component.** This instantiation requires excluding a larger peripheral image component. Take the actual generic matrices on an irreducible common-eigenline incidence chart of [F4], over its finitely generated function field $F$. A two-dimensional image would make $M,L$ algebraically independent and the meridian matrix nonparabolic. Over this field the trace form, cap boundary identity and pair exact sequence in [F3] give boundary dimension two and $2=\dim\ker i_*+\operatorname{rank}i_*=2\operatorname{rank}i_*$; hence its kernel is a line. Every $\mathbb C$-derivation $D$ of $F$ differentiates the actual relators to a cocycle. The explicit word/eigenbasis calculation in [F3] makes $(DL/L,DM/M)$ annihilate that SAME line. Extend $M,L$ to a finite transcendence basis and take its two coordinate derivations. Each extends through the finite algebraic extension to $F$ by $D\alpha=-(Dp)(\alpha)/p'(\alpha)$ at a minimal polynomial $p$; characteristic zero makes the denominator nonzero. Their two logarithmic pairs are independent, a contradiction. Generically reducible representations instead have $L=1$ by knot abelianization and cannot supply a two-dimensional image. Thus every peripheral-image component has dimension at most one. The closed irreducible nonconstant image curve $Y$ in the Statement is contained in their finite union, so it equals one of the one-dimensional components: a proper closed subset of an irreducible affine curve has dimension zero. Consequently [F5] supplies its defining Laurent factor $P$ in the full ordinary polynomial. No omitted two-dimensional component is presumed absent merely from the A-polynomial Definition. [F3, F4, F5, given, construct, algebra]

1.2 **Variable order and sign.** Keep $M$ the meridian eigenvalue and $L$ the longitude eigenvalue. Writing $A_{\mathrm{BFR}}(L,M)=A_{\mathrm{library}}(M,L)$ only changes the order in which the arguments are displayed. Differentiation with respect to the NAMED variables therefore gives the same meridian derivative and the same longitude derivative, not their reciprocal. In the basis [F2], the generic kernel of $(a,b)\mapsto a\,dL/L+b\,dM/M$ has generator $(-dM/M,dL/L)$, so its slope is $(dL/L)/(dM/M)$. This fixes both the sign and the order of the quotient. A common invariant-vector rescaling changes neither coordinate ratio. Swapping the common eigenline inverts $M,L$ and changes both logarithmic differentials by minus one, preserving the projective ratio; [F3] already proves model/conjugation independence. [F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 **Full-polynomial versus component derivatives.** Write $A=uPB$, where $u$ is a Laurent unit and $B$ is the product of the other distinct factors. At a point of $Y$ with both full derivatives nonzero, $B$ cannot vanish: if another factor vanished, every term of either product derivative would contain a vanishing factor, giving zero. On $P=0$ one has $A_M=uB P_M$ and $A_L=uB P_L$. Thus the two component derivatives are nonzero there and the common nonzero factor $uB$ cancels from their quotient. Multiplication of the whole representative by any further Laurent unit has the same effect, since its differentiated unit term is multiplied by $A=0$. This also proves that the stated derivative locus is intrinsic and avoids intersections of distinct peripheral factors. It does not exclude an extra character component with CONSTANT peripheral image at the same point. [F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 **The complete rational instantiation.** The component formula in [F1] is $s^{\mathrm{rat}}=[-MP_M:LP_L]$. Combining steps1.2 and2.1 gives exactly $s^{\mathrm{rat}}=-M A_M/(L A_L)$ in the native BFR variable order wherever the displayed derivatives are nonzero. In particular it is finite there, and the projective extension still retains zero/infinity away from that affine locus. This instantiates the proved component theorem with the FULL square-free ordinary polynomial without changing either convention. It is so far an identity of the rational extension, not a proof about all exceptional actual kernels. [F1, F2, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

3.2 **The actual exceptional-point clause uses the external theorem.** A reducible representation has longitude eigenvalue $L=1$ because its diagonal characters factor through the knot abelianization. Since $A=(L-1)Q$, its meridian derivative is $A_M=(L-1)Q_M$ and vanishes at every such peripheral point. The stipulated nonzero-derivative locus therefore contains only irreducible characters. At every actual admissible smooth point of that locus, including points outside the local rank chart, apply the ALL-character formula of the external Theorem 4.1 in [L1], in the actual homology convention of its Definitions 3.1–3.2. Steps1.2 and2.1 identify the named variables, signs and full square-free representative. This proves the first clause at its entire original locus; the exceptional specialization is supplied externally, not by a density argument. [F2, F5, L1, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 **Actual homology on the proved dense open.** Intersect the nonempty rank-chart open supplied by [F3] with the original smooth/derivative locus, whenever that latter locus is nonempty. The component is irreducible, so this intersection is dense and nonempty. At every point there, the finite homology specialization in [F3] identifies the rational line with the actual ordered peripheral inclusion kernel. Thus step3.1 proves the ACTUAL displayed formula on this open. This uses the direct generic/rank-chart construction, not an unverified extension of the separate rationality lemma beyond its stated dense scheme-smooth hypothesis. It does not assert that every smooth admissible point belongs to the chosen rank chart. [F2, F3, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

4.2 **The full stipulated ideal-point clause.** The curve in the preceding clause is the peripheral eigenvalue curve $Y$. Use its normalized smooth completion, exactly as in [F1], rather than replacing it by an arbitrary character ideal point with affine peripheral image. At its stipulated ideal point the actual local DVR has nonzero valuation pair $(v(L),v(M))$, and the finite representation-field valuation extends with one positive ramification factor. For a boundary circle $a[\lambda]+b[\mu]$ of the actual associated Culler–Shalen construction, [F1]'s inverse-image midpoint and boundary-preserving compression argument gives $a v(L)+b v(M)=0$. The logarithmic projective limit in [F1] is $[v(L):v(M)]=[-b:a]$. By [F2] this is $-b/a=-r$, including zero and infinity in the projective convention. This proves the ENTIRE conditional ideal-point clause: the construction/surface is stipulated by the original conditional, and no existence theorem for an arbitrary unrelated surface is imported or required. [F1, F2, F5, step 3.1, construct, algebra]

5.1 Step4.2 already proves the full conditional ideal-point assertion with the stipulated associated surface; [L1]'s Theorem 5.2 independently gives the same valuation and sign convention. Together with step5.1 this establishes both original clauses without narrowing the admissible smooth locus or adding scheme-smoothness. [F1, L1, step 4.2, step 3.2] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For every nonempty oriented link $K\subset S^3$ and every finite signed Artin braid word $\beta$ whose oriented closure represents $K$, the corrected BMW trace value
$$Q(\beta)=-(-1)^{c(\beta)}a^{-w(\beta)}d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta),$$
where $n$ is the strand count, $c(\beta)$ is the number of closure components, and $w(\beta)$ is the determinant writhe, is independent of the braid representative. It equals the declared writhe-normalized Kauffman ambient-isotopy invariant of $K$ at $A=ia$, $Z=-iz$.

Here $\tau_n(\beta)$ denotes $\tau_n(b_\beta)$, where $b_\beta$ is obtained by replacing each letter $\sigma_i^{\pm1}$ by $g_i^{\pm1}$ in the same order.

## Statement references

[[lem-bmw-markov-trace-stabilization|BMW closure trace and stabilization scalars]]

[[lem-bmw-presentation-tangle-evaluation-is-well-defined|BMW generator images in the tangle algebra]]

[[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions|Dubrovnik and Kauffman conventions]]

[[lem-kauffman-dubrovnik-writhe-component-conversion|Writhe-component conversion and Reidemeister invariance]]

[[thm-markovs-closed-braid-equivalence-theorem|Markov equivalence of braid closures]]

[[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem|Existence of closed-braid representatives]]

[[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem|Oriented Reidemeister equivalence]]

[[def-axiom-of-choice|Axiom of Choice]]

[Goodman and Hauschild, *Affine Birman–Wenzl–Murakami Algebras and Tangles in the Solid Torus*](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0411155)

[Birman and Brendle, *Braids: A Survey*](https://www.math.columbia.edu/~jb/Handbook-21.pdf)

[Kauffman, *An Invariant of Regular Isotopy*](https://homepages.math.uic.edu/~kauffman/IRH.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC, a nonempty oriented link in $S^3$, and a finite signed Artin braid word whose closure represents it.

[A1] Assume the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]).

[F1] Every oriented link is equivalent to the closure of a finite geometric braid; AC is the stated hypothesis ([[thm-alexanders-closed-braid-theorem]]).

[F2] Two braids have equivalent oriented closures if and only if they are related by finitely many conjugations and positive or negative stabilizations/destabilizations; AC is the stated hypothesis ([[thm-markovs-closed-braid-equivalence-theorem]]).

[F3] The trace is cyclic, tower-compatible, and has stabilization factors $a d^{-1},a^{-1}d^{-1}$ for $g_n,g_n^{-1}$ ([[lem-bmw-markov-trace-stabilization]]).

[F4] The closure has one component for each cycle of its strand permutation; the Markov-move convention identifies each Artin generator with the positive geometric half twist, which contributes determinant sign $+1$, and its inverse contributes $-1$. The word exponent sum is the signed sum of these generator exponents ([[def-closure-of-a-geometric-braid]], [[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]], [[def-oriented-crossing-sign-writhe-and-blackboard-framing]], [[def-exponent-sum-of-a-braid]]).

[F5] The Markov moves are conjugation and the two signed stabilizations, with inverses allowed ([[def-markov-conjugation-and-stabilization-moves]]).

[F6] The scalar Dubrovnik value on a nonempty diagram is $D=P/d$, and
$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz)$ while
$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z)$ ([[def-kauffman-regular-isotopy-and-dubrovnik-conventions]], [[lem-kauffman-dubrovnik-writhe-component-conversion]]).

[F7] The BMW-to-tangle homomorphism sends each $g_i^{\pm1}$ to the corresponding positive or negative Artin crossing ([[lem-bmw-presentation-tangle-evaluation-is-well-defined]]).

[F8] AC implies AC$_\omega$ by restriction to countable indexed families, and under AC$_\omega$ equivalent oriented link diagrams are connected by finitely many planar isotopies and oriented Reidemeister moves ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]]).

## Proof


1.1 Fix an oriented link $K$. By [F1], choose a finite signed braid word $\beta_0$ whose oriented closure represents $K$. This use of existence is valid under [A1], as required by [F1]. Define $Q(\beta)$ by the formula in the statement for every braid word with closure equivalent to $K$. [A1, F1, given, choose]

2.1 A conjugation $\beta\mapsto\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$ leaves the closure component count unchanged because the strand permutation is conjugated, and leaves writhe unchanged because the exponent sum of $\gamma$ cancels with that of $\gamma^{-1}$. Cyclicity in [F3] gives $\tau_n(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=\tau_n(\beta)$. Thus $Q$ is unchanged by conjugation. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 For positive stabilization $\beta'=\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$, the new transposition involving strand $n+1$ joins that new strand to the cycle containing strand $n$, so $c(\beta')=c(\beta)$. The exponent sum increases by one, hence $w(\beta')=w(\beta)+1$. By [F3], $\tau_{n+1}(\beta')=a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$. Therefore $$Q(\beta')=-(-1)^c a^{-(w+1)}d^n\,a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ For negative stabilization the cycle count is again unchanged, the writhe becomes $w-1$, and $\tau_{n+1}(\beta\sigma_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$; substituting gives $$-(-1)^c a^{-(w-1)}d^n a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ Thus both stabilizations and their inverse moves preserve $Q$. [F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By [F2], any two braid words whose oriented closures represent $K$ are Markov equivalent. Each move in a finite Markov sequence preserves $Q$ by steps 2.1 and 2.2, so $Q$ is independent of the braid representative. For a representative $\beta$, [F7] identifies $\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)}$ with its oriented closure diagram. By [F3], $\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-n}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})$. Hence $$d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-1}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})=D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)$$ by [F6]. Applying the conversion in [F6] gives $$F_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=(ia)^{-w}L_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^c a^{-w}D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)=Q(\beta).$$ The scalar conversion lemma proves that $F$ is unchanged by each oriented Reidemeister move; [F8] therefore identifies this fixed-diagram value with the declared ambient-isotopy value of $K$. AC is used in [F1], [F2], and [F8]; the trace and local formula calculations are choice-free. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F6, F7, F8, step 2.1, step 2.2] ∎

**Given:** The four concordance sets with their specified concordance relations.

[F2] The mirror-reverse connected sum K#−K bounds a ribbon disk in the standard 4-ball ([[lem-general-knot-reverse-mirror-sum-is-ribbon]]).

[F5] **External TOP/exotic input.** In the category conventions of [F1], connected sum descends to an abelian group on $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}$ and $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{ex}}$, with unknot identity and reverse-mirror inverse. Its underlying TOP ambient gluing and relative-collar conclusion are imported under the run-specific external-source boundary; no new local proof of those unresolved ambient identifications is claimed. The cited CDR definitions and group assertion on printed1–2 were read directly.

[F6] **Compact finite-input convention.** The classical external results are initially used in ordinary ZFC, not assumed choice-free from their citations. For this one application take finitely many charts covering the given compact manifolds and finitely many pair charts covering each given compact disk or annulus, shrinking to closed inner charts inside open outer charts. Such finite subcovers exist by compactness; selecting this finite list uses no axiom of choice. Include the actual boundary/product collars and all supplied homeomorphisms in the list. Encode chart domains and overlaps by their rational balls, continuous maps and their inverses by dense rational data with moduli on the closed inner charts, and smooth maps by all finite-order derivative and Taylor-remainder data. The modulus at each integer scale is the least integer satisfying its uniform-continuity bound; restrictions to rational compact boxes use the least box index. These are uniquely defined choices from subsets of $\mathbb N$, not a countable family of freely selected charts. Include positive open-image and overlap margins, inverse identities, finite cover/Lebesgue bounds, and the pair-section identities with positive separation from the compact outside-patch remainder. On the standard disk/annulus parameters the latter certify the actual plane section, not merely a continuous embedding. One real $r$ codes these finitely many maps and their canonical countable data. 1.1 Specialize the TOP/exotic external assertion [F5] at each finite list of knot representatives and witnessing annuli actually used. For TOP these lie in the standard product; for exotic concordance the supplied boundary-marked homeomorphism to that product is part of the input code. The finite chart and pair-chart extraction in [F6] uses compactness, not a choice of an atlas for a countable family. Inside $L[r]$ use the ordinary CDR group operation, retain the actual output annulus and marked product homeomorphism, and export their compact forward/inverse and collar certificates. This proves the required finite compatibility and transitivity instances in $V$. Since each instance starts with its own given finite data, no simultaneous choice of representatives or witnesses for all classes is made. The quotient group operations and laws follow by universal quantification over these instances; the original $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis is therefore respected, rather than inferred from the unqualified source assertion. The localized category is handled directly by the subsequent homology calculations, with no TOP normal theorem needed. [F1, F5, F6, given, construct]

By local smooth coordinates and straightening of the embedded disk, choose an ambiently standard interior 4-ball $B$ such that $B\cap D$ is a standard 2-disk. An ambient isotopy supported in the interior carries $B$ to a concentric standard ball, so its complement in $B^4$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3\times I$. Removing $\operatorname{int}B$ from $B^4$ and the interior of $B\cap D$ from $D$ gives a smooth annulus. The outer and inner boundary collars give product collars for it. Order the ends with $K\#K^\dagger$ at the lower end and the inner standard unknot at the upper end, and orient the annulus so its boundary is $-(K\#K^\dagger)$ at the lower end and $U$ at the upper end. Reflection gives symmetry and a product gives reflexivity, all with their smooth annulus collars. [F1, F5, step 1.1, given, construct, algebra]

3.1 For localized connected sum choose a smooth product neighborhood $D^3\times I$ of a proper spanning arc inside each witnessing annulus, with the annulus strip in its standard local position, and remove its interior. If $Q$ is the remaining ambient piece, excision gives $H_j(W,Q;R_n)=R_n$ only for $j=3$. The map $H_3(W;R_n)\to H_3(W,Q;R_n)$ is an isomorphism: the boundary fundamental class meets the spanning arc once. The pair sequence therefore makes $Q$ an $R_n$-homology ball. Glue the two such complements on $S^2\times I$, joining the annulus strips. The ribbon inverse in [F2], admissible in all four ambients, supplies the stated reverse-mirror inverse. All ambient and coefficient conditions are those of [F1]. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F5, step 2.1, step 1.2, step 2.2, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. Let P⊂S¹×D² be a winding-zero pattern. Assume the axis has nonzero classical Blanchfield self-pairing in the Alexander module of P(U), with the convention that the axis defines the class paired with itself. For either the locally flat topological concordance group C_top or the smooth concordance group C_sm, let Pⁿ be the n-fold composition of the induced satellite set map, with P⁰ the identity. For every n≥0, the quotient ⟨Pⁿ(C)⟩/⟨Pⁿ⁺¹(C)⟩ has infinite rank, where ⟨S⟩ denotes the subgroup generated by S and rank means dim_Q(A⊗_Z Q) for an abelian group A. For n≥1, Pⁿ is not a group homomorphism under the same hypotheses. No pairwise-coprime Alexander-polynomial assumption is part of these Theorems A and B.

## Statement references

[[def-cdr-satellite-concordance-categories|Smooth and topological concordance conventions]]

[[def-satellite-induced-concordance-operator|Satellite operator iterates]]

[[def-blanchfield-pairing-and-higher-order-rho-invariant|Classical Blanchfield self-pairing convention]]

[Cha–Kim, Theorems A and B and complete proofs](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04629v2)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, the winding-zero pattern and its nonzero classical axis self-value, the smooth and locally flat concordance conventions, and $n\ge0$.

[A1] Full AC is the chosen integral half-solution and analytic convention; it implies the countable-choice hypotheses of the smooth concordance constructions. [[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-integral-half-solutions-strebel-and-l2-signatures]]

[F1] The actual exterior-to-zero-surgery comparison preserves the integral classical Alexander module and its Blanchfield self-values. [[thm-zero-surgery-identifies-exterior-classical-alexander-and-blanchfield-data]]

[F2] In the smooth category, actual integral solution sets are nested subgroups, satellite maps preserve concordance, and every next-iterate image lies in the corresponding integral filtration subgroup plus the cyclic class of the iterate of the unknot. The full proof supplies integral0-solutions, an actual annulus tube with zero boundary framings, homology cobordisms and deep-axis infection solutions. [[thm-smooth-integral-filtration-is-compatible-with-deep-axis-infection]]

[F3] The full finite-prime smooth obstruction theorem excludes every nonzero signed sum of each chosen finite family of $P^n$ iterates from integral $(n+1/2)$-solvability for $n\ge1$, and supplies a separate actual smooth nonslice nonhomomorphism witness. The finite-cyclic half-solution theorem supplies the actual $n=0$ obstruction. [[thm-finite-prime-smooth-infection-obstructions-use-actual-coefficients]], [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]]

[F4] The complete smooth all-iterate theorem assembles [F2]–[F3], including finite-cyclic connected-sum additivity, the $n=0$ case, rational independence modulo integral filtrations, the at-most-one cyclic rank loss and the separate nonhomomorphism conclusion. [[thm-smooth-winding-zero-iterates-have-infinite-rank-in-every-quotient]]

[F5] For supplied initial TOP integral-pair data and the actual finite standard pieces, the Blanchfield-bordism and full-forest meridian calculations hold. Actual finite-projective TOP duality/gluing and the lifted-half-pair vanishing theorem also hold, without smoothing that initial manifold. [[lem-cha-kim-integral-solvability-and-blanchfield-bordism]], [[thm-topological-finite-projective-l2-duality-and-boundary-gluing]], [[thm-topological-lifted-half-pairs-force-amenable-signature-defect-zero]]

[F8] **External TOP geometric input under CLAUDE.md §12:** locally flat concordance classes form the oriented connected-sum group; a locally flat slice disk has a collared normal product whose exterior is an integral homology circle, with prescribed meridian and zero-longitude surgery boundary. The TOP integral solution sets $\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{top}}$, defined by the same finite lifted intersection-pair conditions but allowing collared TOP four-manifolds, are nested subgroups. For winding zero,
$$\langle P^k(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle\subset\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P^k(U)\rangle\quad(k\ge1).$$
These geometric TOP assertions are imported from [Cha–Kim, §1 topological convention, §3 following Theorem3.1 and Lemma3.2, Lemma4.3, and §5.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2402.04629v2). They are not presented as locally reconstructed normal-tube or integral-filtration constructions. Full AC is retained.

[F6] The finite-stage selection and signed domination argument applies to supplied TOP initial bounds: its actual coefficient maps are supplied by [F5], and its boundary defects agree with the independent smooth invariants by the explicit external closed TOP equality in the rho-independence lemma. [[lem-cha-kim-higher-order-rho-bound-and-coprime-separation]], [[lem-l2-rho-invariant-bordism-independence]], [[thm-cheeger-gromov-uniform-rho-bound]]

[F7] An actual TOP integral half-solution with its canonical meridian map to $C_p$ has zero finite-cyclic bounding defect. The exterior/surgery comparison and canonical finite-cyclic signature means use the admitted finite prime signature families. TOP-versus-smooth boundary comparison is supplied by [F6], not assumed in the finite-cyclic theorem. [[thm-finite-cyclic-extensions-over-integral-half-solutions-have-zero-defect]], [[lem-finite-prime-families-have-explicit-separating-knot-signature-bumps]], [[thm-canonical-finite-cyclic-knot-defects-equal-seifert-signature-averages]]

## Proof

**Given:** The complete rich Statement, with full AC as above.

1.1 In the smooth category [F1] identifies the stipulated nonzero classical axis self-value with exactly the integral surgery self-value used in [F4]. The winding and orientation conventions are the same, and AC verifies its actual geometric and analytic hypotheses. Apply [F4] to obtain infinite rational rank of $\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle/\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle$ for every $n\ge0$, including its separate finite-cyclic proof at $n=0$. Its finite families are chosen for each desired rank bound, so no assertion of a single explicit infinite independent sequence is needed. This establishes the entire smooth rank branch of the original Statement. [A1, F1, F2, F3, F4, given, algebra]

1.2 Work in the TOP group of [F8]. Fix $n\ge1$ and any desired finite rank $m$. Choose the finite family in [F6] for size $m+1$. If a nonzero signed sum of its $P^n$ iterates belonged to $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$, its defining TOP solution would have exactly the integral height-$n$ pairs and isotropic height-$(n+1)$ lifts needed by [F5]. The finite forest quotient maps in [F5] have amenable target in the specified $D(k)$ class, with top meridian of infinite order. The accepted TOP half-pair theorem gives zero defect of that actual solution; the smooth standard joining/infection pieces have zero defect as well. Whole-component additivity makes the actual boundary defect sum zero. But [F6] evaluates its bottom terms by canonical cyclic numbers and gives strict signed domination over all pattern terms. This is a contradiction. Thus these $m+1$ classes are rationally independent modulo $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$: a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation. [A1, F1, F5, F6, F8, given, construct, algebra]

1.3 At $n=0$, take any finite family of the signature bumps in [F7], with distinct selected primes. For a nonzero signed sum choose an index with nonzero coefficient and evaluate the canonical cyclic defect at that prime. All cross-prime terms vanish, so the value is the selected nonzero integer coefficient times its positive normalized mean. It cannot vanish. ## Statement

Assume countable choice. Let $(B,G,R)$ be a dualizable framed handle link and
let $X(B,G,R)$ be its associated handlebody. There are finite sequences of
handle slides and cancellations, first sliding $G$ over $B$ and cancelling
the $1$-handle $R$ with the $2$-handle $B$, and then using the reversed roles,
that leave single $0$-framed attaching knots $K_G$ and $K_B$, respectively.
There are diffeomorphisms
$$
X(B,G,R)\cong X_0(K_G)\cong X_0(K_B).
$$

## Statement references

[Piccirillo, Theorem 2.1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1808.02923)

[Hom, §3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2107.09171)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Countable choice and a dualizable framed handle link $(B,G,R)$.

[A1] Countable choice, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is [[def-countable-choice]].
It is used only through the handle-slide and cancellation suppliers below.

[F1] [[def-dualizable-handle-link]]: $R$ is a dotted $1$-handle, $B,G$ are
$0$-framed $2$-handles, each of $B\cup R$ and $G\cup R$ is a meridional
two-component link, and $\operatorname{lk}(B,G)=0$.

[F2] [[def-handle-slide-of-one-k-handle-over-another]] and
[[lem-handle-slides-preserve-the-relative-diffeomorphism-type]]: a slide of
one $2$-handle over another replaces its attaching circle by a band sum with
a signed framed parallel copy and preserves the relative diffeomorphism type.

[F3] [[thm-handle-cancellation]]: a $1$-handle and $2$-handle whose attaching
and belt spheres meet transversely once cancel, preserving the diffeomorphism
type relative to the incoming boundary and transporting all remaining
attaching data.

[F4] [[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]]: the
half-sum of mixed crossing signs is invariant under regular diagram changes

## Statement

For the rank-eight lattice $L_{E_8}$ with Gram matrix $C$ specified in its definition, the form is positive definite, has determinant $1$, and takes even values on every vector. It has no vector of squared norm $1$, so it is not isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ and admits no isometric full-rank embedding into that lattice.

## Statement references

[[def-e8-root-lattice|The E8 Gram matrix and node-edge convention]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Gram matrix $C$ with diagonal entries $2$ and off-diagonal entries $-1$ on the seven stated edges.

[F1] The ordered basis and full list of E8 edges determine the Gram matrix $C$. [[def-e8-root-lattice]]

[F2] A full-rank unimodular sublattice of the standard dot-product lattice of the same rank has index one. [[lem-full-rank-unimodular-sublattice-has-index-one]]

## Proof

**Given:** The matrix and lattice convention in [F1].

1.1 Let $A_7$ be the $7\times7$ leading principal block on vertices $1,\ldots,7$. Its leading principal determinants $d_k$ satisfy $d_0=1$, $d_1=2$, and $d_k=2d_{k-1}-d_{k-2}$ for $2\le k\le7$, by expansion along the last row of the tridiagonal chain matrix. Induction gives $d_k=k+1$, so these seven determinants are positive. [F1, algebra, induction]

2.1 The vector $x=A_7^{-1}e_3$ has coordinates $x_i=\min(i,3)(8-\max(i,3))/8$ for $1\le i\le7$: substitution into $2x_i-x_{i-1}-x_{i+1}=\delta_{i3}$ with $x_0=x_8=0$ verifies $A_7x=e_3$. Hence $e_3^{\mathsf T}A_7^{-1}e_3=15/8$. The Schur-complement determinant of $C=\begin{pmatrix}A_7&-e_3\\-e_3^{\mathsf T}&2\end{pmatrix}$ is $\det(A_7)(2-15/8)=8/8=1$. [F1, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 By Sylvester's criterion, the positive leading principal determinants $d_1,\ldots,d_7$ from step 1.1 and $\det C=1$ from step 2.1 make $C$ positive definite. For any $z\in\mathbb Z^8$, $z^{\mathsf T}Cz=2\sum_i z_i^2-2\sum_{\{i,j\}\text{ an edge}}z_i z_j$ is even. Every nonzero vector therefore has positive even integral norm, hence norm at least $2$; in particular there is no norm-one vector. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 The standard lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ contains norm-one basis vectors, so no isometry from $L_{E_8}$ onto $\mathbb Z^8$ exists by step 3.1. If there were an isometric full-rank embedding, its Gram determinant would be $1$ by step 2.1, and [F2] would force its image to be all of $\mathbb Z^8$, which would be an isometry, again contradicting step 3.1. [F2, step 2.1, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot. For a nonzero Laurent polynomial $f(M,L)$, its Newton polygon is the convex hull in $\mathbb R^2$ of exponent pairs $(a,b)$ for which the coefficient of $M^bL^a$ is nonzero. The enhanced A-polynomial is **thin** when this polygon is contained in an affine line; the constant polynomial $1$ has a one-point Newton polygon and is thin. Then the enhanced A-polynomial of $K$ is thin if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, including the unknot.

## Statement

Assume full AC and let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth knot. For a nonzero Laurent polynomial $f(M,L)$, its Newton polygon is the convex hull in $\mathbb R^2$ of exponent pairs $(a,b)$ for which the coefficient of $M^bL^a$ is nonzero. The enhanced A-polynomial is **thin** when this polygon is contained in an affine line; the constant polynomial $1$ has a one-point Newton polygon and is thin. Then the enhanced A-polynomial of $K$ is thin if and only if $K$ is a torus knot, including the unknot.

[[def-coprime-torus-knot|Coprime torus-knot convention]]

[Baldwin and Sivek, Theorem 1.2 and §4](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2405.19197v2)

## Proof

1.1 The unknot and all positive nontrivial torus knots are thin by [F1]: their enhanced curves have respectively the unit equation and the two explicitly calculated monomial terms. These are actual proved formulas, rather than assumptions on an uncomputed torus character variety. [F1, given, algebra]

1.2 This proves the forward direction for every signed torus knot as well. Reflection carries its oriented meridian to the inverse positive meridian of the reflected knot: it preserves the carried knot orientation and reverses the ambient normal-plane orientation. It carries its preferred longitude to the preferred longitude, because the degree along the knot remains one and its exterior homology class remains zero; uniqueness in [F3] excludes any meridian shift. Composition of representations with this exterior diffeomorphism therefore identifies the peripheral loci by $(M,L)\mapsto(M^{-1},L)$, preserving irreducibility and all closure dimensions. Their reduced curve equations differ by that Laurent substitution and a unit. Reversing the knot orientation instead inverts both peripheral generators and gives $(M,L)\mapsto(M^{-1},L^{-1})$. These invertible integral changes of exponents preserve containment in an affine line. Finally swapping the two complex coordinates of the standard $S^3$ interchanges the two torus parameters and preserves ambient orientation; the radial torus parameter may be changed by a smooth radial isotopy. Thus, using the mirror and orientation conventions in [F1], every coprime torus knot reduces to the positive case, or to the unknot if one parameter has absolute value one. In the latter case the actual sine-cosine circle isotopy and ambient extension in the unit-slope supplier [F1] give the unknot, with its countable-choice hypothesis supplied by full AC. This is a proof of thinness for mirrors, not an assertion that the displayed positive formula applies unchanged to a negative knot. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

2.1 Suppose now that the knot exterior has the complete finite-volume hyperbolic metric. We first construct the necessary SL2 lift on this EXTERIOR; no lift of the holonomy of a closed filling is assumed. Alexander duality in [F3], in degrees one and two, gives $H_1(E_K;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(E_K;\mathbb Z)=0$, since the knot is a connected circle. The universal coefficient exact sequence therefore gives $H^2(E_K;\mathbb Z/2)=0$. On a finite triangulation choose a spanning tree and the associated finitely many vertex base paths. A PSL2 representation labels each oriented edge by its based transport; the labels multiply to identity around every triangle. Lift each edge label to SL2, choosing the reverse lift as its inverse. A triangle product is a central sign. The four triangle signs around each tetrahedron sum to zero in $\mathbb Z/2$: after conjugating to one vertex the intermediate edge factors cancel and the remaining signs commute. They are therefore a simplicial two-cocycle. Its cohomology class is zero, so it is the coboundary of a one-cochain. Multiply each edge lift by its corresponding sign. Every triangle product is now identity, and edge-path homotopy gives an actual SL2 representation lifting the specified PSL2 one. This finite argument uses the space cohomology directly and inserts no spin or closed-three-manifold parallelizability theorem. [F2, F3, given, construct, algebra]

2.2 The lift works for the local holonomy family, not merely its central point. Use the actual local slice representations constructed in [F2], not just the abstract quotient coordinate. The augmented-coordinate supplier cited in [F2] proves that three conditions transverse to the conjugation orbit give a holomorphic slice, with no large-conjugator identifications, and then gives its holomorphic family after the branched substitution $s=4\cosh^2(u/2)$. The complete cusp group is nonelementary. Indeed, if the full discrete group fixed its cusp point, put that point at infinity. It contains a rank-two translation lattice. An element with dilation of modulus different from one would conjugate a nonzero translation to translations tending to identity, contrary to discreteness. The translations in the group form a discrete rank-two lattice containing the cusp lattice; conjugation preserves it. The linear parts therefore belong to the finite orthogonal symmetry group of this lattice, and the Euclidean quotient of each horizontal horosphere has the same finite positive area. Its hyperbolic volume is the area times $\int_0^\infty z^{-3}\,dz=\infty$, contradicting finite volume. Thus the holonomy has no common invariant line and its SL2 lift is irreducible. The same is true in a neighborhood: otherwise invariant lines for a convergent sequence of reducible tuples have a convergent subsequence in compact $\mathbb{CP}^1$, giving an invariant line at the complete point. Now choose the local edge lifts holomorphically, with their values at the center equal to those of step 2.1. Each triangle product is a continuous central sign, hence stays identity. This yields the actual local family of irreducible SL2 representations. On the augmented curve its chosen common peripheral line has eigenvalues $M(u)=\epsilon_\mu e^{u/2}$ and $L(u)=\epsilon_\lambda e^{v(u)/2}$ for fixed signs, because their squares are the eigenvalue ratios in [F2]. [F2, F3, F4, step 2.1, construct, algebra]

2.3 This nonconstant peripheral arc lies in the enhanced curve of [F4]. To check the dimension condition rather than assume it, take the algebraic irreducible-character component through the complete irreducible point. The ordinary local quotient in [F2] is a smooth complex curve, so that component has dimension one; the local finite lift from PSL2 to SL2 does not change this dimension. Adjoining a peripheral eigenline away from $u=0$ is a finite choice of the two eigenlines, so its component is again one-dimensional. Its algebraic peripheral image closure has dimension at most one, and at least one because $M(u)$ is nonconstant. Hence this is an actual one-dimensional irreducible-character image component, not an isolated representation discarded by the enhanced Definition. The enhanced polynomial vanishes on the entire local arc. [F2, F4, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

2.4 A nonzero Laurent polynomial with collinear integral support has the form $M^aL^b P(M^rL^s)$, where $(r,s)$ is a primitive nonzero integral vector and $P$ is a one-variable Laurent polynomial; subtract one support point and divide all support differences by their common primitive direction. If the support is a single point, it has no zero in $(\mathbb C^*)^2$ and already cannot vanish on the arc in step 2.3. Otherwise $P$ has finitely many nonzero complex roots. A connected local arc on its zero set has $M^rL^s$ equal to one fixed root. Applying step 2.2 and differentiating at $u=0$ gives $r+s\tau=0$. Since $\operatorname{Im}\tau\ne0$, this forces $s=0$ and then $r=0$, a contradiction. Thus the enhanced polynomial of a finite-volume hyperbolic knot is not thin. This proves the complete hyperbolic exclusion without treating a PSL2 filling representation as an already lifted SL2 representation. [F2, F4, step 2.2, step 2.3, algebra]

2.5 We also need global image control before the SU2 filling operation, since the enhanced Definition alone omits rather than excludes higher-dimensional images. Take any irreducible component of the finite algebraic representation variety together with one common peripheral eigenline, and its actual generic matrices over its finitely generated function field $F$. Cover the eigenline projective coordinate by its two affine charts. If its peripheral image were two-dimensional, $M,L$ would be algebraically independent by [F5]; in particular a peripheral matrix generically has distinct eigenvalues. Its adjoint system is self-dual by trace. The explicit nonparabolic torus computation in [F5] gives boundary homology dimension two. Here is the rank computation over this arbitrary $F$, without assuming that its transcendence degree is one. Dualizing chains over the field, Lefschetz cap identifies restriction on $H^1$ with the pair connector on $H_2$, up to its degree sign, while restriction is transpose to inclusion on $H_1$. Exactness therefore gives $2=\dim\ker i_*+\operatorname{rank}i_*=2\operatorname{rank}i_*$; both image and kernel have dimension one. The extension of functionals needed to dualize is permitted by the standing full AC, exactly as in [F5]. For any $\mathbb C$-derivation $D:F\to F$, differentiating actual word matrices gives the cocycle $Z(g)=D\rho(g)\rho(g)^{-1}$. The finite word pairing with $u=\rho(\delta)-\operatorname{tr}\rho(\delta)I/2$ annihilates every relator boundary and has peripheral values one common nonzero factor times $(DL/L,DM/M)$, as the explicit moving-eigenbasis calculation in [F5] shows. Hence ALL these pairs annihilate the SAME one-dimensional boundary kernel. But extend $M,L$ to a finite transcendence basis of $F/\mathbb C$ and use the two coordinate derivations on that rational function field. Each extends over its finite algebraic extension to $F$: for a minimal polynomial $p(\alpha)=0$, set $D\alpha=-(Dp)(\alpha)/p'(\alpha)$; characteristic zero ensures $p'(\alpha)\ne0$, and the product/quotient rules verify the extension. Their resulting logarithmic pairs are independent, contradicting that common annihilator line. Thus no image component is two-dimensional. Components with generically reducible representations have $L=1$, because their diagonal characters factor through the meridian abelianization. The central-peripheral case has $M,L\in\{1,-1\}$ and is already zero-dimensional. This proves the dimension bound for the entire eigenvalue image. [F3, F4, F5, construct, algebra]

2.6 There are therefore only finitely many exceptional eigenvalue pairs not lying on one-dimensional irreducible-character image curves. Indeed use the finite representation variety and its common-line incidence variety on the two affine eigenline charts; their coordinate rings are finite type and Noetherian. They have finitely many components by [F5]. For each one, step 2.5 makes its image closure either a curve or a point. The union of the curve images from the irreducible-character locus is precisely the enhanced curve of [F4]; images of remaining components of that locus contribute only finitely many points. Thus an actual irreducible SU2 representation either has its eigenvalue pair on the enhanced curve or in that finite exceptional set. This conclusion was not inferred merely from the wording that the Definition discards zero-dimensional components. [F4, F5, step 2.5, construct, algebra]

3.1 We now complete the nonvertical thinness-to-SU2-averse filling operation. Suppose the thin polynomial has nonconstant support direction $(p,q)$ with $q\ne0$, so its curve components are $M^pL^q=c_j$. Fact [F7] supplies finite multiplicative orders for ALL the constants $c_j$, using the entire thin segment. Let $N$ be divisible by all of them and by $|q|$. For every positive multiple $n$ of $N$, the slope $(np+1)/(nq)$ is primitive: a common divisor of its coefficients divides $q$, while $np+1$ is congruent to one modulo every divisor of $q$. The slopes are distinct and tend to $p/q$. If an irreducible SU2 representation extends over such a filling and lies on a curve component, its filling equation gives $1=M^{np+1}L^{nq}=M c_j^n=M$, impossible: a unitary determinant-one matrix with eigenvalue one is the identity, and a meridian normally generates the knot group, so its representation would be trivial. For any of the finite exceptional pairs from step 2.6 put $c=M^pL^q$. If $c$ is a root of unity, enlarge $N$ by its order; then its filling equation again forces $M=1$. If $c$ is not a root of unity, the equation $M c^n=1$ holds for at most one integer $n$, since two would give $c^{n-n'}=1$. Delete those finitely many integers. All remaining infinitely many primitive fillings have no irreducible SU2 representation. Every reducible unitary representation is abelian: an invariant line has invariant orthogonal complement, so all matrices are simultaneously diagonal. Hence these are actually SU2-abelian fillings. This proves the entire infinite-filling reduction on the stated nonvertical nonconstant branch. A vertical support direction $q=0$ produces no such sequence; ruling out that case for a nontrivial knot remains among the genuine representation/instanton operations in [L1], rather than being hidden by division by $q$. [F3, F4, F7, step 2.6, construct, algebra]

4.1 We supply the classical satellite Alexander formula used in [L2], instead of assuming it from a satellite Definition. Write $X=V\setminus\operatorname{Int}\nu P$ for the pattern exterior and $E_K=X\cup_T E_C$ for the satellite exterior, with outer meridian $\mu_V$ identified with $\mu_C$ and preferred outer longitude with $\lambda_C$. Let $w\ne0$ be the winding number, and let $\Lambda=\mathbb Z[t^{\pm1}]$ act on covers by the satellite's positive-meridian deck transformation. Total linking restricts to $w$ times companion linking on $E_C$, to $w$ on $\mu_V$ and zero on the outer longitude. The pulled-back cover of $T$ has $|w|$ cylinder components, so $H_1(\widetilde T)=\Lambda/(t^w-1)$ generated by a lift of $\lambda_C$; its $H_0$ is the same module. The cover of $E_C$ has $|w|$ components, with module $H_1=\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C$, where $s$ acts by $t^w$. Its $H_0$ map from $T$ is an isomorphism, because the two linking images are the same subgroup $w\mathbb Z$. Its longitude class is zero in $H_1$: a Seifert surface for $C$ lifts, since linking vanishes on all its loops by normal push-off, and its boundary is that lifted longitude. Replace $C$ by the unknot to obtain the pattern closure $P(U)$. Its companion-side cover has $|w|$ contractible components, the same $H_0$ and zero $H_1$. In both lifted Mayer–Vietoris sequences the $H_0$ map is injective, since its companion-side coordinate is an isomorphism. The only $H_1(\widetilde T)$ image is consequently in the SAME pattern-side module. Quotienting that image yields, respectively,
$A_K\cong A_{P(U)}\oplus\bigl(\Lambda\otimes_{\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]}A_C\bigr)$.
All gluings and the chosen longitude bounds are in the actual peripheral marking; no companion character transfer is used in this module calculation. [F3, F6, construct, algebra]

4.2 For $w\ne0$, $\Lambda$ is free of rank $|w|$ over $\mathbb Z[s^{\pm1}]$ via $s=t^w$, with basis $1,t,\ldots,t^{|w|-1}$ after reversing the exponent convention if $w<0$. Extension of scalars is therefore exact, and [F6] supplies a square presentation of its companion summand by the companion Seifert matrix with $s$ replaced by $t^w$. The direct sum in step 4.1 has a block-diagonal square presentation. Taking its determinant gives $\Delta_K(t)\doteq\Delta_{P(U)}(t)\Delta_C(t^w)$. With symmetric normalization and value one at $t=1$, the Laurent unit ambiguity disappears. The winding-zero case gives the same polynomial identity with $\Delta_C(1)=1$: its companion-side cover is now a disjoint union of copies of $E_C$, with $H_1=\Lambda[\mu_C]$ and $H_0=\Lambda$. The torus-side groups are $H_1=\Lambda^2$, $H_0=\Lambda$, and the meridian map onto the companion $H_1$ is an isomorphism while the longitude maps to zero. The same maps hold for an unknot companion. Eliminate the companion meridian generator in both sequences; their identical remaining pattern quotient is $A_K\cong A_{P(U)}$. This proves the Alexander satellite formula also for $w=0$, without claiming that such a pattern can be an instanton L-space satellite. [F6, step 4.1, algebra]

4.3 The finite torus-pattern obstruction is also elementary once the stated coefficient restrictions in [L1] have been supplied. For the nonzero signed winding $w$ put $v=|w|>0$. Symmetric normalization gives $\Delta_C(t^w)=\Delta_C(t^v)$, so the satellite product of step 4.2 uses this positive exponent. Write $a>b\ge2$ coprime and $g=(a-1)(b-1)/2$. The formula in [F6], expanded at infinity, is
$\Delta_{T_{a,b}}(t)=t^g(1-t^{-ab})(1-t^{-1})/((1-t^{-a})(1-t^{-b}))$.
Modulo terms of degree at most $g-a$, its expansion is $\sum_{i=0}^{\lfloor a/b\rfloor}(t^{g-ib}-t^{g-ib-1})$. Thus, for $0\le v<a$, its coefficient $c_{g-v}$ is $1$ if $v=0\pmod b$, $-1$ if $v=1\pmod b$, and zero otherwise. Suppose the companion's normalized polynomial has leading terms $t^h-t^{h-1}+O(t^{h-2})$ and the satellite's nonzero coefficients alternate with absolute value one, exactly the two externally supplied instanton conclusions in [L1]. By step 4.2 its coefficient in degree $g+hv-v$ is $c_{g-v}-1$. If $v=1\pmod b$ this is $-2$, impossible. If $v=qb+r$ with $2\le r<b$, it is $-1$, while the preceding nonzero coefficient is the $-1$ in degree $g+hv-qb-1$: all intervening torus coefficients vanish and no lower companion term reaches those degrees. These consecutive negative coefficients contradict alternation. Consequently $b$ divides $v$ whenever $0<v<a$. This argument is a proved finite polynomial implication and uses the externally supplied instanton properties, without proving their gauge-theoretic foundations. [F6, L1, step 4.2, algebra]

4.4 In particular the torus-pattern configuration required by the minimal-satellite argument is incompatible with those coefficient restrictions. If $ab=k v^2$ for an integer $k\ge1$, then $v<a$, since otherwise $ab\ge a^2>ab$. Step 4.3 makes $b\mid v$, whence $a=k b(v/b)^2$ contradicts $\gcd(a,b)=1$ and $b\ge2$. Mirroring a torus pattern does not change its symmetric Alexander polynomial, so the same contradiction applies after the prescribed mirror reduction. Also $v=1$ is already excluded as soon as both nontrivial pattern and companion have leading terms $t^g-t^{g-1}$ and $t^h-t^{h-1}$: their product has second leading coefficient $-2$. Thus the remaining satellite obstacles in [L2] are the actual geometric/representation transfers, nontriviality/nonzero-winding and genus reduction, not an unauthored Alexander product or finite torus-coefficient calculation. [L1, step 4.2, step 4.3, algebra]

4.5 We now close the classical knot-trichotomy operations, leaving precisely the actual hyperbolization input [L2]. For any smooth knot $J$, an essential smooth torus in its exterior gives the actual satellite construction in [F10], with nontrivial companion, noncore pattern and the correct preferred peripheral marking. If there is no essential torus, its exterior is embedded-atoroidal by definition. If it is Seifert-fibered, the other new supplier in [F10] recognizes the knot by an actual torus-knot ambient isotopy, including the unknot case. Otherwise $J$ is nontrivial: an unknot isotopy and the explicit tube control give a solid-torus exterior, which has a product Seifert fibration. The residual exterior is compact, connected, orientable and has one torus boundary by the actual JSJ proof1.1. It is irreducible and its boundary is incompressible by [F10]. Thus it has ALL the literal hypotheses of [L2], with embedded atoroidality and no assumed map-capture condition. With the metric conclusion treated as the external geometric premise described in [L2], this is the hyperbolic branch. Consequently a nonhyperbolic nontorus knot must have the displayed essential satellite torus, conditionally only on that precise hyperbolization theorem. The geometric and representation satellite operations named at the end of step4.4 have already been discharged by [F8, F9]; no abstract knot trichotomy is being imported in their place. 5.1 We give the complete final assembly, retaining precisely its premises [L1, L2]. Suppose a nontrivial thin knot were not a torus knot. The unit/vertical exclusions required in [L1] make its support a nonconstant segment of finite slope; step 3.1 then supplies actual infinitely many SU2-abelian fillings. Fact [F8] gives nonzero signed winding, nontrivial pattern closure, and $g(K)=g(P(U))+|w|g(C)$; its adjacent-top hypothesis is exactly the supplied instanton property, not inferred from thinness alone. [F8, F10, L1, L2, step 1.2, step 2.4, step 3.1, step 4.5, construct]

5.2 Fact [F9] now makes $P(U)$ and $C$ thin, of the original finite slope and that slope divided by $w^2$, respectively. Both are nontrivial, and their genera are positive; by [F8]'s formula each is strictly smaller than $g(K)$, even if $|w|=1$. Each is nonhyperbolic by step 2.4. By step 4.5 and the exact geometric input described in [L2] each is therefore torus or satellite, and least-genus choice excludes the satellite option. Thus they are torus knots. Their explicit signed torus formulas in [F1] and step 1.2 identify the two slopes. After a common mirror if necessary, and parameter swaps/reversals, write $P(U)=T_{a,b}$ and $C=T_{c,d}$ with $a>b\ge2$, $c>d\ge2$, $\gcd(a,b)=\gcd(c,d)=1$. [F1, F8, F9, F10, L2, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.4, step 4.5, step 5.1, construct, algebra]

Symmetry gives $\Delta_C(t^w)=\Delta_C(t^v)$ and the slope equation is $ab=cdv^2$, so step 4.4 applies with this POSITIVE $v$ and gives a contradiction. This completes the converse assembly with the precise externally supplied or explicitly conditional premises [L1, L2]. All classical geometry, signed peripheral representation transfer, exceptional-value filling control and Alexander coefficient operations used in that assembly are supplied locally or by [F1] through [F10]. This records the finite conditional local derivation; the full classification, including the residual input, follows independently from [F11]. [F8, F9, L1, L2, step 4.3, step 4.4, step 5.1, step 5.2]

The preceding local arguments are preserved; the full completion is source-qualified by the external classification. [F11, given] ∎

## Statement

Let $K$ be a null-homologous knot in a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold $Y$, and suppose $Y\setminus K$ fibers over $S^1$ with connected fiber a Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Then the integral top Alexander group is one copy of the integers:

$$\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(Y,K,[F],g;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z.$$

## Statement references

[[def-top-alexander-grading-of-knot-floer-homology|The integral Alexander grading and Seifert class]]

[[def-balanced-taut-sutured-manifold-and-product-region|The product sutured manifold obtained by cutting along a fiber]]

[Ni, *Knot Floer homology detects fibred knots*, §1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0607156v4)

[Juhasz, *Floer homology and surface decompositions*, Theorem 1.5](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0609779v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

[F1] [[lem-marked-fiber-admits-a-sutured-surface-diagram]] constructs the actual meridionally marked exterior diagram and identifies its fiber cut with the marked product.

[F2] [[lem-permissible-surface-niceification-preserves-admissibility]] gives a finite admissible adapted nice diagram.

[F3] [[lem-relative-sutured-diagrams-have-signed-move-equivalences]] gives the signed comparison for the specified transported orientation class and computes the product by the empty diagram.

[F4] [[lem-fiber-outer-grading-and-integral-cut-euler-matrix]] fixes the absolute Chern anchor: the outer summand has Alexander degree g.

[F5] [[lem-signed-outer-summand-cut-comparison-with-zero-periodic-cut]] identifies the entire outer differential with the cut differential over the integers when the cut periodic group vanishes.

## Proof

**Given:** A null-homologous knot K in the stated general closed oriented Y and its connected fiber F of genus g, with the meridional boundary trivialization in the definition of the integral Alexander grading.

1.1 Use the actual binding bridge and drilling construction to represent the exterior with two meridional sutures, carrying the actual page longitude and the class of F. The adapted surface cut is literally the result of cutting this mapping torus along its fiber, hence is F times an interval with its product sutures. Apply the finite permissible niceification. Signed relative diagram moves compare the resulting complex to the chosen defining complex, with its specified coherent orientation class transported. No restriction on Y or change of coefficient ring is made. [F1, F2, F3]

2.1 In this marked adapted diagram the local Euler obstruction is minus 2g plus twice the number of interior polygon coordinates when evaluated on minus F. Therefore the Alexander degree is g minus that number: degree g is precisely the outer generator set, and no higher degree occurs. The product cut has zero periodic-domain group, either directly from its empty product diagram and the relative handle description, or from its vanishing relative integral homology. The signed cut comparison consequently identifies the whole degree-g differential with the cut differential, after harmless changes of generator signs. [F4, F5, step 1.1]

3.1 The empty diagram of the actual product has one empty-tuple generator and no nonconstant disk, so its integral chain complex is Z with zero differential. The signed relative move equivalences identify its homology with that of the actual cut diagram. Combining with the full top-summand chain identification gives the asserted integral group isomorphism. The exterior orientation character restricts trivially to the zero-periodic cut, so this conclusion holds for the specified defining class without asserting equivalence of arbitrary orientation systems on the uncut exterior. [F3, step 2.1] ∎
