## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is $K$. The normal framing along $K$ given by the inward unit conormal to $K$ in $F$ has self-linking number zero. Here self-linking is the linking number of $K$ with a sufficiently small disjoint push-off along that framing. In the framing-class parameterization by relative winding from the surface framing, this class has integer zero.

## Statement references

[[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing|Framings, self-linking by a small push-off, and the Seifert framing]]

[[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor|Framing classes parameterized by relative winding]]

[[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection|Linking number as signed intersection with a spanning surface under the Axiom of Choice]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** The Axiom of Choice, a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface $F$ whose oriented boundary is $K$.

[A1] The Axiom of Choice implies the Axiom of Countable Choice through dependent choice. ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]) ([[thm-choice-implies-dependent-implies-countable-choice]])

[F1] A Seifert surface is a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface whose oriented boundary is the specified knot; its genus formula assumes $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. ([[def-oriented-seifert-surface]])

[F2] For a knot with a supplied oriented spanning surface, the inward unit surface conormal is a reference normal framing, and relative winding identifies its framing class with zero. ([[thm-oriented-knot-framing-classes-form-z-torsor]])

[F3] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, the inward unit conormal defines the Seifert framing; its self-linking is the linking number with a sufficiently small push-off along that section. ([[def-framed-knot-self-linking-and-seifert-framing]])

[F4] For any normalized tubular-neighbourhood chart and sufficiently small radius, the push-off is embedded and its linking number is independent of the radius, the representative nowhere-zero normal section, and the normalized chart; hence it depends only on the framing class. ([[lem-framed-knot-push-off-self-linking-well-defined]])

[F5] For disjoint oriented circles $J,K$ and an oriented spanning surface $\Sigma$ with $\partial\Sigma=K$, if $J$ is transverse to $\Sigma$ and $D$ is a regular oriented diagram of $J\cup K$, the diagram linking number equals the signed intersection number $J\cdot\Sigma$. The theorem assumes the Axiom of Choice. ([[thm-linking-number-equals-signed-intersection]])

[F6] Under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, every oriented link in $\mathbb R^3$ has a dense set of directions giving a regular diagram with finitely many crossings. ([[lem-every-oriented-link-admits-a-regular-projection]])

[F7] A regular oriented diagram is a projection with only finitely many transverse double points and no triple points. ([[def-regular-oriented-link-diagram]])

[F8] A smooth manifold with boundary has a smooth collar under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$; a collar is a smooth embedding of the boundary times a half-interval, equal to the boundary inclusion at zero and onto an open boundary neighbourhood. ([[thm-collar-neighborhood-theorem]]) ([[def-smooth-collar-of-a-manifold-boundary]])

[F9] A tubular chart exists under $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. It may be normalized as in [F4]: its vertical derivative induces a smooth fibrewise isomorphism $B$ to the normal quotient, and precomposing the chart by $B^{-1}$ makes that identification the identity. A smooth isotopy of a compact boundaryless embedded source, stationary near its parameter endpoints, extends to an ambient isotopy; linking number is unchanged under ambient isotopy of oriented two-component links. ([[thm-tubular-neighbourhood-theorem-in-a-smooth-ambient-manifold]]) ([[lem-a-smooth-isotopy-of-compact-embedded-submanifolds-extends-to-an-ambient-isotopy]]) ([[lem-linking-number-even-sum-and-reidemeister-invariance]])

[F10] The standard smooth step function $\sigma$ is smooth, is zero for arguments at most zero, and is one for arguments at least one. ([[def-the-standard-smooth-step-function]])

## Proof

1.1 By [A1], the $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypotheses in [F1], [F3], and [F6] hold. The given $F$ is a Seifert surface by [F1]. Use its inward unit conormal as the reference normal field. By [F2], this Seifert framing has relative winding integer zero. [given, A1, F1, F2]

1.2 Let $s$ be the inward unit conormal, viewed in the round-metric normal bundle. By [F8], choose a smooth collar $c:K\times[0,\varepsilon_0)\to F$ and orient its levels by the original $K$. For sufficiently small $\delta>0$, set $J_0=c(K,\delta)$. It is embedded, lies in $\operatorname{int}F$, and is disjoint from $K$. No prescribed collar velocity is assumed: since $c$ is an embedding onto a boundary neighbourhood, $\partial_t c(p,0)$ is inward transverse to $K$ in $F$. Its normal quotient is therefore $a(p)s(p)$ for a smooth function $a(p)>0$; a tangential component is allowed. [given, F8, construct]

1.3 Use a normalized tubular chart $\Phi$ of $K$ as in [F4] and [F9], and write $\Phi^{-1}(c(p,t))=(b_t(p),v_t(p))$, with $v_t(p)$ in the normal fibre over $b_t(p)$. Compactness permits one small interval of $t$ on which these expressions are defined for every $p$. At $t=0$ they are $(p,0)$, and normalization identifies the vertical derivative with $a(p)s(p)$. The maps $b_t$ are $C^1$-close to the identity. In a smooth oriented circle coordinate their lifts have the form $u+r_t(u)$ with $r_t$ periodic and $\|r_t'\|_\infty<1/2$ for small $t$; thus the lifts are increasing degree-one diffeomorphisms. Hence each $b_t$ is an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism. Reparametrize the level over $x=b_t(p)$, obtaining a smooth normal section $w_t(x)=v_t(b_t^{-1}(x))$. Taylor expansion in finitely many bundle charts gives, uniformly on $K$, $w_t(x)=t a(x)s(x)+O(t^2)$. Because $a$ has positive minimum and $s$ is unit, after decreasing $\delta$ this implies $\langle w_\delta(x),s(x)\rangle>0$ for every $x$. [given, F4, F9, step 1.2, construct, algebra]

1.4 For $0\le u\le1$, interpolate in each normal fibre by $z_u(x)=(1-\chi(u))w_\delta(x)+\chi(u)\delta s(x)$, where $\chi(u)=\sigma(3u-1)$ is the plateau from [F10]. Every $z_u$ has positive pairing with $s$, so it never meets the zero section. Uniformly these vectors have norm $O(\delta)$; a common disk bundle about the compact zero section lies in the tubular domain, so all interpolating graphs lie in that domain when $\delta$ is small. Each graph projects identically to $K$, hence is an embedded circle, and $\Phi$ carries it to an embedded circle disjoint from $K$. With $K$ as the fixed first component this is a smooth two-component link isotopy, stationary near its parameter endpoints, from $K\cup J_0$ to $K\cup\Phi(\delta s)$. The orientation on $J_0$ agrees with the graph orientation because $b_\delta$ preserves orientation. By [F9] the family extends to an ambient isotopy and its linking number is unchanged. The endpoint $\Phi(\delta s)$ is exactly a sufficiently small normalized-chart push-off in [F3]–[F4]. Consequently the self-linking in the statement equals $\operatorname{lk}(K,J_0)$, without identifying the collar level literally with a chart graph of $\delta s$. [A1, F3, F4, F9, F10, step 1.2, step 1.3, construct]

2.1 Since $F$ is a compact embedded surface, it is closed and has empty interior in $S^3$; hence its complement contains a point $q$. Choose an orientation-preserving stereographic chart from $q$. It places $K\cup J_0$ and $F$ in $\mathbb R^3$. Let $F_0$ be the closure in $F$ of the complement of the open boundary collar $c(K\times[0,\delta))$. Then $F_0$ is compact, is disjoint from $K$, and has boundary set $J_0$. Give $F_0$ its orientation inherited from $F$; at its new boundary the outward collar-normal points back toward $K$, so the induced boundary orientation is the transported orientation of $J_0$, parallel to $K$. Apply [F6] and [F7] to choose a regular oriented diagram $D$ of $K\cup J_0$, with the projection-plane orientation induced from $S^3$. [given, F6, F7, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Apply [F5] with its first component $J$ equal to the original knot $K$, its second (boundary) component equal to $J_0$, and the oriented spanning surface $\Sigma=F_0$. The curve $K$ is disjoint from $F_0$, so it is transverse to $F_0$ with empty intersection and has signed intersection number zero. Thus [F5] gives $\operatorname{lk}_D(K,J_0)=\operatorname{lk}(K,J_0)=0$. This computes the linking number in the same order as the self-linking convention. The Axiom of Choice is the hypothesis used by [F5]; [A1] supplies the countable-choice hypotheses of the other cited suppliers. [A1, F5, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 By [F3] and step 1.4, $\operatorname{lk}(K,J_0)$ is the self-linking of the Seifert framing; step 3.1 makes it zero. Step 1.1 gives relative framing integer zero. [F2, F3, F4, step 1.1, step 1.4, step 3.1, algebra] ∎

## Statement

Assume AC. Let $\phi:A\to B$ be a group homomorphism inducing an isomorphism
$H_1(A;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(B;\mathbb Z)$ and an epimorphism
$H_2(A;\mathbb Z)\to H_2(B;\mathbb Z)$. For a group $X$, define
$\Gamma_1X=X$ and $\Gamma_{n+1}X=[X,\Gamma_nX]$. Then for every finite
$n\ge1$, the induced homomorphism
$$A/\Gamma_nA\longrightarrow B/\Gamma_nB$$
is an isomorphism.

## Statement references

[McCleary, Theorem 8bis.16](https://pages.vassar.edu/mccleary/files/2011/04/MC08bis.fin_.pdf)

[Cochran and Harvey, Introduction](https://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/document?doi=0bcc9546b436e84c2099f89be24699e31bf14276&repid=rep1&type=pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC and a group homomorphism $\phi:A\to B$ satisfying the stated
$H_1$ and $H_2$ hypotheses.

[A1] Full AC, written AC, is [[def-axiom-of-choice]]; it is inherited from the
group-extension homology sequence supplier.

[F1] For every group extension $1\to N\to G\to Q\to1$, the exact sequence
$H_2(G)\to H_2(Q)\to N/[G,N]\to H_1(G)\to H_1(Q)\to0$ is natural in maps of
extensions. [[thm-five-term-homology-sequence-for-group-extensions]]

[L1] AC implies DC by choosing one successor at each stage of a serial relation. [[def-dependent-choice]]

[F2] In the bar complex, degree one has generators $[x]$ and degree-two boundaries $[y]-[xy]+[x]$, so $H_1(X;\mathbb Z)\cong X/[X,X]$. [[lem-diagonal-bar-coinvariants-compute-group-homology]]

## Proof

**Given:** The group map and hypotheses above.

1.1 By [A1] and [L1], the DC condition of the bar-homology supplier in [F2] holds. The case $n=1$ is the map between two trivial quotients. For $n=2$, the induced map $A/\Gamma_2A\to B/\Gamma_2B$ is exactly the assumed isomorphism on $H_1$ by [F2]. These are the base cases. [A1, L1, F2, given]

1.2 Fix $n\ge2$ and assume $A/\Gamma_nA\to B/\Gamma_nB$ is an isomorphism. Apply [F1] to the extensions $1\to\Gamma_nA\to A\to A/\Gamma_nA\to1$ and $1\to\Gamma_nB\to B\to B/\Gamma_nB\to1$. Since $\Gamma_nX\subseteq[X,X]$ for $n\ge2$, the maps $H_1(X)\to H_1(X/\Gamma_nX)$ are isomorphisms. Exactness therefore makes the transgression $H_2(X/\Gamma_nX)\to\Gamma_nX/[X,\Gamma_nX]$ onto, with kernel the image of $H_2(X)$. By definition $[X,\Gamma_nX]=\Gamma_{n+1}X$. [A1, F1, F2, given, algebra]

2.1 Naturality of [F1] makes the map $H_2(A/\Gamma_nA)\to H_2(B/\Gamma_nB)$ compatible with the two transgressions. It is an isomorphism because the quotient-group map is an isomorphism by the induction hypothesis. The epimorphism $H_2(A)\to H_2(B)$ makes the image of $H_2(A)$ in $H_2(A/\Gamma_nA)$ map onto the image of $H_2(B)$ in $H_2(B/\Gamma_nB)$. The induced map on the two cokernels is consequently an isomorphism. By step 1.2 and exactness, those cokernels are $\Gamma_nA/\Gamma_{n+1}A$ and $\Gamma_nB/\Gamma_{n+1}B$. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The inclusions and quotient maps give exact central extensions $$1\to\Gamma_nX/\Gamma_{n+1}X\to X/\Gamma_{n+1}X\to X/\Gamma_nX\to1, \qquad X=A,B,$$ because $[X,\Gamma_nX]=\Gamma_{n+1}X$. The maps on the kernel and quotient terms are isomorphisms by step 2.1 and the induction hypothesis. The middle map is injective: an element in its kernel projects to the identity in the quotient, hence lies in the kernel term, where injectivity holds. It is surjective: for a target element, lift its quotient class through the quotient isomorphism and then correct the chosen middle lift by a kernel element using the kernel isomorphism. Thus $A/\Gamma_{n+1}A\to B/\Gamma_{n+1}B$ is an isomorphism. [step 2.1, algebra, choose]

4.1 Steps 1.1 and 3.1 prove by induction the isomorphism for every finite $n$. Apart from the inherited AC used to obtain the homology sequence [F1], the induction uses only exactness and a single element lift at a time; no additional choice principle is used. [A1, step 1.1, step 3.1] ∎

## Statement

Assume full AC. For every smooth knot $K\subset S^3$, the rational sutured instanton knot homology $KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$ is finite-dimensional and has dimension at least one; it has dimension one if and only if $K$ is the unknot. Moreover, excision gives an isomorphism $I^\natural(K;\mathbb Q)\cong KHI(K;\mathbb Q)$.

## Statement references

[[def-singular-instanton-knot-and-sutured-closure-data|Sutured closure and KHI eigenspace]]

[[lem-knot-exterior-is-irreducible|Irreducibility of a knot exterior]]

[[lem-nontrivial-knot-exterior-boundary-incompressible|Boundary incompressibility for a nontrivial knot]]

[Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, sutures and excision* (2008), Definition 7.13, Proposition 7.16, and §§7.5, 7.8](https://arxiv.org/pdf/0807.4891v2)

[Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Knots, three-manifolds and instantons* (2018), Proposition 4.6 and §5.1](https://math.pku.edu.cn/puremath/docs/2018-10/20181010175415114589.pdf)

[Kronheimer–Mrowka, *Khovanov homology is an unknot-detector* (2011), Proposition 1.4 and §5.4](https://people.math.harvard.edu/~kronheim/khovanov-unknot.pdf)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC, a smooth classical knot $K\subset S^3$, its two oppositely oriented meridional sutures, and the chosen admissible closure from the preceding definition. ## Statement

Assume full AC. Any two connected reduced alternating diagrams on the oriented projection sphere that represent the same oriented link type are related by a finite sequence of sphere planar isotopies and flypes. Composite links are included; the diagrams are required to be connected, and a plane drawing is interpreted as a punctured projection sphere.

## Statement references

[Menasco and Thistlethwaite, *The classification of alternating links* (1993)](https://doi.org/10.2307/2946636)

[Menasco, *Closed incompressible surfaces in alternating knot and link complements*, Theorem 1(b)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(84)90023-5)

[Kindred, *A geometric proof of the flyping theorem*, arXiv:2008.06490v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.06490v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and connected reduced alternating diagrams $D_0,D_1$ of the same oriented link type, on oriented projection spheres. Fix a smooth oriented link isotopy identifying their represented links and hence their oriented component correspondence.

[F1] A connected alternating diagram represents a nonsplit link ([[lem-connected-alternating-link-is-nonsplit]]).

[F2] A connected reduced alternating diagram realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link, under countable choice, which follows here from full AC ([[thm-reduced-alternating-diagram-minimizes-crossings]]).

[F3] **Imported external prime theorem.** For reduced prime oriented alternating link diagrams and a given orientation-preserving homeomorphism of their represented oriented link pairs, the Menasco–Thistlethwaite Main Theorem gives a finite composite of flypes and flat pair maps inducing that given map's oriented component correspondence. A flat pair map is pair-isotopic to one that restricts on the projection band to $h_0\times\mathrm{id}$ for an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h_0:S^2\to S^2$ carrying the decorated diagrams; these definitions and Theorem 2.10 are recorded in [Fontaine, §2.2, Definitions 2.8–2.9 and Theorem 2.10, pp. 11–12](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~bfontain/partiii.pdf). The imported theorem is Menasco and Thistlethwaite's [Main Theorem, p. 116](https://doi.org/10.2307/2946636) of *The classification of alternating links* (1993), not a locally reconstructed proof of its prime case. Its elementary crossing-centered flypes have the turnover convention of [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]. The published planar maps are topological; their conversion to smooth sphere planar isotopies is proved in step 6.1 below. The actual Main-Theorem statement on p. 116 was inspected, but the entire published 59-page proof is not claimed independently reverified here.

[F4] **Imported external primeness theorem.** A connected reduced alternating projection with no simple circle meeting it transversely in two ordinary points and having crossings on both sides represents a prime link, provided the represented link is nontrivial. This is the diagrammatic primeness consequence of Menasco, *Closed incompressible surfaces in alternating knot and link complements* (1984), Theorem 1(b), printed p. 37, with proof on pp. 41–42. The theorem applies to links, not only knots. It is imported here rather than reconstructed from the other normal-form research.

[F5] Given two finite decomposition-sphere systems of the same nonsplit oriented link with nontrivial prime capped factors and their reduced alternating factor diagrams, the component-marked comparison and lift applies. Its actual factor correspondences retain the oriented global component names, cap parameters, roots and boundary collars. Supplying the prime flype sequences with those induced component maps yields the original diagram sequence; no puncture-relative prime theorem is required ([[lem-component-marked-prime-decomposition-comparisons-lift-prime-flype-sequences]]).

[F6] Reducedness, alternatingness, sphere planar isotopy and flypes have the stated diagram meanings ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]], [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]], [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]). All chosen cuts below avoid crossings and carry the strand orientations.

[F7] A smooth embedded circle on the projection sphere bounds smooth disk sides, and every orientation-preserving smooth boundary diffeomorphism between such disks extends over them with a matching collar ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-jordan-disk-parameters-and-prescribed-collars]]).

[F8] Every orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism of $S^2$ is joined to the identity by a jointly smooth isotopy through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms ([[lem-smooth-sphere-diffeomorphisms-extend-over-balls]]).

## Proof

1.1 Identify the two represented oriented links with one smooth link $L$ by the given isotopy. It is nonsplit by [F1]. Full AC supplies the choice hypotheses of [F2] and [F5]. The identification retains the actual oriented component correspondence to be used in all capped factors. [given, F1, F2, F5, construct]

1.2 In either diagram choose a smooth simple circle meeting the diagram transversely in two ordinary points whenever both sides contain crossings. By [F7] its two sides are smooth disks, so cap each cut arc by a crossing-free arc in its cap disk, carrying the endpoint pairing and orientation. Both capped shadows are connected: an additional shadow component on either side would already have been a separate component of the original shadow. Their crossing sets partition that of the piece being cut. The capped diagrams are alternating. The one proper projected arc has an even number of crossing encounters: its self-crossings contribute two visits each, and its intersections with each closed projected component are even. For the latter, decompose the closed component's finite mod-two edge set into simple cycles. Each cycle separates by [F7], and the proper arc begins and ends on the disk boundary outside those cycles, so it crosses each cycle evenly. The first and last encounters on the proper arc therefore have opposite over-under status. Closing its ends introduces no new encounter. [given, F6, F7, construct]

2.1 If $L$ is the unknot, [F2] forces both diagrams to have zero crossings. A connected crossing-free diagram is one embedded oriented circle on the projection sphere, and the two such circles are carried to one another by a sphere planar isotopy with their orientations transported. This proves the conclusion in this case. Henceforth $L$ is nontrivial and both diagrams have positive crossing count. [given, F2, F6, step 1.1, construct]

2.2 The capped diagrams are reduced. Indeed, a nugatory separator through an old crossing in a capped diagram can be moved off the crossing-free cap disk: each part in that disk lies in one of the two complementary disks of its cap arc and can be pushed to the boundary collar. It would then give a nugatory separator through the same crossing in the original piece, contrary to reducedness. The cut and caps have smooth product collars. In the represented link they are the usual twice-punctured decomposition sphere and its standard trivial-arc cap balls. [F6, F7, step 1.2, construct]

3.1 Repeat these cuts in the capped pieces, retaining their cap-ball parameters and attachment collars. A later cut is moved off the interiors of earlier cap balls using their crossing-free trivial-arc product collars; equivalently shorten each artificial cap into its boundary collar before choosing the next cut. Lifting the resulting finite diagrammatic connected-sum decomposition gives pairwise disjoint decomposition spheres in the original link. Termination is finite: if a piece with $a+b$ crossings is replaced by two pieces with $a,b>0$ crossings, the sum of squared crossing counts falls by $2ab$. The final positive-crossing capped diagrams are therefore connected, reduced, alternating and have no two-point splitting circle with crossings on both sides. Crossing-free trivial connectors are suppressed while retaining all other attachment collars. [F6, F7, step 1.2, step 2.2, construct, algebra]

4.1 Every positive-crossing terminal factor is nontrivial by [F2]; otherwise its reduced alternating crossing count would be zero. It is nonsplit by [F1] and prime by [F4]. Thus the two finite systems just constructed, with their actual cap parameters, factor diagrams and oriented component labels, satisfy exactly the decomposition hypotheses of [F5]. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 3.1]

## Statement

Assume full AC. Any two connected reduced alternating diagrams on the oriented projection sphere that represent the same oriented link type are related by a finite sequence of sphere planar isotopies and flypes. Composite links are included; the diagrams are required to be connected, and a plane drawing is interpreted as a punctured projection sphere.

## Statement references

[Menasco and Thistlethwaite, *The classification of alternating links* (1993)](https://doi.org/10.2307/2946636)

[Menasco, *Closed incompressible surfaces in alternating knot and link complements*, Theorem 1(b)](https://doi.org/10.1016/0040-9383(84)90023-5)

[Kindred, *A geometric proof of the flyping theorem*, arXiv:2008.06490v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2008.06490v3)

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** Full AC and connected reduced alternating diagrams $D_0,D_1$ of the same oriented link type, on oriented projection spheres. Fix a smooth oriented link isotopy identifying their represented links and hence their oriented component correspondence.

[F1] A connected alternating diagram represents a nonsplit link ([[lem-connected-alternating-link-is-nonsplit]]).

[F2] A connected reduced alternating diagram realizes the crossing number of its underlying unoriented link, under countable choice, which follows here from full AC ([[thm-reduced-alternating-diagram-minimizes-crossings]]).

[F3] **Imported external prime theorem.** For reduced prime oriented alternating link diagrams and a given orientation-preserving homeomorphism of their represented oriented link pairs, the Menasco–Thistlethwaite Main Theorem gives a finite composite of flypes and flat pair maps inducing that given map's oriented component correspondence. A flat pair map is pair-isotopic to one that restricts on the projection band to $h_0\times\mathrm{id}$ for an orientation-preserving homeomorphism $h_0:S^2\to S^2$ carrying the decorated diagrams; these definitions and Theorem 2.10 are recorded in [Fontaine, §2.2, Definitions 2.8–2.9 and Theorem 2.10, pp. 11–12](https://pi.math.cornell.edu/~bfontain/partiii.pdf). The imported theorem is Menasco and Thistlethwaite's [Main Theorem, p. 116](https://doi.org/10.2307/2946636) of *The classification of alternating links* (1993), not a locally reconstructed proof of its prime case. Its elementary crossing-centered flypes have the turnover convention of [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]. The published planar maps are topological; their conversion to smooth sphere planar isotopies is proved in step 3.2 below. The actual Main-Theorem statement on p. 116 was inspected, but the entire published 59-page proof is not claimed independently reverified here.

[F4] **Imported external primeness theorem.** A connected reduced alternating projection with no simple circle meeting it transversely in two ordinary points and having crossings on both sides represents a prime link, provided the represented link is nontrivial. This is the diagrammatic primeness consequence of Menasco, *Closed incompressible surfaces in alternating knot and link complements* (1984), Theorem 1(b), printed p. 37, with proof on pp. 41–42. The theorem applies to links, not only knots. It is imported here rather than reconstructed from the other normal-form research.

[F5] Given two finite decomposition-sphere systems of the same nonsplit oriented link with nontrivial prime capped factors and their reduced alternating factor diagrams, the component-marked comparison and lift applies. Its actual factor correspondences retain the oriented global component names, cap parameters, roots and boundary collars. Supplying the prime flype sequences with those induced component maps yields the original diagram sequence; no puncture-relative prime theorem is required ([[lem-component-marked-prime-decomposition-comparisons-lift-prime-flype-sequences]]).

[F6] Reducedness, alternatingness, sphere planar isotopy and flypes have the stated diagram meanings ([[def-reduced-alternating-link-diagram]], [[def-planar-isotopy-of-link-diagrams]], [[def-flype-crossing-ball-and-alternating-tangle-data]]). All chosen cuts below avoid crossings and carry the strand orientations.

[F7] A smooth embedded circle on the projection sphere bounds smooth disk sides, and every orientation-preserving smooth boundary diffeomorphism between such disks extends over them with a matching collar ([[lem-choice-free-smooth-jordan-disk-parameters-and-prescribed-collars]]).

[F8] Every orientation-preserving smooth diffeomorphism of $S^2$ is joined to the identity by a jointly smooth isotopy through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms ([[lem-smooth-sphere-diffeomorphisms-extend-over-balls]]).

1.1 Identify the two represented oriented links with one smooth link $L$ by the given isotopy. It is nonsplit by [F1]. Full AC supplies the choice hypotheses of [F2] and [F5]. The identification retains the actual oriented component correspondence to be used in all capped factors. [given, F1, F2, F5, construct]

1.2 If $L$ is the unknot, [F2] forces both diagrams to have zero crossings. A connected crossing-free diagram is one embedded oriented circle on the projection sphere, and the two such circles are carried to one another by a sphere planar isotopy with their orientations transported. This proves the conclusion in this case. Henceforth $L$ is nontrivial and both diagrams have positive crossing count. [given, F2, F6, step 1.1, construct]

2.1 In either diagram choose a smooth simple circle meeting the diagram transversely in two ordinary points whenever both sides contain crossings. Their crossing sets partition that of the piece being cut. The capped diagrams are alternating. The one proper projected arc has an even number of crossing encounters: its self-crossings contribute two visits each, and its intersections with each closed projected component are even. 2.3 Repeat these cuts in the capped pieces, retaining their cap-ball parameters and attachment collars. 2.4 Every positive-crossing terminal factor is nontrivial by [F2]; otherwise its reduced alternating crossing count would be zero. It is nonsplit by [F1] and prime by [F4]. [F1, F2, F4, F5, step 2.3]

3.1 Apply the comparison part of [F5] to those two systems in $L$. It provides the corresponding capped prime factors and actual oriented factor isotopies needed by its lift, including all refinements and suppressed trivial connectors. The correspondence transports the fixed global component names and attachment data from step 1.1. [F5, step 1.1, step 2.4, construct]

3.2 For each corresponding pair of prime factor diagrams needed in that comparison, apply the imported theorem [F3] to the orientation-preserving pair map induced by its actual capped-factor isotopy. By [F7] extend the matched boundary maps over these disk faces with product collars. Gluing produces an orientation-preserving smooth sphere diffeomorphism $g$ inducing exactly $\phi$'s decorated graph map and component bijection. By [F8], $g$ is joined to the identity by a jointly smooth orientation-preserving isotopy. Thus each topological planar map supplied by [F3] is realized by a sphere planar isotopy in the definition, with the prescribed oriented component correspondence. [F3, F6, F7, F8, step 3.1, construct]

3.3 The lift in [F5] now applies with its exact marked prime input supplied by step 3.2. It realizes the attachment transfers and prime sequences by finitely many allowed flypes and sphere planar isotopies, giving $D_0$ to $D_1$ with the fixed oriented component correspondence. Together with the crossing-free case, this proves the stated theorem for connected reduced alternating diagrams, including composite links. [F5, step 1.2, step 3.1, step 3.2] ∎

## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every finite rational polygonal code that records one oriented circle, finitely many transverse double points, and one overpassing branch at each double point, and every basepoint in the interior of an edge, if the first encounter at each crossing is the overpassing branch, then the represented knot is ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms to the standard unknot.

## Statement references

[[def-knot-planar-code|Finite planar code and represented knot diagram]]

[[alg-descending-diagram-unknotting-sequence|The based traversal that produces a descending diagram]]

[[lem-one-extremum-arc-is-boundary-parallel]]

[[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]]

## Facts & Assumptions

**Given:** AC$_\omega$, an admissible finite code $D$, its oriented diagram, and a basepoint in the interior of an edge.

[A1] The Axiom of Countable Choice, written AC$_\omega$. [[def-countable-choice]]

[F1] A valid code represents a smooth regular diagram after its finitely many bend vertices are smoothed; one base edge has a crossing-free subarc around the basepoint. [[def-knot-planar-code]]

[F2] Under AC$_\omega$, every smooth isotopy of embeddings of the compact source circle into the boundaryless $S^3$ extends to an ambient isotopy. [[def-oriented-link-in-s-three-and-ambient-isotopy]], [[thm-isotopy-extension]]

[F3] A proper arc with one height maximum or minimum in a height ball bounds a disk with any prescribed simple boundary arc on its level sphere. [[lem-one-extremum-arc-is-boundary-parallel]]

[F4] A smooth oriented knot bounds a genus-zero spanning surface if and only if it is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot. [[lem-knot-genus-zero-iff-unknot]]

## Proof

**Given:** The code and hypotheses in the statement.


1.1 Cut the based circle at a small crossing-free subarc around the basepoint. Orient the cut subarc from the endpoint where the remaining long arc ends to the endpoint where it begins. Identify the plane with the equatorial sphere $S_0\subset S^3$ minus one point, and write the projected long arc as $\gamma(t)\in S_0$, $0\le t\le1$, and the cut subarc as $\delta(s)\in S_0$, $0\le s\le1$. Thus $\gamma(1)=\delta(0)$ and $\delta(1)=\gamma(0)$. Choose $a=1/2$ and lift these paths by
$$\widehat\gamma(t)=\bigl(\sqrt{1-a^2\cos^2(\pi t)}\,\gamma(t),\ a\cos(\pi t)\bigr),\qquad \widehat\delta(s)=\bigl(\sqrt{1-a^2\cos^2(\pi s)}\,\delta(s),\ -a\cos(\pi s)\bigr).$$
The first height strictly decreases from $a$ to $-a$ and the second strictly increases from $-a$ to $a$; their first derivatives vanish at the joins and their second derivatives match. Reparametrize the projected paths near their endpoints to match the smooth based-diagram jets. The resulting closed knot is smooth and has exactly one maximum and one minimum. The projected cut subarc is disjoint from the rest of the diagram except at its endpoints. [given, F1, construct]

2.1 At every double point of $\gamma$, the first encounter occurs at smaller $t$ and therefore has strictly larger fourth coordinate; hence the lifted knot has exactly the prescribed overpassing branch at every crossing. The long lifted arc is embedded because its fourth coordinate is strictly monotone, and the base subarc is disjoint from its projection away from the endpoints, so their union is an embedding. To identify this lift with the knot represented by the diagram, let $z_0$ be the smooth height function of any realizing lift over the same smoothed projected circle, and let $z_1$ be the height function specified in step 1.1. For $0\le u\le1$, set $z_u=(1-u)z_0+uz_1$. This is a jointly smooth family with values in $(-1,1)$, since the compact image of $z_0$ lies in $(-1,1)$ and $|z_1|\le1/2$. At every crossing the first-encounter inequality holds for both $z_0$ and $z_1$, so it holds strictly for every $z_u$; distinct projected points remain distinct, and the projected derivative is nonzero. Thus the corresponding lifts form a smooth isotopy of embeddings of the compact circle. By [F2] it extends to an ambient isotopy, proving that the constructed lift represents the same knot as the descending diagram. [A1, F1, F2, step 1.1, construct]

3.1 Choose the regular level $S_0$ between the unique minimum and maximum. It cuts the lifted knot into an upper proper arc with one maximum and a lower proper arc with one minimum. Choose one simple joining arc on $S_0$. By [F3], each proper arc bounds an embedded disk with that same joining arc; push their interiors into the opposite open balls, so the disks intersect only in the joining arc. Their union, after smoothing its corner, is an embedded genus-zero spanning surface for the knot. [F3, step 2.1, construct]

4.1 Apply [F4] to the spanning disk of step 3.1. The lifted knot, and therefore the represented descending diagram by step 2.1, is ambient isotopic to the standard unknot. [F4, step 2.1, step 3.1] ∎

citations.quote: Let $V=S^1\times D^2$ be the standard oriented solid torus, with oriented core $S^1\times\{0\}$. A **pattern** is a smooth oriented knot $P$ contained in the interior of $V$, together with a chosen closed tubular neighbourhood $N(P)$ contained in the interior of $V$. Its **winding number** $w(P)$ is the integer by which the homology class $[P]$ maps to $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)\cong\mathbb Z$ under the isomorphism that sends the oriented core to $1$. The **pattern exterior** is $X_P=V\setminus\operatorname{int}N(P)$; its **outer torus** is $\partial V$ and its **inner torus** is $\partial N(P)$. A **companion** is a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$ with a specified orientation-preserving tubular embedding $e:V\to S^3$ that sends the core to $K$ and identifies the solid-torus meridian and product longitude with the positive meridian and preferred longitude of $K$. citations.quote: An oriented circle is a smooth one-dimensional manifold diffeomorphic to the standard oriented circle. An abstract oriented cobordism from an oriented circle $C_0$ to an oriented circle $C_1$ is a compact oriented smooth surface $F$ together with orientation-preserving identifications of its incoming and outgoing boundary components such that $\partial F=-C_0\sqcup C_1$. Here $-C_0$ denotes the same circle with its orientation reversed. The cobordism is abstract: no embedding of $F$, $C_0$, or $C_1$ into a common three- or four-manifold is included in the data.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice when a knot's Seifert pairing is formed. An integral Seifert lattice is a pair $(H,V)$ in which $H$ is a free abelian group of rank $2g$ for some $g\geq0$, and $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ is bilinear with $V-V^T$ unimodular. The rank-zero lattice is allowed, with the determinant of its empty skew matrix equal to $1$. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand $M\subset H$ of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$; the lattice is metabolic when it has a metabolizer. A chosen Seifert surface of an oriented knot gives such a lattice through the positive-push pairing. Its form is algebraically slice when that lattice is metabolic.

An isomorphism of integral Seifert lattices $(H,V)$ and $(H',V')$ is an integral group isomorphism $P:H\to H'$ satisfying $V'(Px,Py)=V(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in H$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the commutative monoid of these isomorphism classes under orthogonal direct sum, where $(H,V)\oplus(H',V')$ has underlying group $H\oplus H'$ and pairing $V\oplus V'$, with the rank-zero lattice as identity. The integral algebraic concordance group $G_{\mathbb Z}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[V]$ for $[V]\in\mathcal S$, subject to $[V\oplus W]=[V]+[W]$ and $[M]=0$ for every metabolic lattice $M$. Two selected Seifert forms are algebraically concordant when they represent the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$. This form relation does not assert the existence of a smooth or locally flat topological concordance annulus between the knots.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the unit four-ball $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.

Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$ with boundary an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected oriented Seifert surface for $K$. After matching product collars and pushing the interior of $F$ slightly into $B^4$, the closed locally flat surface $\Sigma=F\cup_KD$ bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold $R\subset B^4$. The conclusion includes an oriented ambient product neighborhood of $R$ on both sides, with the positive normal push-off along the $F$ portion of $\partial R=\Sigma$ lying on the complementary side of $R$.

derivations.claim: Let $C_0$ be the oriented circle underlying $U$ and $C_1$ the oriented circle underlying $T$. Take the abstract annulus $S^1\times[0,1]$ and identify its lower and upper boundary circles orientation-preservingly with $C_0$ and $C_1$, orienting the annulus so its boundary is $-C_0\sqcup C_1$. By [F1] this is an abstract oriented cobordism from $U$ to $T$.

For the fixed trefoil matrix in [F3], $$V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}.$$ Its characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2+4\lambda+3=(\lambda+1)(\lambda+3)$, so its eigenvalues are $-1,-3$ and its signature is $-2$. More directly, for $x=(a,b)\ne0$ over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$,
$$x^T(V+V^T)x=-2(a^2-ab+b^2)=-(a-b)^2-a^2-b^2<0.$$
Consequently $V$ cannot have a rank-one metabolizer: a nonzero vector in one would have zero value by [F5]. This is a calculation for the displayed Seifert surface and basis; no knot-level signature invariance is being inferred. The unknot's rank-zero form in [F4] still has signature zero.

If $U$ were smoothly concordant to $T$, reverse the interval coordinate to obtain smooth concordance of $T$ to the unknot. By [F6] and [A2], $T$ would bound a smooth proper disk. Apply the proved smooth branch [F7] to the particular trefoil Seifert surface in [F3]. It gives a rank-one metabolizer for $V$, contradicting the strict negative-definiteness calculation and [F5] in step 2.1. Thus the displayed abstract oriented annulus has no realization as a smooth concordance between its specified endpoint knots, refuting the claimed universal realization. citations.quote: An oriented circle is a smooth one-dimensional manifold diffeomorphic to the standard oriented circle. An abstract oriented cobordism from an oriented circle $C_0$ to an oriented circle $C_1$ is a compact oriented smooth surface $F$ together with orientation-preserving identifications of its incoming and outgoing boundary components such that $\partial F=-C_0\sqcup C_1$. Here $-C_0$ denotes the same circle with its orientation reversed. The cobordism is abstract: no embedding of $F$, $C_0$, or $C_1$ into a common three- or four-manifold is included in the data.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.

For disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\setminus L;\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\theta_F(x,y)=\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. The surface and basis are part of the data; this definition asserts no knot-only matrix invariant.

Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

Assume the full Axiom of Choice when a knot's Seifert pairing is formed. An integral Seifert lattice is a pair $(H,V)$ in which $H$ is a free abelian group of rank $2g$ for some $g\geq0$, and $V:H\times H\to\mathbb Z$ is bilinear with $V-V^T$ unimodular. The rank-zero lattice is allowed, with the determinant of its empty skew matrix equal to $1$. A metabolizer is a primitive direct summand $M\subset H$ of rank $g$ such that $V(x,y)=0$ for every $x,y\in M$; the lattice is metabolic when it has a metabolizer. A chosen Seifert surface of an oriented knot gives such a lattice through the positive-push pairing. Its form is algebraically slice when that lattice is metabolic.

An isomorphism of integral Seifert lattices $(H,V)$ and $(H',V')$ is an integral group isomorphism $P:H\to H'$ satisfying $V'(Px,Py)=V(x,y)$ for all $x,y\in H$. Let $\mathcal S$ be the commutative monoid of these isomorphism classes under orthogonal direct sum, where $(H,V)\oplus(H',V')$ has underlying group $H\oplus H'$ and pairing $V\oplus V'$, with the rank-zero lattice as identity. The integral algebraic concordance group $G_{\mathbb Z}$ is the abelian group generated by symbols $[V]$ for $[V]\in\mathcal S$, subject to $[V\oplus W]=[V]+[W]$ and $[M]=0$ for every metabolic lattice $M$. Two selected Seifert forms are algebraically concordant when they represent the same element of $G_{\mathbb Z}$. This form relation does not assert the existence of a smooth or locally flat topological concordance annulus between the knots.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. A smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere bounds a smooth properly embedded disk in the unit four-ball $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ if and only if it is smoothly concordant to the standard unknot.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

In ZF,

$$\mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{DC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_\omega\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,\mathrm{fin}}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_{\omega,2},\qquad \mathrm{AC}\Longrightarrow\mathrm{AC}_2.$$

DC here includes a prescribed initial point.

Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $D\subset B^4$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk with oriented boundary $K$. Then the positive-push Seifert lattice $(H_1(F;\mathbb Z),V)$ is metabolic: it has a rank-$g$ primitive direct summand on which $V$ vanishes identically.

Assume full AC. Let $D$ be a locally flat properly embedded disk in the standard four-ball $B^4$ with boundary an oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, and let $F\subset S^3$ be a connected oriented Seifert surface for $K$. After matching product collars and pushing the interior of $F$ slightly into $B^4$, the closed locally flat surface $\Sigma=F\cup_KD$ bounds a compact connected oriented locally flat three-manifold $R\subset B^4$. The conclusion includes an oriented ambient product neighborhood of $R$ on both sides, with the positive normal push-off along the $F$ portion of $\partial R=\Sigma$ lying on the complementary side of $R$.

derivations.claim: Let $C_0$ be the oriented circle underlying $U$ and $C_1$ the oriented circle underlying $T$. Take the abstract annulus $S^1\times[0,1]$ and identify its lower and upper boundary circles orientation-preservingly with $C_0$ and $C_1$, orienting the annulus so its boundary is $-C_0\sqcup C_1$. By [F1] this is an abstract oriented cobordism from $U$ to $T$.

For the fixed trefoil matrix in [F3], $$V+V^T=\begin{pmatrix}-2&1\\1&-2\end{pmatrix}.$$ Its characteristic polynomial is $\lambda^2+4\lambda+3=(\lambda+1)(\lambda+3)$, so its eigenvalues are $-1,-3$ and its signature is $-2$. More directly, for $x=(a,b)\ne0$ over $\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb R$, $$x^T(V+V^T)x=-2(a^2-ab+b^2)=-(a-b)^2-a^2-b^2<0.$$ Consequently $V$ cannot have a rank-one metabolizer: a nonzero vector in one would have zero value by [F5]. This is a calculation for the displayed Seifert surface and basis; no knot-level signature invariance is being inferred. The unknot's rank-zero form in [F4] still has signature zero.

If $U$ were smoothly concordant to $T$, reverse the interval coordinate to obtain smooth concordance of $T$ to the unknot. By [F6] and [A2], $T$ would bound a smooth proper disk. Apply the proved smooth branch [F7] to the particular trefoil Seifert surface in [F3]. It gives a rank-one metabolizer for $V$, contradicting the strict negative-definiteness calculation and [F5] in step 1.2. Thus the displayed abstract oriented annulus has no realization as a smooth concordance between its specified endpoint knots, refuting the claimed universal realization. No locally flat TOP slice-to-metabolizer assertion is used.

citations.quote: Assume full AC. There exists a closed connected simply connected oriented topological four-manifold $Y_{E_8}$ whose integral intersection form is isometric to the positive-definite even unimodular lattice $L_{E_8}$. This is a topological realization statement and does not assert a smooth structure on $Y_{E_8}$.

For the rank-eight lattice $L_{E_8}$ with Gram matrix $C$ specified in its definition, the form is positive definite, has determinant $1$, and takes even values on every vector. It has no vector of squared norm $1$, so it is not isometric to the standard diagonal lattice $\mathbb Z^8$ and admits no isometric full-rank embedding into that lattice.

derivations.claim: Take the manifold $Y_{E_8}$ furnished by [F1]. It is closed, connected, simply connected, oriented and topological, so it meets the asserted manifold hypotheses.

Its intersection form is positive definite by [F2], but the same local lattice result proves it is not isometric to the standard diagonal form. Thus $Y_{E_8}$ satisfies every hypothesis of the refuted assertion and violates its conclusion.

citations.quote: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $I^*$ be the binary icosahedral group, the group of $120$ unit quaternions acting on the unit sphere $S^3$ by left multiplication, and put $P=S^3/I^*$. The quotient is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with universal cover $S^3$ and deck group $I^*$. Then $H_*(P;\mathbb Z)\cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb Z)$ and $\pi_1(P)\cong I^*$ is nontrivial.

For an open cover $X=U\cup V$, the sequence
$$\cdots\to H_n(U\cap V;G)\to H_n(U;G)\oplus H_n(V;G)\to H_n(X;G)\xrightarrow{\delta}H_{n-1}(U\cap V;G)\to\cdots$$
is exact, with middle map $(u,v)\mapsto u+v$.

Assume AC. Fix the usual orientation of $S^n$. If $K$ is a nonempty proper compact weakly locally contractible subspace of $S^n$ and $R$ is a commutative unital ring, there are isomorphisms
$$\widetilde H_i(S^n\setminus K;R)\cong\widetilde H^{n-i-1}(K;R)$$
for every integer $i$. They are natural for inclusions of such compact subsets, with the reverse inclusions of their complements, and with the fixed sphere orientation.

For the nonempty spaces here, reduced homology in degree zero is the augmentation kernel, reduced cohomology in degree zero is the quotient by constant classes, positive reduced groups are ordinary groups, and negative reduced groups are zero. AC is inherited from Poincaré duality and the neighborhood-retract theorem.

For $n\ge1$, $\widetilde H_k(S^n;G)$ is $G$ for $k=n$ and $0$ otherwise.
For $S^0$, $\widetilde H_0(S^0;G)\cong G$ and all other reduced groups vanish.
Thus $H_0(S^n;G)\cong G$ for $n\ge1$, whereas
$H_0(S^0;G)\cong G\oplus G$.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms
$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$
for every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.

Naturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free
$R$-modules, and $G$ an $R$-module. Then naturally
$$0\to\operatorname{Ext}^1_R(H_{n-1}C,G)\to H^n\operatorname{Hom}_R(C,G)\xrightarrow{\operatorname{ev}_n}\operatorname{Hom}_R(H_nC,G)\to0$$
is exact.

derivations.claim: The unknot $U$ bounds its spanning disk inside $B_0$, so $[U]=0$ in $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)$. For $X=P\setminus\operatorname{int}B^3$, use the collar enlargements [F5] of $X$ and $B^3$ in $P$. They form an open cover, retract to those pieces, and have intersection retracting to $S^2$; apply [F2] to this open cover. Since $H_1(S^2)=0$ by [F3], exactness injects $H_1(X)$ into $H_1(P)=0$, so $H_1(X)=0$. The same exact sequence in degree zero, using $H_1(P)=0$ and $H_0(P)=H_0(S^2)=H_0(B^3)=\mathbb Z$, gives $0\to\mathbb Z\to H_0(X)\oplus\mathbb Z\to\mathbb Z\to0$. Rank comparison yields $H_0(X)\cong\mathbb Z$, so each punctured summand is connected with $H_1=0$.

Apply [F2] to the open collar enlargements [F5] of the two punctured summands in $Y$; the pieces and intersection retract to the punctured summands and $S^2$, respectively. By step 1.1 both summands are connected and have zero $H_1$, and the map $H_0(S^2;\mathbb Z)\to H_0(P\setminus\operatorname{int}B^3;\mathbb Z)\oplus H_0(P\setminus\operatorname{int}B^3;\mathbb Z)$ sends $1$ to $(1,-1)$ and is injective. Exactness gives $H_1(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$. Since $Y$ is closed, connected, and oriented, [F4] gives $H_2(Y;\mathbb Z)=0$ and $H_0(Y;\mathbb Z)=H_3(Y;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$. Hence $Y$ is an integral homology sphere. The duality and UCT uses are under [A1].

for every integer $i$. They are natural for inclusions of such compact subsets, with the reverse inclusions of their complements, and with the fixed sphere orientation.

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$, $n\geq2$, be a bounded smooth domain, and let $\gamma_1,\gamma_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive. If their full physical conductivity Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps agree on all boundary data, then every inward boundary-normal derivative agrees:
$$\partial_{x_n}^k\gamma_1|_{\partial\Omega} =\partial_{x_n}^k\gamma_2|_{\partial\Omega} \qquad(k=0,1,2,\ldots),$$
where $x_n=\operatorname{dist}(x,\partial\Omega)$ in a boundary normal collar.

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice.

Let $(M,g)$ be a compact smooth Riemannian domain with smooth boundary, let $\gamma\in C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ be strictly positive, put $\rho=\sqrt{\gamma}$, and define $q=(\Delta_g\rho)/\rho$. If $v$ solves $\operatorname{div}_g(\gamma\nabla_gv)=0$ and $u=\rho v$, then $u$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q)u=0$. The potential $q$ has trivial Dirichlet kernel. For boundary data $f=v|_{\partial M}$, with $\rho_b=\rho|_{\partial M}$ and the physical flux convention $\Lambda_\gamma f=\gamma\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}v|_{\partial M}$, the exact boundary relation is
$$\Lambda_\gamma f=\rho_b\Lambda_q(\rho_b f)-\rho_b(\partial_{\nu_{\rm out}}\rho)|_{\partial M}f.$$

Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice. Let $n\geq3$, let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^n$ be a bounded, nonempty, connected smooth domain, and let $q_1,q_2\in C^\infty(\overline\Omega,\mathbb R)$. Suppose zero is not a Dirichlet eigenvalue of either $-\Delta+q_j$, and the full Schrödinger Dirichlet-to-Neumann maps satisfy $\Lambda_{q_1}=\Lambda_{q_2}$ on all of $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$. Then $q_1=q_2$ on $\Omega$.

derivations.claim: By [F1], all boundary-normal jets of $\gamma_1$ and $\gamma_2$ agree, so the boundary values and first normal derivatives of $\rho_j=\sqrt{\gamma_j}$ agree. Put $q_j=\Delta_g\rho_j/\rho_j$. Their Liouville boundary relations in [F2], together with $\Lambda_{\gamma_1}=\Lambda_{\gamma_2}$, now give $\Lambda_{q_1}g=\Lambda_{q_2}g$ for every $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$: substitute $f=g/\rho_b$ into the physical-flux relation, using the common positive boundary value $\rho_b$ and common $\partial_\nu\rho_j$. Multiplication and division by smooth positive $\rho_b$ preserve $H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega)$.

Each $q_j$ is nonresonant. If $w\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q_j)w=0$, then $v=w/\rho_j\in H_0^1(\Omega)$ solves $-\operatorname{div}(\gamma_j\nabla v)=0$ by [F2]. Testing weakly with $\overline v$ gives $\int_\Omega\gamma_j|\nabla v|^2dx=0$. Positivity of $\gamma_j$ implies $v=0$, hence $w=0$.

The domain is bounded and smooth in $\mathbb R^3$, the potentials are real and smooth, both operators are nonresonant by step 1.2, and their full Schrödinger DN maps agree by step 1.1. Thus [F3] applies and yields $q_1=q_2=:q$ in $\Omega$.

Each $\rho_j$ solves $(-\Delta_g+q)\rho_j=0$ and the two functions have the same boundary value by step 1.1. Their difference is a zero-trace solution of the nonresonant operator from step 1.2, hence vanishes. Therefore $\rho_1=\rho_2$ and $\gamma_1=\rho_1^2=\rho_2^2=\gamma_2$ in $\Omega$; continuity extends this equality to $\overline\Omega$.
