The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every oriented link $L\subset\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$
is equivalent to the oriented closure $\widehat\beta$ of a geometric braid
$\beta$ on some number $n\ge0$ of strands, with $n\ge1$ when $L$ is nonempty.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their
inverses.

For $n\ge1$, let $\Phi_n$ be the BMW-to-Dubrovnik tangle homomorphism over $T$, let $\widehat{t}$ denote closure of an $(n,n)$ tangle by joining corresponding top and bottom endpoints without a twist, and define
$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$
Then $\tau_n$ is a cyclic $T$-linear trace, compatible with the tower inclusion $\iota_n:BMW_n\to BMW_{n+1}$ that adds one straight strand, and for every $x\in BMW_n$,
$$\tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x))=\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n)=a d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)e_n)=d^{-1}\tau_n(x),$$
where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

Let $n\ge1$ and let $B_n=\langle\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}\mid\text{Artin
relators}\rangle$ be the braid group of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]); recall that $B_0$ and $B_1$
are trivial. The **exponent sum** is the unique homomorphism

$$e_n:B_n\longrightarrow\mathbb Z,\qquad e_n(\sigma_i)=1\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

where $\mathbb Z$ is the additive group of integers. It is well defined because
every defining relator of the Artin presentation has exponent sum $0$: the
braid relator $\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i=\sigma_{i+1}\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}$

sides of exponent sum $2$, so the assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto1$ kills all
relators, and [[thm-von-dyck]] applies. It is surjective for $n\ge2$ and it is

$e_n(\beta^{-1})=-e_n(\beta)$. **Caveat:** $e_n$ is the composite of the
abelianisation $B_n\to B_n^{\mathrm{ab}}$ with a surjection onto the free cyclic
group $\mathbb Z$ (for $n\ge2$): since the target is abelian, every commutator is sent to $0$, so $e_n$ factors through $B_n/[B_n,B_n]$ ([[def-abelianisation-of-a-group]]). No normal form, Garside structure or
faithfulness statement is used anywhere.

Let
$$R_D=\mathbb Z[a^{\pm1},z,d^{\pm1}]/(z(d-1)-(a-a^{-1})),$$
where $z$ is not inverted. A nonempty unoriented regular link diagram is a
finite generic planar projection of one or more circles with only transverse
double crossings and an over/under marking at each crossing. Use the crossing
chart in which the over-strand runs southwest to northeast. Its $D_0$
smoothing joins the left endpoints and the right endpoints (the through
pairing), and its $D_\infty$ smoothing joins the two top endpoints and the two
bottom endpoints (the cup-cap pairing). Thus $D_0$ is the orientation-preserving
smoothing when both crossing strands point downward and the displayed crossing
has positive determinant sign. These are respectively the $A$- and
$B$-smoothings in the stated bracket chart. A positive
curl is a type-I kink whose oriented crossing has determinant sign $+1$; a
negative curl has determinant sign $-1$. The sign is unchanged if the
orientation of the whole component is reversed.

The Dubrovnik regular-isotopy evaluation $P$ is normalized by
$P(\varnothing)=1$, $P(K\sqcup\bigcirc)=dP(K)$, positive and negative curl
factors $a$ and $a^{-1}$, and
$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$
Here $D_+$ and $D_-$ differ only by switching the displayed crossing. For a
nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$
and
$$F_K(A,Z)=A^{-w(K)}L_K(A,Z).$$

retained even when $z$ is not invertible. These are conventions and
normalizations; ambient-isotopy invariance of $F$ is a separate theorem.

For each nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its
determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then
$$D_K(a,z)=-i^{-w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}L_K(ia,-iz),\qquad i^2=-1.$$

whole component. The Dubrovnik value has the stated difference-skein, curl and
circle rules; the Kauffman value has the sum-skein, curl and circle rules; and

diagram moves and uses the universal coefficient relations without dividing
by a skein variable.

In its fixed chart, $D_0$ is through left/right and $D_\infty$ is cup-cap top/bottom. For every $n\ge2$, send the BMW generator $g_i$ to the positive Artin crossing between strands $i,i+1$, its inverse to the negative crossing, and $e_i$ to the adjacent cup-cap tangle. This assignment extends to a unital $T$-algebra homomorphism $\Phi_n:BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta)\to\mathcal{KT}_n(T)$. For $n=0,1$, define the unital $T$-algebra homomorphism by sending each scalar to that scalar times the empty or straight tangle, respectively. Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. Let $D$ and $D'$ be regular oriented link diagrams.

derivations.claim: Fix an oriented link $K$. By [F1], choose a finite signed braid word $\beta_0$ whose oriented closure represents $K$. This use of existence is valid under [A1], as required by [F1]. Define $Q(\beta)$ by the formula in the statement for every braid word with closure equivalent to $K$.

A conjugation $\beta\mapsto\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$ leaves the closure component count unchanged because the strand permutation is conjugated, and leaves writhe unchanged because the exponent sum of $\gamma$ cancels with that of $\gamma^{-1}$. Cyclicity in [F3] gives $\tau_n(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=\tau_n(\beta)$. Thus $Q$ is unchanged by conjugation.

For positive stabilization $\beta'=\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$, the new transposition involving strand $n+1$ joins that new strand to the cycle containing strand $n$, so $c(\beta')=c(\beta)$. The exponent sum increases by one, hence $w(\beta')=w(\beta)+1$. By [F3], $\tau_{n+1}(\beta')=a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$. Therefore $$Q(\beta')=-(-1)^c a^{-(w+1)}d^n\,a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ For negative stabilization the cycle count is again unchanged, the writhe becomes $w-1$, and $\tau_{n+1}(\beta\sigma_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$; substituting gives $$-(-1)^c a^{-(w-1)}d^n a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ Thus both stabilizations and their inverse moves preserve $Q$.

By [F2], any two braid words whose oriented closures represent $K$ are Markov equivalent. Each move in a finite Markov sequence preserves $Q$ by steps 2.1 and 2.2, so $Q$ is independent of the braid representative. For a representative $\beta$, [F7] identifies $\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)}$ with its oriented closure diagram. By [F3], $\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-n}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})$. Hence
$$d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-1}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})=D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)$$
by [F6]. Applying the conversion in [F6] gives
$$F_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=(ia)^{-w}L_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^c a^{-w}D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)=Q(\beta).$$
The scalar conversion lemma proves that $F$ is unchanged by each oriented Reidemeister move; [F8] therefore identifies this fixed-diagram value with the declared ambient-isotopy value of $K$. AC is used in [F1], [F2], and [F8]; the trace and local formula calculations are choice-free.

> (Choice function).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every oriented link $L\subset\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$
is equivalent to the oriented closure $\widehat\beta$ of a geometric braid
$\beta$ on some number $n\ge0$ of strands, with $n\ge1$ when $L$ is nonempty.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\beta,\beta'$ be braids. Then
$\widehat\beta$ and $\widehat{\beta'}$ are equivalent oriented links if and
only if $\beta$ and $\beta'$ are Markov equivalent, that is, related by a finite
sequence of conjugations in a fixed braid group, stabilizations
$\beta\mapsto\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ into the next braid group, and their
inverses.

For $n\ge1$, let $\Phi_n$ be the BMW-to-Dubrovnik tangle homomorphism over $T$, let $\widehat{t}$ denote closure of an $(n,n)$ tangle by joining corresponding top and bottom endpoints without a twist, and define
$$\tau_n(x)=d^{-n}P\!\left(\widehat{\Phi_n(x)}\right),\qquad x\in BMW_n(T;q,\rho,\delta).$$
Then $\tau_n$ is a cyclic $T$-linear trace, compatible with the tower inclusion $\iota_n:BMW_n\to BMW_{n+1}$ that adds one straight strand, and for every $x\in BMW_n$,
$$\tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x))=\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n)=a d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)g_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(x),\quad \tau_{n+1}(\iota_n(x)e_n)=d^{-1}\tau_n(x),$$
where $a=\rho$ and $d=\delta$.

Let $n\ge0$ and let $\beta=(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be a geometric braid with
the fixed real basepoints $q_j=((2j-n-1)/(4(n+1)),0)$ and endpoint
permutation $\pi$, as in [[def-geometric-braid-with-setwise-endpoints]].
Identify the disk with $\{x\in\mathbb C:|x|<1\}$ and put
$$V=(D^\circ\times[0,1])/((x,1)\sim(x,0)).$$
The quotient and its topology use [[def-product-topology]] and the circle
$\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ of [[def-circle-as-real-line-mod-integers]].
The interval images
$$s_j=\{[(z_j(t),t)]:0\le t\le1\},\qquad \operatorname{cl}(\beta)=\bigcup_{j=1}^n s_j$$
are the **closure in the open solid torus**. In general an individual
$s_j$ is an interval image, not a closed circle: its last point is the
first point of $s_{\pi(j)}$.

**Components and orientation.** For a cycle
$(j,\pi(j),\ldots,\pi^{k-1}(j))$ concatenate these $k$ strand maps in
that order, with parameter in $[0,k]$. Their endpoints agree in $V$,
so the concatenation factors through $\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$.
It is injective on this circle: points at distinct nonintegral heights
can agree only when their parameters have the same fractional part,
and the distinct strands at that height have distinct disk coordinates;
at integral heights only the specified adjacent endpoints agree.
Thus each cycle gives an embedded circle. Different cycles give
disjoint circles, and every strand belongs to exactly one cycle.
These circles are precisely the connected components of the closure.
The orientation is increasing concatenation parameter. In particular
the number of components equals the number of cycles of $\pi$.

**The standard axis and fixed framing.** In
$S^3=\{(z,w)\in\mathbb C^2:|z|^2+|w|^2=1\}$, as in
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]], set
$$A=\{(0,w):|w|=1\},\qquad P_\theta=\{(z,w)\in S^3:z\ne0,\ \arg z=\theta\}.$$
Fix the following particular diffeomorphism, including its disk framing:
$$\varphi([(x,t)])=  \bigl(\sqrt{1-|x|^2}\,e^{2\pi it},x\bigr):  V\longrightarrow S^3\setminus A.$$
Its inverse has disk coordinate $x=w$ and circle coordinate
$[t]=[\arg z/(2\pi)]$. Every $P_\theta$ is consequently an open disk.
The **raw topological oriented closure** is
$$\widehat\beta_{\mathrm{top}}=\varphi(\operatorname{cl}(\beta)).$$
This explicit $\varphi$ is part of the construction; the definition
does not allow an arbitrary page-preserving change of framing.

**Page intersections and smooth representatives.** The whole closure
meets every page in exactly $n$ points. A component belonging to a
$\pi$-cycle of length $k$ meets each page in exactly $k$ points:
at any fractional height it uses exactly those $k$ distinct strands.
The page coordinate of its concatenation is $[t]$, for
$t\in\mathbb R/k\mathbb Z$, so its oriented degree is $+k$.
If all disk-coordinate strand maps are smooth and have all positive-order derivatives
zero at their endpoints, their cycle concatenations have matching jets
at every seam. The page coordinate has nonzero derivative, so the
result is a smooth embedding of disjoint oriented circles, in the
sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. For an endpoint-flat smooth braid, its literal $\varphi$-image is therefore a smooth oriented link and is denoted $\widehat\beta$.

**Closure in the smooth oriented-link category.** The raw image need not be smooth, even if individual strands are smooth but their endpoint jets fail to match at the cycle seams. For an arbitrary continuous braid, assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ ([[def-countable-choice]]) and choose a smooth representative $\beta_s$ by [[lem-every-geometric-braid-is-braid-isotopic-to-a-smooth-braid]]. Make it endpoint-flat by composing all disk-coordinate strands with a fixed smooth nondecreasing $\psi:I\to I$, equal to $0$ near $0$ and $1$ near $1$. Interpolation of height maps $(1-u)t+u\psi(t)$ is an endpoint-fixed braid isotopy, because every strand is evaluated at the same height. The smooth-category closure of $\beta$ is the oriented-link isotopy class of this chosen model's literal $\varphi$-image; when a subset is needed, use that chosen closed-braid representative. Independence of the representative is proved by [[lem-closure-depends-only-on-the-braid-isotopy-class]]. Page and cycle properties refer to the chosen constructed closed braid, with the same number of strands and endpoint permutation as $\beta$.

If $\beta$ already has smooth strands with matching cycle-seam jets, in particular if it is endpoint-flat, its literal raw image is a smooth link and is retained as $\widehat\beta$. The raw quotient, fixed $\varphi$, finite cycles, page counts and trivial closures remain choice-free. Finite elementary words have explicit smooth endpoint-flat models, so forming their literal closures also requires no choice assumption; $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ is used for the general continuous-representative convention and its independence theorem.

**The trivial closure.** For the constant braid its circles are
$\{(\sqrt{1-q_j^2}e^{2\pi it},q_j):[t]\in\mathbb R/\mathbb Z\}$.
They are latitudes of the sphere
$S=\{(z,w)\in S^3:\operatorname{Im}w=0\}$, with
$\operatorname{Re}w=q_j$. Each northern cap
$C_j=\{p\in S:\operatorname{Re}w(p)\ge q_j\}$ is a smooth disk:
stereographic coordinates on $S$ give radius
$\sqrt{(1-q_j)/(1+q_j)}$ for this cap. To make their spanning disks
disjoint, let $e$ be the unit vector in the $\operatorname{Im}w$
direction, set $\varepsilon=\pi/16$ and
$f_j(p)=\varepsilon(\operatorname{Re}w(p)-q_j)$ on $C_j$, and use
$$F_j(p)=\cos(f_j(p))p+\sin(f_j(p))e.$$
The boundary is fixed. The tubular parametrization
$(p,s)\mapsto\cos(s)p+\sin(s)e$ is injective for $|s|<\pi/2$,
and $0\le f_j<\pi/8$. On overlapping caps, if $q_i<q_j$ then
$f_i-f_j=\varepsilon(q_j-q_i)>0$, so their graphs are disjoint.
Thus these are pairwise disjoint smooth spanning disks. The trivial
$n$-braid closes to the oriented $n$-component unlink; for $n=1$
this is the unknot.

At $n=0$ all strand and cycle unions are empty, every page has zero intersections,
and the closure is the empty link. The basepoint list and disk constructions
above then have no entries.

Let $(B_n)_{n\ge0}$ be the braid groups of the Artin presentation
([[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]), with generators
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$ and the two Artin relations, and let

$$\iota_n\colon B_n\longrightarrow B_{n+1},\qquad \iota_n(\sigma_i):=\sigma_i\quad(1\le i\le n-1),$$

be the **standard inclusion homomorphism**. It is well defined: the defining
relators of $B_n$ are among the defining relators of $B_{n+1}$ under the
assignment $\sigma_i\mapsto\sigma_i$, so [[thm-von-dyck]] extends the
assignment to a homomorphism. Its image is generated by
$\sigma_1,\dots,\sigma_{n-1}$, and we write $\iota_n(\beta)$ for it; whether
this homomorphism is injective is not needed anywhere on this page, and no
subgroup identification is made. For the geometric description, use the base configuration $Q^{(n+1)}$ of
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]]. Express $\beta$ as an Artin word and
replace its letters by the half twists with the same indices at
$Q^{(n+1)}$. The letters with $i<n$ fix the rightmost point, since their support
discs exclude it. This gives a representative of $\iota_n(\beta)$ under
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]]; it is independent
of the word as a geometric braid class. Thus adding the strand on the right
includes expressing the old braid at the first $n$ target basepoints. Those
points differ from $Q^{(n)}$, so the original parametrized strands are not
literally left untouched. The final half twist is the target $\sigma_n$.

On the disjoint union $\bigsqcup_{n\ge0}B_n$ define two kinds of elementary
**Markov moves**.

**Conjugation.** For $\beta,\gamma\in B_n$, replace $\beta$ by
$\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$, an element of the same group $B_n$. The number of
strands does not change. When $\beta$ is a geometric braid and $\gamma$ the
class of a braid in $G_n$, this is realized on closures by reading $\gamma$
around the axis, as the closure-preservation lemma below shows.

**Stabilization and destabilization.** For $n\ge1$ and $\beta\in B_n$ the **positive
stabilization** is $\beta\sigma_n:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n\in B_{n+1}$ and
the **negative stabilization** is
$\beta\sigma_n^{-1}:=\iota_n(\beta)\cdot\sigma_n^{-1}\in B_{n+1}$; the inverse
operations, from $B_{n+1}$ to $B_n$, are called **destabilizations**. Both
signs occur, and the sign is the sign of the exponent of the new generator. By
[[prop-the-artin-presentation-surjects-onto-geometric-braids]] and
[[def-elementary-geometric-half-twist]] the product $\beta\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ is
the class of the target-basepoint geometric word just described, composed
with the target half twist $\sigma_n^{\pm1}$ in its fixed product position;
that half twist fixes the first $n-1$ target points. Inserting the generator inside a factorization need not produce a conjugate of that fixed stabilization. It nevertheless gives a Markov sequence: if $\beta=uv$, old conjugation by $v$ gives $vu$, its right stabilization is $(vu)\sigma_n^{\pm1}$, and conjugation by $v^{-1}$ gives $u\sigma_n^{\pm1}v$. Only moving a factor past the whole word is cyclic conjugacy. At $n=0$ no $\sigma_0$ exists, so the empty braid has only conjugation moves and is an isolated Markov class.

**Markov equivalence.** Two braids $\beta,\beta'$ (possibly with different
numbers of strands) are **Markov equivalent** when they can be connected by a
finite sequence of moves each of which is a conjugation, a positive or negative
stabilization, or a destabilization. Markov equivalence is an equivalence
relation on $\bigsqcup_n B_n$: it is reflexive, symmetric by allowing inverses
of the listed moves, and transitive by concatenating sequences.

**Convention on orientation and side.** All braids are read with the product
and side conventions fixed on the pages `geometric-braids-and-artin-generators`
and `artin-presentation-completeness-and-braid-combing`: the rightmost factor is
traversed first in geometric time, and stabilization always adds the new
strand on the right. The definition is choice-free: no choice principle is used
in the Artin presentation, in the inclusion, or in the identification of
$\sigma_n$ with the elementary geometric half twist.

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ for the smooth normal-bundle structure used in the
framing clause. For a knot component $K$, its normal bundle is the fibrewise
quotient $\nu K=TS^3|_K/TK$, and a normal section is a smooth section of this
bundle.

Let $D$ be a regular oriented link diagram in a projection plane $P$ of an
oriented $3$-sphere, after moving the link off the point at infinity. Fix the
unit viewing normal $n$ pointing toward the viewer. Orient $P$ by the rule that
an ordered basis $(u,v)$ of $P$ is positive exactly when $(n,u,v)$ is a positive
basis of the ambient $3$-space. At a crossing $c$, let $v_{\rm over}$ and
$v_{\rm under}$ be the nonzero projected tangent vectors following the
orientations of the overpassing and underpassing strands. Define
$$\operatorname{sgn}(c):=\operatorname{sgn}\det_P(v_{\rm over},v_{\rm under})\in\{+1,-1\}.$$
Reversing the orientation of $P$ reverses every crossing sign.

This convention makes the positive geometric Artin half twist positive. In
the braid chart $(x,y,t)$ with ambient orientation $(x,y,t)$, view along $+y$;
the induced positive orientation of the $(x,t)$ projection plane is the ordered
basis $(\partial_t,\partial_x)$. For the positive half twist, label $i$ moves
from $x=-h$ to $x=h$ below the midpoint, while label $i+1$ moves from $x=h$ to
$x=-h$ above it, with $h>0$. Thus the over and under projected tangent vectors
in coordinates $(t,x)$ are $(1,-2h)$ and $(1,2h)$, whose determinant is
$4h>0$.

The **writhe** of $D$ is
$$\operatorname{wr}(D):=\sum_{c\text{ a crossing of }D}\operatorname{sgn}(c).$$
For a link component $K_i$, its **self-writhe**
$\operatorname{wr}_i(D)$ is the sum over crossings whose two branches belong to
$K_i$; the total writhe also includes all mixed crossings between distinct
components.

The **blackboard framing** of a component of $D$ is the homotopy class of the
normal section represented by the positive quarter-turn in $P$ of the projected
oriented tangent. The projection is an immersion, so this vector never
vanishes; it is perpendicular to the projected tangent, hence also to the
spatial tangent, and therefore represents a nonzero normal section of the
component in the ambient $3$-sphere.

```tikz
\begin{tikzpicture}[scale=0.8,>=stealth]
  \draw[->] (-1,0) -- (1,0) node[right] {$v_{\rm over}$};
  \draw[->] (0,-1) -- (0,1) node[above] {$v_{\rm under}$};
  \node[above left] at (0,0) {$+1$};
\end{tikzpicture}
```

In the displayed local chart, the over tangent is the positive horizontal
vector and the under tangent is the positive vertical vector, so the determinant
is $+1$. This figure illustrates the determinant rule only; no proof below
depends on a picture.

$$P(D_+)-P(D_-)=z\bigl(P(D_0)-P(D_\infty)\bigr).$$

nonempty oriented link diagram $K$, let $c(K)$ be its number of components and
let $w(K)$ be the sum of the determinant crossing signs. Define
$$D_K(a,z)=d^{-1}P(K),$$
$$L_K(A,Z)=-i^{w(K)}(-1)^{c(K)}D_K(-iA,iZ),\qquad i^2=-1,$$

For each nonempty oriented regular link diagram $K$, let $w(K)$ be its
determinant writhe and $c(K)$ its number of
components, and define $D,L,F$ by the conventions stated for this page. Then

The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

derivations.claim: Fix an oriented link $K$. By [F1], choose a finite signed braid word $\beta_0$ whose oriented closure represents $K$. This use of existence is valid under [A1], as required by [F1]. Define $Q(\beta)$ by the formula in the statement for every braid word with closure equivalent to $K$.

A conjugation $\beta\mapsto\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1}$ leaves the closure component count unchanged because the strand permutation is conjugated, and leaves writhe unchanged because the exponent sum of $\gamma$ cancels with that of $\gamma^{-1}$. Cyclicity in [F3] gives $\tau_n(\gamma\beta\gamma^{-1})=\tau_n(\beta)$. Thus $Q$ is unchanged by conjugation.

For positive stabilization $\beta'=\iota_n(\beta)\sigma_n$, the new transposition involving strand $n+1$ joins that new strand to the cycle containing strand $n$, so $c(\beta')=c(\beta)$. The exponent sum increases by one, hence $w(\beta')=w(\beta)+1$. By [F3], $\tau_{n+1}(\beta')=a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$. Therefore $$Q(\beta')=-(-1)^c a^{-(w+1)}d^n\,a d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ For negative stabilization the cycle count is again unchanged, the writhe becomes $w-1$, and $\tau_{n+1}(\beta\sigma_n^{-1})=a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)$; substituting gives $$-(-1)^c a^{-(w-1)}d^n a^{-1}d^{-1}\tau_n(\beta)=Q(\beta).$$ Thus both stabilizations and their inverse moves preserve $Q$.

By [F2], any two braid words whose oriented closures represent $K$ are Markov equivalent. Each move in a finite Markov sequence preserves $Q$ by steps 2.1 and 2.2, so $Q$ is independent of the braid representative. For a representative $\beta$, [F7] identifies $\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)}$ with its oriented closure diagram. By [F3], $\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-n}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})$. Hence $$d^{n-1}\tau_n(\beta)=d^{-1}P(\widehat{\Phi_n(b_\beta)})=D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)$$ by [F6]. Applying the conversion in [F6] gives $$F_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=(ia)^{-w}L_{\widehat{\beta}}(ia,-iz)=-(-1)^c a^{-w}D_{\widehat{\beta}}(a,z)=Q(\beta).$$ The scalar conversion lemma proves that $F$ is unchanged by each oriented Reidemeister move; [F8] therefore identifies this fixed-diagram value with the declared ambient-isotopy value of $K$. AC is used in [F1], [F2], and [F8]; the trace and local formula calculations are choice-free.

citations.quote: Let knots be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented S³ and let I=[0,1]. Let C_sm be their smooth concordance classes, where equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in S³×I. Let C_top be their locally flat topological concordance classes in that product. Let C_ex be their exotic-smooth concordance classes: equivalence is witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W together with an orientation-preserving homeomorphism of pairs (W,∂W)≅(S³×I,S³×{0,1}) matching the endpoint knots. The annulus is oriented so that its boundary is −K₀ at the lower end and K₁ at the upper end, and it has product collars at both ends agreeing with the ambient boundary collars. For a nonzero integer n set R_n=Z[1/|n|]. Let C^{1/n} be the classes under equivalence witnessed by a smooth proper annulus in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold W with boundary the two standard endpoint 3-spheres such that each boundary inclusion induces an isomorphism H_i(S³;R_n)→H_i(W;R_n) for every i. The annulus is oriented so that its boundary is −K₀ at the lower end and K₁ at the upper end, with product collars at both ends agreeing with the ambient boundary collars. A knot is pseudo-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold homeomorphic to B⁴, with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³. A knot is Z[1/|n|]-slice if it bounds a smooth proper disk in a compact smooth oriented 4-manifold B with its oriented boundary identified with the standard oriented S³ and with H_i(B;R_n)≅H_i(B⁴;R_n) for every i; such a B is an R_n-homology 4-ball. These are sets of equivalence classes; this definition alone asserts no group structure.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For every smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, let $B^4=\{x\in\mathbb R^4:\lVert x\rVert^2\le1\}$ with boundary $S^3$. The oriented connected sum $K\#K^\dagger$ bounds a smooth properly embedded disk $D\subset B^4$ for which the squared radial function $\rho(x)=\lVert x\rVert^2$ restricts to a Morse function on the interior of $D$ with all critical points of index $0$ or $1$.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. On oriented ambient-isotopy classes of smooth knots in $S^3$, the connected-sum operation is associative and commutative, and the standard unknot is a two-sided identity. Here “commutative monoid” means a set with an associative binary operation, a two-sided identity, and equality after interchanging the two inputs.

Fix a coordinate orientation-reversing reflection $r:S^3\to S^3$ for the mirror convention. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere. A connected-sum datum consists of one smoothly embedded closed three-ball around a short subarc of $K$ and one around a short subarc of $J$, each meeting its knot in a single trivial properly embedded arc, together with the fixed standard orientation-reversing boundary identification of the two standard oriented ball boundaries that joins the oriented arcs into one circle. Choose this standard map once in the standard two-ball model so that it commutes with $r$ and an orientation-preserving half-turn interchanging the two balls preserves the joining convention. Here a trivial arc is an embedded interval in a ball that is carried by an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism of ball-arc pairs to a straight diameter. Remove the interiors of the two balls and glue the remaining boundary spheres using this fixed identification; the resulting oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere is a connected sum of $K$ and $J$, denoted $K\#J$ for the specified datum.

The **standard unknot** is the oriented unit circle in a fixed coordinate two-plane of $S^3\subset\mathbb R^4$. A knot is **nontrivial** if it is not ambient isotopic through orientation-preserving diffeomorphisms of $S^3$ to the standard unknot. A nontrivial knot is **prime** if it has no connected-sum presentation whose two summand knots are both nontrivial.

The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, is the following
statement.

> For every family $(X_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by
> $\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\mathbb{N}$ such that
> $f(n) \in X_n$ for every $n \in \mathbb{N}$.

Equivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most
countable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

derivations.claim: Specialize the TOP/exotic external assertion [F5] at each finite list of knot representatives and witnessing annuli actually used. For TOP these lie in the standard product; for exotic concordance the supplied boundary-marked homeomorphism to that product is part of the input code. The finite chart and pair-chart extraction in [F6] uses compactness, not a choice of an atlas for a countable family. Inside $L[r]$ use the ordinary CDR group operation, retain the actual output annulus and marked product homeomorphism, and export their compact forward/inverse and collar certificates. This proves the required finite compatibility and transitivity instances in $V$. Since each instance starts with its own given finite data, no simultaneous choice of representatives or witnesses for all classes is made. The quotient group operations and laws follow by universal quantification over these instances; the original $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ hypothesis is therefore respected, rather than inferred from the unqualified source assertion. The localized category is handled directly by the subsequent homology calculations, with no TOP normal theorem needed.

The supplied connected-sum theorem gives associativity, commutativity and the unknot identity at the level of oriented knot types. The retained standard smooth boundary-sum construction on witnessing annuli gives concordance compatibility in the standard smooth product; the TOP/exotic compatibility is the external input [F5], and the localized ambient verification is given by the subsequent homology calculations. The knot-type isotopies themselves are admissible annuli in every category.

Let $D\subset B^4$ be the smooth ribbon disk for $K\#K^\dagger$ supplied by [F2]. By local smooth coordinates and straightening of the embedded disk, choose an ambiently standard interior 4-ball $B$ such that $B\cap D$ is a standard 2-disk. An ambient isotopy supported in the interior carries $B$ to a concentric standard ball, so its complement in $B^4$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3\times I$. Removing $\operatorname{int}B$ from $B^4$ and the interior of $B\cap D$ from $D$ gives a smooth annulus. The outer and inner boundary collars give product collars for it. Order the ends with $K\#K^\dagger$ at the lower end and the inner standard unknot at the upper end, and orient the annulus so its boundary is $-(K\#K^\dagger)$ at the lower end and $U$ at the upper end. It is therefore an admissible inverse concordance in the smooth category, and the same product annulus satisfies the TOP, exotic and localized ambient conditions.

The external input [F5] supplies the TOP and exotic ambient gluing/compatibility assertions at exactly the definitions in [F1]. For the localized smooth category, transitivity is stacking along the marked $S^3$: Mayer–Vietoris and the two boundary homology isomorphisms give another $R_n$-homology $S^3\times I$. Reflection gives symmetry and a product gives reflexivity, all with their smooth annulus collars.

For localized connected sum choose a smooth product neighborhood $D^3\times I$ of a proper spanning arc inside each witnessing annulus, with the annulus strip in its standard local position, and remove its interior. If $Q$ is the remaining ambient piece, excision gives $H_j(W,Q;R_n)=R_n$ only for $j=3$. The map $H_3(W;R_n)\to H_3(W,Q;R_n)$ is an isomorphism: the boundary fundamental class meets the spanning arc once. The pair sequence therefore makes $Q$ an $R_n$-homology ball. Glue the two such complements on $S^2\times I$, joining the annulus strips. Mayer–Vietoris gives $R_n$ in degrees0 and3 and zero in other positive degrees; the endpoint connected-sum spheres give the degree3 generator, so each end inclusion is a homology isomorphism. The resulting smooth annulus witnesses connected-sum compatibility in the original localized category. These calculations use no homeomorphism-to-product assertion.

Thus connected sum is well defined in every category: the retained standard smooth construction handles $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$, [F5] handles TOP/exotic, and step2.2 handles the localized case. The oriented knot connected-sum monoid [F3] descends to each quotient, giving associativity, commutativity and the unknot identity. The ribbon inverse in [F2], admissible in all four ambients, supplies the stated reverse-mirror inverse. All ambient and coefficient conditions are those of [F1].

citations.quote:
The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.

> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function
> (Choice function).

Written out: for every set $\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,
there exists a function $g$ with domain $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \in S$ for
all $S \in \mathcal{F}$.

An equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if
$X_i \ne \emptyset$ for every $i \in I$, then $\prod_{i \in I} X_i \ne \emptyset$.
Here $\prod_{i \in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that
$f(i) \in X_i$ for every $i \in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by
itself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.

Assume full AC, matching the chosen finite twisted-chain and maximal-abelian-cover conventions. Let K be a smooth oriented knot, M(K) its preferred-longitude zero-framed surgery, W a compact connected oriented smooth 4-manifold with boundary M(K), and π=π₁(W). Put π^(0)=π and π^(j+1)=[π^(j),π^(j)]. A right Zπ-chain complex with coefficients in a left Z[π/π^(j)]-module is formed by tensoring over Zπ with that module.

For n≥0, W is an integral n-solution for K when H₁(M(K);Z)→H₁(W;Z) is an isomorphism, H₂(W;Z) is free of rank 2r for some finite r, and there are classes x₁,…,x_r,y₁,…,y_r in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n)]) whose equivariant intersection pairings satisfy λ_n(x_i,x_j)=0 and λ_n(x_i,y_j)=δ_ij. It is an integral (n+1/2)-solution when, in addition, each x_i is the image of a class x̃_i in H₂(W;Z[π/π^(n+1)]) and λ_{n+1}(x̃_i,x̃_j)=0 for all i,j. Here λ_j is the equivariant intersection pairing induced by the orientation of W.

For a commutative ring R with 1≠0, a group G belongs to Strebel's class D(R) if every homomorphism between projective RG-modules is injective whenever its tensor with the trivial G-module R is injective. In this page R is Q or F_p for a prime p. For a countable discrete group G, its group von Neumann algebra N G is the weak-operator closure of CG in the left regular representation on ℓ²(G), with trace τ_G(T)=⟨Tδ_e,δ_e⟩. The von Neumann dimension of a finitely generated projective N G-module represented by a projection E is τ_G(E); for an arbitrary module it is the supremum of the dimensions of its finitely generated projective submodules.

For a compact oriented 4-manifold W with boundary, sign(W) is the inertia difference of the symmetric intersection form on H₂(W;R) modulo its radical (the subspace pairing to zero with every class), equivalently on the image of H₂(W;R)→H₂(W,∂W;R). Given a closed oriented 3-manifold M, a homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→G, a compact oriented 4-manifold W with ∂W=M, and an extension ψ:π₁(W)→G of φ, the L²-signature sign_G^(2)(W,ψ) is the von Neumann signature of the nonsingular part of the N G-coefficient intersection form. When such a W and extension exist, the signature defect is sign_G^(2)(W,ψ)−sign(W). It is called the rho invariant of (M,φ) only after its independence of the bounding data is established by a separate bordism argument.

Supply a finite polygonal oriented disk-band Seifert-surface model and local ambient smooth roundings for a smooth oriented knot $K\subset S^3$, with compatible closed product tube, positive meridian $\mu$, preferred longitude $\lambda$, collars and peripheral paths. Put $X=S^3\setminus\operatorname{int}N(K)$, $T=\partial X$, and let $M=X\cup_T V$ be its actual preferred zero-longitude surgery, oriented to extend $X$. Let $k=\mathbb Z$ or a commutative field, $R=k[t,t^{-1}]$, and let $F$ be its fraction field, so $F=\mathbb Q(t)$ when $k=\mathbb Z$. Use the associated based right coefficient systems sending $\mu$ to $t$ with transport by the inverse unit, and their standard parallel Hermitian form.

The actual maps induce isomorphisms
$$i_*:H_1(X;R)\cong H_1(M;R),\qquad j_*:H_1(X;R)\cong H_1(X,T;R).$$
The closed Bockstein–duality pairing $B_M$ is defined on the whole first homology and is nonsingular. On $X$ use the following explicit classical cocycle rule: take an integral $R^\vee$-valued two-cocycle $a$ whose cap class is $\overline{j_*x}$, take one whole $F^\vee$-valued one-cochain $b$ with $\partial^*b=a$, and set $B_X(x,y)=[b(y)]\in F/R$. Such primitives exist, this rule is independent of all representatives and choices, and
$$B_X(x,y)=B_M(i_*x,i_*y).$$
Thus it is the nonsingular exterior classical Blanchfield form with the same positive-meridian, positive-push and first-variable conjugate-linear conventions. Based axis classes in the exterior are carried to their actual surgery classes. The constructions commute with the rational and prime coefficient maps wherever the displayed forms are compared; no choice principle, arbitrary knot projection theorem or four-dimensional normal-neighborhood claim is assumed.

Assume AC. For an integer $h\ge0$ or a half-integer $h=n+1/2$, let $\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{sm}}$ be the set of smooth concordance classes whose preferred-longitude zero surgery bounds an integral $h$-solution. Use the integral lifted-pair definition: $H_1$ is identified with the boundary meridian $\mathbb Z$, $H_2$ is free of rank $2r$, there are exactly $r$ zero/unit pairs over the indicated derived quotient, and at a half level the isotropic classes lift one further derived stage. Every smooth pattern preserves smooth knot concordance. Then $\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{sm}}$ is a subgroup of smooth knot concordance, $\mathcal F_{h'}^{\mathrm{sm}}\subseteq\mathcal F_h^{\mathrm{sm}}$ for $h'\ge h$, and every smooth knot lies in $\mathcal F_0^{\mathrm{sm}}$.

More specifically, let $R$ be a smooth slice knot and let $\eta$ be a supplied unknotted infection axis in its exterior with $[\eta]\in\pi_1(S^3\setminus R)^{(k)}$, where $k\ge1$. For every smooth knot $J$, the infection $R(\eta,J)$ has an actual smooth integral $k$-solution. All constructions use finite smooth disk-band, peripheral product-tube, collar and path data; these data may be chosen under the stated AC.

Consequently, if $P$ is a winding-zero smooth pattern, then for every $k\ge1$ and every smooth knot $J$,
$$[P^k(J)]-[P^k(U)]\in\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{sm}},\qquad \langle P^k(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle\subseteq\mathcal F_k^{\mathrm{sm}}+\langle[P^k(U)]\rangle.$$
No locally flat tubular neighborhood or TOP realization theorem is assumed or concluded.

Assume AC. Fix $n\ge1$ and a smooth winding-zero pattern $P$ whose axis has nonzero integral classical Blanchfield self-value, equivalently using the actual exterior-to-zero-surgery identification. Supply finite smooth disk-band models, peripheral product tubes, paths and compatible collars for the finitely many knots and infection pieces used below.

For every $m\ge1$ there are smooth knots $J_1,\ldots,J_m$ with explicit finite disk-band surfaces such that no nonzero signed connected sum
$$K=\mathop{\#}_{i=1}^m a_i P^n(J_i),\qquad (a_1,\ldots,a_m)\in\mathbb Z^m\setminus\{0\},$$
bounds a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold $V$ with collared boundary $M(K)$ and the following lifted half-pair data: boundary inclusion identifies $H_1(M(K);\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu]$ with $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)$, $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, there are exactly $r$ height-$n$ equivariant pairs $x_i,y_i$ with zero $x$-pairings and unit $x,y$-pairings, and the $x_i$ lift to height $n+1$ with zero pairings. Height $h$ means coefficients $\mathbb Z[\pi_1(V)/\pi_1(V)^{(h)}]$. Signed knots use the marked mirror-and-reverse inverse convention.

There is also one smooth knot $J$, with explicit finite disk-band surface, for which
$$P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#\bigl(-P^n(J\#J)\bigr)$$
is not smoothly slice. More generally its zero surgery bounds no compact connected smooth integral homology-circle four-manifold with boundary-meridian $H_1$ isomorphism.

The coefficient maps and all signature sums used to obtain these obstructions are maps on the actual smooth bounding manifolds and infection pieces. No TOP-to-smooth rho comparison, choice-free analytic conclusion, integral-filtration subgroup construction, or quotient-rank conclusion is implicit in this supplied-data obstruction theorem.

Assume AC. Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented collared topological four-manifold with connected boundary $M$, with $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(V;\mathbb Z)$ the isomorphism $\mathbb Z[\mu]\to\mathbb Z[\mu]$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$. Supply $r$ ordinary zero/unit pairs $x_i,y_i$, and supply isotropic lifts of the $x_i$ to the abelian cover of $V$. Let $p$ be any prime, let $C_p$ be the cyclic group of order $p$, and let $\phi:\pi_1(V)\to\mathbb Z\to C_p$ send the meridian to its positive generator. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}_{C_p}^{(2)}(V,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}(V)=0.$$
The completed coefficient homology has $b_0^{(2)}(V)=b_1^{(2)}(V)=1/p$, $b_2^{(2)}(V)=2r$ and $b_3^{(2)}(V)=b_4^{(2)}(V)=0$, and the middle intersection form has zero radical. In particular, when $V$ is smooth, its boundary restriction has $\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi|_M)=0$. Every smooth integral $1$-solution satisfies the supplied pair hypotheses. No comparison between a nonsmooth TOP defect and a smooth bounding-defect invariant is asserted.

Assume AC. Let $P$ be a smooth winding-zero pattern whose axis has nonzero integral classical Blanchfield self-pairing in the Alexander module of $P(U)$. Let $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}}$ denote smooth oriented knot concordance with its reverse-mirror inverse, and let $P^0$ be the identity. Then for every $n\ge0$ the abelian-group quotient
$$\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle/\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle$$
has infinite rational rank. For every $n\ge1$ the smooth satellite map $P^n$ is not a group homomorphism. The proof uses finite companion families depending on a prescribed rank bound; no infinite choice of an explicit independent sequence is required. No coprime Alexander-polynomial condition is imposed. This theorem retains full AC and makes no assertion identifying nonsmooth TOP defects with smooth bounding invariants.

Let $n\ge1$. Supply a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold $V$ with boundary a marked knot zero surgery, $H_1(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$, and exactly $r$ integral pairs $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, satisfying $\lambda(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Form $W$ by any finite sequence of the actual marked standard connected-sum and winding-zero infection cobordism adjunctions along outgoing knot-surgery components, including orientation reversals, using supplied smooth peripheral products and collars. Let $\phi:\pi_1(W)\to\Gamma$ have PTFA target and restrict on $V$ through $\pi/\pi^{(n)}$. Take $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ and put $A=k[\Gamma]$, with involutive Ore fraction division ring $K$ and the based standard parallel Hermitian structure.

The image pairs $\ell_i,d_i\in H_2(W;A)$ satisfy $\lambda(\ell_i,\ell_j)=0$ and $\lambda(\ell_i,d_j)=\lambda(d_j,\ell_i)=\delta_{ij}$. Their localized boundary-intersection cokernel has dimension at most $2r$. For each boundary component $M_0$ on which $\phi$ is nontrivial, $H_1(M_0;K)=0$, its coefficient Bockstein–duality linking form is defined, and its actual inclusion kernel is isotropic:
$$B_{M_0}(z,w)=0\quad\text{for all }z,w\in\ker\{H_1(M_0;A)\to H_1(W;A)\}.$$
Thus every boundary class with nonzero self-pairing survives in $H_1(W;A)$ and lies outside every isotropic submodule. If a component's coefficient image is cyclic, its form additionally has the nonsingularity furnished by the cyclic-image coefficient theorem; no unrestricted PTFA nonsingularity is asserted.

For a finite forest of iterated winding-zero infections with these initial data, suppose each top meridian generates $H_1(W_n;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z$ up to sign, and each pattern-axis integral classical self-pairing is nonzero. Use the actual intermediate $W_j$, rational mixed coefficients through index $n$, and one bottom field $\mathbb F_p$. For every odd prime outside the explicit finite exceptional set of the axis values, every branch meridian has a nonzero class in $P^{n-j}\pi_1(W_j)/P^{n-j+1}\pi_1(W_j)$, of infinite order when $j>0$ and order $p$ when $j=0$. All these conclusions hold for the supplied locally flat topological bordisms and smooth bordisms without a choice principle. Existence of the initial $V$ and its lifted pairs from a concordance relation is a separate hypothesis, as are analytic rho invariance and signature vanishing.

Assume full AC. Let $M$ be a compact oriented Hausdorff topological manifold with supplied boundary collar, and supply a based homomorphism on each component to a discrete group $G$, with compatible paths when maps or gluings are considered. Use $R=\mathbb CG$, with involution conjugating complex scalars and sending $g$ to $g^{-1}$, and its based right regular local system with standard parallel Hermitian form. Let $A=\mathcal NG$ have the canonical group trace. Then its singular coefficient complex has an actual bounded finite-projective $R$ chain-homotopy model. Absolute, relative and finite whole-component gluing diagrams admit such models and finite matrix comparison maps.

After extending these finite projective matrices to $\ell^2(G)$, write $\mathscr H_i(M)$ for completed reduced homology, with boundaries replaced by their Hilbert closures. If $p_Z,p_B$ are the cycle and boundary-closure projections in a finite ambient projection module, the corresponding algebraic reduced module is $P_i=(p_Z-p_B)A^r$, and
$$H_i(M;A)\twoheadrightarrow P_i\hookrightarrow\mathscr H_i(M)=(p_Z-p_B)\ell^2(G)^r.$$
The first map has dimension-zero kernel, and the second is injective with dense image and need not be onto. Pair and whole-component Mayer–Vietoris sequences are weakly exact on the completed modules. Oriented cap duality gives bounded mutually inverse maps on their completed reduced homology and cohomology, with the cap-boundary and restriction identities. These structures and the resulting spectral signature do not depend on the finite-projective model.

For a four-manifold the middle intersection form is the bounded Hermitian form defined by inverse relative cap duality, restriction and evaluation. Its Hilbert radical is the kernel of its self-adjoint operator. Its signature is the trace of the positive spectral projection minus the trace of the negative projection; no closed range or bounded inverse is required for a manifold with boundary. For a closed four-manifold its middle intersection operator is boundedly invertible.

Let $W_0,W_1$ be compact oriented topological four-manifolds, let $N$ be a union of entire closed boundary components, and glue the two marked copies of $N$ by an orientation-reversing identification and the supplied collars. Put $W=W_0\cup_N W_1$ and supply one compatible regular coefficient system on $W$. Other boundary components may remain. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(W_1),\qquad\operatorname{sign}(W)=\operatorname{sign}(W_0)+\operatorname{sign}(W_1).$$
Orientation reversal changes the corresponding sign. No finite CW type, triangulation, smoothing of a topological four-manifold, equality of ordinary and $L^2$ signatures on arbitrary closed manifolds, or analytic eta-to-defect comparison is asserted or assumed. For an arbitrary possibly uncountable $G$, the finite-matrix construction has the same dimensions and signatures as its countable coefficient image, so it agrees with the countable-group convention.

Assume full AC. Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented topological four-manifold with a supplied collar and connected boundary $M$, and choose a based loop $\mu\subset M$ such that
$$H_1(M;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z[\mu],\qquad H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\xrightarrow{\cong}H_1(V;\mathbb Z),\qquad H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}.$$
Put $\pi=\pi_1(V)$, take $n\ge0$, and supply classes $x_i,y_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n)}])$, $1\le i\le r$, satisfying $\lambda_n(x_i,x_j)=0$ and $\lambda_n(x_i,y_j)=\delta_{ij}$. Supply classes $\widetilde x_i\in H_2(V;\mathbb Z[\pi/\pi^{(n+1)}])$ mapping to $x_i$ with $\lambda_{n+1}(\widetilde x_i,\widetilde x_j)=0$. These are actual lifted half-pair data on the supplied manifold; existence of such a manifold or lifts is not asserted.

Let $k=\mathbb Q$ or $\mathbb F_p$ for any prime $p$. Let $G$ be a discrete amenable group in $D(k)$ with $G^{(n+1)}=1$, and supply $\phi:\pi\to G$ such that $\phi(\mu)$ has infinite order. Use its based regular unitary local system and the finite-projective topological intersection convention. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_G(V,\phi)=0=\operatorname{sign}(V),$$
so its actual bounding signature defect is zero. This applies to the full supplied locally flat topological category as well as smooth manifolds; no finite CW type, smoothing, closed-manifold ordinary-versus-$L^2$ index equality or rho bordism-independence theorem is assumed. If a separately applicable bordism-independence result identifies a rho invariant with this bounding defect, that invariant is consequently zero.

Assume full AC and a smooth winding-zero pattern $P$ whose axis has nonzero integral classical Blanchfield self-value. Use oriented zero surgery $M(K)$ and the first-positive-push Levine–Tristram signature function $\sigma_J$. Let $L>0$ exceed the uniform Cheeger–Gromov bound for every rho value of $M(P(U))$ under every group representation. For every $n,m\ge1$, there are distinct odd primes $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ outside the finite exceptional set for reduction of this self-value and finite disk-band companion knots $J_i$ such that, writing $\zeta_p=\exp(2\pi i/p)$,
$$D_i=\frac1{p_i}\sum_{r=0}^{p_i-1}\sigma_{J_i}(\zeta_{p_i}^{r})>mnL,$$
with $\sigma_{J_i}(1)=0$, $\sigma_{J_i}(\zeta_{p_i})=\sigma_{J_i}(\zeta_{p_i}^{-1})>p_i mnL/2$, all other nonidentity $p_i$-th-root signatures zero, and every $p_j$-th-root signature zero for $j\ne i$. Thus $D_i$ is the canonical $\mathbb Z/p_i$ cyclic defect of $M(J_i)$. In any candidate smooth bounding bordism for a nonzero integer vector $(a_i)$ used in the actual finite-prime infection obstruction assembly, choose $i_*$ with $|a_{i_*}|=\max_i|a_i|$. Its supplied quotient using $p_{i_*}$ gives signed bottom boundary contribution $a_{i_*}D_{i_*}$; the remaining $n\sum_i|a_i|$ pattern terms have total absolute value less than $nL\sum_i|a_i|\le nmL|a_{i_*}|<|a_{i_*}|D_{i_*}$. Thus the total signed boundary rho value has the sign of $a_{i_*}$ and is nonzero.

For every $n\ge1$, the three-branch obstruction assembly also admits a finite disk-band companion knot with a canonical cyclic defect $D>3nL$. For any supplied candidate smooth homology-circle bound in that assembly, its quotient kills the distinguished negative bottom branch and gives either $0$ or $D$ on each positive bottom branch, with at least one value $D$. Its $3n$ remaining pattern terms have total absolute value less than $3nL$, so the total boundary rho value is positive. For a locally flat TOP pair-family application, the initial bordism must supply the actual height-$n$ pairs and height-$(n+1)$ isotropic lifts; for a TOP three-branch application it must supply the actual homology-circle bound. In either case the finite-projective coefficient quotient must satisfy the stated survival and vanishing hypotheses, and the boundary rho values must agree with the smooth bounding defects by the closed TOP bordism equality. Pairwise relatively prime Alexander polynomials belong only to the separate Theorem C comparison of distinct patterns; they are not hypotheses of Theorems A or B.

Assume full AC. Let M be a closed oriented 3-manifold, Γ a discrete group, and φ:π₁(M)→Γ. If (W₀,ψ₀) and (W₁,ψ₁) are compact oriented 4-manifolds with boundary M over which φ extends, then sign_Γ^(2)(W₀,ψ₀)−sign(W₀)=sign_Γ^(2)(W₁,ψ₁)−sign(W₁). Hence the signature defect depends only on (M,φ).

Assume full AC. For every closed oriented 3-manifold M there exists a finite constant C_M such that for every discrete group Γ and every homomorphism φ:π₁(M)→Γ for which the rho invariant is defined, |ρ(M,φ)|≤C_M. The constant may depend on M but not on Γ or φ.

Assume AC. Let $V$ be a compact connected oriented collared topological four-manifold with connected boundary $M$, with $H_1(M;\mathbb Z)\to H_1(V;\mathbb Z)$ the isomorphism $\mathbb Z[\mu]\to\mathbb Z[\mu]$ and $H_2(V;\mathbb Z)=\mathbb Z^{2r}$. Supply $r$ ordinary zero/unit pairs $x_i,y_i$, and supply isotropic lifts of the $x_i$ to the abelian cover of $V$. Let $p$ be any prime, let $C_p$ be the cyclic group of order $p$, and let $\phi:\pi_1(V)\to\mathbb Z\to C_p$ send the meridian to its positive generator. Then
$$\operatorname{sign}_{C_p}^{(2)}(V,\phi)=\operatorname{sign}(V)=0.$$
The completed coefficient homology has $b_0^{(2)}(V)=b_1^{(2)}(V)=1/p$, $b_2^{(2)}(V)=2r$ and $b_3^{(2)}(V)=b_4^{(2)}(V)=0$, and the middle intersection form has zero radical. In particular, when $V$ is smooth, its boundary restriction has $\rho_{\mathrm{sm}}(M,\phi|_M)=0$. Every smooth integral $1$-solution satisfies the supplied pair hypotheses. No comparison between a nonsmooth TOP defect and a smooth bounding-defect invariant is asserted.

Supply distinct odd primes $p_1,\ldots,p_m$ with $m\ge1$ and positive real numbers $C_1,\ldots,C_m$. Put $\omega_j=\exp(2\pi i/p_j)$. A finite construction gives smooth oriented knots $K_1,\ldots,K_m$, each with a supplied connected one-boundary oriented Seifert surface and ordered integral basis with exact positive-push matrix $V_i$. Define its chosen-surface signature function by
$$s_i(z)=\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-z)V_i+(1-\bar z)V_i^T\bigr),\qquad z\in S^1.$$
There are positive integers $N_i$ such that
$$s_i(\omega_i)=s_i(\omega_i^{-1})=2N_i>C_i,$$
while $s_i(\omega_i^r)=0$ when $r\not\equiv\pm1\pmod{p_i}$, and $s_i(\omega_j^r)=0$ for all integers $r$ when $j\ne i$. Each $s_i$ is nonnegative on the entire unit circle. In particular,
$$\frac1{p_i}\sum_{r=0}^{p_i-1}s_i(\omega_i^r)=\frac{4N_i}{p_i}>\frac{2C_i}{p_i},\qquad \frac1{p_j}\sum_{r=0}^{p_j-1}s_i(\omega_j^r)=0\quad(j\ne i).$$
The surface for $K_i$ has genus $4N_i$. No choice principle, concordance classification, cabling formula, signature-to-rho formula or uniform analytic bound is assumed.

Assume AC. For every supplied finite smooth oriented disk-band Seifert surface $F$ with one-boundary knot $K$, ordered homology basis and first-variable positive-push matrix $V$, let $W_F$ and its meridional extension $\psi_d:\pi_1(W_F)\to\mathbb Z/d$ be the actual construction of the finite disk-band bounding-manifold construction. For every positive integer $d$, set $\zeta_d=\exp(2\pi i/d)$ and
$$D_d(F)=\operatorname{sign}^{(2)}_{\mathbb Z/d}(W_F,\psi_d)-\operatorname{sign}(W_F).$$
Then
$$D_d(F)=\frac1d\sum_{r=0}^{d-1}\operatorname{sign}\bigl((1-\zeta_d^r)V+(1-\zeta_d^{-r})V^T\bigr).$$
The sign is exactly the positive $L^2$ signature minus ordinary signature convention. The formula allows singular character forms and all $d$, including $d=1$ and even $d$. The term $r=0$ is defined by the zero Hermitian matrix and contributes zero; its equality to the trivial-character signature follows from the ordinary metabolic calculation, not from specialization of a localized homology basis.

The boundary is the actual oriented zero surgery and its positive meridian map, not the knot exterior or a simply connected trace. The displayed formula proves this **canonical bounding defect**. Whenever a separately proved applicable bordism-independence assertion identifies the rho invariant with the defect of this bounding extension, it consequently gives the same value for that rho invariant. No such general independence assertion, global signature invariance, rho identification, uniform bound, infinite-cyclic formula or arbitrary-group index theorem is asserted here.

derivations.claim: In the smooth category [F1] identifies the stipulated nonzero classical axis self-value with exactly the integral surgery self-value used in [F4]. The winding and orientation conventions are the same, and AC verifies its actual geometric and analytic hypotheses. Apply [F4] to obtain infinite rational rank of $\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle/\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{sm}})\rangle$ for every $n\ge0$, including its separate finite-cyclic proof at $n=0$. Its finite families are chosen for each desired rank bound, so no assertion of a single explicit infinite independent sequence is needed. This establishes the entire smooth rank branch of the original Statement.

For $n\ge1$, [F4] also gives a knot $J$ for which $P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#(-P^n(J\#J))$ is not smoothly slice. A homomorphism on smooth concordance would make this class zero, contradicting the actual witness. Thus the entire smooth nonhomomorphism branch follows as well. Neither [F4]'s rank proof nor this witness uses a pairwise-coprime Alexander-polynomial condition, so the original A/B scope is retained.

Work in the TOP group of [F8]. Fix $n\ge1$ and any desired finite rank $m$. Choose the finite family in [F6] for size $m+1$. If a nonzero signed sum of its $P^n$ iterates belonged to $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$, its defining TOP solution would have exactly the integral height-$n$ pairs and isotropic height-$(n+1)$ lifts needed by [F5]. The finite forest quotient maps in [F5] have amenable target in the specified $D(k)$ class, with top meridian of infinite order. The accepted TOP half-pair theorem gives zero defect of that actual solution; the smooth standard joining/infection pieces have zero defect as well. Whole-component additivity makes the actual boundary defect sum zero. But [F6] evaluates its bottom terms by canonical cyclic numbers and gives strict signed domination over all pattern terms. This is a contradiction. Thus these $m+1$ classes are rationally independent modulo $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}$: a rational relation clears denominators to the excluded nonzero signed integer relation.

By [F8], $\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$ lies in $\mathcal F_{n+1}^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P^{n+1}(U)\rangle$. Quotienting a rational vector space by the span of one element loses at most one dimension. Step3.1 therefore gives rank at least $m$ for the image of $\langle P^n(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$ modulo that larger subgroup, hence also for its quotient by $\langle P^{n+1}(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$. Since $m$ was arbitrary, the rank is infinite. This uses finite families of each requested size, not an unproved explicit infinite sequence.

At $n=0$, take any finite family of the signature bumps in [F7], with distinct selected primes. For a nonzero signed sum choose an index with nonzero coefficient and evaluate the canonical cyclic defect at that prime. All cross-prime terms vanish, so the value is the selected nonzero integer coefficient times its positive normalized mean. It cannot vanish. A TOP integral1-solution would give an integral half-solution at height0 and force the same defect to vanish by [F7] and [F6]. These classes are therefore independent modulo $\mathcal F_1^{\mathrm{top}}$. Since $\langle P(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle\subset\mathcal F_1^{\mathrm{top}}+\langle P(U)\rangle$, the same at-most-one rank loss proves infinite rank of $\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}}/\langle P(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{top}})\rangle$.

For $n\ge1$, choose the three-branch companion in [F6] with normalized positive cyclic defect exceeding $3nL$. If $P^n(J)\#P^n(J)\#(-P^n(J\#J))$ were TOP slice, [F8] would give an actual collared TOP homology-circle disk exterior. This is the zero-pair case of [F5], and its three-branch quotient kills the distinguished negative bottom restriction while at least one positive bottom restriction has the required cyclic order. The actual half-pair zero defect and piecewise gluing force total defect zero, while [F6] gives a strictly positive bottom sum exceeding all $3n$ pattern terms. This contradiction proves the TOP nonhomomorphism witness. Steps1.1–2.1 already supplied the smooth conclusions. No coprime Alexander hypothesis was used. The full original Statement follows, with precisely the TOP geometric foundations and closed TOP equality declared external.
