          "quote": "Throughout this page $\mathbb{R}$ is the complete ordered field
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]) constructed in this library, in particular a
field, so that "vector space" below always means vector space over $\mathbb{R}$
([[def-vector-space]]).

Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb{R}$, with zero vector $0_V$. A **norm on
$V$** is a function $N : V \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $u, v \in V$ and all
$\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

- **(N1) Separation.** $N(v) = 0$ if and only if $v = 0_V$.
- **(N2) Absolute homogeneity.** $N(\lambda v) = |\lambda|\,N(v)$, the absolute
  value being that of [[def-abs-value]].
- **(N3) Triangle inequality.** $N(u + v) \le N(u) + N(v)$.

A **normed space** is a pair $(V, N)$ consisting of a vector space $V$ over
$\mathbb{R}$ and a norm $N$ on it. When only one norm is in play we write
$\lVert v\rVert$ for $N(v)$; when several are, the norm is always named.

**The values of a norm are real numbers.** The codomain is $\mathbb{R}$, so
$N(v)$ is an honest element of the complete ordered field and no infinite value
is permitted. The same real-valued codomain is required of a metric by
[[def-metric-space]].

### Nonnegativity is a theorem, not an axiom

Many texts add a fourth condition $N(v) \ge 0$. It is redundant. Applying (N2)
with $\lambda = -1$ gives $N(-v) = |-1|\,N(v) = N(v)$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]],
[[lem-vector-space-elementary-consequences]] for $(-1)v = -v$), and then (N3)
with $u = v$ and $-v$ gives

$$0 \;=\; N(0_V) \;=\; N\bigl(v + (-v)\bigr) \;\le\; N(v) + N(-v) \;=\; N(v) + N(v),$$

where $N(0_V) = 0$ is (N1). So $N(v) + N(v) \ge 0$, and if $N(v) < 0$ then
$N(v) + N(v) < 0$ by addition of inequalities, which trichotomy forbids
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]). Hence $N(v) \ge 0$ for every $v \in V$.

**Consequently the verification of a candidate norm has three things to check and
not four**, exactly as the verification of a candidate metric has three and not
four ([[def-metric-space]], [[lem-metric-nonnegativity]]). No item in this
library assumes nonnegativity of a norm before the argument above.

### The induced metric

Let $N$ be a norm on $V$ and define

$$d_N(u,v) \;:=\; N(u - v) \qquad (u, v \in V),$$

where $u - v = u + (-v)$ ([[def-vector-space]]). **Then $d_N$ is a metric on
$V$** ([[def-metric-space]]), and the three axioms are the three conditions
above, in order:

- **(M1)** $d_N(u,v) = 0$ means $N(u-v) = 0$, which by (N1) says $u - v = 0_V$,
  that is $u = v$; and conversely $d_N(v,v) = N(0_V) = 0$.
- **(M2)** $d_N(v,u) = N(v-u) = N\bigl((-1)(u-v)\bigr) = |-1|\,N(u-v) = d_N(u,v)$,
  by (N2), [[lem-of-abs-value]] and $(-1)w = -w$
  ([[lem-vector-space-elementary-consequences]]).
- **(M3)** $d_N(u,w) = N\bigl((u-v) + (v-w)\bigr) \le N(u-v) + N(v-w) = d_N(u,v) + d_N(v,w)$,
  by (N3).

A normed space is therefore a metric space, and every notion defined for metric
spaces — open set ([[def-metric-topology]]), convergence, Cauchyness,
continuity, compactness — is available in it with no further definition. **This
library never introduces a second notion of any of them for normed spaces.**

### Two properties an arbitrary metric need not have

The metric $d_N$ satisfies, for all $u, v, w \in V$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

- **translation invariance**, $d_N(u + w, v + w) = N\bigl((u+w)-(v+w)\bigr) = N(u-v) = d_N(u,v)$;
- **absolute homogeneity**, $d_N(\lambda u, \lambda v) = N\bigl(\lambda(u-v)\bigr) = |\lambda|\,d_N(u,v)$, by (N2).

**Not every metric on a vector space arises from a norm**, and homogeneity is
what fails. The published bounded remetrisation [[lem-bounded-remetrisation]]
replaces a metric $d$ by $d' = \min\{d, 1\}$, a metric with the same topology
whose values never exceed $1$; on a vector space $V$ containing a vector $v$ with
$d(v, 0_V) > 0$ this $d'$ cannot be $d_M$ for any norm $M$, since absolute
homogeneity would force $d'(\lambda v, 0_V) = |\lambda|\,d'(v, 0_V)$, which is
unbounded in $\lambda$, while $d'$ is bounded by $1$. So the passage from norms
to metrics is not reversible, and a statement about a metric on a vector space is
strictly weaker than the corresponding statement about a norm.",

          "quote": "Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere. Assume for this specified data that the differential is nonincreasing in the Alexander filtration, that the absolute Alexander formula below takes integer values, and that $H(\\widehat{CF}(\\mathcal H))\\cong\\mathbb F_2$. To form the zero-framed surgery, remove a tubular neighborhood of $K$ and glue in a solid torus whose meridian is the longitude induced by $F$. The surface $\\widehat F$ is obtained by deleting a boundary collar of $F$ and capping its longitude by the meridian disk of that solid torus.           "source": "def-countable-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$, is the following\nstatement.\n\n> For every family $(X_n)_{n \\in \\mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by\n> $\\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\\mathbb{N}$ such that\n> $f(n) \\in X_n$ for every $n \\in \\mathbb{N}$.\n\nEquivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most\ncountable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "lem-tau-of-the-unknot-is-zero",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For the standard oriented unknot $U$ and its standard genus-zero one-pointed Heegaard diagram, the normalized Alexander-filtered hat complex has total homology $\\mathbb F_2$ generated at filtration level $0$.           "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "lem-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus-minima-exist",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. For each surface, $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Both sets are nonempty and have least elements.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "lem-puncturing-smooth-four-ball-surfaces-gives-genus-preserving-knot-cobordisms",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume countable choice. Let $F\\subset B^4\\subset\\mathbb R^4$ be a compact connected oriented smoothly properly embedded surface of genus $g$, with its supplied smooth boundary collar and oriented boundary the knot $K\\subset S^3$. There is an orientation-preserving ambient diffeomorphism $\\Psi:B^4\\to B^4$ equal to the identity on a neighborhood of the outer boundary, and $0<\\varepsilon<1$, such that $\\Psi(F)\\cap B^4_\\varepsilon$ is exactly a flat two-disk in a plane through $0$. The surface $\\Psi(F)\\setminus\\operatorname{int}B^4_\\varepsilon$, in the explicitly round shell $B^4\\setminus\\operatorname{int}B^4_\\varepsilon\\cong S^3\\times[0,1]$, is a connected smooth oriented knot cobordism between $K$ and a standard unknot, with genus $g$ and Euler characteristic $-2g$. Both boundary components have product collars in a shell identification fixing $K$ and the inner sphere. The ambient diffeomorphism $\\Psi$ fixes a sufficiently small restriction of the supplied outer collar; the shell coordinates may be adjusted there to make that surface collar a product. No assertion about the complement of an arbitrary embedded four-ball is used.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F4",
          "source": "lem-tau-is-independent-of-heegaard-grid",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Their diagramwise thresholds agree. Moreover, every grid presentation of $(K,F)$ gives this same value after the full filtered grid complex is converted to the normalized singly pointed model, with all basepoint-variable and stabilization factors accounted for.           "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]

        {

          "source": "lem-knot-floer-large-surgery-and-filtered-cobordism-input",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $g$ be the genus of $S$, and use the standard absolute Alexander normalization for the endpoint knot Floer complexes. Then\n$$|\\tau(K_1)-\\tau(K_0)|\\le g.$$\nIn particular, a smooth concordance annulus gives equal tau values, and a genus-$g$ surface from a knot to the unknot gives the four-ball genus estimate.",

          "source": "lem-tau-connected-sum-filtered-tensor-product",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots in the standard oriented three-sphere, with chosen minimum-genus oriented Seifert surfaces. A normalized $CFK^\\infty(K)$ is a free finite-rank chain complex over $\\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]$ with two integer filtrations $(i,j)$, where multiplication by $U$ lowers both coordinates by one. Give the connected sum $K\\#J$ the fixed oriented gluing convention and the sum filtrations and Maslov/Alexander gradings. Then $CFK^\\infty(K\\#J)$ is bifiltered chain homotopy equivalent to $CFK^\\infty(K)\\otimes_{\\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]}CFK^\\infty(J)$, with an equivalence and homotopies preserving both filtration coordinates. Moreover, the normalized finite filtered hat complex of $K\\#J$ is filtered chain homotopy equivalent to $C_K\\otimes C_J$ with tensor filtration $F_s(C_K\\otimes C_J)=\\sum_{p+q\\le s}F_pC_K\\otimes F_qC_J$. Consequently,\n$$\\tau(K\\#J)=\\tau(K)+\\tau(J).$$",

          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For every smooth oriented knot $K\\subset S^3$, the function $\\Upsilon_K:[0,2]\\to\\mathbb R$ defined by the finite cycle minimax is continuous and piecewise linear with finitely many breakpoints, satisfies $\\Upsilon_K(0)=0$ and $\\Upsilon_K(t)=\\Upsilon_K(2-t)$, and has right derivative $\\Upsilon'_K(0+)=-\\tau(K)$. For smooth oriented knots $K,J$ and $t\\in[0,2]$,\n$$ \\Upsilon_{K\\#J}(t)=\\Upsilon_K(t)+\\Upsilon_J(t),\\qquad \\Upsilon_{-K}(t)=-\\Upsilon_K(t), $$\nwhere $-K$ is the reverse mirror, the inverse under connected sum in the smooth concordance group. If $g_4^{\\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ is the minimum genus of a smooth properly embedded compact connected oriented surface in the four-ball with boundary $K$, then\n$$ |\\Upsilon_K(t)|\\le t\\,g_4^{\\mathrm{sm}}(K)\\qquad(0\\le t\\le1). $$",

          "source": "lem-epsilon-stable-equivalence-and-not-a-homomorphism",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Let $K$ and $J$ be smooth oriented knots, and use the epsilon sign convention from the preceding definition. If their knot Floer complexes are stably filtered equivalent, meaning that there are totally acyclic bifiltered complexes $A$ and $B$ with $\\mathrm{CFK}^{\\infty}(K)\\oplus A$ filtered-chain-homotopy equivalent to $\\mathrm{CFK}^{\\infty}(J)\\oplus B$, then $\\epsilon(K)=\\epsilon(J)$. The acyclic summands here need not be acyclic after taking either associated-graded filtration.\n\nThe invariant satisfies $\\epsilon(-K)=-\\epsilon(K)$, $\\epsilon(K)=0\\Rightarrow\\tau(K)=0$, and the tensor rules\n$$ \\epsilon(K)=\\epsilon(J)\\Rightarrow\\epsilon(K\\#J)=\\epsilon(K),\\qquad \\epsilon(K)=0\\Rightarrow\\epsilon(K\\#J)=\\epsilon(J). $$\nThe converse of $\\epsilon(K)=0\\Rightarrow\\tau(K)=0$ fails: the knot $T_{2,5}\\#-T_{4,5}\\#T_{2,3;2,5}$ has $\\tau=0$ and $\\epsilon=1$, where $T_{p,q}$ is the positive $(p,q)$ torus knot and $T_{2,3;2,5}$ is the $(2,5)$ cable of the right-handed trefoil with longitudinal winding two. Epsilon is not an integer-valued homomorphism on the smooth concordance group: the right-handed trefoil has $\\epsilon=1$ and its connected sum with itself also has $\\epsilon=1$, not $2$.",
          "uses": [

The coefficient extension uses $U=v^2$.           "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [

          ]

          "source": "def-knot-seifert-pairing-and-matrix",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K:S^1\\hookrightarrow S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere, and let $F\\subset S^3$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, oriented so that its boundary orientation is the given orientation of $K$. Let $g$ be the nonnegative integer determined by $\\chi(F)=1-2g$. Choose an ordered integral basis $a_1,\\ldots,a_{2g}$ of the first singular homology group $H_1(F;\\mathbb Z)$, represented by integral one-cycles on $F$. Orient the normal line of $F$ by requiring $(n,u,v)$ to be positively oriented in $S^3$ whenever $(u,v)$ is a positive tangent basis of $F$. The positive push-off $a_i^+$ is the cycle carried to a sufficiently small positive normal level in a bicollar of $F$.\n\nFor disjoint oriented closed curves $J,L\\subset S^3$, orient a meridian $\\mu_L$ of $L$ so that a positive tangent to $L$ followed by a positive basis of its normal disk gives the ambient orientation. The linking number $\\operatorname{lk}(J,L)$ is the integer determined by $[J]=\\operatorname{lk}(J,L)[\\mu_L]$ in $H_1(S^3\\setminus L;\\mathbb Z)$, using the Alexander-duality identification that sends $[\\mu_L]$ to $1$. Extend linking additively over integral one-cycles. The Seifert pairing is $\\theta_F(x,y)=\\operatorname{lk}(x^+,y)$, and its matrix in the chosen basis is $V=(V_{ij})_{i,j=1}^{2g}$, where $V_{ij}=\\theta_F(a_i,a_j)=\\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$.           "source": "def-seifert-matrix-s-equivalence",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Let $V$ be an even-order square matrix with integer entries, of size $n=2g$. For $x,y\\in\\mathbb Z^n$ as column vectors and $z\\in\\mathbb Z$, the two elementary enlargements of $V$ are\n$$E_0(V;x,y,z)=\\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\\\y^T&z&0\\\\0^T&1&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad E_1(V;x,y,z)=\\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\\\y^T&z&1\\\\0^T&0&0\\end{pmatrix}.$$\nTwo even-order integral matrices are **S-equivalent** if one can be obtained from the other by a finite sequence of unimodular congruences, elementary enlargements, and reverse elementary enlargements.",

          "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "lem-seifert-matrices-of-a-knot-are-s-equivalent",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume full AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the oriented standard $3$-sphere, and let $F,F'$ be any connected compact smooth oriented spanning surfaces for $K$. For any ordered integral bases of $H_1(F;\\mathbb Z)$ and $H_1(F';\\mathbb Z)$, the matrices of the positive-push Seifert pairing are related by a finite sequence of integral unimodular congruences and the two rank-two elementary Seifert enlargements or their reverses.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "lem-arf-quadratic-enhancement-from-seifert-form",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume full AC. For a knot Seifert surface $F$ with Seifert matrix $V$, the function $q_F(x)=x^TVx\\pmod2$ is well-defined on $H_1(F;\\mathbb F_2)$ and satisfies\n$$q_F(x+y)=q_F(x)+q_F(y)+x\\cdot_F y.$$\nIts polarization is nondegenerate. For any symplectic basis $(a_1,b_1,\\ldots,a_g,b_g)$, the sum $\\sum_iq_F(a_i)q_F(b_i)$ is independent of that basis. It is unchanged by either elementary Seifert enlargement, so it depends only on the knot.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "lem-conway-polynomial-from-seifert-determinant",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume full AC. Every nonempty smooth oriented link $L\\subset S^3$ bounds a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface. If $F$ is any such surface with Seifert matrix $V$, and $u$ is a formal Laurent variable, then\n$$D_L(u)=\\det(u^{-1}V-uV^T)$$\nis independent of the surface and integral basis, belongs to $\\mathbb Z[u-u^{-1}]$, equals $1$ for the unknot, and satisfies\n$$D_{L_+}(u)-D_{L_-}(u)=(u-u^{-1})D_{L_0}(u)$$\nfor every oriented skein triple. Thus $D_L(u)=\\nabla_L(u-u^{-1})$ for the unique Conway polynomial normalized by $\\nabla_U=1$ and $\\nabla_+-\\nabla_-=z\\nabla_0$.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F4",
          "source": "def-seifert-s-equivalence-and-conway-normalization",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume full AC. For an even-order integral matrix $V$ that is the Seifert matrix of a knot, **S-equivalence** means the equivalence relation generated by integral unimodular congruences $V\\mapsto P^TVP$ with $\\det P=\\pm1$, where $x,y\\in\\mathbb Z^n$ and $z\\in\\mathbb Z$, and the two enlargements\n$$E_0(V;x,y,z)=\\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\\\y^T&z&0\\\\0^T&1&0\\end{pmatrix},\\qquad E_1(V;x,y,z)=\\begin{pmatrix}V&x&0\\\\y^T&z&1\\\\0^T&0&0\\end{pmatrix},$$\nand their reverses. For an assignment $P$ of an integer polynomial in $z$ to each ambient-isotopy class of oriented links, call $P$ **Conway-normalized** when $P_U(z)=1$ for the unknot $U$ and\n$$P_{L_+}(z)-P_{L_-}(z)=z\\,P_{L_0}(z)$$\nwhenever the three oriented links agree outside one crossing ball and inside it are respectively the positive crossing, negative crossing, and orientation-compatible smoothing; positive means $\\det_P(v_{\\rm over},v_{\\rm under})>0$, where $v_{\\rm over},v_{\\rm under}$ are the projected oriented tangent vectors and $P$ is oriented so the viewing normal followed by a positive basis of $P$ is ambient-positive. The smoothing reconnects the four oriented half-arcs in the unique noncrossing way compatible with their directions. No existence of such an assignment is presupposed: the Seifert-determinant lemma constructs a unique assignment and denotes it by $\\nabla_L(z)$. For a knot, let $\\Delta_K^\\#(t)$ be the unique associate of its Alexander polynomial satisfying $\\Delta_K^\\#(1)=1$ and $\\Delta_K^\\#(t^{-1})=\\Delta_K^\\#(t)$; existence and uniqueness follow from the Alexander-normalization corollary. Set $z=t^{1/2}-t^{-1/2}$, with $t^{1/2}$ a formal Laurent variable, and use $\\Delta_K^\\#(t)=\\nabla_K(z)$ as the normalization convention.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F5",
          "source": "lem-arf-seifert-determinant-congruence-near-minus-one",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume full AC. In the quotient ring $\\mathbb F_2[t,t^{-1}]/(1+t)^4$,\n$$\\Delta_K^\\#(t)=1+\\operatorname{Arf}(K)\\frac{(1+t)^2}{t}.$$",

          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

Its nonempty finite intersections are contractible, with contractions depending smoothly on the endpoint and contraction parameter. The cover can be chosen with a smooth subordinate partition of unity whose supports lie in their assigned cover members. For its finite nerve $N$, there is a homotopy equivalence $M\\to |N|$, and simplicial nerve cohomology identifies with singular cohomology of $M$ with coefficients in any abelian group. These identifications commute with coefficient homomorphisms, in particular reduction $\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathbb F_2$.",

          "source": "lem-lens-space-q-one-triangles-and-cyclic-handle-maps",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For each integer $p\\ge1$ there is a pointed genus-one triple $(\\alpha,\\beta,\\gamma)$ whose three manifolds are $Y_{\\alpha\\beta}=S^3$, $Y_{\\beta\\gamma}=S^3$ and $Y_{\\alpha\\gamma}=-L(p,1)$, where $L(p,1)$ is positive $p$-surgery on the unknot. For each $0\\le i<p$, a fixed Spin$^c$ triangle class from the two sphere generators to the lens generator $x_i$ has Maslov index zero, basepoint multiplicity zero, and mod-two count one. Its extension over the capped triple manifold has $\\langle c_1,[P]\\rangle=2i-p$, $[P]^2=-p$, $\\chi=1$, and $\\sigma=-1$. The cyclic triple $(\\gamma,\\alpha,\\beta)$ gives a fixed-Spin$^c$ map from $L(p,1)$ to $S^3$ with coefficient one from $[x_i,0]$ to the sphere generator at exponent zero and the same four-dimensional data. These are individual fixed-structure coefficients, not sums over extending structures. The boundary labels are $2i-p$ modulo $2p$; conjugation replaces $i$ by $p-i$ modulo $p$.",

          "source": "lem-rational-heegaard-floer-absolute-grading-and-cobordism-maps",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For a closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere and each Spin$^c$ structure, the pointed minus, infinity and plus Heegaard Floer complexes over $\\mathbb F_2$ admit an absolute rational grading, independent of the surgery presentation, extending their relative Maslov grading, with $\\deg U=-2$ and $\\deg[\\mathbf x_0,0]=0$ for the standard generator of $S^3$. Heegaard-move isomorphisms preserve this grading and commute with the minus/infinity/plus sequence. A smooth connected Spin$^c$ cobordism between such manifolds induces infinity and plus maps, compatible with that sequence, homogeneous of degree $(c_1(\\mathfrak s)^2-2\\chi(W)-3\\sigma(W))/4$. These maps are obtained from the fixed-Spin$^c$ triangle counts and the one- and three-handle maps, independently of their handle presentation. Here the Chern square uses the rational relative lift of the boundary-torsion Chern class.",
          "uses": [

            "1.3"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "lem-heegaard-floer-correction-term-heegaard-invariance",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For every closed connected oriented rational homology three-sphere $Y$ and Spin$^c$ structure $\\mathfrak t$, the standard Heegaard Floer groups $HF^\\infty(Y,\\mathfrak t)$ and $HF^+(Y,\\mathfrak t)$ constructed from admissible pointed Heegaard diagrams are independent, up to grading-preserving isomorphism, of the diagram and regular auxiliary data. The image of $HF^\\infty\\to HF^+$ is a graded plus tower, isomorphic as an $\\mathbb F_2[U]$-module to $\\mathbb F_2[U,U^{-1}]/U\\mathbb F_2[U]$ with an absolute rational grading shift and with $U$ of degree $-2$. Its nonzero homogeneous elements have a least grading; this least grading $d(Y,\\mathfrak t)$ exists and is independent of choices. Every tower element is $U$-torsion and is divisible by every power of $U$. The normalization is $d(S^3,\\mathfrak t_0)=0$.",

          "source": "def-lens-space-surgery-orientation-convention",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$. An oriented lens space is an oriented closed $3$-manifold obtained by gluing two solid tori by an orientation-reversing boundary homeomorphism. Thus this library uses the convention $L(p,q)=E_U(p/q)$; no symbol $L(0,q)$ is assigned.",

          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Let $B$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $H_*(B;\\mathbb Q)\\cong H_*(\\mathrm{point};\\mathbb Q)$ and connected rational homology sphere boundary $Y$. Choose a smoothly embedded closed four-ball $D$ in its interior and put $W=B\\setminus\\operatorname{int}D$. Its rational homological Euler characteristic is zero and its rational intersection module $H_2(W;\\mathbb Q)$ is zero.           "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

          "quote": "In ZF,\n\n$$\\mathrm{AC}\\Longrightarrow\\mathrm{DC}\\Longrightarrow\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega\\Longrightarrow\\mathrm{AC}_{\\omega,\\mathrm{fin}}\\Longrightarrow\\mathrm{AC}_{\\omega,2},\\qquad \\mathrm{AC}\\Longrightarrow\\mathrm{AC}_2.$$\n\nDC here includes a prescribed initial point.",

          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "def-complex-projective-space-and-holomorphic-charts",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "For an integer $n\\ge1$, **complex projective space** is the set of complex lines in $\\mathbb C^{n+1}$ with the quotient topology\n$$\\mathbb P^n(\\mathbb C):=(\\mathbb C^{n+1}\\setminus\\{0\\})/\\mathbb C^\\times,\\qquad [z_0:\\cdots:z_n]:=\\mathbb C^\\times(z_0,\\ldots,z_n).$$\nThe quotient projection is continuous and surjective.           "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

          "source": "def-cyclic-branched-cover-of-a-knot",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented $3$-sphere, choose its compact exterior $E_K$ with boundary torus $T_K$, and let $\\mu$ and $\\lambda$ be its positive meridian and preferred longitude. The exterior homology theorem gives $H_1(E_K;\\mathbb Z)=\\mathbb Z[\\mu]$. Let $\\phi:\\pi_1(E_K)\\to\\mathbb Z$ be the composite of abelianization with the homomorphism $[\\mu]\\mapsto1$. For an integer $q\\ge2$, let $\\phi_q$ be the composite $\\pi_1(E_K)\\xrightarrow{\\phi}\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathbb Z/q\\mathbb Z$, and let $p_q:E_q\\to E_K$ be the connected cover classified by $\\ker\\phi_q$. On $T_K$, the homomorphism sends $[\\mu]\\mapsto1$ and $[\\lambda]\\mapsto0$, so the preimage of $T_K$ is a connected torus cover whose fundamental group corresponds to $\\langle\\mu^q,\\lambda\\rangle$. Let $\\widetilde\\mu$ be the closed lift of $\\mu^q$. Attach a solid torus to $E_q$ with its meridian identified with $\\widetilde\\mu$; the resulting oriented closed $3$-manifold is the $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $\\Sigma_q(K)$. In tubular coordinates near $K$, the extended map to $S^3$ has local form $(s,w)\\mapsto(s,w^q)$, and the deck group $\\mathbb Z/q\\mathbb Z$ acts by $w\\mapsto e^{2\\pi i/q}w$.",

          "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [

          ]

          "source": "lem-slice-disk-double-cover-is-rational-homology-ball",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $K\\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $D\\subset B^4$ be a smooth properly embedded disk with boundary $K$. Let $W_D$ be the connected double cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$. Then $W_D$ is a rational homology four-ball and its oriented boundary is the double branched cover $\\Sigma_2(K)$ formed using the positive-meridian convention. This assertion concerns smooth disks only and makes no claim for locally flat topological disks.",
          "uses": [

            "3.1"
          ]

          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $B$ be a compact connected oriented smooth four-manifold with $H_*(B;\\mathbb Q)\\cong H_*(\\mathrm{point};\\mathbb Q)$ and connected rational homology sphere boundary $Y$. Assume $Y$ has a nonsingular framed-link surgery presentation with the boundary orientation and linking convention of the surgery linking-form result. The coefficient sequence $0\\to\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathbb Q\\to\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z\\to0$ gives an isomorphism $\\beta:H^1(Y;\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z)\\to H^2(Y;\\mathbb Z)$. Define the cohomological linking pairing by\n$$\\lambda_Y(x,y)=\\langle\\beta^{-1}(x)\\smile y,[Y]\\rangle\\in\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z.$$\nLet $M$ be the image of restriction $H^2(B;\\mathbb Z)\\to H^2(Y;\\mathbb Z)$ and $M^\\perp=\\{x:\\lambda_Y(m,x)=0\\text{ for every }m\\in M\\}$. Then the boundary Spin$^c$ structures extending over $B$ form one affine coset of $M$, the pairing is nonsingular, $M=M^\\perp$, and $|M|^2=|H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z)|$.",

          "source": "thm-correction-term-obstruction-from-rational-ball",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Let $B$ be a smooth compact four-manifold with $H_*(B;\\mathbb Q)\\cong H_*(\\mathrm{point};\\mathbb Q)$ and oriented boundary the rational homology sphere $Y$, where $H_*(Y;\\mathbb Q)\\cong H_*(S^3;\\mathbb Q)$. If a boundary Spin$^c$ structure $\\mathfrak t$ extends over $B$, then its Heegaard Floer correction term vanishes: $d(Y,\\mathfrak t)=0$. The extension hypothesis is essential; no vanishing is asserted for Spin$^c$ structures that do not extend.",
          "uses": [
            "3.1"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F4",
          "source": "lem-branched-cover-surgery-presentation-from-seifert-surface",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ bound a connected compact oriented Seifert surface $F$ of genus $g$. Choose a disk-band decomposition of $F$ with one disk and $2g$ bands, and use its band-core basis $a_1,\\ldots,a_{2g}$ to form the positive-push Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. For $q\\ge2$, define the symmetric block matrix $M_q(V)$ of size $2g(q-1)$ by specifying its $2g\\times2g$ blocks, indexed by $1\\le k,\\ell\\le q-1$:\n$$(M_q(V))_{k\\ell}=\\begin{cases}V+V^T,&k=\\ell,\\\\-V^T,&\\ell=k+1,\\\\-V,&k=\\ell+1,\\\\0,&|k-\\ell|\\ge2.\\end{cases}$$\nPush the interior of $F$ into $B^4$ while keeping $K$ on $S^3=\\partial B^4$, cut $B^4$ along a thickened copy of the pushed-in surface, and take $q$ copies. For $i=1,\\ldots,q-1$, glue the positive face of copy $i$ to the negative face of copy $i+1$ by reflecting the normal coordinate; do not glue the last positive face to the first negative face. Call the resulting $q$-fold cyclic branched cover $W_q(F)$. It has one $0$-handle and $2g(q-1)$ $2$-handles, and its framed attaching link has linking matrix $M_q(V)$. The boundary branched cover, with the boundary marking induced by the covering map, is $\\Sigma_q(K)$.",

          "source": "lem-cyclic-cover-linking-form-inverse-matrix",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $J=J_1\\cup\\cdots\\cup J_n$ be an oriented link of $n\\ge1$ smooth components in $S^3$. Choose pairwise disjoint closed tubular neighborhoods $N(J_i)$, let $X=S^3\\setminus\\operatorname{int}(\\bigcup_iN(J_i))$, and let $\\mu_i$ be the positive meridian of $J_i$. Let $\\lambda_i$ be the longitude parallel to $J_i$ with zero self-linking. Alexander duality identifies $H_1(X;\\mathbb Z)$ with $\\mathbb Z^n$ on the meridian basis $[\\mu_1],\\ldots,[\\mu_n]$; for $i\\ne j$, define $\\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ to be the $j$-th coordinate of $[\\lambda_i]$, the usual oriented linking number. Use the boundary-torus intersection convention $\\mu_i\\mathbin{\\cdot}\\lambda_i=+1$. Give $J_i$ an integer framing $f_i$ and fill along $\\delta_i=\\lambda_i+f_i\\mu_i$. Let $A$ be the symmetric integer matrix with $A_{ii}=f_i$ and $A_{ij}=\\operatorname{lk}_{S^3}(J_i,J_j)$ for $i\\ne j$. Assume $\\det A\\ne0$, and let $Y$ be the resulting oriented surgery manifold, oriented as the boundary of the 4-dimensional surgery handlebody with outward normal first. Then $H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z^n/A\\mathbb Z^n$. For torsion classes $[C],[D]\\in H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z)$ represented by oriented 1-cycles, choose $m>0$ and an integral 2-chain $F$ with $\\partial F=mC$ and define $\\lambda_Y([C],[D])=(F\\mathbin{\\cdot}D)/m\\pmod{\\mathbb Z}$, where the intersection is signed by the orientation of $Y$. If $x,y\\in\\mathbb Z^n$ are meridian-coordinate representatives of $[C],[D]$, then\n$$\n\\lambda_Y([x],[y])=-x^TA^{-1}y\\pmod{\\mathbb Z}.\n$$",

          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

          "quote": "A compact orientable three-manifold $M$ is **irreducible** if every embedded $2$-sphere in its interior bounds an embedded $3$-ball in $M$. $\mathbb{R}$ and a norm $N$ on it. When only one norm is in play we write
$\lVert v\rVert$ for $N(v)$; when several are, the norm is always named.

**The values of a norm are real numbers.** The codomain is $\mathbb{R}$, so
$N(v)$ is an honest element of the complete ordered field and no infinite value
is permitted. The same real-valued codomain is required of a metric by
[[def-metric-space]].

Let $V$ be a vector space over $\mathbb{R}$, with zero vector $0_V$. A **norm on
$V$** is a function $N : V \to \mathbb{R}$ such that for all $u, v \in V$ and all
$\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

- **(N1) Separation.** $N(v) = 0$ if and only if $v = 0_V$.
- **(N2) Absolute homogeneity.** $N(\lambda v) = |\lambda|\,N(v)$, the absolute
  value being that of [[def-abs-value]].
- **(N3) Triangle inequality.** $N(u + v) \le N(u) + N(v)$.

A **normed space** is a pair $(V, N)$ consisting of a vector space $V$ over
$\mathbb{R}$ and a norm $N$ on it. When only one norm is in play we write
$\lVert v\rVert$ for $N(v)$; when several are, the norm is always named.

**The values of a norm are real numbers.** The codomain is $\mathbb{R}$, so
$N(v)$ is an honest element of the complete ordered field and no infinite value
is permitted. The same real-valued codomain is required of a metric by
[[def-metric-space]].

### Nonnegativity is a theorem, not an axiom

Many texts add a fourth condition $N(v) \ge 0$. It is redundant. Applying (N2)
with $\lambda = -1$ gives $N(-v) = |-1|\,N(v) = N(v)$ ([[lem-of-abs-value]],
[[lem-vector-space-elementary-consequences]] for $(-1)v = -v$), and then (N3)
with $u = v$ and $-v$ gives

$$0 \;=\; N(0_V) \;=\; N\bigl(v + (-v)\bigr) \;\le\; N(v) + N(-v) \;=\; N(v) + N(v),$$

where $N(0_V) = 0$ is (N1). So $N(v) + N(v) \ge 0$, and if $N(v) < 0$ then
$N(v) + N(v) < 0$ by addition of inequalities, which trichotomy forbids
([[def-complete-ordered-field]]). Hence $N(v) \ge 0$ for every $v \in V$.

**Consequently the verification of a candidate norm has three things to check and
not four**, exactly as the verification of a candidate metric has three and not
four ([[def-metric-space]], [[lem-metric-nonnegativity]]). No item in this
library assumes nonnegativity of a norm before the argument above.

### The induced metric

Let $N$ be a norm on $V$ and define

$$d_N(u,v) \;:=\; N(u - v) \qquad (u, v \in V),$$

where $u - v = u + (-v)$ ([[def-vector-space]]). **Then $d_N$ is a metric on
$V$** ([[def-metric-space]]), and the three axioms are the three conditions
above, in order:

- **(M1)** $d_N(u,v) = 0$ means $N(u-v) = 0$, which by (N1) says $u - v = 0_V$,
  that is $u = v$; and conversely $d_N(v,v) = N(0_V) = 0$.
- **(M2)** $d_N(v,u) = N(v-u) = N\bigl((-1)(u-v)\bigr) = |-1|\,N(u-v) = d_N(u,v)$,
  by (N2), [[lem-of-abs-value]] and $(-1)w = -w$
  ([[lem-vector-space-elementary-consequences]]).
- **(M3)** $d_N(u,w) = N\bigl((u-v) + (v-w)\bigr) \le N(u-v) + N(v-w) = d_N(u,v) + d_N(v,w)$,
  by (N3).

A normed space is therefore a metric space, and every notion defined for metric
spaces — open set ([[def-metric-topology]]), convergence, Cauchyness,
continuity, compactness — is available in it with no further definition. **This
library never introduces a second notion of any of them for normed spaces.**

### Two properties an arbitrary metric need not have

The metric $d_N$ satisfies, for all $u, v, w \in V$ and $\lambda \in \mathbb{R}$:

- **translation invariance**, $d_N(u + w, v + w) = N\bigl((u+w)-(v+w)\bigr) = N(u-v) = d_N(u,v)$;
- **absolute homogeneity**, $d_N(\lambda u, \lambda v) = N\bigl(\lambda(u-v)\bigr) = |\lambda|\,d_N(u,v)$, by (N2).

**Not every metric on a vector space arises from a norm**, and homogeneity is
what fails. The published bounded remetrisation [[lem-bounded-remetrisation]]
replaces a metric $d$ by $d' = \min\{d, 1\}$, a metric with the same topology
whose values never exceed $1$; on a vector space $V$ containing a vector $v$ with
$d(v, 0_V) > 0$ this $d'$ cannot be $d_M$ for any norm $M$, since absolute
homogeneity would force $d'(\lambda v, 0_V) = |\lambda|\,d'(v, 0_V)$, which is
unbounded in $\lambda$, while $d'$ is bounded by $1$. So the passage from norms
to metrics is not reversible, and a statement about a metric on a vector space is
strictly weaker than the corresponding statement about a norm.",

$$\lVert x\rVert_p \;:=\; \Bigl(\sum_{k<n} |x_k|^{p}\Bigr)^{1/p},$$

[[thm-minkowski-finite]] supplies the corresponding triangle inequality for
rational $p \ge 1$. This item makes no claim with $p$ ranging over a real
interval; its rational domain is unchanged.

$$\lVert x\rVert_\infty \;:=\; \max\{\, |x_k| \;:\; k < n \,\},$$

used ([[lem-rational-power-well-defined]]).

the maximum of a nonempty finite set of reals, which exists and is one of its

          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Work in the smooth category ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Fix once and for all the
three-sphere as the one-point compactification

$$S^3:=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$$

of Euclidean three-space, carrying its standard smooth structure, and fix the
standard orientation of $S^3$: the orientation induced by the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$ under the one-point compactification, so that the
charts of the standard atlas away from $\infty$ are orientation-preserving and
the orientation is that of a connected oriented $3$-manifold in the sense of
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. For $r>0$ write
$\overline B_r:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2\le r\}$, the closed ball of
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]] with the following restriction convention. Smoothness on a closed ball means
local extension to a smooth map on an open neighborhood in Euclidean space;
smoothness on $M\times I$, for a smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, means
local extension across $t=0,1$ in $M\times\mathbb R$. Thus these closed domains
are not asserted to be manifolds without boundary in the cited definition.

**Links.** The **standard oriented circle** is the circle
$S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with its standard counterclockwise orientation,
regarded as a smooth $1$-manifold; a
**finite disjoint union of oriented circles** is a smooth manifold
$C=S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1$ ($k$ summands, $k\in\mathbb N$)
diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of $k$ standard oriented circles. An
**oriented link** (with $k$ components) is a smooth embedding

$$L\colon C\longrightarrow S^3$$

of such a disjoint union in the sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. So $L$ is
injective, is an immersion, and is a homeomorphism onto its image with the
subspace topology, and its image $L(C)$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly
embedded circles. Thus every link considered here is finite and tame: the
smoothness of $L$ is exactly the standing convention, and no polygonal or other
tame model is used. The **components** of $L$ are the images of the individual
summands, and the number of components is $k$.

**Ambient isotopy.** Let $I=[0,1]$. An **ambient isotopy** of $S^3$ is a smooth
map

$$H\colon S^3\times I\longrightarrow S^3$$

such that $H_0=\mathrm{id}_{S^3}$, each $H_t\colon S^3\to S^3$,
$H_t(x):=H(x,t)$, is a diffeomorphism ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
and each $H_t$ is orientation-preserving with respect to the fixed orientation.
The last clause is in fact automatic: $t\mapsto H_t$ is continuous in the
$C^\infty$ topology of the diffeomorphism group, the orientation sign is locally
constant in $t$, and $H_0=\mathrm{id}$ is orientation-preserving, so it is kept
only for emphasis.

**Equivalence of links.** Two oriented links $L_0\colon C_0\to S^3$ and
$L_1\colon C_1\to S^3$ are **equivalent** (written $L_0\sim L_1$), or
**ambient isotopic**, when there are an ambient isotopy $H$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $f:C_0\to C_1$ with
$H_1\circ L_0=L_1\circ f$. Thus parametrizations and component labels are
irrelevant, while the induced orientation of each image component is preserved. The relation is an equivalence relation on links:
it is reflexive with $H=\mathrm{id}$, transitive by composing isotopies, and
symmetric because a smooth family of diffeomorphisms has a smooth family of
inverses. An equivalence class is an **(oriented) link type**.

**Moving off $\infty$.** Because the definition of equivalence allows the
isotopy to move a link through $\infty$, the standard practice of this page is
to first apply an ambient isotopy that carries a given link into the open ball,
and only then to project; every projection and every Reidemeister move below is
read after moving the link off $\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ in this way. The
orientation-preserving clause in the definition of ambient isotopy is exactly
what the oriented Reidemeister moves and the oriented closure construction must
respect. The unoriented theory uses the same ambient isotopies but forgets
the orientations of the link components.

**Links in the three-sphere versus links in $\mathbb R^3$.** A link contained in
$\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$ is a link in $S^3$; conversely every link may be
assumed after isotopy to lie in $\mathbb R^3$, by choosing a point outside the compact one-dimensional image and moving that
point to $\infty$ by a smooth rotation of the standard sphere. When comparing
links already in $\mathbb R^3$, an isotopy can also be arranged to avoid
$\infty$ throughout; the track-avoidance argument is given in

          "quote": "Work in the smooth category ([[def-smooth-manifold]]). Fix once and for all the
three-sphere as the one-point compactification

$$S^3:=\mathbb R^3\cup\{\infty\}$$

of Euclidean three-space, carrying its standard smooth structure, and fix the
standard orientation of $S^3$: the orientation induced by the standard
orientation of $\mathbb R^3$ under the one-point compactification, so that the
charts of the standard atlas away from $\infty$ are orientation-preserving and
the orientation is that of a connected oriented $3$-manifold in the sense of
[[def-oriented-smooth-manifold-and-oriented-chart]]. For $r>0$ write
$\overline B_r:=\{x\in\mathbb R^3:\lVert x\rVert_2\le r\}$, the closed ball of
[[def-euclidean-spheres-and-closed-balls]] with the following restriction convention. Smoothness on a closed ball means
local extension to a smooth map on an open neighborhood in Euclidean space;
smoothness on $M\times I$, for a smooth manifold $M$ without boundary, means
local extension across $t=0,1$ in $M\times\mathbb R$. Thus these closed domains
are not asserted to be manifolds without boundary in the cited definition.

**Links.** The **standard oriented circle** is the circle
$S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with its standard counterclockwise orientation,
regarded as a smooth $1$-manifold; a
**finite disjoint union of oriented circles** is a smooth manifold
$C=S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1$ ($k$ summands, $k\in\mathbb N$)
diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of $k$ standard oriented circles. An
**oriented link** (with $k$ components) is a smooth embedding

$$L\colon C\longrightarrow S^3$$

of such a disjoint union in the sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. So $L$ is
injective, is an immersion, and is a homeomorphism onto its image with the
subspace topology, and its image $L(C)$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly
embedded circles. Thus every link considered here is finite and tame: the
smoothness of $L$ is exactly the standing convention, and no polygonal or other
tame model is used. The **components** of $L$ are the images of the individual
summands, and the number of components is $k$.

**Ambient isotopy.** Let $I=[0,1]$. An **ambient isotopy** of $S^3$ is a smooth
map

$$H\colon S^3\times I\longrightarrow S^3$$

such that $H_0=\mathrm{id}_{S^3}$, each $H_t\colon S^3\to S^3$,
$H_t(x):=H(x,t)$, is a diffeomorphism ([[def-diffeomorphism-and-local-diffeomorphism-of-manifolds]]),
and each $H_t$ is orientation-preserving with respect to the fixed orientation.
The last clause is in fact automatic: $t\mapsto H_t$ is continuous in the
$C^\infty$ topology of the diffeomorphism group, the orientation sign is locally
constant in $t$, and $H_0=\mathrm{id}$ is orientation-preserving, so it is kept
only for emphasis.

**Equivalence of links.** Two oriented links $L_0\colon C_0\to S^3$ and
$L_1\colon C_1\to S^3$ are **equivalent** (written $L_0\sim L_1$), or
**ambient isotopic**, when there are an ambient isotopy $H$ and an orientation-preserving diffeomorphism $f:C_0\to C_1$ with
$H_1\circ L_0=L_1\circ f$. Thus parametrizations and component labels are
irrelevant, while the induced orientation of each image component is preserved. The relation is an equivalence relation on links:
it is reflexive with $H=\mathrm{id}$, transitive by composing isotopies, and
symmetric because a smooth family of diffeomorphisms has a smooth family of
inverses. An equivalence class is an **(oriented) link type**.

**Moving off $\infty$.** Because the definition of equivalence allows the
isotopy to move a link through $\infty$, the standard practice of this page is
to first apply an ambient isotopy that carries a given link into the open ball,
and only then to project; every projection and every Reidemeister move below is
read after moving the link off $\infty$ into $\mathbb R^3$ in this way. The
orientation-preserving clause in the definition of ambient isotopy is exactly
what the oriented Reidemeister moves and the oriented closure construction must
respect. The unoriented theory uses the same ambient isotopies but forgets
the orientations of the link components.

**Links in the three-sphere versus links in $\mathbb R^3$.** A link contained in
$\mathbb R^3\subset S^3$ is a link in $S^3$; conversely every link may be
assumed after isotopy to lie in $\mathbb R^3$, by choosing a point outside the compact one-dimensional image and moving that
point to $\infty$ by a smooth rotation of the standard sphere. When comparing
links already in $\mathbb R^3$, an isotopy can also be arranged to avoid
$\infty$ throughout; the track-avoidance argument is given in
[[thm-oriented-reidemeister-equivalence-theorem]].",

local extension across $t=0,1$ in $M\times\mathbb R$. Thus these closed domains

$S^1=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$ with its standard counterclockwise orientation,
regarded as a smooth $1$-manifold; a
**finite disjoint union of oriented circles** is a smooth manifold
$C=S^1\sqcup\dots\sqcup S^1$ ($k$ summands, $k\in\mathbb N$)
diffeomorphic to the disjoint union of $k$ standard oriented circles. An
**oriented link** (with $k$ components) is a smooth embedding

$$L\colon C\longrightarrow S^3$$

of such a disjoint union in the sense of [[def-smooth-embedding]]. So $L$ is
injective, is an immersion, and is a homeomorphism onto its image with the
subspace topology, and its image $L(C)$ is a finite disjoint union of smoothly
embedded circles. Thus every link considered here is finite and tame: the
smoothness of $L$ is exactly the standing convention, and no polygonal or other
tame model is used. The **components** of $L$ are the images of the individual
summands, and the number of components is $k$.

$$H\colon S^3\times I\longrightarrow S^3$$

symmetric because a smooth family of diffeomorphisms has a smooth family of
inverses. An equivalence class is an **(oriented) link type**.

          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components.           "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

        {
          "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "lem-slice-disk-exterior-has-homology-of-a-circle",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $D\\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk and let $X_D$ be its compact exterior. Then $X_D$ is connected, $H_1(X_D;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z$ generated by the positive meridian, and $H_i(X_D;\\mathbb Z)=0$ for every $i\\ge2$.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-homology-over-a-pid",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free\nright $R$-modules, and $G$ a left $R$-module. Then naturally in $C,G$,\n$0\\to H_n(C)\\otimes_RG\\to H_n(C\\otimes_RG)\\to\\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_{n-1}(C),G)\\to0$\nis exact.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "def-infinite-cyclic-cover-of-a-slice-disk-exterior",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $X_D$ be the exterior of a smooth proper disk, with positive-meridian isomorphism $H_1(X_D;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z$. Let $X_{D,\\infty}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of $\\pi_1(X_D)\\to H_1(X_D;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z$, and let $t$ denote the deck transformation represented by the positive meridian. For $q\\ge2$, define $X_{D,q}=X_{D,\\infty}/\\langle t^q\\rangle$.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1",
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "thm-long-exact-sequence-in-homology",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Let\n$$0\\to A_\\bullet\\to B_\\bullet\\to C_\\bullet\\to0$$\nbe a short exact sequence of complexes in an abelian category. Then there is an\nexact sequence\n$$\\cdots\\to H_n(A)\\to H_n(B)\\to H_n(C)\\xrightarrow{\\partial_n}H_{n-1}(A)\\to H_{n-1}(B)\\to H_{n-1}(C)\\to\\cdots.$$",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1",
            "3.1"
          ]
        }
      ],

          "step": "1.1",
          "claim": "The deck transformation acts trivially on $H_0(X_{D,\\infty};\\mathbb F_p)\\cong\\mathbb F_p$ because the cover is connected. From the first sequence in [F2], its homology exact sequence and [F1] show that $t-1$ is an isomorphism on $H_i(X_{D,\\infty};\\mathbb F_p)$ for every $i\\ge1$: for $i\\ge2$ both neighboring homology groups of $X_D$ vanish, while in degree one exactness uses $H_2(X_D)=0$, $H_1(X_D)=\\mathbb F_p$, and the zero map $t-1$ on $H_0(X_{D,\\infty})$.           "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "def-q-fold-branched-cover-of-a-slice-disk",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $K\\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot bounding a smooth proper disk $D\\subset B^4$, and let $q\\ge2$. Write $X_D$ for the compact disk exterior and let the positive meridian induce $\\pi_1(X_D)\\to H_1(X_D;\\mathbb Z)\\cong\\mathbb Z\\to\\mathbb Z/q$. Let $X_{D,q}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of this map. Attach $D^2\\times D^2$ to $X_{D,q}$ along the connected cover of $D^2\\times S^1$ using the normal-disk map $z\\mapsto z^q$. The resulting compact oriented $4$-manifold $W_{D,q}$ is the $q$-fold cyclic cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$; its boundary is $\\Sigma_q(K)$, and the local branched model is $(x,z)\\mapsto(x,z^q)$.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1",
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "lem-prime-power-cyclic-cover-homology-of-slice-disk-exterior",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $D\\subset B^4$ be a smooth proper disk, let $p$ be prime, $q=p^k$ with $k\\ge1$, and let $\\mathbb F_p$ be the field with $p$ elements. For the connected $q$-fold cyclic cover $X_{D,q}$ of the disk exterior, $H_0(X_{D,q};\\mathbb F_p)\\cong\\mathbb F_p$, $H_1(X_{D,q};\\mathbb F_p)\\cong\\mathbb F_p$, and $H_i(X_{D,q};\\mathbb F_p)=0$ for every $i\\ge2$.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "lem-compact-smooth-manifolds-have-finite-cw-models-under-countable-choice",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$. Every compact smooth manifold, with boundary\nallowed, has the homotopy type of a finite CW complex. If its boundary is a\nsupplied finite CW manifold, the collar may be retained in a finite relative CW\nmodel.",
          "uses": [
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "def-countable-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Countable Choice**, written $\\mathrm{AC}_\\omega$, is the following\nstatement.\n\n> For every family $(X_n)_{n \\in \\mathbb{N}}$ of nonempty sets indexed by\n> $\\mathbb{N}$ there is a function $f$ with domain $\\mathbb{N}$ such that\n> $f(n) \\in X_n$ for every $n \\in \\mathbb{N}$.\n\nEquivalently, in the vocabulary of Choice function: every at most\ncountable family of nonempty sets has a choice function.",
          "uses": [
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

        {

          "source": "thm-mayer-vietoris-sequence-in-singular-homology",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For an open cover $X=U\\cup V$, the sequence\n$$\\cdots\\to H_n(U\\cap V;G)\\to H_n(U;G)\\oplus H_n(V;G)\\to H_n(X;G)\\xrightarrow{\\delta}H_{n-1}(U\\cap V;G)\\to\\cdots$$\nis exact, with middle map $(u,v)\\mapsto u+v$.",

        },

          "source": "thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-homology-over-a-pid",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free\nright $R$-modules, and $G$ a left $R$-module. Then naturally in $C,G$,\n$0\\to H_n(C)\\otimes_RG\\to H_n(C\\otimes_RG)\\to\\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_{n-1}(C),G)\\to0$\nis exact.",

          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [

          ]

          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $K\\subset S^3$ be a smooth oriented knot bounding a smooth proper disk $D\\subset B^4$, and let $q\\ge2$. Let $X_{D,q}$ be the connected cover classified by the kernel of this map. Attach $D^2\\times D^2$ to $X_{D,q}$ along the connected cover of $D^2\\times S^1$ using the normal-disk map $z\\mapsto z^q$. The resulting compact oriented $4$-manifold $W_{D,q}$ is the $q$-fold cyclic cover of $B^4$ branched along $D$; its boundary is $\\Sigma_q(K)$, and the local branched model is $(x,z)\\mapsto(x,z^q)$.",

          "quote": "Assume AC.           "source": "thm-casson-gordon-third-bordism-group-finite",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC, as in the smooth Casson–Gordon bordism convention. For every prime-power integer $d$ and $G=\\mathbb Z/d\\oplus\\mathbb Z$, the oriented bordism group $\\Omega_3^{SO}(K(G,1))$ is finite.",
          "uses": [

          ]
        },

          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "def-oriented-bordism-group-of-a-space",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Let $X$ be a path-connected CW space. The oriented bordism set $\\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ consists of classes of pairs $(M,f)$, where $M$ is a closed smooth oriented $n$-manifold and $f:M\\to X$. Two pairs are bordant when there is a compact oriented $(n+1)$-manifold $W$ with $\\partial W=M_0\\sqcup(-M_1)$ and a map $F:W\\to X$ restricting to $f_0$ and $f_1$ on the boundary. Disjoint union defines the operation. For a group $G$, $K(G,1)$ denotes a connected CW space with fundamental group $G$ and contractible universal cover.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "lem-oriented-bordism-classes-over-a-space-form-an-abelian-group",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For every path-connected CW space $X$, disjoint union makes $\\Omega_n^{SO}(X)$ an abelian group with identity the empty manifold with its unique map to $X$ and inverse of $(M,f)$ represented by $(-M,f)$.",
          "uses": [

          "source": "thm-compact-smooth-manifolds-with-corners-admit-relative-finite-triangulations",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice as an ambient hypothesis; the finite construction and\nthe ODE interfaces below use no additional choice, so this hypothesis is\ndispensable. A smooth manifold with corners here is Hausdorff and second\ncountable, with charts in relatively open subsets of $[0,\\infty)^c\\times\\mathbb R^{n-c}$\nand transition maps smoothly extendible with invertible derivative at corner\npoints; transitions preserve the local depth and its face germs. Let $M$ be\ncompact. Then $M$ has a finite corner-adapted whole-star smooth triangulation.\nCorner faces are locally subpolyhedra, and any specified finite union of\nclosed faces is a subpolyhedron.\n\nIf the total boundary already has a finite piecewise smooth triangulation\n$f:L\\to\\partial M$ compatible on all local face intersections, with its\ndifferential fan giving a homeomorphism onto the union of boundary faces of the\ntangent orthant at each point, the triangulation extends to $M$, pointwise\npreserving $f$ with compatible subdivisions allowed. In the resulting finite\nunion construction all intersections may be made full subcomplexes. The same\nrelative conclusion applies to a fixed corner-adapted triangulated closed neighbourhood piece\nwhose smaller protected subcomplex lies in its relative interior: fitting is\nperformed away from that protected subcomplex. No extension of arbitrary\nincompatible boundary data is asserted.",

          ]

        {
          "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [

          ]
        }

          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",

    "lem-prime-power-branched-cover-homology-is-finite": {

        {
          "fact": "A1",
          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "lem-cyclic-cover-order-root-product-and-rational-sphere-test",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $F$ be a connected compact oriented Seifert surface of genus $g$, and let $V$ be its positive-push Seifert matrix in an ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\\mathbb Z)$. Write $\\Delta_K(t)$ for the Alexander polynomial normalized up to multiplication by $\\pm t^k$, and let $q\\ge2$ with $\\zeta_q$ a primitive $q$-th root of unity. Then $H_1(\\Sigma_q(K);\\mathbb Z)$ is finite if and only if $\\Delta_K(\\zeta_q^j)\\ne0$ for every $1\\le j<q$, and, when it is finite,\n$$\n|H_1(\\Sigma_q(K);\\mathbb Z)|=\\prod_{j=1}^{q-1}|\\Delta_K(\\zeta_q^j)|.\n$$\nThe same criterion and order hold when $\\Delta_K(t)$ is replaced by $\\det(V-tV^T)$.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1",
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "lem-seifert-matrix-skew-part-is-surface-intersection",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented embedded circle in the oriented standard three-sphere, let $F$ be a connected compact smooth oriented embedded surface with boundary $K$, and let $a_1,\\ldots,a_{2g}$ be any ordered integral basis of $H_1(F;\\mathbb Z)$ with Seifert matrix $V_{ij}=\\operatorname{lk}(a_i^+,a_j)$. Let $J_F$ be the matrix of the algebraic intersection form on $F$, with a transverse intersection of oriented curves $u,v$ counted positively exactly when their ordered tangent vectors form a positive basis of $TF$. Then $V-V^T=J_F$. The matrix $J_F$ is skew-symmetric and unimodular; when $a_1,\\ldots,a_{2g}$ is a standard handle basis, it is a direct sum of blocks $\\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\\\-1&0\\end{pmatrix}$.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "thm-cyclotomic-polynomials-are-irreducible-over-the-rationals",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "For every $n\\ge1$ the cyclotomic polynomial $\\Phi_n$\n([[def-cyclotomic-polynomial]]) is irreducible in $\\mathbb Q[t]$\n([[def-irreducible-and-prime-elements-in-a-domain]]).",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F4",
          "source": "lem-linking-pairing-on-rational-homology-sphere-is-nonsingular",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. If $Y$ is a closed connected oriented $3$-manifold with finite $H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z)$, then the bounding-chain torsion linking pairing $\\lambda_Y$ is symmetric and nonsingular: its adjoint $H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z)\\to\\operatorname{Hom}(H_1(Y;\\mathbb Z),\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z)$ is an isomorphism.",
          "uses": [
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F5",
          "source": "thm-universal-coefficient-theorem-for-homology-over-a-pid",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $R$ be a PID, $C$ a chain complex of free\nright $R$-modules, and $G$ a left $R$-module. Then naturally in $C,G$,\n$0\\to H_n(C)\\otimes_RG\\to H_n(C\\otimes_RG)\\to\\operatorname{Tor}^R_1(H_{n-1}(C),G)\\to0$\nis exact.",
          "uses": [
            "3.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F5",
          "source": "thm-poincare-duality-for-oriented-topological-manifolds",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $M$ be an $R$-oriented boundaryless $n$-manifold, with $R$ commutative unital; manifolds are Hausdorff and second countable here. Then cap with the compatible compact orientation classes gives isomorphisms\n$$D_M:H_c^p(M;R)\\xrightarrow{\\sim}H_{n-p}(M;R)$$\nfor every integer $p$, including disconnected, noncompact and empty $M$.\n\nNaturality means that for an open inclusion $i:U\\hookrightarrow M$ with restricted orientation, $D_M e=i_*D_U$, where $e$ is extension of compact supports. For compact $M$, $H_c^p(M;R)=H^p(M;R)$ canonically and $D_M(a)=a\\cap[M]$. For arbitrary $M$ the isomorphism is the direct sum of those on its components. AC is used in the countable coordinate-neighborhood selection for exhaustion and in the local universal-coefficient proof.",

          ]

          "source": "def-axiom-of-choice",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "The **Axiom of Choice** (AC) is the following statement.\n\n> Every family of nonempty sets has a choice function\n> (Choice function).\n\nWritten out: for every set $\\mathcal{F}$ all of whose members are nonempty,\nthere exists a function $g$ with domain $\\mathcal{F}$ satisfying $g(S) \\in S$ for\nall $S \\in \\mathcal{F}$.\n\nAn equivalent formulation is that a product of nonempty sets is nonempty: if\n$X_i \\ne \\emptyset$ for every $i \\in I$, then $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i \\ne \\emptyset$.\nHere $\\prod_{i \\in I} X_i$ is the set of functions $f$ with domain $I$ such that\n$f(i) \\in X_i$ for every $i \\in I$; when a family of nonempty sets is indexed by\nitself, such an $f$ is precisely a choice function for it.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F1",
          "source": "lem-prime-power-branched-cover-homology-is-finite",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot and let $q=p^k$ for a prime $p$ and $k\\ge1$. Then $H_1(\\Sigma_q(K);\\mathbb Z)$ is finite, so $\\Sigma_q(K)$ is a rational homology sphere and carries a nonsingular torsion linking form.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F2",
          "source": "lem-slice-disk-induces-branched-cover-metabolizer",
          "source_section": "Statement",
          "quote": "Assume AC. If a smooth oriented knot $K$ bounds a smooth proper disk $D$ in $B^4$ and $q$ is a prime power, then\n$$P_D=\\ker\\bigl(H_1(\\Sigma_q(K);\\mathbb Z)\\to H_1(W_{D,q};\\mathbb Z)\\bigr)$$\nis a metabolizer for the torsion linking form of $\\Sigma_q(K)$.",
          "uses": [
            "1.1",
            "2.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F3",
          "source": "def-smooth-and-topological-slice-genus",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot in the standard oriented three-sphere and let $B^4$ be the standard four-ball with boundary $S^3$. Let $\\mathcal S_{\\mathrm{sm}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable smooth properly embedded surfaces $F\\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. Let $\\mathcal S_{\\mathrm{top}}(K)$ be the set of genera of connected compact orientable locally flat topologically properly embedded surfaces $F\\subset B^4$ with oriented boundary $K$. For each such surface, its genus $g(F)$ is the nonnegative integer determined by $\\chi(F)=1-2g(F)$. Define the smooth slice genus and the locally flat topological slice genus by\n\n$$\ng_4^{\\mathrm{sm}}(K):=\\min\\mathcal S_{\\mathrm{sm}}(K),\\qquad g_4^{\\mathrm{top}}(K):=\\min\\mathcal S_{\\mathrm{top}}(K).\n$$",
          "uses": [
            "1.1"
          ]
        },
        {
          "fact": "F4",
          "source": "def-finite-linking-form-and-metabolizer",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "A finite nonsingular linking form is a pair $(A,\\lambda)$, where $A$ is a finite abelian group and $\\lambda:A\\times A\\to\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z$ is symmetric and induces an isomorphism $A\\to\\operatorname{Hom}(A,\\mathbb Q/\\mathbb Z)$. For $P\\le A$, put $P^\\perp=\\{a\\in A:\\lambda(a,p)=0\\text{ for every }p\\in P\\}$. A metabolizer is a subgroup $P$ with $P=P^\\perp$; equivalently, $\\lambda$ vanishes on $P\\times P$ and $|P|^2=|A|$.",
          "uses": [
            "2.1"
          ]
        },

          "fact": "F5",
          "source": "def-finite-order-character-of-a-branched-cover",
          "source_section": "Definition",
          "quote": "Assume AC. Let $K$ be a smooth oriented knot, let $q\\ge2$, and let $M=\\Sigma_q(K)$ be its $q$-fold cyclic branched cover.           "uses": [
